title: Rodgers says he's done with Steelers, claims McCarthy asleep in meetings
summary: The Steelers are releasing Aaron Rodgers, sources told ESPN, after the quarterback said Wednesday on "The Pat McAfee Show" that coach Mike McCarthy has been sleeping through team meetings.
full_text:
The Pittsburgh Steelers are releasing Aaron Rodgers , sources told ESPN, after the quarterback said Wednesday on "The Pat McAfee Show" that he wouldn't return to the team after his stunning benching and alleged that coach Mike McCarthy has been sleeping through team meetings.
Because this move is happening after the NFL's trade deadline, Rodgers will be available to be claimed by any other team on waivers. If he goes unclaimed, he will become an unrestricted free agent.
"That ship has sailed," Rodgers said of his time with the Steelers.
He said he found out from teammate Pat Freiermuth that he was being benched and still hasn't heard the news from McCarthy.
Rodgers said Freiermuth told him on a phone call, "I can't believe they're doing this," and Rodgers said he replied "'Doing what?'"
Rodgers said his agent has been in contact with Steelers general manager Omar Khan, however.
The four-time MVP said he had extensive conversations with McCarthy over the past two days, and the word "benching" never came up.
Rodgers then went on to recount his past week with McCarthy and said the coach was "snoring" in team meetings and said this was "not an abnormal week."
"Last Wednesday, we were in a quarterback meeting. Mike came in late, sat down, and within 10 minutes began snoring. Woke himself up, was rattling his papers. We all looked around. Five minutes later, you hear the snoring again. And less than five minutes after that, he walks out of the room like nothing happened," Rodgers said.
He then went on to describe what happened on Sunday when the Steelers struggled in a 19-16 loss to the Philadelphia Eagles .
"... there was some guys early on that didn't like the way things were going, especially defensive guys that Mike didn't want to get to know the defense. At one point I told him, 'You should really lean into the defensive guys a little bit more and talk to those guys.' And he said, 'Well, I don't think I need to.' And I said, 'Well, I disagree with that.' So, a lot of those guys, he kind of already lost a lot of those guys. And I think the nail in the coffin for so many of us was at halftime, towards the end of it, we're kind of on the offense on one side of defense on the other side. And there's some rambling or something and without even a heads up, he says, 'All right, one, two, three Packers.'
"That's what he broke it down on in the locker room."
Rodgers said he and his teammates "looked around going, "What the f---? What is going on? Where's his head at at this point?'"
Multiple league sources corroborated Rodgers' account to ESPN. One source texted: "It's all true." Another source told ESPN that McCarthy "crossed" Rodgers, leading to the quarterback's account Wednesday.
Rodgers said he and McCarthy talked on Monday, and he said to the coach, "'Hey, this last week, this is not what we talked about. We've had these conversations for months now and it began as a concerned friend about somebody who's unhealthy. If you're sleeping in meetings, you're unhealthy. If you're not coming to everything, you should be coming to as a playcaller.'"
Rodgers said the issues with McCarthy go back to training camp. He said it's a "delicate situation because the coaching staff is worried about their job security and the players are worried about their money and their job security. And I don't. I've made money."
"There's no one else who can tell him. And again, I'll reiterate, originally, I'm talking about in training camp when this stuff was going on, when he was missing meetings and the word was he's sleeping and then he's sleeping in the coaches' film sessions and he's not alert here. And he doesn't want to get to know the defense. I'm telling the defense, "Hey, just trust me. You just got to give him time. He'll be fine." And then he's telling me I don't need to get to know the defense at all," Rodgers said.
Rodgers said "other individuals" have talked to McCarthy about his habits "and he just shoots off at it and gets super angry and goes into getting after the person bringing it, not the actual content of what's going on."
He said he believes that McCarthy doesn't "know the plan."
"I think he learns the plan during the week. And multiple times he said that he doesn't watch film when I've talked to him on Tuesdays. He hasn't seen the film yet. Hadn't seen the film yet. I don't know how that's possible on a Tuesday after you play on a Sunday," Rodgers said.
He called McCarthy's attitude "disrespectful to the game itself."
"... you have people's careers involved, people's livelihood, players and coaches. And I'm sure there'll be some sort of gag order or something around the conversations. Also, like I said earlier, it's not the easiest thing to talk about. And I don't expect people to come out strong in my defense, even everybody in there knows what the truth is. Everybody knows the truth. I'm talking about training staff, equipment staff, strength and conditioning, players in the locker room, the people upstairs, they all know the truth.
"And the difference between, I've said this in the show before, conspiracy and the truth is what? It's time. At some point, this stuff's going to get out, and people are going to realize what is actually going on. It's crazy and it shouldn't be like that. And I came to him many, many times to try and help him."
Rodgers said he "vouched" for McCarthy to Khan to interview him for the Steelers' head coaching job but this is "not what I signed up for."
Rodgers said he "looked into what was going on in Dallas [when McCarthy was the Cowboys' coach] and what happened there. And it's the same thing that went on in Green Bay for a decade because the coaches and the support staff there know exactly what happened."
Rodgers said he told McCarthy on Monday that, "'we can't even have an honest conversation. I'm telling you, you snored in the meeting twice, in a quarterback meeting, that's unacceptable. And you're telling me you've never slept at a facility before. And I'm telling you, I have a hundred witnesses and collaborating people who would support what I'm saying. I'm not saying that to f---ing bury you.
"I'm saying that because this behavior and these habits are not healthy and they're not becoming of someone falling to place, intimately involved in the game plan. And that's my whole point. And so, I left it with him that if you try and bench me or don't change the play call, then you should just release me because I feel like at this point, I'm doing what's right for the organization."
Rodgers says McCarthy told him he would do what's right for the organization which Rodgers believed was "getting rid of me."
"Now obviously you got the owner and GM on the side, which is also comedy because I've talked to the GM multiple times. We've made jokes in the hallway about him having intimate knowledge about Mike's sleeping habits at the facility. So, I'm just like, you know what it is," he said. "You know what's actually going on. What are we even talking about at this point? We could have kept this all quiet and made these changes. It shouldn't even get to that in the first place. It should be a level of professionalism that is kind of the baseline of doing your job at the highest level because nobody knows this is going on. Nobody knew what was going on for 10 years in Green Bay."
Despite how his time in Pittsburgh is ending, Rodgers said he loved his time in the city.
"I thanked Mike T [Tomlin] last year for giving me that joy and passion back. I mean, in the two years I've been here, I've made some super tight friendships, and we got such a good group of guys, such a great veteran leadership, guys that give a s---, guys that play hard, great personalities all over the board," he said. "That's the hard part. It could be easy. And I think from the beginning there was a resentment that we were a veteran team and that Cam [Heyward] had an opinion and T.J. [Watt] had opinion and Jalen Ramsey had an opinion and DK Metcalf had an opinion. HAnd…

title: Sources: Rodgers excused from Steelers facility to process stunning benching
summary: The Steelers have benched Aaron Rodgers in a stunning twist that could signal the end of the star QB's NFL career.
full_text:
PITTSBURGH -- The Steelers have benched Aaron Rodgers in a stunning twist that could signal the end of the star quarterback's NFL career.
Rodgers, who will be inactive for Pittsburgh's Black Friday game against the Denver Broncos , was excused from being at the team facility Wednesday while he processes his benching, a source told ESPN's Adam Schefter.
The four-time MVP was not at the Steelers' 8 a.m. ET meeting and is not expected to attend the noon practice. Steelers coach Mike McCarthy is scheduled to address reporters before the practice.
The Steelers announced their decision one day after McCarthy unequivocally told reporters that Rodgers was Pittsburgh's quarterback. The Steelers reversed course, however, announcing Tuesday in a late-night social media post that longtime backup Mason Rudolph will start Friday against the Broncos.
The move to bench Rodgers, who turns 43 next week, was a coach's decision, sources told ESPN. That means Rodgers, who previously announced this would be his last season after a 22-year career, might have played his final snap.
As of Wednesday morning, the Steelers had no immediate plans to release Rodgers, sources told NFL Network's Mike Garafolo.
The Steelers are searching for a spark on offense amid Rodgers' struggles during Pittsburgh's two-game losing streak.
The Steelers held a series of offensive staff meetings Tuesday, sources told ESPN's Adam Schefter. Sources described the meetings as "some good, some bad," and the Steelers ultimately opted to bench Rodgers and start Rudolph.
One topic discussed in those meetings, sources told Garafolo, was a change in Pittsburgh's playcalling process. The proposed change was for quarterbacks coach Tom Arth to relay plays in to Rodgers, at Rodgers' behest, sources told Garafolo.
The Steelers also held meetings with players, including Rodgers, sources told NFL Network's Ian Rapoport.
Rodgers has completed 60.9% of attempts this season, marking one of his worst campaigns since he became a full-time starter with the Green Bay Packers in 2008. He has been sacked 31 times this season, surpassing last season's total of 29, and leads the NFL with 257 yards lost on sacks.
His 18.9% off-target percentage ranks 28th of 30 qualified passers this season, ahead of only Atlanta Falcons quarterback Michael Penix Jr. (22.1%) and the New York Giants ' Jameis Winston (24.8%).
In a 19-16 loss against the Philadelphia Eagles in Week 11, Rodgers missed a wide-open Jaylen Warren on a play that could have turned into a 30-yard score.
"I feel like I had to throw it maybe harder than I usually do to the backs," Rodgers said Sunday, explaining that Eagles cornerback Cooper DeJean 's movement on the play affected his throw. "But yeah, that was a missed opportunity for sure."
Rodgers returned to the Steelers this season on a one-year deal worth up to $25 million after going 10-6 as Pittsburgh's starter in 2025. The four-time MVP was instrumental in McCarthy's eventual hire in Pittsburgh, suggesting general manager Omar Khan take a look at his former Green Bay coach during the hiring process to replace Mike Tomlin.
On Monday, McCarthy pointed to the struggles of the entire offense when asked how he evaluated Rodgers' play in the team's losing streak.
"Just like anything, when you talk about the quarterback position, I think there's things offensively we need to do better and that always benefits and leads into quarterback play," McCarthy said. "So I just need him to just keep plowing away. We got a lot of work to do."
Rudolph, a 2018 third-round pick by the Steelers, is no stranger to taking over in difficult situations. In 2023, Rudolph went 3-0 in the final three regular-season games when he took over for Mitchell Trubisky and Kenny Pickett as the team searched for -- and found -- a spark. That experience, coupled with his tenure in the organization and rapport with teammates in the locker room, sources told ESPN, was critical in making the decision to start Rudolph on a short week against the Broncos.
author: Brooke Pryor

title: Aiyuk to sign with Commanders, will reunite with college QB Daniels
summary: Wide receiver Brandon Aiyuk is signing with the Commanders on their practice squad, agent Drew Rosenhaus told ESPN's Adam Schefter.
full_text:
ASHBURN, Va. -- Wide receiver Brandon Aiyuk is signing with the Washington Commanders on their practice squad, agent Drew Rosenhaus told ESPN's Adam Schefter on Wednesday.
Aiyuk now will once again become teammates with Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels , who Aiyuk played with at Arizona State in 2019.
The San Francisco 49ers released Aiyuk on Tuesday, two weeks after the NFL reinstated him. He cleared waivers, making him an unrestricted free agent.
Washington coach Dan Quinn said Aiyuk looked strong and fast in workouts, but there is no timetable for when he might see the field.
"It'll take a lot of work to get to that spot to be ready and impact the team in a strong way," Quinn said. "I'm excited to add him to the group. This is the type of competitor I love coaching, competing with and competing against. Let's get started."
Washington general manager Adam Peters, who was with Aiyuk in San Francisco from 2020 to 2023, praised the receiver during his paid weekly appearance on 106.7 The Fan earlier Wednesday. He called Aiyuk a "smart football player" and said he was one of the "hardest workers on the team" with the 49ers.
"One of the things that I don't think anyone can dispute is his work ethic," Peters said. "That's how he became an All-Pro-type player."
He then discussed Aiyuk's on-field talent, pointing to his final full season of 2023 when he was named second-team All-Pro.
"He was a true No. 1 receiver at the time. He's a guy who's a tough cover, he's great after the catch. There's a lot of great things about him on the field," Peters said. "It wasn't just that he was the most gifted guy; he's self-made too. There's a lot of positives."
Peters said he hasn't talked to Aiyuk in "a couple years."
"I can't speak on all what happened between him and the 49ers," Peters said. "What I do remember is he's a very motivated player."
Aiyuk has not played since tearing the ACL, MCL and meniscus in his right knee on Oct. 20, 2024, and was placed on the 49ers' reserve/left squad list last December. He could not be removed from that list until he reported and passed a physical, which he did Nov. 9.
"I'm feeling great, feeling healthy," Aiyuk told 49ers reporters earlier this month. "It was a long recovery process, a long rehab process, but I'm back to 100%."
In 2023, his last full season before his injury, Aiyuk was named second-team All-Pro after catching 75 passes for 1,342 yards and seven touchdowns.
A rift between Aiyuk and Daniels appeared to have developed following a series of social media posts by the receiver. Aiyuk targeted Daniels in several posts and in one referenced Daniels' mother.
However, Daniels and Aiyuk spoke more than a month ago to clear the air, according to multiple sources.
Daniels befriended Aiyuk early in their time together at ASU -- before Daniels had won the starting quarterback job. During workouts, Daniels would throw with Aiyuk, who was going into his senior season and coming off a 33-catch, 474-yard season.
They quickly developed a rapport as Aiyuk ended the season with Associated Press All-America honors after catching 65 passes for 1,192 yards and eight touchdowns.
author: John Keim

title: Bills' Kincaid, Benford among 5 starters who are questionable vs. Chiefs
summary: The Bills are listing five starters -- including tight end Dalton Kincaid and cornerback Christian Benford -- as questionable for Thursday night's showdown with the Chiefs.
full_text:
ORCHARD PARK, N.Y. -- The Buffalo Bills are listing five starters as questionable for one of the biggest games of the year.
Tight end Dalton Kincaid , cornerback Christian Benford , guard O'Cyrus Torrence , linebacker Dorian Williams and defensive lineman T.J. Sanders are all questionable for Thursday's night's matchup between the Bills (9-1) and Kansas City Chiefs (8-2) at Highmark Stadium (8:20 p.m. ET, NBC) in a Thanksgiving game with significant AFC playoff implications.
Kincaid (ankle/thumb), Benford (groin), Williams (calf) and Sanders (shoulder) all sat out the Bills' Week 11 win over the Miami Dolphins . Benford was the only player who was listed with a "did not participate" classification on any of the Bills' injury reports this week, a designation that occurred on Monday, a day after the win over Miami.
Instead of holding a full-speed practice Tuesday, Bills coach Joe Brady opted for a walk-through lasting roughly one hour. He credits his team for having the right type of veteran composure and demeanor that allows him to trust that the players will be prepared for Thursday without needing a standard practice day.
Without Benford, the Bills relied on young cornerbacks Davison Igbinosun and Maxwell Hairston as starters versus Miami, but rotated in veteran Tre'Davious White , who was elevated up from the practice squad on Saturday. Kincaid's absence necessitated a full philosophical overhaul; the Bills went from using 11 personnel (1 tight end and 1 running back) on just 44% of plays through the first nine games to a whopping 80% without Kincaid available.
Kincaid still ranks as the Bills' second leading receiver in receptions and yards, even after missing last week's game. Benford is second on the Bills in pass breakups this season. Williams is tied for the team lead with two interceptions while ranking second on the team in tackles.
Torrence's likely replacement would be veteran Austin Corbett , who started one game last month when left guard Alec Anderson was out. Williams' backup is rookie Kaleb Elarms-Orr , and the defensive line rotation minus Sanders consists of Landon Jackson , Greg Gaines and DeWayne Carter .
author: Nick Suss

title: Falcons 'aware' of insinuations Pearce still trying to contact ex Jackson
summary: Kevin Stefanski said he and the team are aware of assertions made by Rickea Jackson that insinuated James Pearce Jr. is still trying to contact her.
full_text:
FLOWERY BRANCH, Ga. -- Atlanta Falcons coach Kevin Stefanski said he and the team are aware of social media assertions made by WNBA player Rickea Jackson that insinuated defensive end James Pearce Jr . is still attempting to contact her, the coach said.
An agreement with a Florida court prohibits Pearce, Jackson's ex-boyfriend, from contacting or coming near Jackson.
"I'm aware," Stefanski said Wednesday. "We've spoken to James. But we don't have much more to add."
A video posted to TikTok by someone seemingly unrelated to the situation showed a scroll of dozens of missed calls from a no-ID number. Jackson reposted the video on her own TikTok and left comments on the original post, saying this is a situation she is "actively going through."
In the comment, Jackson said she has not spoken to or about "this person" in nearly a year and "won't say anything else ever again." She implied that she has not told the court, because she would be told that there isn't enough evidence that the unknown calls are coming from Pearce.
Pearce, 23, was arrested last Feb. 7 after allegedly ramming his car multiple times into a vehicle driven by Jackson in Doral, Florida, and not allowing her to enter a police station. Police responded, and Pearce fled in his car before crashing and then fleeing on foot.
Pearce was charged with felony aggravated battery with a deadly weapon and felony fleeing police and resisting arrest, as well as misdemeanor stalking, before entering into a one-year pretrial diversion program that allowed him to avoid trial . Those charges will be dropped if Pearce stays out of trouble for that one-year period, passes random drug tests and remains compliant with a mental health treatment program.
Jackson filed a petition for a protective order against Pearce in February, and she dropped it in lieu of the intervention program. Pearce must also stay away from Jackson and not contact her as part of that program.
Jackson wrote in the initial petition following Pearce's arrest that she was "in fear of my life" and that if the court did not intervene, she believed "James will kill me," according to Miami-Dade County court documents obtained by ESPN.
Pearce was suspended eight games by the NFL due to a violation of the personal conduct policy at the end of training camp. He returned to the field with the Falcons in Week 9.
Pearce has not spoken to the media at all this season and has declined multiple attempts by media members for comment.
author: Marc Raimondi

title: Chiefs rule RB Walker (groin) out for showdown vs. Bills
summary: Chiefs running back Kenneth Walker III (groin) has been ruled out for Thursday's showdown against the Bills, the team announced Wednesday
full_text:
KANSAS CITY, Mo. -- Chiefs running back Kenneth Walker III will not play in Thursday night's showdown against the Buffalo Bills , the team announced Wednesday.
Walker will miss his third consecutive game with a grade-two groin strain. Since the Chiefs are playing on a short week, the team is holding Walker out against the Bills to give him more time to rest. After playing the Bills, the Chiefs will face the Los Angeles Rams on the road next Thursday night.
Walker was a limited participant in Tuesday's practice, the Chiefs' lone on-field work this week.
Starting in Walker's place will be rookie running back Emmett Johnson , who has been impressive in his past four games. During that stretch, Johnson produced 491 all-purpose yards and five total touchdowns, including back-to-back 100-plus yard rushing efforts in wins over Atlanta and Arizona the last two weeks in Walker's absence.
"It's been great having an opportunity to watch Emmett do his thing because that's what he's supposed to do," offensive coordinator Eric Bieniemy said Monday. "The next man should always have that mentality because we're coaching the starter to be the starter, but we're also coaching that next man to be prepared to be the man. I think Emmett has done a great job, but we also understand the value that Kenneth brings."
The Chiefs expect to have right guard Trey Smith back in the starting lineup after he missed last week's win over the Cardinals while in the NFL's concussion protocol. Right tackle Jaylon Moore , who has a right ankle injury, has also been ruled out against the Bills. Joshua Ezeudu is once again expected to step in for Moore.
author: Nate Taylor

title: Longtime Lions owner Martha Firestone Ford dies at age 101
summary: Martha Firestone Ford, who served as the primary owner of the Lions from 2014 to 2020, has died at the age of 101, the team announced Tuesday night.
full_text:
Martha Firestone Ford, who served as the primary owner of the Detroit Lions from 2014 to 2020, has died at the age of 101, the team announced Tuesday night.
"Over more than six decades with the Detroit Lions, she was a loyal and constant fixture of the franchise, sharing in its history and traditions," the team said in a statement announcing her death. "She remained present with the team even this season, attending games with a devotion that endured throughout her life."
No cause of death was given, although the team said she died at home surrounded by her family.
Ford and her husband, William Clay Ford Sr., bought the Lions in 1963, and she took over his controlling interest in the team after his death in 2014.
Although she seldom spoke to reporters or commented publicly on the direction of the franchise, her influence was felt. She was in charge of the team from 2014 until 2020, when she turned the Lions over to her daughter, Sheila Ford Hamp.
Ford had since served as chair emeritus.
"Martha was special," NFL commissioner Roger Goodell said in a statement. "She cared so deeply about her family, the players, their fans, and the city of Detroit. She was committed to making the Lions -- and the game of football -- better. Martha and her husband, William Clay Ford, led the franchise with dignity and integrity. We will miss her kindness and sweet sense of humor. We extend our deepest condolences to her children, the entire Ford family, and the Lions' organization."
The Lions made the playoffs in Ford's first year in charge in 2014 but lost seven of their first eight games the following season. In November 2015, the team fired its president and general manager in a midseason shake-up. When Ford announced the changes, she told fans the franchise intended to "identify and hire the very best leadership in order to produce a consistently, winning football team."
The Lions played better down the stretch that season, and after hiring Bob Quinn as their new general manager, they returned to the playoffs a year later.
Although Ford kept a low profile, the 2015 shakeup was a sign that she was more than willing to bring about change in an effort to reverse the team's fortunes. Then-coach Jim Caldwell said she was very much a presence within the organization.
"I think visible ownership is great, and Mrs. Ford does it extremely well," Caldwell said in 2015. "She's there before games and she's there after games, and I think guys enjoy that part of it. She comes to practice and things of that nature, so it's been fun."
Ford also made an impact in the Detroit community. She was an officer on the board for Detroit Lions Charities and on the board of the Henry Ford Health System. Martha and William Clay Ford were credited with helping establish the Maplegrove Center, a substance abuse treatment facility in West Bloomfield, Michigan.
Born Sept. 16, 1925, in Akron, Ohio, Martha Parke Firestone was a granddaughter of tire magnate Harvey Firestone. She graduated from Vassar College in 1946 and married William Clay Ford Sr., Henry Ford's grandson, the next year.
In 2017, Forbes estimated her net worth at more than $1.4 billion.
She is survived by her four children, 14 grandchildren and 17 great-grandchildren.
The Associated Press contributed to this report.

title: Broncos' Payton: RB Dobbins suspended one game for detrimental conduct
summary: The Broncos suspended running back J.K. Dobbins for one game for conduct detrimental to the team.
full_text:
ENGLEWOOD, Colo. -- Denver Broncos coach Sean Payton said Tuesday that he has suspended running back J.K. Dobbins for Friday's game against the Pittsburgh Steelers due to "conduct detrimental.''
Dobbins will not practice or take part in any team activities this week. The Broncos (8-2) face the Steelers on Friday at Acrisure Stadium in Pittsburgh.
"There is one team announcement, I'm not going to comment afterwards: I'm suspending J.K. Dobbins for this weekend's game, conduct detrimental, that's all I'm going to say about it,'' Payton said after Tuesday's practice. "Head coach's decision.''
Asked if he wanted to elaborate on any of the circumstances that surrounded the decision, Payton said no and added "think it's better that way.''
Dobbins was in the Broncos' facility earlier Tuesday and then left, multiple team sources said. Payton then told players of the suspension in the team's normally scheduled group meeting.
Dobbins, in his second season with the team and a player Payton had called one of the "top priorities'' to re-sign this past offseason, had one carry, for no gain, in the Broncos' 38-24 victory Sunday over the Las Vegas Raiders . It marked the first time since the 2020 season Dobbins had a single carry in a game he was in uniform to play -- he had two one-carry games for the Baltimore Ravens that year.
Dobbins was visibly frustrated at times on the sideline during Sunday's game and high-fiving teammates at other times. When asked about the running back rotation Monday, Payton had offered that Dobbins "is healthy'' and that "J.K. is going to be super important for what we're doing in this stretch.''
Jonah Coleman , who sat out four games earlier this season because of an ankle injury, has steadily received more work since his Week 7 return to the lineup. Coleman got 24 of the team's 27 carries by running backs Sunday. Coleman's 111 yards rushing were also the team's first 100-yard rushing game since Dobbins' 111 in a Week 8 win last season over the Dallas Cowboys .
The Broncos also designated running back Tyler Badie for return from injured reserve Tuesday, and he practiced with the team and was listed as a full participant. Asked if Badie would play Friday or how the rotation might look against the Steelers, Payton said, "I'm not going to get into who's playing.''
Running back RJ Harvey (knee) is eligible to return from injured reserve next week.
Quarterback Bo Nix , when asked about the suspension, said: "Well, obviously I have nothing to do with it,'' Nix said. "Just keep finding our way to figure out how to win games, fortunately it has nothing to do with me.''
Cornerback Pat Surtain II , also a team captain like Nix, offered a similar answer with, "I ain't got nothing much to say, it's coach's decision at the end of the day.''
It's all a long way from Dobbins' promise -- he termed it a "pinkie swear'' -- both during the team's minicamp in June as well as training camp, that he would play in every game this season and lead the league in rushing.
"This year, forget a top-three, I keep saying it, people think I'm crazy but I'm going to be No. 1, and I'm going to keep it there for the whole year,'' Dobbins said in August. "You know, 17 games. A lot of people get mad when I say the injuries are over, cause I said it last year, but that one was pretty fluky, right? This year there won't be any.''
Dobbins has dealt with several injuries in his career, including a career-threatening knee injury, and he sat out the final seven regular-season games because of a foot injury as well as both of the Broncos' playoff games last season. His 15 games played in 2020, as a rookie for the Baltimore Ravens, is still the most games he has played in a season.
It is believed Dobbins, who signed a two-year, $16 million deal with the team this past offseason, is the first player suspended by the Broncos during a season for conduct detrimental to the team since wide receiver Brandon Marshall in 2009.
author: Jeff Legwold

title: 'A big part of what we do': Johnson to stick with Swift's role in Bears' run game
summary: Chicago Bears running back D'Andre Swift won't have an extended stay in Ben Johnson's doghouse after fumbling in the fourth quarter against the Saints.
full_text:
LAKE FOREST, Ill. -- Chicago Bears running back D'Andre Swift won't have an extended stay in Ben Johnson's doghouse after fumbling in the fourth quarter against the Saints.
Swift has lost three fumbles through 10 games, which are his most since the 2023 season. The 27-year-old back was pulled from the lineup after New Orleans recovered his fumble at its own 46-yard line and did not return to the game.
That's the second time this season Swift has been benched in game after fumbling.
Swift's fumbles have gone from an aberration to an issue that has become more frequent than at any other point of his Bears tenure. But when asked Tuesday whether Swift needs to regain the trust of his head coach, Johnson rebuffed the idea.
"No, he just needs to hold on to the ball and we'll be fine," Johnson said.
The Bears rushed for 146 yards against the Saints, their third-highest output of the season. Still, Johnson was displeased with the run game's efficiency, spotlighted by Swift's 13 carries for 51 yards (3.9 yards per carry). The veteran back also recorded his first touchdown reception of the season.
"We weren't as consistent running the ball as we had wanted to be coming off the bye, that was a point of emphasis for us," Johnson said postgame. "When I looked at our runners, they were under four yards a carry. That efficiency stat that we talked about, we weren't hitting that."
The Bears' offense centers on a rushing attack that ranks third leaguewide at 142.4 yards per game. That figure would not be possible without Swift, who has played in all 10 games and shouldered a heavier load while running back Kyle Monangai missed five straight weeks with turf toe and a thumb injury. Monangai returned in Week 11 but was limited to eight carries for 18 yards.
With a quick turnaround before facing the Lions on Thanksgiving and seeking their first NFC North win, the Bears are quickly searching for a way to get their run game on track.
From Johnson's perspective, the solution is right in front of them.
"We're going to continue to stress that running game," Johnson said Tuesday. "We got too many good players for it to be lacking behind like it is right now. So, we got to continue to sink into that. It's a big part of what we do and who we are. Whether that's Swift, whether that's Monangai, Salvon [Ahmed] came on and played some big snaps for us. We're going to do that, and we're going to continue to possess the ball and those types of things so that opens up our passing game eventually."
Swift ranks 14th in rushing yards (627), and his 10 rushing TDs are tied for the third in the league. He signed a three-year, $33.75 million contract extension with Chicago before Week 1.
author: Courtney Cronin

title: 👀 11 players who have the most to gain or lose over the rest of the season
summary: Big money on the line for George Pickens and Brian Branch? QB1 role at stake for J.J. McCarthy? Here are 11 players with something to prove over the next seven weeks.
full_text:
Thanksgiving week is the start of the sprint to the end of the NFL's regular season . And while there are players who know their teams don't have much to play for between now and then, there are plenty more who have quite a bit riding on what happens over the rest of the 2026 campaign.
Those stakes can be different things. For some, it's money, especially for young players on rookie deals who haven't yet signed a potentially lucrative second contract. For others, it's opportunity. There are rotational players who want to establish themselves as starters and veterans hanging on who want to stick in the starting lineup for another season.
Subscribe: 'The Bill Barnwell Show'
I'll take a look at 11 of those players who have the most to gain or lose over the remainder of the season, inspired by what they did in Week 11 and what's to come over the rest of the year.
Jump to: Cousins | Metcalf | Pickens McCarthy | Lassiter | Rice Branch | Shough | Andrews Watson | Van Ness
Well, the honeymoon is over. Last week, Vikings fans who had witnessed two months of Kyler Murray and Carson Wentz struggling to move the ball welcomed Cousins back with open arms, and despite a few hiccups, the good outweighed the bad. Cousins threw for 207 yards and two touchdowns in a comfortable victory over the rival Packers .
On Sunday in what amounted to a de facto home game for the 49ers in Mexico City, the magic dissipated. A great outing from Cousins likely wouldn't have made the difference on a day when the vaunted Vikings defense allowed the 49ers to score touchdowns on three of their first four drives in a 35-10 loss , but coach Kevin O'Connell might have hoped to find out.
Instead, playing a pass defense that Dak Prescott and the Cowboys picked apart last week , the Vikings struggled. Cousins went 26-of-38 for 235 yards with a brutal pick-six on an underneath pass that Ji'Ayir Brown jumped and returned to the house without even needing to break stride. After a touchdown on their second drive of the game and a field goal on their third, the Vikings didn't score again the rest of the way, with Justin Jefferson losing a fumble and two fourth-quarter drives failing on downs.
Cousins bears the brunt of the blame for the interception, and I suspect he'll wish he played better. But the most notable clip of this game from a Vikings perspective will probably be Cousins shouting at his offensive linemen on the sideline; he was knocked down seven times in the loss. And the issues that plagued Minnesota during the collective stints of Murray and Wentz at quarterback are likely to create problems for it against good teams moving forward.
Again, they couldn't run the ball. Aaron Jones Sr . had a physically impressive finish to his touchdown run, but the Vikings turned 21 carries into 69 yards and five first downs. Jordan Mason had a 16-yard carry, but it came against San Francisco's backups in the fourth quarter with Wentz on the field. The run game was mostly hopeless with Cousins out there.
An absent run game and a trailing game script takes Cousins away from play-action, which is where he has been at his best as a pro, 2026 included. The Raiders couldn't run the ball, either, but Klint Kubiak is excellent at creating throws for his quarterback with play-fakes, run game be damned. Before his trade to the Vikings , Cousins was third in the NFL in QBR when using play-action and 14th in the league when he was dropping back as a pure passer. Seven of Cousins' eight interceptions with the Raiders came in those pure dropback situations.
On Sunday, Cousins was effective using play-action, going 7-of-12 for 91 yards, averaging 7.6 yards per throw. Without it? He went 19-of-26 for 144 yards, averaging 5.5 yards per attempt. That included the pick-six, too. With nothing threatening Brown downfield or any sort of run fake to throw off his read, the 49ers safety was able to come from the backside of the play and poach Cousins' attempted slant to Brown, all but deciding the contest late in the first half.
Cousins has made more than $333 million in his career and has a minimum of another $10 million on the way in 2027. While many players on this list might have significant money riding on their performance over the rest of this season, that's probably not as important for Cousins. What might matter, though, is opportunity. If Cousins thrives in his second stint with the Vikings, O'Connell & Co. will likely bring him back as their starter in 2027, especially given the regrets the organization has about letting everyone from Cousins to Sam Darnold to Daniel Jones (and now potentially J.J. McCarthy ) walk out the door in years past. And even if the Vikings decide to go in a different direction, a successful second half from Cousins likely would earn the 38-year-old a starting opportunity somewhere else next season.
There's still plenty of time for Cousins to get things right, and there won't be many teams capable of getting a multi-touchdown lead on Brian Flores' defense over the rest of the season. After mostly unbridled enthusiasm from all sides about Cousins returning to the Vikings, though, the blowout loss was the coming-back-to-Earth moment for everyone involved.
Let's start with two wideouts who were essentially part of a multi-deal trade of sorts. The Steelers didn't want to re-sign Pickens, who was one year from unrestricted free agency, and traded him to the Cowboys in 2025 for a third-round pick. That third-rounder became Drew Allar , who is playing behind Aaron Rodgers at quarterback. The Steelers filled their need for a top wideout by sending a second-rounder to the Seahawks for Metcalf. The Seahawks used that pick to move up and select a cornerstone safety in Nick Emmanwori .
This sure looks like a three-team trade where two teams won and the Steelers lost. And it's not ideal to see your top wideout finish the day with as many receiving yards as personal foul penalties, but that was the Steelers' situation Sunday. In a frustrating loss to the Eagles , Metcalf caught just one pass on four targets for 2 yards before being ejected late in the third quarter for attempting to poke cornerback Cooper DeJean in the eye. Rodgers dropped back 53 times and was sacked five times, but he spent most of the day targeting rookies Germie Bernard and Max Hurleman .
This was probably rock-bottom for Metcalf's very disappointing tenure in Pittsburgh. In addition to trading that second-round pick to the Seahawks for Metcalf, the Steelers gave their new wideout a four-year, $132 million extension. (Emmanwori will make less than $12 million combined over his four-year deal in Seattle.) Metcalf racked up a career-low 850 yards in his first season with the Steelers before a late-season suspension after getting into an altercation with a fan ; he had just two catches in last season's playoff loss to the Texans .
Though Rodgers was optimistic about the blossoming connection with his training camp roommate this summer, Metcalf has looked even more detached from the offense this season. He's on pace to finish with just 738 receiving yards and three touchdowns, both of which would be career lows. His 1.3 yards per route run is also a career low, down from his 1.9 YPRR in Seattle and 1.8 YPRR a year ago.
At his best, Metcalf has shown the ability to win downfield and overwhelm smaller defensive backs in contested-catch situations. Rodgers didn't make that throw very often in 2025, as Metcalf was targeted just 14 times on deep shots all season. Seven of those throws came in two games, suggesting that the Steelers had it as a priority heading into the game a couple of times and then forgot about getting Metcalf the football for multiple weeks.
With Mike McCarthy in the fold in 2026, Rodgers has targeted Metcalf downfield more often, but it hasn't been effective. Metcalf has just five catches on 22 deep shots this season, and that is nearly half of the league's completion rate (39.2%) on those throws. On Sunday, Metcalf…
author: Bill Barnwell

title: How will Packers use Micah Parsons in return from torn ACL?
summary: Parsons and the Packers must balance protecting his surgically repaired knee with turning him loose Wednesday.
full_text:
INGLEWOOD, Calif. -- Micah Parsons ' first game with the Green Bay Packers last season could serve as a blueprint for what his expected 2026 debut might look Wednesday against the Los Angeles Rams ( 8:00 p.m. ET, Netflix ).
Just like in Week 1 last season, when he played less than two weeks after he was acquired from the Dallas Cowboys , Parsons will be on a snap count.
But this time, he might not be able to talk his way into additional snaps.
Last year, Parsons played 30 official snaps out of 67 (45%) in first game in a Packers uniform. The edge rusher wasn't even supposed to play that many, according to coach Matt LaFleur, who joked at the time that he would "investigate" how that happened .
"Sometimes you've got to fight for your own right to play," Parsons said at the time.
On Wednesday, however, the Packers figure to be stricter. Last year, he was trying to shake off rust after missing all of the Cowboys' training camp following a trade request. Now, Parsons is coming back from a torn ACL and meniscus in his left knee suffered on Dec. 14.
But that doesn't mean he won't try.
"I think once I'm in the zone, I'm in the zone, and people don't really mess with you when you're in a zone," said Parsons, who on Monday was cleared to return . "And I think where we're at in the season, every win matters. And you don't want to lose games because you're worried about the outcome, when at this point we can say every game is going to be the difference between playoffs or [going on vacation in] Cancun.
"I'm into that mindset, preparing for more and doing more than what my job requires."
It has taken Parsons longer to return than the typical nine to 10 months for a surgically repaired ACL, although he also had a torn meniscus. The Rams game comes 347 days after his injury. That's 11 months and 11 days. From the date of Parsons' surgery, it's 333 days, or 10 months and 29 days. For comparison, receiver Christian Watson made his return from a torn right ACL 294 days (nine months and 24 days) after his injury.
"I wish he would stay out one more week," Rams defensive tackle Aaron Donald said with a smile. "He come back next week or something. A fan of Micah, I think he's one hell of a football player, fast, explosive, plays with an unbelievable motor. If he does play this week, that's going to be huge for them.
"Micah, if you want to take one more week to get yourself 100%, make sure everything is where it needs to be, I'd like to see you on TV. I know they're going to be happy to have him back, a hell of a football player."
Upon his return to practice earlier in November, Parsons admitted he may not be up to his own standards right away.
"I think you'll see flashes of All-Pro Micah when I get to pass rush, and there's going to be times when you're going to be like, 'Dang, what was Micah doing?'" Parsons said. "There's going to be times when I question myself, too."
• Has Puka played his final snaps for Rams? • How will Packers use Micah in ACL return? • Joe Milton's big chance on Thanksgiving • Can Vikings' O win when D doesn't dominate? • Inside the gymnastics lore of Ja'Marr Chase
Parsons might take a repeat of his debut performance last season, when he had three pressures with a sack. His pressures resulted in a 2-yard loss on a completion, an interception by safety Evan Williams and the sack on his 23rd snap of the game.
Of Parsons' 30 snaps, 13 of them came on third downs and two on fourth downs.
Perhaps even more than what Parsons did on the field, his arrival in Green Bay sent a jolt through the entire organization, just like it is this time.
"Definitely," quarterback Jordan Love said. "I always say, any time you watch somebody get injured and you see them go through the whole process of rehab and training on the side and just how hungry they are to get back and get back on the field, I think any time somebody steps into that role and is able to come back on the field, it feels good.
"It's definitely just positive energy for everybody, but you add that it's Micah Parsons, the type of player he is and what he brings to that defense, and obviously how much teams got to game-plan for him. So if he's out there on Wednesday, he'll definitely bring some energy and some juice. I know the defense will be fired up to have him back, and they'll be flying around."
So will Jonathan Gannon. The Packers' first-year defensive coordinator hasn't had the chance to coach a game with Parsons yet, but he has been thinking about it for a while. The day before Parsons practiced for the first time this season, Gannon was asked how often he thinks about game-planning with Parsons in the lineup.
When asked if he'll have any trouble incorporating Parsons into a defense that has played 10 games without him, Gannon didn't hesitate.
"No," he said. "Obviously when you have very talented players, you want to highlight them and put them in good positions as much as we can to impact the game, and understanding a player of his caliber, people are going to play you different."
It's a new defense for Parsons, too, who played last season for Jeff Hafley, who is now the Dolphins' head coach.
"It's just about me showing what I can do and then however they want to incorporate and add to the system, I just got to be open and ready and willing to learn," Parsons said. "I think we've all had that adjustment so far."
ESPN Rams reporter Sarah Barshop contributed to this report.
author: Rob Demovsky

title: Has Puka Nacua played his final snaps in a Rams uniform?
summary: Nacua is in the final season of his rookie deal. The factors of signing him to an extension are glaring.
full_text:
IT WAS LATE in the fourth quarter against the Washington Commanders and coach Sean McVay and the Los Angeles Rams needed a first down to win the game.
Facing a third-and-11 with 1 minute, 44 seconds to go, McVay called a jet sweep to Rams star wide receiver Puka Nacua , the player he and quarterback Matthew Stafford often turn to with the game on the line. Nacua was tackled after a 5-yard gain. He stayed down longer than usual after the hit, but eventually walked off the field.
The Rams won that Week 9 game to improve to 5-4, but the hit to Nacua was costly. The tackle left the fourth-year wideout with a sprained MCL and PCL in his right knee, as well as turf toe. Nacua had surgery on his MCL a week ago , and his recovery time is expected to be four to five months, forcing him to miss the rest of this season, including the playoffs. He is expected to be ready for the start of the 2027 season.
The day after the surgery, the NFL announced that Nacua was suspended for three games for violating the league's personal conduct policy. The suspension came after a woman in Los Angeles filed a lawsuit in March alleging Nacua made an "unprovoked antisemitic statement" and later bit her on the shoulder. Nacua denied the allegations and later entered a rehab center.
Nacua is in the final season of his rookie deal, one the 2023 fifth-round pick has outplayed since his historic rookie year . But will he actually be back in Los Angeles next season? While the Rams have acknowledged both his off-the-field incidents and the way his physical play style affects his availability, neither changes the Rams' thinking about a contract extension, a team source said.
"I think you're watching young guys -- no different than I'm continuing to try to mature as a man -- figure out how do you navigate these responsibilities in all parts of your life being a professional," McVay said this week. "And I think he's growing and I trust his heart and I think he's making a lot of steps that are in the right direction.
"I'm bummed for him that he got injured. It was a tough year because he kind of was banged up and playing through stuff, even more so than normal just with the style of play. And then obviously his season is over now with regards to him getting that surgery, but do expect him to return and be back in a couple months and ready to go."
When asked whether he expects Nacua to be a key player in 2027, McVay said while the Rams have a long list of pending free agents, Nacua is "a huge part of the conversation."
"He's obviously a guy that is a very important piece for us for now and for the future, but there's a lot of guys that fall into that category," McVay said.
There's no doubt Nacua is a difference-maker for this Rams offense. The wide receiver has a 26% target share in his career, the sixth highest among anyone with at least 50 games played since 2023, per ESPN Research.
"I can't see him anywhere else than being here," Rams team captain Quentin Lake said. "He has been such a cornerstone of this franchise for the last four years, but at the same time, whatever happens, happens. And we're all hoping that everything gets figured out and that he does stay. I think that's everybody's main priority. And I'm always in his corner as well."
RAMS WIDE RECEIVERS coach Eric Yarber has a motto for his room: "You can't live forever, so don't try to."
No one embodies that more than Nacua, whose style of physical play is part of what makes him so good and has made him such an ideal fit in McVay's offense.
"[Nacua] talks about being the hammer, not the nail ," Yarber told ESPN last season. "And that makes your run after catch that much more violent. DBs don't want to hit you; they're going to go low and they lose their technique and stuff like that. So when you're physical -- more physical than them -- they don't want to tackle you."
But with that physicality comes a cost: Nacua has not played a full season since his rookie campaign. After Nacua's season-ending hit in Washington in Week 9, McVay was asked about the playcall. The Rams were up by a touchdown and McVay and the Rams knew one more first down would effectively end the game. Instead, the Rams had to punt the ball back to Jayden Daniels and the Commanders. McVay said he'd be lying if he hadn't "questioned the decision-making on that last play over and over in my head."
"It's stuff that I feel tremendous responsibility for, and we have to be able to figure out how to protect these guys while also putting them in positions that help our team and allow them to be able to shine," McVay said. "He's a guy that we have to be intentional about because it's a bummer and because he can do so much, you want to make sure you don't take that for granted."
But while McVay said he and Nacua have talked about the possibility of not always taking big hits, "that's like telling a tiger not to be a tiger."
• Has Puka played his final snaps for Rams? • How will Packers use Micah in ACL return? • Joe Milton's big chance on Thanksgiving • Can Vikings' O win when D doesn't dominate? • Inside the gymnastics lore of Ja'Marr Chase
Nacua missed two games earlier this season after injuring his hip during practice. He missed just one game in 2025 with an ankle injury, but he was on injured reserve for five games the previous season with a knee injury.
"We try to educate them on situations," McVay said. "Where are the things that you can avoid? I do also believe ... part of that responsibility is on myself to make sure, how much are you exposing him to those types of plays? And it's not something that I take lightly."
During training camp, Nacua was asked for his personal goals entering the season.
"I think staying healthy is one of the biggest things," Nacua said. "I know that physicality that I play with I don't think it's ever going to change. It's ingrained in me, so continue to take care of my body in the ways that I need to."
IN MCVAY'S FIRST public comments after the lawsuit against Nacua came out in March of this year, the coach said the team had known about the incident since it happened on New Year's Eve and that he trusted Nacua and wanted to "be able to put my arm around him."
It was not Nacua's first off-the-field incident. In mid-December 2025, Nacua issued a statement to apologize for performing a gesture on an internet livestream that was "antisemitic in nature and perpetuated harmful stereotypes against Jewish people." On that same livestream, he said he thinks some NFL referees make calls just to get shown on TV during games.
Nacua released the statement the morning before the Rams played the Seattle Seahawks on Dec. 18. That night after the game, Nacua tweeted, "Can you say i was wrong. Appreciate you stripes for your contribution. Lol."
In the 2026 offseason, Nacua became eligible for a contract extension. Based on his on-field production, Nacua was expected to be in line for a record-setting payday. Seahawks wide receiver Jaxon Smith-Njigba , who was a first-round pick in Nacua's draft class, reset the market in March when he signed a four-year, $168.6 million contract extension that made him the highest-paid receiver in NFL history.

Nacua denies, later enters rehab center. • Nov. 8: Suffers PCL/MCL sprain, turf toe injury in game vs. Washington. • Nov. 12: Nacua placed on injured reserve, to miss at least next 4 games. • Nov. 19: NFL suspends Nacua for three games for personal conduct policy violation. WR to serve ban while on IR; eligible for reinstatement Dec. 14. • Nov. 20: Announced Nacua had MCL surgery on Nov. 17 and is likely out for at least the rest of the regular season. NFL unaware of surgery when it imposed suspension, source tells Adam Schefter.

author: Sarah Barshop

title: Latest NFL Week 12 buzz: Fits for Daniel Jones? Still no head coach changes?
summary: Where could Daniel Jones land? What's the latest on coaching hot seats? What's next for Puka Nacua? And who is getting MVP love in league circles?
full_text:
Week 12 of the 2026 NFL season comes with a serving of Thanksgiving football, and insiders Jeremy Fowler and Dan Graziano have been calling sources around the league for the latest news and notable buzz.
We begin this week with updates on the coaching carousel. There were already two changes by this point last season (Titans and Giants), but zero teams have moved on from their head coaches so far in 2026. What's the latest on hot seats around the league? Could we really make it through the regular season with no jobs coming open?
With Daniel Jones clearing waivers and becoming a free agent this week, our insiders also asked around on potential landing spots for him. And while Puka Nacua 's season might be over, his future is a big talker right now. Fowler and Graziano tried to get a sense of what comes next for the star receiver and whether the Rams will hand him a big extension in the offseason. And finally, they canvassed the league for a quick poll of who should win MVP as of now.
It's all here, as Fowler and Graziano answer big questions, hand out useful fantasy football nuggets and empty their reporting notebooks heading into Week 12.
Jump to: Head coach hot seat updates Fits for Jones | MVP candidates Nacua's future | Fantasy advice More notes, intel
Graziano: Well, it's not like no team has done anything . The Colts fired their GM weeks ago. The Panthers fired their defensive coordinator . The Cardinals fired their defensive coordinator . The Cowboys didn't fire their defensive coordinator, instead demoted him and kept him around to suffer with everyone else. But you want to know about head coaches, so fine. Situations I'm watching for potential change at the end of the season include the Jets, Buccaneers, Colts, Eagles and maybe Commanders, though Dan Quinn seems to be turning things around in D.C.
Would any of those teams move on from their head coach before the end of the season? I personally doubt it, in large part because I'm not sure which coordinators or assistants would be candidates to have audition roles the rest of the season. It is still early, and things could get bad enough in one or more of these spots that a team could decide to change for change's sake, but that's my read right now. Jeremy, how did I do?
Fowler: Nailed it! To be fair, there's usually a coaching change by this part of the season. The Titans' Brian Callahan and the Giants' Brian Daboll were properly fired before this point last season. Thanksgiving spelled the end for Chicago's Matt Eberflus in 2024. In 2023, Carolina's Frank Reich and Las Vegas' Josh McDaniels were gone before December. So, change is inevitable, and possibly soon. But I'm with you for this season, Dan -- it seems several ownership groups are willing to show some level of patience with their hot seat coaches.
That seems to be the case in Washington, where Quinn is rallying the Commanders and has a soft schedule coming up. The Bucs could wait until season's end for clarity on Todd Bowles' future, though Monday night vs. Carolina feels important (the Bucs would be three games out in the NFC South with a loss). It seems like Aaron Glenn, fresh off a win , should get the rest of the season with the Jets. Why not give him more time to see what he can do? There's no real rush there. So, if we're taking temperatures, your gauge on the five jobs above is correct, and I'll raise you a few more for the radar: the Saints and Cowboys.
Saints coach Kellen Moore making run-game staff changes during the bye week wasn't the best sign. And the vibes out of Dallas leadership are not great. The Christian Parker move was not universally well-received in the building. This might be a case where coach Brian Schottenheimer needs a playoff berth to ensure a third season.
Graziano: A wild note I saw recently is that the Saints have trailed in all 27 games in which Moore has been their head coach. They must figure out if Tyler Shough is their long-term future at QB, and if they don't think Moore is the coach to help get the most out of him, that could spell trouble, even after only two seasons.
And I agree on Schottenheimer. The Cowboys are more patient with coaches than their reputation would lead you to believe, but they had very high hopes for this season. If it fizzles out because they blew the defensive coordinator hire, and Schottenheimer gets to the end of the year with another losing record, I think there would be some smoke there.
Fowler: The Chargers are firmly on the radar despite coach Jim Harbaugh's massive buyout on a five-year deal (do the math on what was reported as a five-year, $80 million deal in 2024). If Harbaugh finishes, say, 2-15 in Los Angeles, ownership must do some soul-searching at that point, no? (Particularly when the team plays home games in a stadium it doesn't even own.) And if the Chargers still believe in Harbaugh , the bigger question becomes: Do they trust him to hire a third offensive coordinator in as many years? The Mike McDaniel hire has been flashy but has produced a 30th-ranked scoring offense and lack of a clear identity. The McDaniel era pales in comparison to the Greg Roman era (Roman is thriving with the Giants, by the way).
And Tennessee seems like one to watch because of the Titans' penchant for firings in recent years. I'm curious whether Tennessee breaks precedent and gives Robert Saleh time. The roster is not good, but no rebuild is ever easy for the coach because of the inevitably bad product. The Titans are 1-9, and a 51-30 loss to Dallas prompted Saleh to call his defense "dogs---" in a news conference. I'm not sure where to go with that, but what I'm saying is Tennessee is usually a wild card based on recent history.
Editor's note: As of Wednesday afternoon, Aiyuk is signing with the Commanders practice squad .
Fowler: Let's start with Jones. Now that he has cleared waivers, he must weigh whether to sign somewhere right away or wait this out to see what develops injury-wise around the league as the playoffs approach. Some people I've talked to inside the league wonder whether he'll choose the latter . The natural fit right now is New England, which is 5-5 and will be without Drake Maye for what looks like the rest of the regular season . But coach Mike Vrabel seems intent on starting Tommy DeVito , at least this week. So, maybe that's the play -- wait this week out, see what happens with New England or if another team develops an opening.
But I'm not sure which job would actually rebuild Jones' free agency value at this point. It depends what's important to him: a chance to start, take over for an older quarterback, be next season's bridge guy or learn a new system on a winning team.
Graziano: If I were considering signing Jones, I'd be thinking more about next season than this one based on everything we've seen from him this year. An Achilles injury is awfully serious, and he wouldn't be the first player we've seen look a lot better in his second season after that surgery than his first. The notion that the 2026 version of Jones could step in and help save someone's season is far-fetched.
I believe the Patriots want to go with DeVito in the hopes that he can keep their train on the track, but as we saw with that disastrous Carson Wentz start for the Vikings a couple of Monday nights ago , poor performance can absolutely change a team's plan. Jones seems like a guy who's going to get another chance somewhere at some point, but my expectations for him being a significant help to a team the rest of this season are quite low.
Fowler: As for Aiyuk, teams I've spoken to this week have real reservations about whether he gets a job right away, though those conversations occurred before news of his midweek visit to Washington . "I think he's unemployed for a bit," an NFC exec said. At least three unknown variables exist: health, conditioning and motivation. On the flip side, buying low isn't the worst thing. He's only 28, and practice squads are tailored for fliers like…
author: Jeremy Fowler and Dan Graziano

title: Will Brandon Aiyuk fit in Washington? What to expect, his role and fantasy impact
summary: Our experts answer the biggest questions surrounding Aiyuk agreeing to join the Commanders practice squad.
full_text:
ASHBURN, Va. -- Brandon Aiyuk advertised his desire to play for Washington quite often this year. He posted pictures of himself in Commanders gear. He said he bought a $10 million house in Loudoun County, Virginia, where Washington trains.
It wasn't exactly a secret.
The only question became whether that desire would be shared by the Commanders -- and, depending on the social media post, it seemed to ebb and flow over the past seven or eight months. They long had their eye on him as someone who could provide more juice to their offense, if he were healthy.
• Has Puka played his final snaps for Rams? • How will Packers use Micah in ACL return? • Joe Milton's big chance on Thanksgiving • Can Vikings' O win when D doesn't dominate? • Inside the gymnastics lore of Ja'Marr Chase
On Wednesday, Aiyuk agreed to a deal to join the Commanders' practice squad . If that leads to Aiyuk playing for Washington, the question becomes: What now? He hasn't played since Oct. 20, 2024, after tearing his ACL, MCL and meniscus in his right knee. Can he actually return to the NFL without having practiced since that time and contribute? If so, how quickly?
And can he ever again become the player he was in 2023, when he caught 75 passes for 1,342 yards and seven touchdowns en route to being named second-team All-Pro?
That's what both sides may be about to find out.
Commanders reporter John Keim, 49ers reporter Nick Wagoner, NFL analyst Matt Bowen and Fantasy analyst Mike Florio weigh in on everything you need to know.
Because he was available. And if he hits, he can become the No. 1 receiver in 2027 with Terry McLaurin 's future in Washington uncertain. McLaurin tore the patellar tendon in his left knee in Week 6 and has a $34 million cap hit next season. Not only is his return date unknown, but so will be his ability to play at a certain level.
That's why they need to explore their options to find someone who can provide some help now but be a top option in 2027 and beyond. One team source said they know how hard it can be to find an elite receiver in free agency so they need to be creative, whether through trades, the draft or a signing like this one.
If they're fortunate, he can contribute down the stretch for a team that became more interesting after a 22-20 win over Cincinnati on Monday night. At 4-5-1 the Commanders can contend for a playoff spot over the final seven games; perhaps he can contribute at some point to help them achieve that goal.
They also have two key people who know him well: quarterback Jayden Daniels and general manager Adam Peters .
Daniels and Aiyuk played together at Arizona State and have remained close, even through a rough patch this summer when Aiyuk put out multiple social media posts directed at Daniels and, in one, his mother.
Peters was an assistant general manager in San Francisco with Aiyuk from 2020 to '23. He would know how Aiyuk gets along in the locker room and would be well-suited to get intel from people with whom he remains close in the organization, including coach Kyle Shanahan.
"One of the things that I don't think anyone can dispute is his work ethic," Peters said during his paid weekly appearance on 106.7 The Fan in D.C. "He was one of the hardest workers on the team. That's how he became an All-Pro type player."
As far as concerns over what transpired in San Francisco, Peters said until Aiyuk visited he hadn't talked to him in "a couple years." "I can't speak on all that happened between him and the 49ers," Peters said. "What I do remember is, he's a very self-motivated player ... and a smart football player. Those are the things that led him to get the contract he got. He earned all that by doing the right things in and out of the building when I was there." -- Keim
How much time do we have? The relationship between the team and player started heading the wrong way during a rocky contract extension negotiation in 2024. Aiyuk was a "hold-in" -- someone who attended practices but didn't participate -- at that camp as he sought to be paid among the game's top receivers coming off a season in which he was a second-team All Pro in 2023.
During that standoff, Aiyuk requested a trade that the Niners nearly granted, having a deal in place with the Pittsburgh Steelers before Aiyuk changed his mind, told coach Kyle Shanahan he wanted to stay and signed a deal the team had put on the table long before that, a four-year extension worth $120 million.
Money didn't cure any of the tension, though, as Aiyuk and Shanahan had an awkward exchange on the practice field soon after Aiyuk signed regarding Aiyuk wearing the wrong color of shorts. From there, Aiyuk struggled to regain his 2023 form before he tore the ACL, MCL and meniscus in his right knee in Week 7.
Tired of the issues with Aiyuk, the Niners hoped to trade him that offseason, sources told ESPN, but the injury ruined any chance of that happening. Meanwhile, Aiyuk rehabbed away from the facility but wasn't showing up for his regular check-ins to monitor his recovery progress.
In July, the 49ers informed Aiyuk that they were voiding roughly $27 million in guarantees on his deal because he failed to show for those check ups. Aiyuk stopped showing up altogether once that news became public.
The Niners placed Aiyuk on the reserve/left team list in December 2025 and general manager John Lynch made it clear in January that Aiyuk had played his last snaps with the 49ers. The team again hoped to trade him all offseason but the injury, his contract and the odd situation in San Francisco prevented any market from materializing.
Because Aiyuk was on the "left team" list, he needed to apply for reinstatement but he didn't do that until hiring agent Drew Rosenhaus to help facilitate all of that in late October.
There was never a doubt that the Niners would release Aiyuk. It was always just a matter of when. -- Wagoner
Aiyuk has the route-running traits to play a productive role in coordinator David Blough's system. With West Coast elements and reduced formations, Aiyuk will see targets on quicks and in-breakers, while Blough can set him up on play-action throws from Daniels. These are defined reads that create open voids in the coverage. Catch and go.
Plus, with Aiyuk's ability to shake press coverage and track the ball vertically, he would add a much-needed playmaking presence, generating matchups as a boundary X target, which complements the skill sets of Stefon Diggs and rookie Antonio Williams in the Commanders' route tree. When Aiyuk is game-ready (conditioning, scheme), he can boost the Washington passing game. -- Bowen
They will need to see where he's at with his game and his motivation. This isn't about trying to get a quick fix to help boost their playoff chances. Rather, what they hope to get is a player motivated to prove he can still play in the NFL.
However, if he is in shape, he could provide a spark in some games as a downfield option. In 2023-24, Aiyuk was second in the NFL in yards per catch at 17.2 and his air yards per target also was second.
That would pair well with underneath targets such as Williams, coming off a nine-catch, 122-yard game vs. Cincinnati, and Stefon Diggs. They also have Treylon Burks , who has helped downfield and averages 18.1 yards per catch on 16 receptions.
But they do miss McLaurin, who had filled the No. 1 role for Washington since it made him a third-round pick in 2019. If Aiyuk can help in this area, it gives the Commanders another option.
The good news for Washington is that if he's motivated, and wants to change the narrative around him, then he'll be on his best behavior. It's uncertain if one month or so can result in a multiyear deal, so it's possible Washington -- or another team -- could sign him to one-year prove-it deal in 2027.
But right now he has the opportunity to begin rehabilitating his game -- and his reputation -- with a strong showing, whatever that might mean.
Peters told 106.7 that it would be "foolish to say he'd jump right…
author: John Keim and Nick Wagoner and Matt Bowen and Michael F Florio

title: Guide to the NFL's Thanksgiving schedule: Matchup previews, predictions, picks and nuggets
summary: We have the top storylines, bold predictions, stats to know, fantasy/betting nuggets and more for four Wednesday and Thursday games in Week 12.
full_text:
Holiday football is here, and the NFL is starting this season 's Thanksgiving week slate a day earlier than normal.
On Wednesday night, two 6-4 teams (the Packers and Rams) will battle it out in Southern California. Then two 8-2 teams (the Lions and Packers) will kick off the Thanksgiving Day games, followed by an NFC East showdown between the Eagles and Cowboys. And to conclude Thursday's games, Patrick Mahomes and the Chiefs will visit Josh Allen and the Bills in the first clash of NFL MVPs on the holiday, per the Elias Sports Bureau.
Ahead of the matchups, our NFL Nation reporters take you inside each locker room with key storylines and a look back at each team's history playing on Thanksgiving. ESPN Research provides optimistic stats for all eight teams, and betting analyst Pamela Maldonado hits betting insights for each contest. Plus, analytics writer Seth Walder makes bold predictions and fantasy analyst Eric Moody shares fantasy football intel. We also have Football Power Index (FPI) game projections, and three analysts -- Maldonado, Moody and Walder -- give us final score picks for the four games.
