title: From practice squad to prime time: A look at Joe Milton's big chance on Thanksgiving
summary: Ex-Cowboys QB Milton is set to headline the Eagles' Thanksgiving game, can he make the most of it?
full_text:
Patrick Mahomes . Josh Allen . Dak Prescott . Jared Goff . Caleb Williams . Joe Milton .
A Thanksgiving slate chock-full of household quarterback names has one notable exception, though there is some growing intrigue around the 6-foot-5, 246-pound 26-year-old who goes by the name of "Mr. Rocket." He'll be making his third career start Thursday when the Philadelphia Eagles face the Dallas Cowboys (4:30 p.m. ET, Fox)
The popular nickname for him had been "Bazooka Joe" -- a hat-tip to a right arm that might be as strong as any in the league -- but he said last week he prefers Mr. Rocket because "bazookas only travel so far." (It doesn't take more than a single interaction to realize confidence is not an issue for Milton.)
Rookie receiver Makai Lemon experienced that arm strength up close when Milton delivered a laser of an intermediate pass that was too hot to handle in Sunday's 19-16 win over the Pittsburgh Steelers . DeVonta Smith had to rethink a previously held belief when he was unable to track down a Milton deep ball in that game.
"I felt I couldn't be overthrown," Smith said with a smile, "but he did it."
There were plays Sunday that spoke to his physical gifts, like on a third-and-long midway through the first quarter when he escaped pressure to his left and threw a dime to Darius Cooper along the sideline while on the run. And he showed quality decision-making in spots, including on the game-deciding completion to Smith when he was tasked with calling one of two plays at the line of scrimmage based on the defensive look and correctly dialed up Smith's number.
"I think he's probably one of the best throwers of the football I've ever seen in my life. Like how far he's able to throw it. It's just pretty," said Saquon Barkley , who is finding a little more space in the running game due to Milton's dual-threat ability. Milton has 71 rushing yards on 14 carries through two games for Philly.
"He's very smart. He just got thrown into the fire in the last two games. He's doing a really good job of getting an understanding of the playbook, knowing what we want to do, and doing a good job of executing it."
It's not like Milton has been lighting it up since taking over for Tanner McKee , who took over for Jalen Hurts . The Eagles have scored a total of 30 points in his two starts. He has completed 53% of his throws and has been sacked 10 times. The passing offense has a success rate of 27.7%.
But it's also true that he's brand-new to this team and this offense. Milton was signed off the Cowboys' practice squad on Oct. 16 and was thrust into the starting lineup behind a shaky offensive line three weeks later. He has yet to throw an interception but has fumbled twice.
There are areas of his game he is actively trying to improve, including knowing when to take something off his throws. Milton revealed after the Steelers game that to manage his arm strength -- especially on deep throws like the one he had to Smith -- he will say the name of his 1-year-old daughter, Maleia, as he releases the ball "so I can relax a little bit."
"Basically it kind of tells [me] in my mind that I'm throwing the ball to her, so it can't be as hard. Show a little love," he said.
Milton, from Pahokee, Florida, is cousins with former NFL receiver standout Anquan Boldin . He attended Michigan and then Tennessee before being drafted in the sixth round by the New England Patriots in 2024.
He acquitted himself pretty well in his lone appearance with the Patriots -- a win over the Buffalo Bills late in the '24 season -- before being traded that April to the Cowboys along with a 2025 seventh-round pick in exchange for a 2025 fifth-round pick.
He appeared in four games for Dallas in '25, with mixed results. Milton was released by the Cowboys and signed to their practice squad this offseason after being beaten out for the No. 2 role by Sam Howell .
If Thursday's return trip to Dallas holds significance, Milton is not showing it, saying he is "just going to go play another football game."
But there is opportunity, both on a national stage on Thanksgiving against a down Cowboys defense as well as the following two weeks against the Arizona Cardinals and Indianapolis Colts , for Milton to generate some momentum both for the Eagles and his own career.
"I think that we see on a daily basis what you guys don't get to see, the work that he puts in on a daily basis. He's constantly in here," coach Nick Sirianni said.
"The guys that love football [and] are tough, God willing, reach their ceiling. So, I think you're going to see him continue to improve because of the way he works. You prepare yourself and what you do on Sunday is a direct reflection of the work that you put in throughout the week. I think he's just been getting great preparation each week and it was good to see that show up."
author: Tim McManus

title: To stay alive in NFC East, Cowboys need first back-to-back wins in a year
summary: If Dallas is going to catch up to New York in the division, it needs to start stringing wins together.
full_text:
FRISCO, Texas -- If anything, the Dallas Cowboys ' 51-30 win against the Tennessee Titans kept them afloat with six games to play.
At 5-6, the Cowboys will need the NFC East --leading New York Giants (6-3-1) to lose some games if they want to win the division, but in the minutes after the Tennessee victory, owner and general manager Jerry Jones spoke optimistically about what his team had just done.
Fifty-one points. Six different players scored a touchdown. Only three first-half field goals for the Titans. Five sacks for the defense.
"It gives me hope that we can do some of the things that we want to do," Jones said.
Hope, however, can be a week-to-week thing. And in this case, maybe even shorter than that considering the Cowboys play NFC East rival Philadelphia Eagles (3-7) on Thanksgiving ( 4:30 p.m. ET, Fox ).
The Cowboys are not out of the NFC East race, but they're not exactly in it either. To get there, they have to keep winning, and a year has passed since they last posted consecutive wins.
Last Thanksgiving, the Cowboys beat the Kansas City Chiefs for their third straight win to improve to 6-5-1. They won only one game the rest of the way.
This season, the Cowboys had four other opportunities to post back-to-back wins and came up short. Going one step forward and one step back has kept the Cowboys mired in mediocrity.
Coaches and players have been asked so often about whether they can string together wins that they can only go to gallows humor.
"When the clock says zero, we have to have more points than the other team," coach Brian Schottenheimer said.
"Yeah, you can quote me," he smiled.
If there is an advantage for the Cowboys this week, it is that they are used to the holiday turnaround, although every team plays on Thursdays these days. The Cowboys will hold walkthrough-type practices on Monday and Tuesday. Prescott said he will cram six days of film work into three.
The physical test is getting their bodies right without as much time to recover. The Eagles will be on a plane Wednesday for Dallas, while the Cowboys will be able to rest at home.
• Has Puka played his final snaps for Rams? • How will Packers use Micah in ACL return? • Joe Milton's big chance on Thanksgiving • Can Vikings' O win when D doesn't dominate? • Inside the gymnastics lore of Ja'Marr Chase
"Obviously continue to do what we did on offense, go out there with that same mindset this Thursday of scoring every possession, and it's not just going to happen again because we did it today," Dak Prescott said. "It's really about our preparation and the game plan and just all of that coming together. If we do that on offense and the defense goes out and makes some stops to get some turnovers, I think it's pretty doable."
This week, the Cowboys can feel like their offense has turned a corner. In the past two games, they have combined for 91 points, the third most in a two-game span in team history. Prescott has tied a personal best with three straight 300-yard passing games. Receivers CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens both topped 100 yards and scored Sunday.
Defensively, there were positive moments against the Titans with Mike Pettine replacing Christian Parker as the playcaller -- five sacks, a takeaway and defensive tackle Quinnen Williams was difficult to block. There were also setbacks, as they allowed 126 rushing yards and failed to touch receiver Carnell Tate down, allowing him to score a 59-yard touchdown in the third quarter.
In other words, similar to what it had been in previous weeks -- at times competent but not without issues.
"It's better," Jones said of the overall showing of the Cowboys. "This improvement. I think I could say that we have improved this week and we ought to be a better team going into Philadelphia in about two or three days than we were before this game. So we need this kind of thing, any team does. And we need to feel it and get a little wind beneath our wing, so to speak."
Will the flight be short or is it one the Cowboys can extend?
"We don't have time to pat ourselves on the back," Schottenheimer said. "We're just on to the next opponent."
author: Todd Archer

title: Can Vikings' offense win when the defense doesn't dominate?
summary: If the offense with Kirk Cousins at the helm can't get going, a deep playoff run might not be in the offing.
full_text:
EAGAN, Minn. -- The unusual coalition of forces that surged the Minnesota Vikings to a 6-0 start has collapsed over the past month. The breakdown has left the team's decision-makers to evaluate how much to credit their high-level opponents over that stretch, and -- most notably -- whether they are equipped to beat quality opponents when their defense does not dominate.
The essential facts are as follows: The Vikings lost three of four games against teams that currently have a combined record of 32-8. Those teams -- the Detroit Lions , Buffalo Bills and San Francisco 49ers -- would win their respective divisions if the season ended this week. All four, including the team they beat in the Green Bay Packers , would make the playoffs in that scenario.
Although the stretch has left the Vikings with a 7-3 record and dropped them to third place in the NFC North , their postseason chances have been minimally impacted. ESPN's Football Power Index gives them a 93% chance to make the playoffs, thanks in part to the NFL's seventh-easiest remaining schedule that includes NFC South opponents (Atlanta, followed by Carolina) in their next two games.
But the question is not so much whether they will advance to the postseason. Instead, it's this: Have the Vikings already demonstrated they are unlikely to make the kind of playoff run that a 6-0 start otherwise might suggest?
After a 35-10 loss Sunday night to the 49ers in Mexico City, a game that for the first time exposed vulnerabilities in their top-ranked defense, the Vikings arrived back at their facility at 7 a.m. local time Monday to begin assessing the damage.
"We're going to work through it as we do every game," coach Kevin O'Connell said, "and make sure we have the discussions about each individual play and also the big picture of how we were attacked from their offense, how we were defended, anything that came up in the kicking game. Then we're going to apply that to how we game plan."
Through 10 games this season, the Vikings have scored 16 touchdowns -- tied for the fewest in the NFL and the lowest total for any Vikings team since at least 2000. They are averaging 17.9 offensive points per game, fifth lowest in the NFL.
The Vikings traded for quarterback Kirk Cousins to elevate their offense enough to release some pressure on their defense and special teams. Receiver Justin Jefferson has said that the offense needs only to be "mediocre" to do its part. In two games with Cousins, the Vikings rank No. 24 in EPA.
Well into the second half of the season, is it reasonable to expect a significant improvement?
ESPN Research looked at all 255 teams that were averaging fewer than 20 offensive points through 10 games over the past 20 seasons. The average team improved its scoring by 1.4 points per game over the remainder of the season. A total of 11 increased by an average 10 or more points per game. In other words, there isn't much precedent for the kind of boost the Vikings were looking for -- leaving their early-season performance as the most reliable winning formula.
• Has Puka played his final snaps for Rams? • How will Packers use Micah in ACL return? • Joe Milton's big chance on Thanksgiving • Can Vikings' O win when D doesn't dominate? • Inside the gymnastics lore of Ja'Marr Chase
For six games over seven weeks to start the season, the Vikings' defense and special teams ranked at or near the top of the NFL, based on expected points allowed, and thus covered for a mostly punchless offense that ranked No. 31. The Vikings further minimized the impact of their offense's ineffectiveness by ranking No.1 in turnover margin (-7) and No. 2 in penalties (6.5 per game), while O'Connell kept it simple by calling the NFL's fourth-highest rate of designed runs (43%).
Placekicker Will Reichard converted 18 of 19 field goal attempts, including six from at least 50 yards, tied for most in the NFL. Returner Myles Price ranked No. 1 in punt returns (19.2 yards) and No. 2 in kickoff returns (30.7).
But that combination of achievement came against teams that now have a combined 24-37 record. During their downturn over the ensuing four weeks, Reichard missed three field goals attempts. All were from at least 50 yards, and one from 71, but those kicks had earlier been a lifeline for the offense.
Meanwhile, Price's kickoff return average (25.7) dropped to No. 18 and opponents found ways to limit him to three punt returns in four games. That coincided with O'Connell trying to activate his passing game, dropping their run rate to 34%, No. 28 in the NFL. O'Connell said Monday that he viewed some of the shift as an attempt to use short completions "as an extension of the run game."
• Full schedule » | Standings » • Depth charts for every team » • Transactions » | Injuries » • Football Power Index » More NFL coverage »
All told, the Vikings have demonstrated only incremental progress in supporting their defense while some of their other bulwarks have shown cracks. Notably, the Vikings are tied for No. 20 in turnover margin (-1) over this four-game stretch.
It all helps explain the enormous burden that remains on the defense, and the vital questions that Sunday night's game presented. The 49ers did not simply roll to 35 points. They attacked defensive coordinator Brian Flores' blitz schemes so thoroughly that quarterback Brock Purdy finished with the highest QBR (96.8) of any quarterback against a Vikings defense in 20 years.
O'Connell said he is balancing his reaction between an acknowledgement that Purdy "was able to make some pretty, pretty high level throws on some critical downs" with the reality that "there were some things that we can do a little bit better assignment-wise at all three levels."
Flores said he expects to see teams attempt to emulate the 49ers' approach, particularly with quick throws over the middle to combat pressure but noted it wasn't the first time his defense has seen that strategy.
"That's something that our opponents have tried previous games," Flores said. "We just didn't play them as well. They got to those spaces. And I would say there's been other games where teams have gotten to those spaces, but we have a batted ball, or got in there one-on-one inside and got to the quarterback and there was enough disruption to limit the opportunities for them to create plays on those.
"But against a team like the 49ers, you've got to be more precise for not letting them in there, winning your one-on-ones, all those things have got to come together. There's a fine line between making some of those plays and not making them."
At the moment, at least, that line appears the likeliest indicator of the Vikings' potential postseason success.
author: Kevin Seifert

title: Facts vs. Feelings: The facts you need to feel right about your flex decisions
summary: Making a tough flex decision this week?  Here are some hard facts to help you feel good about the decision.
full_text:
Greetings from above the clouds! Jan from Milford, a librarian and gardening enthusiast, has just nodded off and the plane's Wi-Fi has finally decided to connect. It's been another action-packed few days in Bristol and I am, once again, reminded of the clock's elusivity. At present, time seems to be both limping along and galloping by, leaving me feeling equal parts accomplished and anxious. So many tasks completed and so many more left unfinished. The space for rest has shrunk.
It's instances like these that I envy folks who excel at setting boundaries. I know it's a buzzword, but people who can confidently "protect their peace" are such enigmas. It requires gravitas -- especially in today's hustle culture -- to guiltlessly prioritize one's well-being. Whether it's taking a sick day or passing on a social outing, sometimes we have to be comfortable saying "no."
• Rankings: Weekly | Season | Knockout • Weekly projections and outlooks • Strength of schedule (SOS) cheat sheet • Scoring leaders | Consistency Ratings • xFP leaderboard | xTD leaderboard • Fantasy depth chart | Latest Buzz
The same is true in fantasy. You don't need to entertain every trade offer you're sent. Nor are you obligated to work the waiver wire each week. It's OK to roster a player because you're a fan of their playing style. Injuries will happen. The rest-of-season strength of schedule remains a moving target. All you can do is your best. Actually, scratch that. Your "best" implies 100% effort at all times. And, sometimes, you don't have 100% to give. That's fine. This is supposed to be a joy point, not an obligation.
So, release yourself from the Parker Washington no-TD fury, lean into the roller-coaster ride that is Jameson Williams (playing with a projected game total of 55.5 in Week 12), and whoo-sah your way through the A.J. Brown injury saga. These things are all out of your control. Do what you need to do to keep yourself upright and feeling good.
By the way, that also includes refusing to choke down your mother-in-law's stuffing, clapping back at your weird cousin who wants to debate crypto at the dinner table, and guarding the remote like your life depends on it during the late-afternoon kickoff.
With five games to be played before Sunday's slate even kicks off, you might be pondering decisions involving teams playing days apart.  Here are five players who won't take the field until Sunday but who you may be considering as flex (or superflex) options. No matter your decision, remember, the one with the later start time is the one you put in your flex spot.  Keep your options open.
It is a not-so-new dawn in Indy. I know, I know... I can feel your eyes smacking the front of your brain through the screen. We have been here before, but not quite like this. With the 3-8 Colts using the final six games to evaluate Richardson's future -- and only Riley Leonard and newly signed Shane Buechele behind him on the depth chart -- he has total job security and a green light from Shane Steichen to play aggressively.
There is no denying the passing metrics are ugly. His 51% career completion percentage and 24% off-target rate would rank last and second-to-last (ahead of only Jameis Winston ) among qualified QBs this season. However, Richardson's fantasy appeal has always been built on his legs, and having Jonathan Taylor in the backfield helps unlock that upside. Because defenses have to focus on stopping Taylor, Richardson gets open running lanes on keepers and easier throws off play-action.
In the 12 career starts where he avoided a first-half injury, Richardson averaged 17.4 fantasy points per game -- clearing 20 points six times -- while accounting for 19 total touchdowns and 48 rushing yards per game (a mark that would easily pace all signal-callers in 2026, where only one other QB averages over 30). He gets a prime spot to showcase that rushing floor right out of the gate in Week 12 against a Giants defense that has surrendered the second-most rushing yards to quarterbacks (271, trailing only the Bengals), making him well worth a speculative roster spot ahead of Sunday.
This backfield is a soup of agita-inducing frustration, though that doesn't mean the Etienne shares you've painstakingly stashed on your IR spot are worthless. New Orleans offered some much-needed clarity in Week 11. While Etienne matched CJ Donaldson with a 45% snap share (leaving just 10% for Alvin Kamara ), Donaldson was on the field for only one rushing play, allowing Etienne to command 14 of the team's 16 running back carries. His snap rate has already climbed from 34% in his return to 45% last week -- trending back toward the 58% and 53% shares he logged in his first two games before getting hurt -- which points to an even larger workload down the stretch.
Etienne also looked sharper than his backfield mates, averaging 5.4 yards per touch while Donaldson and Kamara combined for just 2.7. Paired with the seventh-best running back rest-of-season schedule , that efficiency gives Etienne genuine late-season upside. It starts with a Week 12 matchup against a Bengals defense that's coming off a short week and allowing 5.1 yards per carry, the NFL's second-worst mark behind Dallas (5.2). Additionally, look for Etienne to regain ground in the passing game -- leaning on his career track record and five-target Week 10 involvement -- working as a checkdown option while the Saints chase points as 10-point road 'dogs in a contest carrying a 50.5 point total . Consider the Louisiana native a low-end RB2/high-end flex option heading into Week 12.
Better later than never? That was the sentiment Jim Harbaugh intimated when asked about using Hampton as a sure-fire RB1, replying "Yeah, in hindsight we should have done that sooner." At least this late-season realization comes with enough underlying usage to suggest Hampton's recent surge isn't a mirage.
Hampton has logged 13 or more rushing attempts in three straight games, matching his total from Weeks 1 through 8 combined. He has also monopolized the high-value touches, accounting for all five of the Chargers' carries inside the 5-yard line and 12 of their 14 goal-to-go attempts ( Keaton Mitchell and Kimani Vidal have recorded just one apiece). title: Seven things Solak thinks: Much-needed test for the Chiefs, Bills?
summary: Get ready for Week 12! Why the Giants are a playoff sleeper and what to expect in Micah Parson's return.
full_text:
Are you excited for NFL Week 12 ? Last week, only one game closed with a spread of less than three points (and that was just barely, as the Panthers were 2.5-point favorites with juice over the Ravens). This week, we're in for closer contests. There are seven games from Wednesday to Monday in national windows. Two of them have spreads within a field goal, and only one (Eagles vs. Cowboys) has a spread greater than 4.5 points. How lucky are we!
Every Tuesday of the NFL season , I'll turn the page from the previous week to the upcoming one with seven things I think. These aren't full-scale predictions. They aren't concrete takeaways from the past week of NFL action, either; those are fired off Sunday or Monday. Instead, these are the uncertain topics. They are things that might be true, but it'll probably take the next few games to find out. And at the bottom, you'll find a few extra half-thoughts ... just those little inklings I'm unable to shake.
Subscribe: 'ESPN's Leaguewide'
This week, I'll start by previewing one of those island games (Chiefs at Bills, obviously), wonder what Micah Parsons brings to an already testy Packers' defense, and try to learn something from the rise and fall of the Colts (2025-26). Here we go!
Jump to: Chiefs-Bills is a much-needed test 49ers found offensive blueprint for Vikings Lessons to be learned from Colts' fall Giants could win a playoff game Lions have the best offense in football Parsons return means more Packers blitzes Quinn is saving his job with Commanders Let's revisit five inklings
The 8-2 Chiefs and 9-1 Bills have two of the best records and two of the best offenses in football as they approach a critical late-season head-to-head matchup that might decide the No. 1 seed in the AFC. What year is this? Every year in recent history?
Seriously. The Chiefs and Bills last played on Nov. 2, 2025. The Chiefs were 5-3, the Bills were 5-2, and they both had top-five offenses by advanced metrics -- success rate, EPA per drive, points per drive, everything. Before that, it was Nov. 17, 2024. The Chiefs were 9-0, the Bills were 8-2, and they both had offenses ranked in the top eight by advanced metrics. Before that, they played on Dec. 10, 2023. The Chiefs were 8-4, the Bills were 6-6 (they'd end the year 11-6 in the No. 2 seed), and you guessed it -- they each had a top-10 offense.
The nice thing about these consistent regular-season bouts is we know that they both matter and don't matter. Winning this game can position either team nicely for a first-round bye or home-field advantage in a playoff rematch. Those are real advantages. But we also know that these two teams and two quarterbacks are so good that one loss won't derail their seasons or preclude them from postseason success. In that 2023 season, the Bills won the regular-season matchup and got a home game in the divisional round against the Chiefs for their trouble. The Chiefs won that game and went on to win the Super Bowl.
If this game has postseason consequences but isn't particularly disqualifying for either franchise, then what makes this 2026 contest different from the first 10 games these two quarterbacks have played against each other? This particular moment is an interesting one for both franchises because of who they've recently played.
Let's start with the Bills, the AFC's lone one-loss team. The Bills are obviously awesome again. The offensive line hasn't missed a beat despite losing David Edwards in free agency and enduring some injuries through the first three months of the season. The addition of receiver DJ Moore has been exactly as hoped for (when he has been on the field). And Jim Leonhard's defensive scheme change has facilitated breakouts for edge rusher Greg Rousseau and defensive tackle Deone Walker .
But the defensive riddle is a little difficult to solve given the strength of competition. Through the first six weeks of the season, the Bills faced the following quarterbacks: C.J. Stroud , Jared Goff , Justin Herbert , Drake Maye , Matthew Stafford and Kirk Cousins . Entering their Week 7 bye, they were 31st in defensive EPA per drive and 30th in defensive success rate. No defense -- not the Cowboys, the Titans, any team -- was giving up more points per drive than the Bills' defense.
Leonhard was reaching for solutions, and he started to find them entering the bye week. The Bills were in single-high coverages on 61% of their snaps in Week 6 against the Raiders after going single-high 45% of the time in the five previous weeks. In all of the Bills' first five games, they played quarters on at least 23% of opponent dropbacks; in each of the past five games, they've never played quarters more than 17% of the time.
These solutions look effective. Let me amend that. These solutions look like an immeasurable revolution of defense. The Bills have not given up a touchdown drive in three straight games -- that's 43 consecutive drives, going back to Week 8 vs. the Ravens -- for the first time in franchise history.
Here's the issue. The following quarterbacks have taken snaps against the Bills in their four-game stretch since the bye. Dolphins backup Kyle McCord (37 dropbacks), Jets backup Cade Klubnik (26), Vikings backup Carson Wentz (25), Ravens third-stringer Joe Fagnano (25), Jets starter Geno Smith (22), Vikings third-stringer Max Brosmer (seven), Ravens backup Tyler Huntley (five) and Ravens starter Lamar Jackson (one).
Two things are simultaneously true. First, the Bills defense has, without question, improved through October and into November. Second, the Bills' have not been sufficiently tested to measure the size of that improvement. Are they the 25th-best defense? The 12th? We could be anywhere in that range of outcomes. We don't have the necessary data to know.
Assuming (knock on wood) Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes plays a full game against the Bills' defense, we will gain a critical datapoint in our measure of the Bills as a top-tier AFC contender. They are obviously capable of winning a Super Bowl this season -- they've been capable for several seasons now, and as long as Josh Allen is playing quarterback, they will remain so. But we still don't know if the defense will carry its own water during January football, and their performance against Mahomes and the Chiefs will give us their first real litmus test to that end.
On the flip side, the Chiefs' offense is undergoing a smaller but still significant revolution of its own. Early in the season, it was the running game. The free agent acquisition of Kenneth Walker III and commitment to an under-center rushing attack brought newfound balance and explosiveness to a Chiefs offense in desperate need of both.
But as the season has gone along, the Chiefs have begun tilting their offense back to a pass-heavy approach, just as the Bills have tinkered with their coverages. In Weeks 1-7, the Chiefs were fifth in pass rate over expectation at plus-1.5%, per NFL Next Gen Stats. Since Week 8, they're second to only the Bengals at plus-6.2%.
And it's not just that they've become more pass-happy; they're also getting the ball downfield more often. Mahomes has averaged over 8 air yards per pass attempt in consecutive games for the first time since Weeks 2-3 of last season.
Week 10 against the Falcons was a bit more successful than Week 11 against the Cardinals. Mahomes completed two passes of 40-plus air yards against Atlanta, which is the first time he has done that in a game since 2022. But the larger impact of the addition of receiver Josh Downs and emergence of an under-center dropback game is beginning to become apparent. The Chiefs can push the ball downfield both in moderate ways (hitting intermediate throws) and extreme ways (pushing the ball deeper than deep).
This is a concerted, schematic shift. It is not the result of scramble-drill plays. On in-structure throws (dropbacks of four seconds or less, per Next Gen Stats), Mahomes is averaging 8.1 air yards per attempt in the past two…

title: Power Rankings: Best and worst teams after 11 weeks, plus their extension candidates
summary: How does every NFL team stack up heading into Week 12? We made our 1-32 list and picked players who could get a new contract.
full_text:
Week 11 of the 2026 NFL season kicked off Thursday with another strong performance from Texans quarterback C.J. Stroud , who notched his fifth straight game with multiple touchdown passes in a win over the Colts. On Sunday, Jaguars wide receiver Parker Washington had his third game with 100 receiving yards this season, though it wasn't enough to defeat the Giants. And Broncos cornerback Ja'Quan McMillian put away the Raiders with a late pick-six.
What do these players have in common? They're all eligible for extensions, whether on their rookie deals or otherwise. They're also all mentioned below, as along with our 1-32 rankings, we asked our NFL Nation reporters to pick a player from each team who could receive a contract extension this offseason.
To form the 1-32 list, our power panel of more than a dozen NFL analysts evaluates how all 32 teams stack up against one another. Here are a couple of highlights from this week's rankings:
The Jaguars are out of our top six for the first time since Week 4 after their 23-18 loss to the Giants . Before Week 11, Jacksonville was one of two teams that hadn't trailed by more than 10 points this season (Bills), but it trailed by 11 for almost 30 minutes Sunday. Quarterback Trevor Lawrence faced the most pressure he has seen all season, which resulted in two interceptions.
The Lions climbed four spots from last week's rankings after their sixth straight game of allowing 21 or fewer points, tied for their second-longest streak over the past 50 seasons, per ESPN Research. On offense, quarterback Jared Goff had his sixth game of 2026 with multiple TD passes and zero INTs. It came against the Bucs , who entered Sunday with the league's best defensive EPA, per NFL Next Gen Stats.
The Eagles showed signs of life in Week 11, snapping a seven-game losing streak with a 19-16 win over the Steelers . Philly rose three spots from last week's rankings, and while it is all but out of the playoff race, it can hurt the Cowboys' chances on Thanksgiving . Eagles running back Saquon Barkley is on a career-high streak of four straight games with a rushing touchdown.
Let's get into the full list, starting with the same team as last week .

Week 11 result: Beat the Vikings 35-10 Week 11 ranking: 1
Extension candidate: G Dominick Puni
Puni, who will be eligible for an extension for the first time this offseason, is the clear choice based on consistency and production. But it's a bit more complicated than that. Since coach Kyle Shanahan and general manager John Lynch arrived in 2017, they've never given big bucks to a guard. With left tackle Trent Williams closer to retirement, center Jake Brendel slated to be an unrestricted free agent and right tackle Colton McKivitz recovering from a fractured left ankle , finding a fair deal for Puni would at least offer some stability on an O-line that could have plenty of change the next couple of seasons. -- Nick Wagoner
Week 11 result: Beat the Dolphins 26-9 Week 11 ranking: 2
Extension candidate: G Alec Anderson
An underrated aspect of the Bills' success since drafting quarterback Josh Allen has been offensive line continuity. The Bills prioritize developing and rewarding homegrown blockers, which in recent years has meant big contracts for OT Dion Dawkins , OT Spencer Brown and G O'Cyrus Torrence . Anderson is a unique case because he arrived in Buffalo as an undrafted rookie and spent four seasons as a reserve before starting in 2026. However, it's certainly within the Bills' M.O. to stick with their developmental player rather than cast him aside. He's a tenacious blocker who is integral to the Bills' run game. -- Nick Suss
Week 11 result: Beat the Cardinals 34-7 Week 11 ranking: 5
Extension candidate: WR Josh Downs
An argument can be made that the Chiefs got ahead of the market by acquiring Downs just ahead of the trade deadline to help convince him to stay with the team beyond this season. He has already made an impact on the Chiefs in only two games, recording eight receptions on nine targets for 112 receiving yards and a touchdown. Because Downs has been able to quickly build a connection with quarterback Patrick Mahomes , the Chiefs should try to offer a quality extension to the receiver to keep him from entering free agency. -- Nate Taylor
Week 11 result: Beat the Saints 21-13 Week 11 ranking: 4
Extension candidate: QB Caleb Williams
Williams becomes eligible for his first extension after this season. He's the franchise quarterback the Bears searched decades to find, and pairing him with coach Ben Johnson for the foreseeable future is the priority. Chicago's front office has an incentive to get ahead of a rapidly inflating QB market, which will see the likes of C.J. Stroud and Lamar Jackson come to the table, along with others in Williams' draft class. Though Williams said in September that "money's not a motivating factor for me," his top-10 play on a contending team could lead to him earning around $70 million per year. Signing Williams early would allow the Bears to keep his 2027 cap hit low while prorating a massive signing bonus into future years. -- Courtney Cronin
Week 11 result: Beat the Raiders 38-24 Week 11 ranking: 7
Extension candidate: CB Ja'Quan McMillian
There isn't any guarantee the Broncos can, or will, give McMillian an extension. But his teammates have made their feelings clear while McMillian makes one big-moment play after another -- "they need to make that happen,'' is how CB Pat Surtain II put it after McMillan's pick-six Sunday. McMillian is also one of the best find-and-develop players of GM George Paton's tenure. He was signed as an undrafted free agent, spent almost all of his rookie season on the practice squad and now approaches unrestricted free agency as one of the league's best nickel corners. That isn't exactly the kind of player the Broncos have re-signed in recent years. -- Jeff Legwold

Branch and TE Sam LaPorta are playing out the 2026 season on their four-year rookie deals, but general manager Brad Holmes has reiterated that he would like to reach long-term extensions with both players, though LaPorta has expressed doubts . Branch has made an immediate impact since returning from an Achilles injury that he sustained in Week 7 of last season. In 2026, he has five passes defended and one interception in four games. Depending on how the rest of the season plays out for Branch, the Lions could use the franchise tag or agree to long-term deal with him. -- Eric Woodyard

title: Resale markets, upsets and Thanksgiving: How NFL survivor pools have been upended
summary: Why spend up to nearly $80,000 in order to win a survivor contest over halfway through the NFL season?
full_text:
Paul Jager was browsing the marketplace for Splash Sports' Survivor World Championship on Friday, Nov. 20, when one specific entry caught his eye ahead of Week 11. The seller had other entries listed and hadn't yet listed this one, but Jager found it and was in awe at the teams used to get it to this point. He knew he had to have it.
Jager purchased the entry on the marketplace for $133,000, the largest transaction that Splash has facilitated since it launched its flagship contest this season. Upon taking ownership of it, he made his Week 11 pick: the Pittsburgh Steelers to defeat the Philadelphia Eagles.
"If I can get through with the Steelers, this entry is set up to win the whole thing," Jager told ESPN of his mindset at the time. "I was like, 'I'm going to take one chance, and if Pittsburgh wins, I am literally set.' I knew five minutes into the game, I was regretting taking Pittsburgh."
The Steelers lost to their in-state rivals, ending that entry's hopes of winning at least a share of the $21 million grand prize. But Jager wasn't out of the running. The investor by trade in Kansas City, Kansas who dabbles a lot in sports betting, currently has six entries alive at Splash and two in Circa Sports' famed Survivor contest, which features a prize pool of over $25 million this season.
Jager's experience is part of what's shaping up to be the new normal for players in high-stakes survivor contests. It fits perfectly into the new look for a sports betting world that is increasingly taking a more stock market-esque approach.
When Splash announced its completely online contest before this season, it was with the goal of expanding the space on top of the remarkable bedrock Circa (which requires in-person registration and proxies) has built since 2020. That included a built-in marketplace that allows players to buy and sell whole or partial tickets within the app using their connected payment methods. So far this season, Splash has already facilitated more than $4 million in transactions.
Circa also launched its own official marketplace by partnering with online platform Survivor Sweat. Circa Sports director of operations Jeff Benson says that the partnership "has driven significantly more engagement and activity than in previous years."
Gabe Patgorski, a former Circa champion, current contestant and founder of the research website Survivor Atlas, describes the contest as more "portfolio-style," given that there is no limit to the number of entries each player can have. Contestants can be more liberal with their selections, knowing that the quantity of entries they keep alive will just increase each's value, if nothing else.
It's a whole new branch of strategy in a game with over 21 sextillion possible combinations throughout the season. And when the stakes are as high as $1,000 per entry, players are looking for any edge they can get to ultimately come out profitable.
"The marketplace is a really cool way to turn any static entry you have in a contest to a tradable asset that you can get out of, or take some chips off the table at any time in the year, or buy back in. And so we've actually seen way more activity than I would've expected," Splash co-founder and co-CEO TJ Ross told ESPN.
Some of the trade activity comes after a particularly brutal first seven weeks of the season whittled down the fields to a fraction of the original entries. Over that span, favorites of seven points or greater -- the teams toward which many survivor contestants gravitate -- lost eight games straight-up, marking the first time since 1972 in which each of the first seven weeks of the season featured such an upset, according to ESPN Research.
Those results had an extensive impact on survivor contests: Following Week 7, Circa Survivor had lost 97.4% of its field (24,357 of the 25,017 entries). Entering Week 12, Circa Grandissimo, the $100,000 entry contest with a $7.7 million prize pool, is down to just three players from the 77 who started.
"In short, 2026 has combined the largest field Circa has ever seen with a run of upsets concentrated on the most popular survivor selections," Benson told ESPN via email after Week 7. "The absolute carnage is record-setting in scale; the underlying dynamic (chalk getting eliminated in bunches) is a familiar and defining feature of the format, just playing out more dramatically this year."
Though the raw volume of eliminations seems shocking, the early portion of the 2026 season was actually not the most carnage the contest has experienced by percentage. That honor belongs to the infamous 2024 season , which saw 99.5% of the field eliminated going into Week 8. The 2022 campaign had 98.0% of its field gone by the same time, which ultimately produced only two winners that year, the fewest in the contest's history.
The favorites have been more reliable since Week 7; the top four most-picked teams in Circa Survivor have won each week and favorites of at least seven points have gone 16-1 straight up from Week 8 through Sunday's games. Week 11 featured an average point spread of 8, the third-largest for any week (excluding the final two weeks of the season in which playoff positioning can dramatically affect spreads) in the last 50 years, per ESPN Research.
Players in the high-stakes contests must now brace for the holiday season. In the Circa pool, each entry must choose a team playing in one of the five Thanksgiving-adjacent games and one of the four Christmas-adjacent games, in addition to the usual games on Sunday and Monday. In Splash, each entry must choose two teams in Weeks 12 through 16, as well as in Week 9, regardless of when they are played.
"It's felt like a normal survivor season to me so far, very different from last year but similar to 2024 and 2022 in terms of pace of eliminations," 2025 Circa Survivor champion Jason Somerville told ESPN over text. He has one entry still alive in Circa. "It never feels real to me 'til Thanksgiving anyway, so fingers crossed I have some decisions to make in December."

The way this season has played out supports the notion that this could be a much more generous holiday season for the contestants than usual, especially with how things shook out at the NFL trade deadline.
Patgorski noticed that many of the already bad teams got worse at this season's deadline, and teams that began the season with high hopes -- like the Indianapolis Colts and Philadelphia Eagles -- became big sellers. There are also teams dealing with injured or underperforming quarterbacks, like the Baltimore Ravens , Los Angeles Chargers and New England Patriots , for whom the bottom has fallen out.
"The path to the end seems a lot easier for almost everyone," said Patgorski. "Every week there are so many big favorites where people are going, 'Oh, that's a lock. That's a free square.' And it's a pretty big shift from a few weeks ago where people thought, 'Okay, this contest has a big chance not to go to the end.' And now, everyone's thinking, 'Oh, there's going to be 50 winners. It's so easy to get to Christmas now. It's so easy to get to the end.'"
Philadelphia presents a juicy opportunity for Circa players given it is one of the few teams playing in both the Thanksgiving and Christmas mini-weeks ... but that in itself creates a paradoxical dilemma unique to high-end survivor contests.
As of Tuesday, the Eagles are 8.5-point road underdogs to the Dallas Cowboys on Thanksgiving according to DraftKings, easily the largest spread between the five games that make up the Wednesday-through-Friday slate. Patgorski estimates that 60-70% of the field will pick Dallas.
"The math says you're supposed to avoid that just because randomness happens often enough to pop that bubble. I think a lot of players have a sense of that, but of course you have to weigh that against, 'Well, maybe it's worth joining the crowd because my entry is strong enough…
author: Doug Greenberg

title: Derrick Henry placed in concussion protocol, limited in Wednesday's practice
summary: Derrick Henry has been placed in concussion protocol, but Ravens head coach Jesse Minter told reporters on Wednesday that the running back is likely to play on Sunday against the Texans.
full_text: Derrick Henry has been placed in concussion protocol, but Ravens head coach Jesse Minter told reporters on Wednesday that the running back is likely to play on Sunday against the Texans. “Derrick had a couple brief symptoms of a concussion right toward the end of that game,” Minter said. “Tested [and] cleared. We put him back in [the] protocol, just to kind of really make sure. So when it comes out today, he would’ve been limited. We do expect him to be back, obviously.” Henry rushed for 94 yards on 13 carries with a touchdown and caught four passes for 17 yards in Sunday’s loss to Carolina. Henry has not rushed for 100 yards in a game since Baltimore’s overtime victory over the Falcons on Oct. 4. In 11 games so far this season, Henry has 793 yards with 11 touchdowns, averaging 4.0 yards per carry. He was up to 5.2 yards per carry last season. Baltimore’s full Wednesday injury report will be released later in the day.
author: Myles Simmons

title: Report: Steelers are expected to release Aaron Rodgers
summary: Its not done yet, but it's reportedly coming.
full_text: Things are escalating quickly. It's to be expected, given that quarterback Aaron Rodgers has poured rocket fuel on the fire that Steelers started last night when the Steelers benched Rodgers. Via Gerry Dulac of the Pittsburgh Post-Gazette , the Steelers are expected to release Rodgers . Dulac said the decision was "hastened" by Rodgers's comments on Pat McAfee's show. If/when it happens, Rodgers will initially be subject to waivers. He could be claimed, in theory. (It's unlikely.) He then would be a free agent. What comes next will be fascinating. The passion and intensity of Rodgers's remarks suggest he won't go quietly, and that he'll want to play for someone else in order to prove that, with a functional head coach, Rodgers can still win games. Of course, someone else will have to be willing to welcome the Aaron Rodgers Experience to town, where anything the coach says or does can and will be used against him in a future episode of The Pat McAfee Show .
author: Mike Florio

title: Steelers suddenly have a major mess
summary: The Steelers need to figure things out, immediately.
full_text: '' Last night, Steelers fans who weren't already familiar with the name "Burt Lauten" became instantly acquainted with him, when his name appeared in large, bold print as the person announcing the benching of quarterback Aaron Rodgers. And Lauten will be earning every bit of pay and then some in the coming hours. Lauten serves as the team's senior director of communications. He's basically in charge of P.R. And the Steelers have a P.R. mess unlike any they've ever experienced. The benching of Rodgers has prompted a predictable reaction. Rodgers went straight to the McAfee show and pressed "play" on his various complaints and concerns about coach Mike McCarthy. It was specific. It was detailed. It was damning. The things Rodgers said created the clear impression that McCarthy should not be coaching the team. This becomes a problem that goes beyond P.R. strategy. Owner Art Rooney II needs to get involved, determine whether Rodgers's version is accurate, and take action. It's simple. If what Rodgers is saying is remotely true, he should not currently be the coach of the team. If Rodgers isn't telling the truth, the Steelers need to set the record straight immediately. However it goes, it's a mess. A gigantic mess. An unprecedented mess for the Steelers and perhaps for any NFL franchise.
author: Mike Florio

title: Brock Bowers is practicing on Wednesday after missing Sunday's game
summary: The Raiders could get a key player back for their Sunday night matchup against the Browns.
full_text: The Raiders could get a key player back for their Sunday night matchup against the Browns. Tight end Brock Bowers is practicing on Wednesday as Las Vegas begins its work week, according to multiple reporters on the scene. Bowers did not play in last Sunday's loss to the Broncos as he deals with ankle and quad injuries. He did not practice on Wednesday before being limited on Thursday and Friday. Reporters noted that Bowers' ankle is not taped as heavily as it was last week. Bowers’ level of participation will be revealed later in the day with Las Vegas’ injury report. In eight games this season, Bowers has 50 receptions for 676 yards with six touchdowns.
author: Myles Simmons

title: Brock Purdy out of practice Wednesday with ankle injury
summary: The 49ers will practice without their starting quarterback on Wednesday.
full_text: The 49ers will practice without their starting quarterback on Wednesday. Head coach Kyle Shanahan said that Purdy will miss practice after hurting his ankle in the second quarter of last Sunday night's win over the Vikings. Shanahan said the injury is not a high-ankle sprain and that Purdy is considered day-to-day heading into this Sunday's game against the Seahawks. When asked if there's a chance Purdy could miss that game, Shanahan said that his absence from practice means that is a possibility. That likelihood will rise if Purdy continues to miss practices in the coming days. Mac Jones is the backup quarterback for the 49ers. He started eight games last season, but has only made three relief appearances this season.
author: Josh Alper

title: Aaron Rodgers: Mike McCarthy fell asleep in meeting last week, broke down Steelers with "1-2-3 Packers"
summary: Rodgers's first comments since being benched by the Steelers came on The Pat McAfee Show.
full_text: Aaron Rodgers made his first public comments since being benched by the Steelers on The Pat McAfee Show on Wednesday afternoon and they were very critical of head coach Mike McCarthy. Rodgers said he did not hear the news of the quarterback change directly from McCarthy or anyone else on the coaching staff, but got the word from tight end Pat Freiermuth after it was announced on Tuesday night. Rodgers said that the change came after "months of conversation" about the offensive operation, including the playcalling, and that "things went to a different place" in recent days. Rodgers said that McCarthy fell asleep in an quarterback meeting last Wednesday and missed other meetings leading into their loss to the Eagles on Sunday. Rodgers said McCarthy also broke down the team with "1-2-3 Packers" at halftime of that game and that McCarthy was not regularly watching film while preparing for games. Rodgers said he also believes McCarthy has lost the team in general. "Everybody in that building knows the truth," Rodgers said. Rodgers said similar things happened when the two men were with the Packers and that he believes McCarthy blames him for being fired in Green Bay after the 2018 season. He said he saw that McCarthy was not connecting with Steelers players early in training camp, but tried to help smooth things out. "I protected him," Rodgers said. "I didn't talk about the things publicly. I didn't talk about his habits." Rodgers also said he pushed to have changes made to the playcalling and game-planning that he believed were going to take place before Tuesday's benching pushed things in a different direction. Rodgers said that he told the team that if they weren't going to make those alterations that they should release him and said that there was no chance of a reconciliation with the team after how they handled things on Tuesday. "That ship has sailed," Rodgers said. The comments guarantee that Steelers players will be asked for their accounts of how things have been in the building since McCarthy's arrival this offseason and their responses will likely determine whether or not things go completely off the rails for the team in the final weeks of the season.
author: Josh Alper

title: Dalton Kincaid, Christian Benford among five Bills listed as questionable
summary: The Bills could be getting tight end Dalton Kincaid and cornerback Christian Benford back in the lineup on Thursday night.
full_text: The Bills could be getting tight end Dalton Kincaid and cornerback Christian Benford back in the lineup on Thursday night. Kincaid and Benford are listed as questionable to play against the Chiefs. Kincaid missed last Sunday's win over the Dolphins with thumb and ankle injuries while Benford sat out with a groin injury. Both players were limited participants in practice the last two days. The Bills also listed defensive lineman TJ Sanders (shoulder), right guard O'Cyrus Torrance (ankle), and linebacker Dorian Williams (calf) as questionable for this week. Every other player on the injury report was a full participant on Wednesday and no other players received injury designations.
author: Josh Alper

title: Brandon Aiyuk agrees to join Commanders practice squad
summary: The long rumored landing spot will become a reality for Aiyuk, who was released by the 49ers earlier this week.
full_text: Earlier on Wednesday, Brandon Aiyuk's agent, Drew Rosenhaus, told ESPN's Adam Schefter that a decision on whether or not the wideout would join the Commanders was unlikely to happen on Wednesday. Things have changed. Schefter now reports Aiyuk has agreed to sign with Washington's practice squad, putting an end to the wideout's long journey to the team. San Francisco released Aiyuk earlier this week after his roster exemption expired. The receiver cleared waivers and was then free to sign with any franchise. Aiyuk has not played since 2024. That year, he played seven games, catching 25 passes. In his last full season of 2023, he caught 75 passes for 1,342 yards with seven touchdowns.
author: Myles Simmons

title: Falcons are "aware" of suggestion that James Pearce Jr. has been trying to contact Rickea Jackson
summary: Falcons defensive end James Pearce Jr. has returned from an eight-game suspension arising from an incident with his former girlfriend, WNBA player Rickea Jackson.
full_text: Falcons defensive end James Pearce Jr. has returned from an eight-game suspension arising from an incident with his former girlfriend, WNBA player Rickea Jackson. On Wednesday, coach Kevin Stefanski addressed a suggestion on social media that Pearce has been attempting to contact Jackson, in violation of his plea deal. " I’m aware ," Stefanski told reporters, via Marc Raimondi of ESPN. "We've spoken to James. But we don't have much more to add." It's not clear that Pearce has been trying to contact Jackson. Her online comments carry a clear implication that she believes "dozens" of calls from a phone number with no ID came from Pearce. Raimondi also notes that, since his return from suspension, Pearce has not spoken to reporters, declining multiple attempts by the media to question him. League rules require all players to be available after every game and once during the week. Pearce faces potentially significant consequences if it can be proven that he has violated the terms of his one-year diversion program. Beyond the possibility of an additional suspension, Pearce could face a prison term for the charges that will be dismissed only if he fully complies with the program.
author: Mike Florio

title: Jets designate T'Vondre Sweat for return from injured reserve
summary: The Jets will have defensive tackle T'Vondre Sweat back at practice this week.
full_text: '' The Jets will have defensive tackle T'Vondre Sweat back at practice this week. Sweat has been out since hurting his knee in Week 7, but the Jets announced that he has been designated for return from injured reserve on Wednesday. The move opens up a 21-day practice window and he can be activated at any point in that span. Sweat joined the Jets in an offseason trade with the Titans. He started six of the team's first seven games this season and had 17 tackles while appearing in every game. The Jets are coming off of their third win of the season and they'll try for their first winning streak since Weeks 2 and 3 of the 2024 season when they travel to Miami this weekend.
author: Josh Alper

title: Marlon Humphrey takes part in Wednesday's Ravens practice
summary: Cornerback Marlon Humphrey returned to the Ravens' facility on Monday and he returned to their practice field on Wednesday.
full_text: Cornerback Marlon Humphrey returned to the Ravens' facility on Monday and he returned to their practice field on Wednesday. Humphrey was sent home last week and deactivated for the team's loss to the Panthers after saying that Baltimore was the best at "making criminals" on an episode of his podcast. Humphrey apologized for that comment, but was criticized by the city's mayor and many others for the way he characterized local residents. The Ravens welcomed Humphrey back this week, but head coach Jesse Minter did not commit to playing him in this Sunday's game against the Texans. Reporters at the open portion of practice also noted that defensive tackle Nnamdi Madubuike and safety Jaylinn Hawkins are not practicing. Both players were out in Week 11.
author: Josh Alper

title: Titans sign CB Corey Thornton off of the Panthers practice squad
summary: The Titans have made an addition to their ailing defense.
full_text: The Titans have made an addition to their ailing defense . They announced that they have signed cornerback Corey Thornton off of the Panthers' practice squad. There was no corresponding move needed to clear space for Thornton on the roster in Tennessee. Thornton appeared in two games for the Panthers this month. He had an interception in their Week 9 loss to the Broncos and also recorded eight tackles and three passes defensed. After last Sunday's 51-30 loss to the Cowboys, the Titans rank 30th in the league in points allowed and dead last in yards allowed. They'll be hoping Thornton helps them improve on both fronts.
author: Josh Alper

title: Brandon Aiyuk finishes visit with Commanders, but decision is not expected on Wednesday
summary: Brandon Aiyuk may still join the Commanders soon, but it sounds like that's not imminent.
full_text: Brandon Aiyuk may still join the Commanders soon, but it sounds like that's not imminent. Drew Rosenhaus, Aiyuk's agent, said the receiver's visit with Washington is over, via ESPN's Adam Schefter. Rosenhaus added that “ Discussions are ongoing and positive ,” but there probably will not be a decision today. Aiyuk, who has not played since 2024, was released by the 49ers earlier this week and cleared waivers, making him free to sign with any team. The Commanders have long been thought of as the frontrunner to land Aiyuk We’ll see if Aiyuk takes more visits before joining a club.
author: Myles Simmons

title: Quinyon Mitchell has no injury designation for Thanksgiving
summary: The Eagles will have cornerback Quinyon Mitchell in the lineup for Thursday's game in Dallas.
full_text: '' The Eagles will have cornerback Quinyon Mitchell in the lineup for Thursday's game in Dallas. Mitchell did not receive an injury designation for the Thanksgiving game. He was listed as out of practice on Monday due to a hamstring injury, but moved up to limited participation Tuesday and was a full participant on Friday. Running back Saquon Barkley, defensive tackle Jalen Carter, tight end Dallas Goedert, and wide receiver DeVonta Smith are also without designations after appearing on the injury report this week. Linebacker Arnold Ebiketie (oblique) and cornerback Jonathan Jones (ankle) are the only players who did receive designations. Both of them have been ruled out for the Eagles this week.
author: Josh Alper

title: Panthers designate LB Thomas Incoom for return from IR
summary: The Panthers have opened the practice window for linebacker Thomas Incoom.
full_text: The Panthers have opened the practice window for linebacker Thomas Incoom. Incoom has been designated for return from injured reserve and will be able to practice for the next 21 days as a result. The Panthers can activate him at any point in that window. Incoom was placed on injured reserve ahead of Week 7 due to a calf injury. He had six tackles and a fumble recovery in five games before his injury. The Panthers have now designated seven players for return this season. They will be able to do it one more time during the regular season and that spot is expected to be filled by cornerback Jaycee Horn once he is ready to get back on the field.
author: Josh Alper

title: PFT's Thanksgiving and Week 12 2026 NFL picks
summary: All games picked for one of the most compelling weeks of the season.
full_text: It was inevitable. After flirting a couple of times with landing under .500 in a given week of picks, it finally happened. For Week 11, I went 6-7. That's what I get for trying to pick upsets. In Week 11, it was Chalk City — and 12 of 13 home teams won. And so, from now on, I'm not getting cute. I'm sticking with my first impulse. I'm not overthinking it. The first number that pops into my head will be the pick. For the year, I'm at 102-60-1. The success rate is still 62.5 percent. Here's hoping I can find a way to push it a little higher with the 16 games to be played from Wednesday through Monday. Packers at Rams (Wednesday night) Sean McVay is 0-5 against Matt LaFleur. A loss on Wednesday night would put the preseason favorites in grave danger of missing the playoffs, especially in light of an upcoming schedule that includes games against the Chiefs, the 49ers, the Cowboys, the Seahawks (twice), and the Buccaneers. Rams 24, Packers 20. Bears at Lions (Thursday) It's the biggest early-window Thanksgiving game ever, with both teams at 8-2. Ben Johnson's Bears gave up 52 points during last year's visit to Ford Field. They'll be determined to achieve a different result this time, in what becomes a true litmus test for the new-look Bears. If they're truly contenders, this is a game they win. Bears 23, Lions 21. Eagles at Cowboys (Thursday) It won't be a cakewalk. For Philly, it's the closest they'll get this year to a game with a postseason vibe. But the Cowboys have a chance to make a run at the Giants — if Dallas can also hold off the Commanders. Cowboys 41, Eagles 24. Chiefs at Bills (Thursday) Josh Allen is 5-0 against Patrick Mahomes in the regular season, 0-4 against Mahomes in the postseason. The trend continues, thanks to conditions that are more conducive to Allen making the right throw at the right time. Bills 23, Chiefs 17. Broncos at Steelers (Friday) This one had the feel of a game the Steelers would find a way to win, until the benching of Aaron Rodgers threw everything into disarray. Broncos 20, Steelers 13. Saints at Bengals The Bengals need to get back on track, quickly, after Monday night's sluggish performance. A slump could open the door for the Browns to steal the division. Bengals 31, Saints 20. Ravens at Texans It feels like an elimination game in Houston, even if the winner will still be facing an uphill climb to the postseason. When in doubt, ride with the clearly better quarterback. Texans 27, Ravens 23. Giants at Colts This will be a far cry from the 1958 NFL Championship. The Giants are surging, and the Colts are slowly disintegrating. Giants 24, Colts 9. Titans at Jaguars As the saying goes, it's not the size of the dog in the fight but the size of the fight in the dog. Unfortunately, this fight is round two of Doberman vs. Chihuahua. Jaguars 35, Titans 20. Jets at Dolphins The Dolphins are running out of chances to get a second win (if they even want one). Dolphins 23, Jets 13. Falcons at Vikings Kirk Cousins gets the double whammy — his first home game in his second stint with the Vikings, and his first shot at revenge against the team that signed him and then drafted his replacement. Vikings 27, Falcons 13. Patriots at Chargers It's fitting that a game pitting two struggling teams coached by former Ohio State and Michigan players happens one day after a game between struggling Ohio State and Michigan teams. Patriots 16, Chargers 10. Commanders at Cardinals Monday night's upset of the Bengals means nothing if the Commanders bungle a winnable game at Arizona. Commanders 27, Cardinals 10. Seahawks at 49ers Having an extra week to prepare, coupled with the urgency of a 6-4 record, is just what the doctor ordered for the Seahawks. Seahawks 27, 49ers 23. Raiders at Browns The NFL will be happy it flexed this one into primetime. (For reasons other than getting Patriots-Chargers out of that window.) Browns 30, Raiders 27. Panthers at Buccaneers Tampa Bay is running out of chances to pull themselves back into contention. Buccaneers 27, Panthers 20.
author: Mike Florio

title: Devontez Walker wins AFC special teams player of the week
summary: The Ravens didn’t beat the Panthers on Sunday, but they did have one individual do enough to win a player of the week award.
full_text: The Ravens didn’t beat the Panthers on Sunday, but they did have one individual do enough to win a player of the week award. The NFL named returner Devontez Walker special teams player of the week. Walker had an 86-yard kickoff return for a touchdown in the second quarter of the contest. He ended up returning seven kicks for 211 yards, becoming the second player to have at least 200 kickoff return yards in a game this season. His touchdown return was just the second kick returned for a TD this season. This is Walker’s first player of the week award.
author: Myles Simmons

title: Abdul Carter wins first NFC defensive player of the week award
summary: Giants edge rusher Abdul Carter was a game wrecker during Sunday's victory over the Jaguars.
full_text: Giants edge rusher Abdul Carter was a game wrecker during Sunday's victory over the Jaguars. Now he's been named NFC defensive player of the week. Carter had four tackles with 2.0 sacks in the 23-18 victory. The NFL notes that according to Next Gen Stats, Carter had 12 QB pressures in Week 11, which is the second most recorded in a single game this season. This is Carter’s first defensive player of the week award. Carter now has 4.0 sacks, five tackles for loss, and 13 quarterback hits this season.
author: Myles Simmons

title: Commanders K Drew Stevens is the NFC special teams player of the week
summary: The Commanders called on kicker Drew Stevens often in Week 11 and he came through each and every time.
full_text: The Commanders called on kicker Drew Stevens often in Week 11 and he came through each and every time. Stevens was asked to attempt field goals at the end of all five of Washington's possessions in the second half of their home date with the Bengals and Stevens made all five of those kicks. The last of them came on the final snap of the game and the 26-yard kick gave the Commanders a 22-20 win. Stevens was named the NFC special teams player of the week on Wednesday. The Commanders signed Stevens as an undrafted rookie this offseason and he is now 22-of-25 on field goals and 16-of-19 on extra points on the year.
author: Josh Alper

title: Will Anderson named the AFC defensive player of the week
summary: The Texans hurt their playoff chances with a slow start to the regular season, but they are still in the hunt and having defensive end Will Anderson will help their chances.
full_text: '' The Texans hurt their playoff chances with a slow start to the regular season, but they are still in the hunt and having defensive end Will Anderson will help their chances. Anderson helped them to their fourth win in the last six games last Thursday by recording five tackles, a sack, two tackles for loss and four quarterback hits against the Colts. Anderson's sack of Daniel Jones came in the end zone for the first sack of the Texans pass rusher's career. The NFL named Anderson the AFC defensive player of the week on Wednesday. It's the second time he's won the award in his career. Anderson leads the league with 11.5 sacks and the Texans' postseason hopes will keep improving as long as he continues to produce off the edge on defense.
author: Josh Alper

title: Brock Purdy wins fourth career NFC offensive player of the week award
summary: Brock Purdy is an MVP candidate and had another strong performance in Sunday’s victory over the Vikings.
full_text: Brock Purdy is an MVP candidate and had another strong performance in Sunday’s victory over the Vikings. Now he’s been named NFC offensive player of the week. Purdy finished the game 21-of-26 passing for 255 yards with three touchdowns and no interceptions — good for a 146.0 passer rating. This was Purdy’s seventh career game with a passer rating of at least 145, which is the most by a player in his first five seasons in league history. Purdy is one of two quarterbacks with a passer rating of at least 100 in eight games this season, the other being Cincinnati’s Joe Burrow. Purdy has now won four career offensive player of the week awards. The current No. 1 seed in the conference, Purdy and the 49ers will host the Seahawks on Sunday afternoon.
author: Myles Simmons

title: Jonah Coleman is the AFC offensive player of the week
summary: Broncos rookie Jonah Coleman has moved to the top of the running back depth chart in Denver since returning from injured reserve late last month and he had his biggest game yet against the Raiders in Week 11.
full_text: '' Broncos rookie Jonah Coleman has moved to the top of the running back depth chart in Denver since returning from injured reserve late last month and he had his biggest game yet against the Raiders in Week 11. Coleman ran 24 times for 111 yards and three touchdowns to help the Broncos to a 38-24 win. Those were all season-highs for Coleman, who now has five touchdowns in the last three weeks. The NFL named Coleman the AFC offensive player of the week in recognition of that effort. Coleman is the first Bronco to win the award since quarterback Bo Nix at the end of the 2024 season and the Broncos will be hoping that the duo is just at the start of a fruitful partnership.
author: Josh Alper

title: Kenneth Walker ruled out for Thanksgiving night vs. Bills
summary: Rookie RB Emmett Johnson is now set to start his third consecutive game.
full_text: The Chiefs will not have Kenneth Walker when they play the Bills on Thursday. Kansas City has officially ruled Walker out for the contest, putting rookie Emmett Johnson in line to start for the third consecutive game. Walker (groin) returned to practice on Tuesday in a limited capacity. But Walker would not have practiced on Wednesday and won’t play against Buffalo. Walker has used for 872 yards with seven touchdowns in eight games. He still leads the league averaging 5.5 yards per carry. He’s also caught 26 passes for 172 yards with four touchdowns. Johnson, a rookie fifth-round pick, has rushed for 100 yards in each of the last two games. In Sunday’s win over the Cardinals, he had 105 yards on 23 carries with a touchdown and four catches for 38 yards. The Chiefs also ruled out right tackle Jaylon Moore (ankle) and defensive tackle Omarr Norman-Lott (knee). Tight end Noah Gray (rib) and defensive lineman Peter Woods (neck) are questionable. Cornerback Mansoor Delane (shoulder), receiver Rashee Rice (knee), guard Trey Smith (concussion), and quarterback Patrick Mahomes (knee/right elbow) are all off the injury report and are set to play.
author: Myles Simmons

title: Report: Steelers were changing the play-calling process as of Tuesday
summary: More and more information is emerging as to the surprise decision to bench Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers.
full_text: More and more information is emerging as to the surprise decision to bench Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers. Here's an interesting nugget, from Mike Garafolo of NFL Network. As Garafolo explains it, the Steelers were changing their play-calling process . Starting Friday, quarterbacks coach Tom Arth, not head coach Mike McCarthy, would have been communicating the plays to Rodgers. Previously, Arth handled play-calling during the two-minute drill. Moving forward, Arth would have been doing it for the entire game. They worked on the new approach at practice on Tuesday. It was something Rodgers wanted. At some point, that changed. McCarthy opted to bench Rodgers instead. The situation dusts off the drama from nearly eight weeks ago, when Rodgers and McCarthy's on-field unpleasantries during a loss to the Browns flowed from Rodgers's frustrations regarding the pace of McCarthy's play calls. And it suggests that Tuesday's move was simply the last domino in a chain that started falling the moment Rodgers shouted, " What the fuck? Call it! " and McCarthy responded by saying, "Fucking asshole."
author: Mike Florio

title: Jalen McMillan to return to practice for the Buccaneers

title: Report: Aaron Rodgers was "excused" from work on Wednesday
summary: The sudden, late-night benching of quarterback Aaron Rodgers has created a slew of questions that are being answered in real time.
full_text: The sudden, late-night benching of quarterback Aaron Rodgers has created a slew of questions that are being answered in real time. One of the obvious questions was answered on Wednesday morning, when Gerry Dulac of the Pittsburgh Post-Gazette reported that Rodgers didn’t show up for work on Wednesday. Implicit in that report was the idea that he chose to no-show. Now, Adam Schefter of ESPN reports that Rodgers's absence was " excused " as he processes the fact that coach Mike McCarthy has decided to play Mason Rudolph on Friday against the Broncos. At some point, Rodgers will have something to say. Maybe he'll make a surprise appearance on McAfee's show today, even if that development would surprise no one. Rodgers will surely have an opinion on the situation. Chances are that his opinion will be something other than, "You know, they were right to bench me." We've seen this movie before. Rodgers has no qualms about airing grievances. Now, the Steelers have given him a specific reason to feel aggrieved. The surprise at this point wouldn't be Rodgers showing up on McAfee's show and flaming the Steelers. The surprise would be Rodgers saying nothing. Silence could easily be interpreted as acceptance of, and possibly agreement with, the move. Beyond that, Rodgers has shown (specifically since his 2021 heel turn) that he's never silent on topics about which he has strong feelings.
