title: NFL Week 12 expert picks, best bets: Lions spoil Bears Thanksgiving, Patrick Mahomes picks up rare win
summary: Tyler Sullivan picks every game on the Week 12 schedule, including five locks against the spread
full_text:
The only thing that pairs better with football than Thanksgiving is betting on football. Fortunately for us, we don't have to compromise this week, as the NFL is locked and loaded with tons of action over the holiday weekend. We are about to embark on a marathon that has five days of games over a six-day stretch.
This is why we put in the work over the offseason and stay in tip-top betting shape. It's so that when we reach pockets like this where the games are coming in one after another, we have the stamina (and bankroll) to keep up.
This barrage of games comes at a swell time for us in this little betting corner of the internet, as I'm heading into this stretch with a strong record over the last month or so. Week 11 was a more modest outcome, but our heads were above water. I was 9-4 straight-up and 7-6 against the spread for the entire slate and went 3-2 ATS on my five locks of the week. That brings me to a 35-7 straight-up mark and a 10-5 ATS record with my locks over the last three weeks. That's certainly something to be thankful for, and I'll look to keep it rolling as we step toward Week 12.
All lines via DraftKings ; All times ET
I get that Chicago is riding a five-game winning streak into this Thanksgiving matchup and that they've looked like a bona fide Super Bowl threat after acquiring Jeffery Simmons . That said, I think the Lions are getting disrespected a bit with this line making them a home dog.
Detroit has largely owned the Bears as of late, sweeping them in each of the last two seasons. Over that stretch, Jared Goff has averaged 305.5 passing yards per game and has 11 touchdowns with just one interception. Jahmyr Gibbs has reached at least 100 scrimmage yards in all four of those games as well.
While that history is nice to lean on, the true reason I like taking the home dog in this matchup is their defense. Sure, Simmons will get a lot of shine for his impact on Chicago, but Brian Branch has also helped change the fortunes of Detroit's unit. Since Branch has returned to the secondary, the Lions are 5-0 and allowing 14.4 points per game. Their 248.6 yards per game allowed and 168.6 passing yards per game allowed are both top five in the NFL over that span.
Projected score : Lions 27, Bears 23 The pick : Lions +2.5
Thursday's Thanksgiving finale will mark the 11th time that Patrick Mahomes and Josh Allen have squared off against one another in their careers. On the whole, this rivalry has been one-sided depending on the time of year. In the regular season, Allen is 5-1 against Mahomes, but the Chiefs quarterback is a perfect 4-0 in the playoffs. Seeing as this is a regular-season matchup, one would think this trend could continue, especially with the Bills playing at Highmark Stadium. However, I think Mahomes gets a rare regular-season win over his rival.
Mahomes comes into Week 12 with his hair on fire, totaling 13 touchdowns and zero interceptions over his last four games. Not only do those numbers bolster his sure-fire Comeback Player of the Year candidacy, but they're making him a dark-horse MVP candidate. Buffalo's defense has put up some eye-popping numbers as they've gone three straight games without allowing a touchdown. However, these are the quarterbacks they've faced over that stretch: Carson Wentz , Max Brosmer , Geno Smith , Cade Klubnik , and Kyle McCord . Mahomes is in another stratosphere.
Meanwhile, Kansas City's defense has been sneaky great this year, owning the best red zone scoring efficiency (36%) in the league entering Week 12.
Projected score : Chiefs 28, Bills 24 The pick : Chiefs +3
I've already covered the fact that Pittsburgh firmly has its back against the wall — and rather extensively — this week. They're 0-2 since coming out of their bye week and have seen their playoff position start to slip, falling from the No. 6 seed to the No. 7 seed last weekend. This is, in part, why I'm taking them to pull off the upset at home over the Broncos . They're simply the more desperate team. If they don't win here, it could be the beginning of the end to their season.
If they lose, they run the risk of falling out of the playoff picture entirely and set up another do-or-die matchup with the Texans in Week 13. Playing at home, this is a gotta-have-it moment for Mike McCarthy and Aaron Rodgers .
Fortunately for them, they do matchup pretty well against Denver. While their ground game has been one of the main reasons for their struggles over the past two weeks, it has a strong opportunity to get back on track this Friday. The Broncos are allowing 4.6 yards per carry this season, which is tied for the fifth-highest in the NFL. During Sunday's win over the Raiders , Denver allowed Ashton Jeanty to post 169 yards from scrimmage. Jaylen Warren has the ability to make that same type of impact as both a receiver and runner out of the backfield.
Moreover, the Steelers ' run defense should be able to contain what has blossomed into a strong Broncos ground attack headlined by Jonah Coleman . Pittsburgh's 3.6 yards per carry allowed average this season is tied for the second-fewest in the league. The defense has also allowed the seventh-fewest points per game (20.1). If they can bottle up Coleman and put more emphasis on Bo Nix , that could be the winning formula.
Projected score : Steelers 23, Broncos 20 The pick : Steelers +3
The Vikings are likely frustrated with how their Week 11 loss to the 49ers went down in Mexico City. While the 35-10 final score looks lopsided, Minnesota had self-inflicted wounds, including a pick-six by Kirk Cousins and a brutal fumble by Justin Jefferson at the start of the second half. They have a great opportunity to get back on track when they return home and host a Falcons team that is nowhere close to the caliber of San Francisco.
We all know that Brian Flores deploys blitzes like no other coordinator in the NFL. While Brock Purdy sliced it up last Sunday in Mexico City, Michael Penix ranks 27th out of 32 quarterbacks in EPA per dropback when blitzed this season, according to TruMedia.
Meanwhile, the Falcons defense is allowing touchdowns on 67.6% of red zone trips this season, the sixth-highest rate in the NFL. That should result in Cousins having much easier sledding against his former team. This is as ripe a bounce-back spot as you'll find.
Projected score : Vikings 27, Falcons 17 The pick : Vikings -7
This is a bad spot for the Ravens , who can't seem to catch a break this season. Baltimore is currently on a six-game losing streak, coinciding with Lamar Jackson's injury. They also have a historically poor defense and now have to go on the road to face a Texans team that possesses the rest advantage after playing last Thursday. That's a recipe for this losing skid to continue.
The Ravens' defense ranks 26th in scoring this season, and their 26.7 points per game allowed is on pace to be the second-most in team history. They've also allowed 30 or more points in four of the last five games.
That's music to C.J. Stroud's ears, as the Texans quarterback has completely revitalized himself in 2026 and reestablished himself as one of the top signal-callers in the league. Stroud is currently tied with Mahomes for the best TD-INT ratio in the NFL. He's also top seven in the league in passing yards and passing touchdowns. Stroud has thrown at least three touchdowns in three straight games entering Week 12.
Getting this line under a touchdown is an auto-bet, considering how Stroud and the Ravens defense are playing right now.

Take the top of the Eastern Conference, for example. The teams involved in the most highly scrutinized trade of the offseason are about where they figured to be through the first 20% or so of the campaign. One has a slightly higher stress level than the other , but both are far from panic mode, according to our John Gonzalez. Here are the 76ers' and Celtics' stress levels:

title: NFL playoff picture: Ranking AFC wild card contenders, from Super Bowl-hopeful Chiefs to rebuilding Raiders
summary: Outside of Kansas City, the battle for a wild card berth in this conference is wide open
full_text:
The road to the Super Bowl runs through the Buffalo Bills , who stand atop the AFC through 11 weeks and are poised to dominate their division en route to a potential first-round bye in the postseason. Most of the division leaders in this conference, Bills included, are runaway favorites, so the drama in the battle for the top four seeds should be limited over the final two months of the regular season. But the wild card race is a different story.
The bottom is falling out in the AFC in real time, leaving an uninspiring crop of teams vying for the final spots in the bracket. The Houston Texans stand two games below .500 but have just as strong a chance as practically any non-division leader of clinching a spot in the field. That goes to show how few competent squads exist outside of the top four.
Quarterback injuries are to blame for some of these woes, but the middle tier's struggles go beyond Drake Maye's fractured fibula and Lamar Jackson's thumb surgery. Three teams will rise from this group of wild card hopefuls nonetheless, earning spots in the seven-team bracket.
Here is a breakdown of the AFC playoff picture and a ranking of the seven strongest wild card contenders.
Division title and playoff odds via DraftKings Sportsbook
Defense is an increasingly concerning issue for the Raiders . They rank 29th in EPA per play allowed and have surrendered at least 30 points in all but one game since Week 4. It is going to be nearly impossible to win games unless Fernando Mendoza quickly turns his promise into production as a prolific young quarterback. This offense, as currently constructed, is not built to put 30 or more points on the board every week.
But signs in Mendoza's second start suggested the future is bright. He still took too many sacks and completed only 18 of 37 passes, but the No. 1 pick displayed real dual-threat playmaking ability in a three-touchdown effort against the Broncos. Ashton Jeanty even got off the schneid with a much-needed standout performance, breaking loose for a 46-yard run and scoring on the longest receiving play of his career: a 68-yarder. That Mendoza and Jeanty found so much success even without Brock Bowers in the lineup provides room for optimism.
The question is whether this will carry forward through the rest of the season or if it will take until 2027 and beyond for the offense to realize its potential. It at least has the makings of a unit that could win a game or two down the stretch.
Projected final record: 6-11
By the time Lamar Jackson returns — if he comes back at all this season — it will be too late to salvage Year 1 of the Jesse Minter era. Six consecutive losses completely tanked what was once an exciting start to a new coaching tenure. The Ravens would be hard-pressed to lose out since Jacoby Brissett has finally stabilized the offense a bit, but where will the wins come from as they work their way through a schedule that still features four games against divisional opponents in a surprisingly competitive AFC North?
A bigger issue than the offense is the defense, which is a complete surprise given Minter's track record as a premier coach on that side of the ball. He was supposed to turn the group around with his acumen and the uptick in talent the franchise experienced over the offseason when it brought in Trey Hendrickson and retained stars in the secondary. Instead, his unit ranks 21st in DVOA and 18th in EPA per play allowed. Every opponent in the last five games, save the Chargers, scored at least 33 points against Minter's squad. And the Chargers won their matchup to get their first win of the season.
Slightly better days are ahead now that Derrick Henry is rolling again and the passing game is at least somewhat functional with Brissett under center. But the playoffs are probably out of reach.
Projected final record: 6-11
The Patriots are difficult to handicap at this juncture because the quarterback shakeup hasn't had much time to marinate. The safe bet is to assume Tommy DeVito will not rebound much from the dismal showing he put up in Week 10, when he stepped in early in the loss to the Lions and led the team on just one scoring drive over the final three quarters. Considering the plethora of injuries elsewhere on the roster — most notably with A.J. Brown set to miss multiple weeks and the offensive line remaining a revolving door — New England lacks the weapons to make up for any bleak play from DeVito.
Drake Maye was essentially the only reason the Patriots still had life in the postseason hunt. At his best, he held together an injury-riddled roster and willed it to victories with performances that reflected his near-MVP-caliber play in 2025. But then there were the disastrous outings that showed just how bad this team is when its quarterback is not pulling off heroics.
Unfortunately for New England, it should expect more of the latter so long as DeVito is in the lineup. With Maye out indefinitely as he recovers from a fractured fibula, this season is headed down the drain.
Projected final record: 7-10
Something is not quite right in Pittsburgh and now Aaron Rodgers has been benched for Mason Rudolph. Two weeks ago, the Steelers had the inside track to a top-four seed. Now they are on the outside of the playoffs looking in. The last two games were two of their worst all year and sounded every alarm.
The Steelers basically no-showed in a primetime divisional showdown with the Bengals two weeks ago and followed that embarrassing contest with a loss to the Eagles , who hadn't won a game in two months. In the process, DK Metcalf lost his composure and earned an ejection, the defense allowed Joe Burrow and Ja'Marr Chase to do whatever they wanted and a typically efficient run game reverted into a non-factor. Nothing went right.
Pittsburgh is at a crossroads. The vibes in the Steel City are sour, and unless this team gets itself right in short order, it could be in for a downward spiral. But at the same time, Mike McCarthy had his team looking like a surefire playoff contender through the first half of the campaign, so a return to form could lead to a trip to the postseason.
Projected final record: 9-8
A thrilling comeback against the Texans ensured the Browns didn't hit their bye week on an extended skid, which could do wonders for team morale as they enter the stretch run. In erasing a 17-0 deficit and stunning Houston, the Browns put themselves in the driver's seat in the wild card race. With a manageable remaining schedule that offers plenty of winnable games outside of two contests against the Bengals, Cleveland could be in line to get into the dance for the first time since 2023 and just the fourth time this century.
Even if they come up short, Todd Monken deserves ample credit for making the Browns one of the NFL's most pleasant surprises of the year. The first-year coach inherited a roster hardly anyone believed in and turned it into a division contender, while making the Deshaun Watson contract look a little less disastrous and turning Denzel Boston and KC Concepcion into Rookie of the Year candidates. The defense is fairly solid even in a post-Myles Garrett world, too.
Ideally, Cleveland would jumpstart its run game when it returns from its off week and get Quinshon Judkins rolling, but with the young wide receiver corps performing and Watson playing above expectations, the Browns might be able to throw their way into the playoffs.
Projected final record: 9-8
The further removed the Texans become from their 0-4 start, the more baffling it becomes that they did, in fact, start the season winless. C.J. Stroud continues to play the best football of his career. Will Anderson Jr . is a top-tier Defensive Player of the Year candidate. The wide receiver group is deep and helped Houston field the seventh-best passing attack by yards per game over the first 11 weeks. Three of their last four wins came by 22 or 23 points. The full product of late is more in line with preseason expectations than…
author: Carter Bahns

title: NFL Week 12 most important games for playoff picture: Rams-Packers, Panthers-Bucs key duels in NFC
summary: This week is chock-full of potential make-or-break games from Wednesday to Sunday
full_text:
The term "feast week" has long been associated with college basketball, but this week, the NFL is rolling out a spread unlike any seen before. It hasn't even been that long — Week 17, 2024 — since the last NFL week with games on five different days.
But this specific combination of games on Wednesday, Thursday, Friday, Sunday and Monday?
Never, ever before, according to CBS Sports Research.
If the last few weeks have felt like duds, this week will feel like drinking water from a firehose, and not just in terms of quantity but quality. With all 32 teams in action and several games between teams vying for a playoff spot in the same conference, the playoff picture is bound to get a major makeover. According to CBS Sports' forecasts and projections, 12 teams could see their playoff leverage swing by at least 15% depending on their outcomes. These are the five most important contests for the playoff picture.
Monday, 8:15 p.m. on ESPN (Stream: fubo, try for free )
The Panthers are already two games clear of every other team in the division, but this is Carolina's chance to deliver an early dagger, as their drastic swing in postseason chance indicates. Not only would the Panthers be three games up on the Buccaneers in the standings with a win, but they'd also even the head-to-head tiebreaker. A Buccaneers win, though, would draw Tampa Bay within a game, secure the head-to-head tiebreaker over Carolina and push Baker Mayfield and Co. to 3-0 in the division.
A fittingly crucial finale to a crucial week.
Wednesday, 8 p.m. on Netflix
The week ends with a bang, but it starts with a bang, too. The Packers currently own the final NFC playoff spot, but the Seahawks and the Rams have the same record and trail only on tiebreakers. It's not quite an elimination game, but the fact that both teams' chances drop so drastically with a loss shows it's close to one.
Sunday, 8:20 p.m. on NBC (Stream: fubo, try for free )
The Browns have been one of the season's biggest surprises, currently sitting sixth in the AFC. Right now, there's some separation between the back half of the AFC playoff field and the teams trying to chase it down, and if Cleveland keeps stacking wins, teams on the outside will continue to look in, unable to draw any closer. An upset loss, though, would open the door some.
Sunday, 1 p.m. on CBS, streaming on Paramount+
Speaking of teams trying to track down the Browns (or, perhaps more likely, the Steelers ) at the back end of the AFC playoffs, the Texans have to take care of business here against the Ravens. A Texans win plus a Steelers loss to the Broncos would draw Houston to within a game of Pittsburgh.
Sunday, 4:25 p.m. ET on Fox (Stream: fubo, try for free )
Our projections currently favor the Seahawks most among the three 6-4 NFC teams (Seattle, Green Bay, Los Angeles), but either Green Bay or Los Angeles will get to 7-4 on Wednesday, and Seattle won't want to fall a game off pace. Remember, the Seahawks already blew one critical game against the 49ers, turning the ball over four times in a 32-29 Week 5 loss.
Sunday, 1 p.m. on CBS, streaming on Paramount+
In this series, when we've talked about the playoff picture, we've thought of it as if teams are included, not where .
But the Thanksgiving Day opener, airing on CBS and streaming on Paramount+ , is too big to ignore. The Bears and Lions are both playoff shoo-ins, but this will go a long way in determining which one is the king of the North. And remember, it's not just a potential division title on the line, but playoff seeding and home-field advantage, too.
author: Zachary Pereles

title: Rams vs. Packers prediction: Can Green Bay find continue success with deep ball? Will L.A. overcome injuries?
summary: Micah Parsons makes his season debut for Green Bay as an injury-depleted Los Angeles offense leans on its ground attack in the NFL's first Thanksgiving Eve showdown
full_text:
In the first-ever Thanksgiving Eve NFL game, the Los Angeles Rams play host to the Green Bay Packers .
The Rams enter this game coming off their bye week, and they are incredibly banged up on offense. Puka Nacua is likely out for the year, as is Terrance Ferguson , after they each underwent surgery on lower-body injuries. Davante Adams remains out with his hamstring injury as well. The Rams will need their defense and their running backs to carry the day against a tough Packers team.
Green Bay is also coming off the bye, but is getting healthier for this game as Micah Parsons will make his season debut after tearing his ACL toward the tail end of last season. Parsons returning to the fold provides a significant boost to what has already been a good defense under Jonathan Gannon, and the offense remains one of the league's most explosive units with Jordan Love targeting Christian Watson and Matthew Golden down the field.
Will the Rams hold off the Packers at home, or will Green Bay pull off the upset? We'll find out soon enough. Before we break down the matchup, here's a look at how you can watch the game.
Green Bay's offense is entirely based on the passing game because the Packers simply cannot run the ball. Green Bay is last in the league at 3.1 yards per carry. The Packers' 670 rushing yards are 124 fewer than the next-closest team in the league (the Bengals ). The Rams allow only 3.9 yards per carry and sport Myles Garrett and Aaron Donald up front.
The Packers are not going to find success on the ground here — and honestly, they might not even try to do so. They're probably just going to let Jordan Love drop back and let it rip. That's what they've largely done throughout this season, and it's worked quite well for them.
Love has completed 63% of his passes at 7.7 yards per attempt, with 20 touchdowns and seven interceptions. He's ninth in the league in EPA per play, according to Tru Media, thanks largely to the fact that he's created explosives at the fourth-highest rate in the league. When you have Christian Watson and Matthew Golden by your side, that's how the offense is likely going to be built. The Packers really lean into their strengths by having the strong-armed Love target their speedy wideouts with deep routes; Love has thrown 20-plus yards downfield at the second-highest rate in football.
The Rams have been the NFL's third-best defense against deep passes this year, according to Tru Media, with opponents completing only 8 of 30 deep passes for 257 yards, 1 touchdown and 1 interception. The 30 deep passes they've faced are the sixth-fewest in the league.
It'll be fascinating to see whether Green Bay continues to attack deep downfield or if Love, Watson, Golden and tight end Tucker Kraft instead work the short and intermediate areas of the field that the Rams encourage opposing offenses to throw to because of their coverage structures. It'll also be interesting to see if Trent McDuffie shadows one of the two wideouts or if the Rams play sides with him and Josh Wallace , who has taken the place of the injured Jaylen Watson .
L.A. has allowed the league's fewest catches and second-fewest yards to wide receivers this season, according to Pro-Football-Reference, with opposing quarterbacks targeting tight ends and running backs more often than they do against other teams. Tight ends have been targeted at the fourth-highest rate (27.4% of passes, according to Tru Media) against the Rams, while backs have been targeted at the second-highest rate (20.6%).
This could be a game where Kraft is more involved in the proceedings. The Packers don't throw to their backs very often because they are not good players, so they'll probably still force the ball to Watson and Golden, even if the Rams do limit wide-receiver production.
In their first game without all three of Nacua, Adams and Ferguson, the Rams used a highly unusual personnel rotation.
Their three leading skill-position players in snaps were all tight ends — and none of those tight ends was the one the Rams drafted in the second round. Their running backs shared the field for 18 snaps after having never previously played together in their careers, according to Tru Media. And one of their two primary wide receivers (rookie sixth-round pick CJ Daniels ) played more than seven times as many snaps in Week 10 (44) as he had in his entire career before that (six).
The Rams were nevertheless able to rack up 436 yards, 28 first downs and 34 points against the decrepit Cardinals' defense. They ran the ball extremely well (202 yards) and were efficient in the passing game, with each of the wideouts creating an explosive play and the backs and tight ends chipping in with short and intermediate grabs. Matthew Stafford threw only 26 passes, but five of them created gains of at least 19 yards, and he averaged nearly 10 yards per attempt.
The Packers, though, are not the Cardinals. Green Bay enters this game allowing the third-fewest net yards per attempt in the league, which accounts for yardage lost due to sacks in addition to passing yards allowed. The Packers have also yielded only 15 touchdowns through the air while intercepting a league-high 14 passes. Their safeties, in particular, have been ballhawks, with Evan Williams and Xavier McKinney combining for nine of those 14 picks and McKinney leading the league with six on his own.
Green Bay has been just about average in generating pressure so far this season, recording a sack, hit or hurry on 36.2% of opponent dropbacks, according to Tru Media. (The league average is 36.4% this year.) Getting Parsons back in the fold should help tremendously. He led the NFL in total pressures between 2021 and 2025 despite rushing the passer considerably less often than players like Myles Garrett and Maxx Crosby , who are the only players within 30 pressures of Parsons' total during that span. Parsons will likely play limited snaps, but those snaps should be concentrated on important downs and Matthew Stafford and Co. will need to be aware of where he is at all times.
The Packers have also done a pretty strong job of limiting opposing run games, allowing only 4.0 yards per carry. The Rams, though, have sported one of the best rushing attacks in the league, with Williams and Corum combining to average 4.6 yards a pop. The offensive line has cleared the way for 1.79 yards before contact per attempt, which is the second-best mark in the league behind only that of the Bills . Williams and Corum (and Ronnie Rivers) also have a combined 21.0% avoided tackle rate, per Tru Media, which is the seventh-best in football.
The Rams will likely have to lean on their run game here to move the ball, because the situation does not line up well for them through the air. The offensive line's ability to dictate the game at the line of scrimmage will likely determine whether they can achieve any degree of offensive success.
The lift the Packers get from Micah Parsons' return, plus the limitations the Rams' offense should have while working without Nacua, Adams and Ferguson, push me toward Green Bay in this game. I don't foresee the Rams moving the ball as consistently against the Packers as they did against the Cardinals in their first game without all their playmakers. Meanwhile, the Packers have the goods to challenge L.A.'s secondary downfield with Watson and Golden and over the middle with Kraft. Love should be able to get going through the air, even if Green Bay still can't run the ball. Pick: Packers 24, Rams 17
author: Jared Dubin

title: Prisco's Week 12 NFL picks: Packers edge Rams, Cowboys feast on Eagles, Bills win thriller over Chiefs
summary: Pete Prisco reveals all of his Week 12 picks, including the Steelers to upset the Broncos on Black Friday
full_text:
That's three consecutive winning weeks for me, which is a big positive. I was 7-6 against the spread last week and 9-4 straight up. My straight-up record is now 104-58-1, while my ATS record is 75-85-3.
I can see .500 now after being buried under it at the start of the season.
This is Thanksgiving Week, which is usually a good week for me. And I feel good about the picks.
It starts Wednesday night with a good one between the Packers and Rams , and it ends Monday night with the Bucs against the Panthers . I really like the teams in both of those games.
We have NFL games Wednesday, Thursday (Thanksgiving), Friday, Sunday and Monday. What a feast.
I know I will as the climb to .500 ATS continues.
All lines via DraftKings ; All times ET
The Packers get Micah Parsons back, while the Rams will be without Puka Nacua for the rest of the season. Their offense is limited without him. But this game will be decided by how well the Packers' line can block Aaron Donald and Myles Garrett . They've been bad, but I think they will be better here. The defense will keep this close, and Jordan Love will win it late.
This should be an offensive show. Both teams can score, even if Chicago hasn't been great on offense the past two games. On this fast track, look out. The Bears defense has played well since getting Jeffrey Simmons in a trade, but they won't stop the Lions here. Look for a lot of points with the home team getting the victory on Thanksgiving.
Dak Prescott has thrown nine touchdown passes and no picks in the past two weeks. The Dallas offense is rolling. The Eagles defense will be a challenge. Joe Milton, who was on the Cowboys ' practice squad, will start at quarterback for the Eagles. Dallas will play better defense against him this week. Cowboys big.
Pick: Cowboys 34, Eagles 17
This is the game of the week. Patrick Mahomes vs. Josh Allen . What's not to like as two of the best in the league go at it? The Bills have played much better defense lately, but they've faced a bunch of backup quarterbacks. Not here. So look for both passers to have good days. In the end, Allen will make the big play late to win it.
This Friday game pits two teams who would be in the playoffs right now. But the Steelers have lost two straight and haven't looked good. Denver has won six in a row. But I think the Steelers will find a way to show up and win this one behind their running game. It won't be pretty, but the Steelers will find a way.
Pick: Steelers 21, Broncos 20
The Bengals are coming off a tough road loss at Washington, while the Saints are playing consecutive road games. The Bengals offense didn't score as it had in Monday's game, but that will change here. Joe Burrow gets back on track. Bengals big.
Pick: Bengals 37, Saints 20
The Giants are coming off an impressive victory over the Jaguars , while the Colts are coming off a bye. They released quarterback Daniel Jones , which means Anthony Richardson will be starting. The Giants' defense should dominate in this one. The Colts have packed it in, so the Giants take it.
The Jets are playing consecutive road games, while the Dolphins are home for the first time in three weeks. The Jets played well in beating the Chargers last week, while Miami lost to the Bills. The Dolphins are limited on offense, but the Jets' defense has struggled. Look for Miami to hang around.
Pick: Jets 23, Dolphins 21
The Vikings are home after getting blown out by the 49ers in Mexico. The Falcons are off a bye. The Minnesota offense struggled against the 49ers, but the Falcons have had defensive problems lately. Look for the Minnesota defense to get back on track as well. Vikings take it.
Pick: Vikings 28, Falcons 14
The Jaguars are coming off a bad showing in the loss to the Giants, while Tennessee gave up 51 to the Cowboys last week. Ouch. The Jaguars scored 40 against them two weeks ago. They won't get that many here, but it will still be ugly as Trevor Lawrence and the passing game get back on track.
Pick: Jaguars 33, Titans 13
This is essentially a playoff game of sorts for these two. The loser is pretty much done. The Texans are home off a Thursday game, while the Ravens are playing consecutive road games. Edge Houston. The Texans have played well on offense, and the Ravens' defense is a mess. Look for a big day for C.J. Stroud .
Pick: Texans 31, Ravens 23
This was once scheduled for prime time, but it was moved because both teams have flopped this year. The Patriots will start Tommy DeVito for the injured Drake Maye . That's a problem. The Chargers might not have Justin Herbert (concussion) either, which would put D.J. Uiagalelei in as the starter. He's thrown seven passes in his career. Even so, give me the home team here.
Pick: Chargers 23, Patriots 16
The Commanders are coming off an impressive home victory Monday night over the Bengals, while the Cardinals got rocked by the Chiefs last week. Arizona has big-time issues and fired the defensive coordinator this week. That defense will struggle to stop Jayden Daniels . The Commanders stay hot.
Pick: Commanders 30, Cardinals 19

title: NFL Thanksgiving 2026: A look at every NFL halftime show performer for the holiday slate
summary: There will be four performances between Thanksgiving Eve and Thanksgiving
full_text:
Thanksgiving is all about family, friends, reflecting on what you're thankful for, food, and of course, football. Pigskin and turkey have gone hand-in-hand since 1934, when the Detroit Lions ' owner started the Turkey Day game tradition as a way to attract more fans.
Since then, with the exception of 1939 to 1944 (World War II), the Lions have played on the holiday. The Dallas Cowboys have played on Thanksgiving since 1966, with the exception of 1975 and 1977. This year is no different, with the Lions and Cowboys once again hosting games .
Bears vs. Lions will be played at 1 p.m. ET on CBS and stream on Paramount+ . Eagles vs. Cowboys will take place at 4:30 p.m. ET on FOX, and the Chiefs and Bills face off at 8:20 p.m. on NBC.
But the entertainment isn't just what happens while the clock is running. The Thanksgiving games will also feature halftime performances. With football and music, there's something for everyone to enjoy. Plus, it's not just the Thanksgiving game getting a halftime show: the Thanksgiving Eve matchup between the Rams and Packers will also feature mid-game entertainment.
Here's a look at each halftime show performance during the holiday week:
Game: Rams vs. Packers Location: SoFi Stadium (Inglewood, California) Time: 8 p.m. ET Streaming: Netflix
For the first time ever, NFL football will be played on Thanksgiving Eve, and U2 will take the stage at halftime. The band is celebrating their 50th anniversary and just released their 16th studio album "Carnaval De Luz," with a tour attached. The Rock & Roll Hall of Famers have 22 Grammy Awards, two Academy Award nominations, two Golden Globe Awards and many more. The group has over 300 total award show nominations with 150 wins.
This will not be the first time the group has performed during an NFL game. They took the stage for the Super Bowl XXXVI halftime performance for a moving performance that paid tribute to the victims of 9/11, which had happened just months before.
Game: Bears vs. Lions Location: Ford Field (Detroit, Michigan) Time: 1 p.m. ET Network: CBS Streaming: Paramount+
The 87th Thanksgiving Day Classic will feature a performance from the legendary Wu Tang Clan . The hip-hop group has influence that goes beyond music and into fashion, film and television. They are part of the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame class of 2026 and are currently on their farewell tour. Members of the group include RZA, GZA, Method Man, Raekwon, Ghostface Killah, U-God, Masta Killa, Inspectah Deck, Cappadonna and the late Ol' Dirty Bastard (ODB).
Eminem and his longtime manager, Paul Rosenberg, selected the performer and will be executive producers of the show for the second straight year.
Game: Cowboys vs. Eagles Location: AT&T Stadium (Arlington, Texas) Time: 4:30 p.m. ET Network : FOX (Stream: fubo , try for free)
Country superstar Miranda Lambert will take the stage during the break in the NFC East rival game. The halftime performance kicks off the Salvation Army's annual Red Kettle Campaign, encouraging fans to give back to those in need. This performance will mark the 30th consecutive Red Kettle Kickoff halftime show.
Lambert has 31 Grammy nominations, with three wins, 40 Academy of Country Music Awards, and 14 Country Music Association Awards. She is the most-awarded artist in the Academy of Country Music's history.
Game: Chiefs vs. Bills Location: Highmark Stadium (Orchard Park, New York) Time: 8:20 p.m. ET Network: NBC (Stream: fubo , try for free)
The Bills are bringing in a hometown group to perform for the primetime Thanksgiving Day game. The band has been together for over three decades, has four Grammy nominations and holds the all-time radio record for "Most Top 10 Singles."  They have sold over 15 million records worldwide and have hits that include "Iris" and "Nothing Lasts Forever." The members of the band are John Rzeznik and Robby Takac, with past members George Tutuska and Mike Malinin.

title: Brandon Aiyuk to meet with Commanders, per report: Free agent WR seeks reunion with Jayden Daniels
summary: Aiyuk may already have a destination lined up shortly after his release from the 49ers and waiver clearance.
full_text:
Now that wide receiver Brandon Aiyuk is no longer tied to the San Francisco 49ers and is officially a free agent , he has his sights set on a new contract and a fresh start. That journey back to the field will start with the Washington Commanders . Shortly after officially clearing waivers, Aiyuk scheduled a visit with the Commanders for Wednesday, according to ESPN , a key step toward playing for the first time since 2024.
During his public spat with the 49ers in which he sought a release from his contract, Aiyuk made it abundantly clear that he preferred to sign with the Commanders. In social media posts, Aiyuk repeatedly mentioned the Commanders,  either requesting a trade to Washington or reinstatement from the reserve/left squad list with the intention of pursuing a deal with the Commanders.
Aiyuk played with star Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels in college at Arizona State, so their connection makes Washington a logical destination as he aims to rekindle a once-promising career. If any quarterback could squeeze whatever juice is left in the former first-round pick, it ought to be the one with whom he starred in college and who ranks among the NFL's top young signal-callers.
Aiyuk and Daniels got into a social media feud over the summer when Aiyuk went on a posting spree and voiced his displeasure with his situation in San Francisco, calling out Daniels and the Commanders in the process. Daniels responded by telling him to "enjoy retirement, pal," but they reportedly mended their relationship .
Prior to a devastating knee injury in 2024, Aiyuk shined over four seasons with the 49ers. He upped his receiving production year after year and peaked in 2023, racking up 1,342 yards and seven touchdowns on 75 receptions. In those campaigns before he tore his ACL and MCL, Aiyuk never posted fewer than 748 yards or five touchdowns in a season.
This is so far removed from his last game appearance; it's unclear how much Aiyuk has to offer. But if he can contribute as part of a wide receiver rotation, adding him to the roster should be enticing for the Commanders.
Washington lost its top receiver, Terry McLaurin , for the season after five games and has been thin at the wideout spot ever since. Rookie Antonio Williams is fresh off the best game of his career and is developing into a starting-caliber option, but the Commanders would still benefit from another veteran option in a room that features Stefon Diggs , Treylon Burks , Dyami Brown and Van Jefferson . The offense ranks in the bottom half of the league in EPA per pass at No. 21, and Monday's win over the Cincinnati Bengals marked the first time in Daniels' career that he did not record a touchdown of any kind.
author: Carter Bahns

title: Broncos suspend RB J.K. Dobbins one game for conduct detrimental to team
summary: Dobbins will not play against the Steelers on Friday as Denver holds a slight lead over Kansas City in the AFC West race
full_text:
The Denver Broncos will play their Week 12 game against the Pittsburgh Steelers without running back J.K. Dobbins . Coach Sean Payton announced that he suspended the veteran ball carrier for one game for conduct detrimental to the team, which takes him out of the offensive rotation for the Black Friday contest. Payton did not comment further on the suspension or what prompted his decision, adding that "it's better that way" to not speak on the matter.
Although Dobbins leads the team in carries (99) and rushing yards (324), with three touchdowns on his ledger this season, he slipped in the pecking order in recent weeks behind RJ Harvey and rookie Jonah Coleman . Dobbins' role reached a new low in last week's win over the Las Vegas Raiders when he played just one snap.
Coleman emerged as the primary option in the backfield and took firm command of the starting job when he set career highs with 28 touches, 129 scrimmage yards and three touchdowns in that victory against the Raiders.
Harvey is on injured reserve due to a knee issue that popped up in practice in late October. He will not play on Friday and is not eligible to return until Week 13 against the Miami Dolphins .
With two of the top three running backs out for the matchup with the Steelers, Coleman projects to take on a sizable workload for the second time in as many weeks. Payton declined to answer questions about the group but insisted that the Broncos will have depth at the position. If anyone steps into a more meaningful role, it would likely be Cody Schrader , whom the Broncos activated to their 53-man roster for each of the last three games. Tyler Badie's practice window is open, but the Broncos have not activated him from injured reserve.

title: Week 12 Super Bowl stock report: 49ers separate from pack, Jaguars show imperfections
summary: We assess the NFL title race after Week 11 and identify three upcoming games that could reshape the Super Bowl picture
full_text:
Thanksgiving week is where the rubber meets the road in the NFL . Division races either heat up or see one team separate itself from the pack, like the San Francisco 49ers are beginning to do in the NFC West. The dust has settled on the biggest moves from this month's trade deadline, and they are either paying dividends or, in the Jacksonville Jaguars ' case, raising eyebrows for their minimal impact. The sense of urgency cranks up across the league from this week forward.
The holiday itself provides two monumental collisions that will help sort the playoff race and pave the road to the Super Bowl . And just a couple of days later, the 49ers will face a critical battle as part of the traditional Sunday slate. Win that matchup against the Seattle Seahawks , and San Francisco can practically bank on reaching the postseason if not winning the division altogether.
Here are the latest trends in the Super Bowl race heading into Week 12.
Odds via DraftKings , +2000 or better
General manager John Lynch reportedly agreed to terms on a contract extension with the 49ers this week. It is well deserved, because he has constructed an absolute behemoth of a team. Lynch's biggest moves of 2026 paid sizable dividends in the drubbing of the Minnesota Vikings in Mexico City. None were more fruitful than Mike Evans , easily among the most impactful free-agent signees of the year, who racked up 109 yards in his first game back from Achilles tendinitis.
Speaking of Achilles tendons, it's easy to forget that George Kittle tore his less than a year ago. His remarkable recovery is practically superhuman. He just turned in the best performance by a tight end against the Vikings this season with two touchdowns.
And then there is Brock Purdy . It is a close race between him and Joe Burrow for the NFL MVP award, and Sunday's showing closed any gap between the two. No quarterback had logged a passer rating above 90.0 against Minnesota all year until Purdy went nuclear on the typically ferocious defense and posted an eye-popping passer rating of 146.0. He continues to master Kyle Shanahan's offense, and his acumen has never been more obvious than it was in how he picked apart the Vikings' blitz-heavy scheme. Purdy completed 16 of 18 passes for 195 yards and two touchdowns against the blitz, and his 12.4 yards per attempt on quick passes were the most against a Brian Flores-led Vikings defense.
All of these pieces came together for the 49ers' most impressive outing of the season — one that cemented San Francisco not only at the top of the NFC but also at the front of the Super Bowl race. And the margin between them and the rest of the pack is only getting wider.
Before their 23-18 loss to the New York Giants, the Jaguars were among the buzziest teams in the league thanks to a two-loss record, a scorching offense, and a couple of trade deadline splashes. How quickly things change. The Jaguars are now two games back of the AFC's No. 1 seed instead of just one, the offense is fresh off perhaps its worst showing of the year, and Jordan Davis — who cost a first- and second-round pick at the trade deadline — was a non-factor in run defense in his team debut.
Some of those knocks against Jacksonville will prove to be one-offs in time. It is more likely than not that this squad rebounds in a big way against the Titans in Week 12 and gears up for a surge deep into the postseason. But if any of those issues persist, the most likely culprit would be the offense.
It starts up front where the offensive line is far from full strength. These three positions are of the biggest concern:
The Giants controlled the trenches, and that had a cascading effect on the rest of the Jacksonville offense. Trevor Lawrence took three sacks, faced 23 pressures, and threw two interceptions. It was his worst game by EPA this year and only his second with a negative EPA (-12.8). He was under duress all game and saw a 45% pressure rate for only the third time this season. And in the run game, the Jaguars matched their least-productive effort of the campaign with just 77 yards and saw lead running back Bhayshul Tuten sustain an ankle injury.
Little's anticipated return to action against the Titans should help the offense bounce back, at least somewhat.
There was no better time for the New York Giants to notch their best win of the season than last week, because the rest of the NFC East also won. New York maintained its divisional advantage and needs to keep stacking victories to fend off a Dallas Cowboys team that, for all its flaws, can score with anyone and a Washington Commanders squad that is rounding into form and faces a cushy schedule over the next four weeks.
The combination of John Harbaugh's rebuilt culture and the growing pool of prolific young talent on the roster creates a real playoff contender. For instance, second-year edge rusher Abdul Carter racked up a career-high 12 pressures against the Jaguars, which was the second-highest total by any player in any game all year. And behind his disruptive effort on the defensive front, the Giants logged their first win against a team five or more games above .500 since 2023, when they beat a Philadelphia Eagles team that sat most of its starters in the final week of that regular season.
The Giants will have to win their division to get into the dance. It will be another six weeks until they see another head-to-head matchup against an NFC East team, so in the meantime, they need to keep stacking efforts like the one they just displayed against a Super Bowl hopeful.
Thursday, 1 p.m., CBS, stream on Paramount+
The Detroit Lions' annual Thanksgiving game is the biggest NFC North matchup of the year to date. Every team in this division is on track to make the playoffs, but these kinds of showdowns are where Super Bowl contenders separate themselves from the average postseason hopeful. Both defenses have been better of late and need to stay that way for Detroit or Chicago to surge all the way to February, so this will be an excellent test, as they match up against some of the best offensive talent and most renowned play-callers in the NFL.
Thursday, 8:20 p.m., NBC, stream on Fubo ( try for free )
A pair of franchises that have regularly butted heads during the Josh Allen and Patrick Mahomes eras clash once again in the Thanksgiving finale. This battle ranks among the greatest Thanksgiving contests in league history, as the combined 17-3 record between the teams is the second-best win percentage entering a holiday game in the last 50 seasons. Allen owns a commanding 5-1 lead in regular-season games against Mahomes, while the latter is unbeaten in the postseason at 4-0. There is a strong chance that this will be the first of two meetings between the legendary quarterbacks with the second potentially sending the winner to the Super Bowl.
Sunday, 4:25 p.m., Fox, stream on Fubo ( try for free )
As it stands entering Week 12, only one team from the NFC West is set to reach the postseason. That is a stunning turn of events, considering the division was initially projected to send three teams to the playoffs. Seattle is on the outside looking in, and while the gap between it and the 49ers is likely too wide to close before the end of the regular season, this would be a colossal win on the Seahawks' road back to a second consecutive championship. The 49ers took the first matchup in the Pacific Northwest and thus should feel confident about pulling off a sweep when the series heads to the Bay Area this weekend.

title: Ranking NFL division races from first to worst: NFC North, NFC South entertaining for very different reasons
summary: Plus, one division race is already over, per our projections
full_text:
The NFC East might be the best example of the NFL's unpredictable nature. Earlier this season, it made history by becoming the first division to go winless over a two-week span in which every team played both weeks. Yes, that included the infamous Commanders-Giants tie that featured a fumble and an all-time clock mismanagement on the final two drives.
Then in Week 11, the division went 4-0 collectively, with the Eagles , Giants, and Commanders all springing upsets over AFC teams currently in the playoff field. A $10 NFC East parlay of the Eagles beating the Steelers , the Giants beating the Jaguars , the Commanders beating the Bengals and the Cowboys beating the Titans would have netted you a handsome $345.51.
As Al Pacino, playing Michael Corleone in The Godfather Part III, said: "Just when I thought I was out, they pull me back in!"
Ahead of a packed Thanksgiving week chock full of divisional matchups, we rank all eight division races, taking into account the quality of the teams involved, the quality of the races themselves and the potential for pandemonium.
CBS Sports forecasting and projections:
The NFC North's main quest is potentially being the first team to place all four teams in the postseason. But the division race itself is a thriller, especially with Lions-Bears looming on Thanksgiving. Yes, Detroit looks like the clear NFC North favorite for now, but a Chicago win on Turkey Day would boost the Bears' chance to win the division to 45%. Regardless, this race projects to end in a thriller: In Week 18, the Lions play the Packers, and the Bears play the Vikings.
CBS Sports forecasting and projections:
Does it get much better than a 50/50 split? Technically, our projections give Denver a 50.1% chance and Kansas City a 49.9% chance, if you're into that level of detail. The two teams have already played both of their head-to-head matchups (they split). The Broncos do have, on paper, an easier schedule remaining, which certainly helps.
CBS Sports forecasting and projections:
All of a sudden, this division race doesn't look fun-bad and might just be ... fun! The Giants and Cowboys have the eighth- and ninth-hardest remaining schedules, while the Commanders don't face a team with a winning record until Week 16. A finishing stretch featuring Giants at Cowboys in Week 17 followed by Cowboys at Commanders and Eagles at Giants in Week 18 could provide plenty of twists and turns.
CBS Sports forecasting and projections:
Last year, the Buccaneers beat the Panthers in Week 18 to stay alive, only to lose the NFC South on a tiebreaker the next day when the Falcons beat the Saints. Could we see similar madness this year? Week 12 will go a long way: If Tampa Bay beats Carolina on Monday Night Football, its chance to win the division jumps to 53%, per our calculations.
The NFC South: It might be bad, but it's certainly not boring!
CBS Sports forecasting and projections:
Even with the bunched standings at the top, our projections see Cincinnati as a clear favorite. The Bengals have several games where they should be huge favorites: Saints, at Panthers, at Colts , Ravens. It's far from wrapped up, though, and two games vs. the Browns loom large.
CBS Sports forecasting and projections:
The 49ers look like the best team in the NFL, and with a three-game lead in the division, this one might not have much drama. If that changes, it must start this week, when the Seahawks visit San Francisco. A Seattle win would only knock the 49ers' NFC West title chances to 81%, but it'd be a start.
CBS Sports forecasting and projections:
Never say never, but it's hard to see this one getting competitive, even after the Texans won and the Jaguars lost in Week 11. Houston needs another upset loss or two by Jacksonville. If that happens, remember Houston holds the head-to-head tiebreaker. That could turn up the heat.
CBS Sports forecasting and projections:
With Drake Maye out until the final week or two at best, it would take something catastrophic (basically a Josh Allen injury) for this to be an actual race. And then, Tommy DeVito trying to chase down Kyle Allen would be more sad than fun.

title: Sean McVay on Puka Nacua: 'Can't say for certain' what his Rams future will be amid pending free agency
summary: Nacua is set to hit free agency this offseason
full_text:
Los Angeles Rams wide receiver Puka Nacua is likely out for the remainder of the season after undergoing surgery for an MCL injury he sustained on the final offensive snap of the team's Week 9 victory over the Washington Commanders . Nacua is also set to be a free agent this coming offseason now that his rookie deal is set to expire, and Rams head coach Sean McVay delivered a mixed message about Nacua's future with the team.
"Yeah, we have a lot of guys that are free agents," McVay told reporters earlier this week. "What I've tried to really do is focus on right here, right now. He's obviously a guy that is a very important piece for us for now and for the future, but there are a lot of guys that fall under that category."
That makes it sound like Nacua will be back with the Rams, and there's not much to speculate about. But a later quote indicated there may not be as much certainty on that front, mostly because McVay said those words pretty much exactly.
"I can't say for certain anything," McVay said. "Here's what I'm not interested in: something being taken out of context because my focus and concentration are on a Friday practice, even though I know it's Monday. I am trying to see how well we can play as a team against an excellent opponent [the Green Bay Packers ] on Wednesday night.
"When you go through the amount of free agents that we have, Puka is a huge part of the conversation that you love, but there are also guys that are part of his draft class. There are guys on our offensive line, there are some guys defensively — so there are a lot of guys that are up that, as of right now, would not be under contract. There are mechanics that we'd like to be able to try to figure out how to keep these really good players and people that we love, and certainly Puka is at the forefront of our mind."
In addition to Nacua, the Rams have Kevin Dotson , Coleman Shelton , Steve Avila , Byron Young , Josh Wallace , Colby Parkinson , Davis Allen , Davante Adams , Omar Speights and Kobie Turner , among others, set to hit free agency this offseason. While the Rams' $75.2 million in projected cap space is the fifth-most in the league ( according to Over the Cap), that's a lot of players. Many of the Rams' pending free agents are significant contributors. However, none of them is nearly as integral to the team's success as Nacua is.
Nacua is the Rams' best offensive player. He is one of the best receivers in the league, and he's well on his way to being one of the best in recent memory if he can stay healthy. His 383 catches are the seventh-most all time through four seasons despite the fact that he's only played 3.5 years so far. His 4,906 receiving yards are the seventh-most as well. He's the all-time leader in receiving yards per game (96.2), and he's averged over 100 yards per game in each of the last two seasons.
But he's also somewhat unreliable from a health perspective, as a regular visitor to the medical tent and someone who will have missed 17 of the team's 51 games over the last three seasons by the time this year is up. And he's had very public off-field issues over the last year or so that resulted in a three-game suspension for violating the league's personal conduct policy. The league reportedly did not know Nacua needed season-ending surgery when it suspended him and allowed him to serve the suspension during his stint on injured reserve.
It wouldn't be surprising, then, if the Rams were at least somewhat hesitant to commit what it would take to secure a long-term contract. The best wide receivers in the league are making over $40 million per year. Jaxson Smith-Njigba averages $42.5 million per year on his extension. To lock Nacua in, it would likely take a deal that exceeds JSN's average annual value, given Nacua's track record.
Meanwhile, the franchise tag is projected to be worth "only" $30.91 million next season, according to Over the Cap, so that may be an option for the Rams to explore instead. That would allow them to retain Nacua for at least next season, even if they don't reach a long-term agreement, while also letting them negotiate an extension and retain the ability to explore potential trade opportunities if they decide they don't want to commit to him long term. And it seems like him not being around long-term is at least a possibility in the ether.
"Very uncertain, up in the air as it pertains to the future with the L.A. Rams because going into free agency he's got two different injuries, including a significant MCL injury that Sean McVay says will keep him out a few months," ESPN's Jeremy Fowler said this weekend . "Probably ends his tenure with the Rams — plus the three-game suspension for the off-field stuff this offseason, so it's just not the kind of way you want to go into free agency with momentum. On the field, he's the best free agent in 2027 of any player, so the Rams have got to sort that out."
Fowler may have misspoken when he said the injury probably ends Nacua's tenure with the Rams. Based on the rest of the quote, it seems like he meant that the injury will end Nacua's season with the Rams. But the idea that his future is uncertain at all is obviously notable, given how important he is to the team. If Nacua isn't going to be on the team, then the Rams don't have much to build their offense around in the future, whenever the post-Matthew Stafford era begins. They wouldn't exactly be setting Ty Simpson up for success if they decided to go that route.
Because Nacua is so good and so important to the Rams' offensive infrastructure, it seems likely they'll eventually come to an agreement on an extension. But the lack of certainty in that regard, both from McVay and in outside reporting, makes this situation one to watch.

title: Cardinals extend TE Elijah Higgins for three-years
summary: This is the time of year that in the NFL, if coaches and GMs want to keep players whose deals are about to expire, they begin doling out contract extensions. On Tuesday, the Arizona Cardinals gave TE Elijah Higgins a three-year $25 million extension that will keep him in-house through the 2028 season. This new […]
full_text: SEATTLE, WASHINGTON - NOVEMBER 08: Elijah Higgins #84 of the Arizona Cardinals runs the balla against Nick Emmanwori #3 of the Seattle Seahawks during the second quarter at Lumen Field on November 08, 2026 in Seattle, Washington. (Photo by Olivia Vanni/Getty Images) | Getty Images This is the time of year that in the NFL, if coaches and GMs want to keep players whose deals are about to expire, they begin doling out contract extensions. On Tuesday, the Arizona Cardinals gave TE Elijah Higgins a three-year $25 million extension that will keep him in-house through the 2028 season. This new Cardinals offense requires two and three tight ends, and Higgins fit the bill. RELATED: WHO IS NEXT ON THE CHOPPING BLOCK? The new deal has $17.087 million guaranteed plus a $1.5 million signing bonus. In addition, his 2028 salary has an injury guarantee of $6 million, workout bonuses, and annual per-game bonuses. Higgins’ (6’-3”, 235 pounds) production this year isn’t great. In fact, it isn’t even good. He has played in all 11 games with 7 starts, but his receiving numbers are pedestrian. He has 21 targets with 19 receptions for 166 yards, an 8.7 yards per catch average, has converted 8 first downs, scored a single TD, 0 rushes, 122 YAC numbers, and one drop. He has played on 319 snaps, or 44% of offensive plays. He also has 155 snaps on special teams. His cap hit this year is $4.1 million. That comes out to be $213,668 per reception so far this season. Of course, that will increase beginning next year. Currently, the Cardinals have Trey McBride, Higgins, Hunter Long, and Teagan Quitoriano in their tight end room. They also have Shawn Bowman and Kenny Yeboah on the practice squad and Tip Reiman on IR. This offense plays a lot of 12 and 13 personnel. Higgins is a Stanford graduate and was selected in the sixth round of the 2023 NFL Draft by the Miami Dolphins. He was a last day cut to which Arizona then claimed him off waivers and has been a roster member ever since. He is very durable and played in all 17 games the past two seasons. He has 802 career receiving yards with 4 touchdowns. Originally, Higgins was a wide receiver in college and then transitioned to tight end as he got bigger. He is quick and runs a 4.54 in the 40. He is just okay in in-line blocking but is willing, and is just average on contested balls. His forte is intermediate throws and is a physical runner once it’s in his hands. Like McBride, Higgins has a large route tree. The extension is a sign that the coaching staff is preparing for future seasons, and likes his play in the tight end group. On November 15, 2026, the Cardinals posted Higgins was their “2026 Salute to Service Award” nominee.

title: Another QB the Cardinals could be interested in
summary: The Arizona Cardinals have started four quarterbacks this year. The NFL record for the most in a single season is five, set by the 1987 New England Patriots and the 2023 Cleveland Browns. QB Gardner Minshew just completed successful surgery, and rookie Carson Beck’s back issues aren’t exactly solved. For now, it looks like journeyman […]
full_text: BALTIMORE, MD - NOVEMBER 05: Kedon Slovis #18 of the Baltimore Ravens attempts a pass before the game against the Jacksonville Jaguars at M&T Bank Stadium on November 5, 2026 in Baltimore, Maryland. (Photo by Scott Taetsch/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Arizona Cardinals have started four quarterbacks this year. The NFL record for the most in a single season is five, set by the 1987 New England Patriots and the 2023 Cleveland Browns. QB Gardner Minshew just completed successful surgery, and rookie Carson Beck’s back issues aren’t exactly solved. For now, it looks like journeyman Josh Johnson under center on game days. RELATED: CARDINALS SAID TO BE IN THE MIX FOR DANIEL JONES There has been speculation that former Indianapolis Colts signalcaller Daniel Jones just might be a target for the Cardinals. Jones made it known recently that he isn’t in any hurry to decide upon his next team. If he is looking for a team that needs a starter, then Arizona should be at the top of his list. There is another quarterback that has surfaced that the Cardinals might be interested in: Kedon Slovis. The #Ravens are waiving QB Kedon Slovis. They’d like to bring him back to the practice squad if he clears, though there are teams with QB needs, including his former team in the #AZCardinals . — Mike Garafolo (@MikeGarafolo) November 24, 2026 Slovis (6’-2”, 223 pounds) was in Cardinals training camp and played well in preseason games. He was a last day cut as Arizona kept just three quarterbacks: Minshew and Beck along with their Week 1 starter Jacoby Brissett. Slovis was picked up by the Green Bay Packers and signed to their practice squad. When the Baltimore Ravens started having QB issues, they claimed Slovis in early November to backup undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano. But then the Ravens traded for Brissett which made Slovis expendable. On Tuesday, Baltimore waived Slovis. The Ravens plan on signing him to their practice squad if he goes unclaimed. Yes, this isn’t huge news and isn’t going to rock the world of the Cardinals fanbase. But Slovis went through all the processes and mini-camps being taught this new offense. Johnson filled in adequately in the 34-7 loss to the Kansas City Chiefs, but had one day of practice. At least Slovis had spent time on this offense. Slovis played in 42 college games at USC, Pitt, and BYU and was named First Team All-Pac 12 in 2020. He finished with a 64.5% completion ratio and threw for 11,689 career yards with 80 touchdowns against 39 interceptions. He went undrafted in the 2024 NFL Draft and then was on the roster of the Indianapolis Colts and Houston Texans before being signed to the Cardinals practice squad in 2025. After Kyler Murray injured his ankle, the coaching staff elevated Slovis to the main roster where he sat behind Brissett for the remainder of the season, but was inserted into two games. To date, that is his only NFL experience.

title: With Rallis out, who is new Cardinals DC Teryl Austin?
summary: By now you have heard that the Arizona Cardinals first coaching casualty in this disaster of a season has been DC Nick Rallis. Most of the Cardinals fanbase has been questioning what took them so long to ax him. On Monday, the team made it official. In his place, head coach Mike LaFleur elevated assistant […]
full_text: Arizona Cardinals senior defensive assistant Teryl Austin walks the sidelines during their training camp red and white practice at State Farm Stadium in Glendale on Aug. 9, 2026. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co By now you have heard that the Arizona Cardinals first coaching casualty in this disaster of a season has been DC Nick Rallis. Most of the Cardinals fanbase has been questioning what took them so long to ax him. On Monday, the team made it official. Cardinals Fire Defensive Coordinator Nick Rallis https://t.co/x95mNSPv1a — Preme Football (@premefootball) November 23, 2026 In his place, head coach Mike LaFleur elevated assistant coach Teryl Austin to fill the position for the remainder of the 2026 schedule. RELATED: CARDINALS FIRE RALLIS AFTER ANOTHER BLOWOUT LOSS The Cardinals under Rallis had a boatload of issues. A lot of folks just thought he wasn’t qualified to run a complicated NFL defense and was in over his head. But LaFleur interviewed several candidates for the DC job and decided to retain Rallis. This defense just doesn’t have any consistency at all. Now, to be fair, Rallis lost his best pass defender in Will Johnson. One of this year’s best tacklers, S Andrew Wingard, is on season-ending IR. Rookie DT Kaleb Proctor was supposed to help anchor the middle of the defensive front and was also lost for the season. LB Jordan Burch was just added to IR. Other defenders on IR are DT Zachary Carter and S Joey Blount. Other defensive players have lost time as well with various injuries that they were able to get back to practices such as DT Walter Nolen. Perhaps if Rallis had all of these guys in every game, he would still be Arizona’s DC. Or maybe not. Great players make an average coach look pretty good. Bill Belichick without QB Tom Brady became just another coach that eventually was no longer their coach. After 11 games, Arizona sits at 3-8-0 in its regular spot in the basement of the NFC West Division. There are a lot of clubs with worst records, but winning just three contests in 11 games is still pretty bad. And their victories have been a cross section of the NFL’s landscape: Los Angeles Rams (6-4-0), Dallas Cowboys (5-6-0), and the Los Angeles Chargers (1-9-0). The past three games have been horrid, losing 34-7 to the Kansas City Chiefs, 34-6 to the Rams, and 17-3 to division foe Seattle Seahawks. The latter wasn’t as close as the score indicated as the Seahawks completely dominated the Cardinals. In all, Arizona has lost six games in which their opponent scored 30+ points, allowed the Cowboys to score 30 points in a win, and lost 45-21 to the Detroit Lions in Week 5. That is eight out of 11 games that the other team just kept scoring, and the Cardinals’ defense had no answer. As far as stats, Arizona is ranked #29 in pass defense and #28 in run defense. According the ESPN, they are the #26 overall ranked defense. They have allowed the highest number of passing TDs (25) and are #31 in passing yards per completion (8.4). This group has the worst passing rating and allowed the fifth most first down conversions via the pass (123). They have allowed 34 completions of 20+ yards and seven passing plays of 40+ yards. They are ranked #19 in sacks (22), #1 in total tackles (721), and #1 in tackle assists (357). Any defense that allows that many points will have high tackling numbers because the other team is on the field for the majority of the game. LB Mack Wilson leads the team in total tackles with 80, which is ranked #21 in the league. Why fire Rallis now? The Cardinals have six games left on the schedule. There are lots of starters on IR, some of them on the defensive side of the ball that aren’t coming back this season. So, why did LaFleur wait until this juncture to let Rallis go? They certainly aren’t going to the postseason this year. LaFleur stated: “Every decision that we make, that I make, I feel like is in the best interest for this organization. I just felt in my heart (Monday) morning that we needed a change. We needed a fresh perspective, a fresh voice.” The defense was just giving up too many points, and couldn’t stop the run. Only the Las Vegas Raiders have given up more points with 327 compared to Arizona’s 323. That’s 29.4 points a game on average. Changes to the defense won’t come at all this year. The Cardinals will have the second-most projected cap space in the offseason with six picks in the top four rounds of the 2027 NFL Draft. Even if all six go towards the defense, there is a developmental stage that must be adhered to. Look at first rounders DT Walter Nolen and DE Darius Robinson. Either of them tearing up the league? Right out of the gate, the Arizona defense was overhyped. In Week 2, the Cardinals were destroyed 31-7 by the Seattle Seahawks. There was only one sack, the Seahawks gained 162 yards on the ground, WR Jaxon Smith-Njigba had nine catches for 155 yards, Seattle converted six of 13 third downs, and were 3 for 5 in the Red Zone. Plus, the Seahawks scored three touchdowns and one field goal on their final four possessions. Early on, LaFleur defended Rallis. Then the injury bug hit and now backups are starters. LaFleur was basically boxed into a corner regarding the Rallis hire. After head coach Jonathan Gannon was fired, usually the next regime brings in his own guys, so everybody on the coaching staff is also fired. But LaFleur was hired very late because his Rams were playing in the NFC Championship Game. By the time LaFleur was looking to fill a staff, the DC candidates were picked over pretty good. Despite interviewing a few defensive coaches, in the end the Cardinals decided to retain Rallis who was entering the fourth year of his four-year deal he signed under Gannon. Basically, it was one less thing for LaFleur to be concerned about. Change of title So now, the Cardinals’ DC is Teryl Austin. He was hired this year with the title of Senior Defensive Assistant. He was the DC of the Pittsburgh Steelers from 2022-2025 and Senior Defensive Assistant from 2019-2021. Austin grew up in Sharon, Pennsylvania and attended Sharon High School. Playing safety at Sharon, Austin helped the Tigers go 10-1 overall and capture the first-ever Keystone League Championship in 1983. He then went to the University of Pittsburgh where he started three years at cornerback and played in 35 games. Austin led Pitt with seven interceptions and finished his career with 10 interceptions. He was also the primary punt returner for the Panthers and averaged 6.7 yards per return on 96 career returns. In his senior year, Pitt played in the Bluebonnet Bowl, a 32-27 loss. He went undrafted in the 1987 NFL Draft and signed with the Washington Redskins but was a training camp cut. Austin played for the Hamilton Tiger-Cats in the CFL for one season and the Montreal Machine with the WLAF in 1991. His first coaching position was as a grad assistant at Penn State in 1991. Two years later, he was hired by Wake Forest to coaching their defensive secondary along with Penn State assistant coach Jim Caldwell. He was also hired by Syracuse (1996-1998) and Michigan (1999-2002). In 2003, he landed the job of DB coach with the Seattle Seahawks under head coach Mike Holmgren, a position he held until 2006. During this time, the Seahawks won four division titles, one NFC championship, and lost in Super Bowl XL 21-10 to the Pittsburgh Steelers. In 2007, Austin was hired by the new head coach of the Cardinals, Ken Whisenhunt, to coach defensive backs. He stayed through the 2009 season helping the team reach Super Bowl XLIII. Under his tutelage, he coached three Pro Bowl defensive backs: S Antrel Rolle, CB Dominique Rodgers-Cromartie, and S Adrian Wilson. He was then employed by the University of Florida (DC), Baltimore Ravens (DB coach), Detroit Lions (DC), and Cincinnati Bengals (DC) before getting the Steelers gig. As stated, before being hired by LaFleur this offseason, Austin was the DC with Pittsburgh. His defensive rankings while with the…

title: Michael Penix’s fifth-year option is now a coin flip for the Falcons
summary: When Michael Penix earned NFC Offensive Player of the Week honors after Week 7, the debate over his future as the Atlanta Falcons’ franchise quarterback seemed settled. Yet a month later, the conversation has shifted entirely, with the pivotal decision over whether to exercise his fifth-year option before May 2027 looming. Back then, taking the […]
full_text: VALDEBEBAS, SPAIN - NOVEMBER 05: Michael Penix Jr. of Atlanta Falcons attends during the NFL Madrid 2026, week of game, between Atlanta Falcons and Cincinnati Bengals at Ciudad Deportiva Real Madrid on November 05, 2026, in Madrid, Spain. (Photo By Oscar J. Barroso/Europa Press via Getty Images) | Europa Press via Getty Images When Michael Penix earned NFC Offensive Player of the Week honors after Week 7, the debate over his future as the Atlanta Falcons’ franchise quarterback seemed settled. Yet a month later, the conversation has shifted entirely, with the pivotal decision over whether to exercise his fifth-year option before May 2027 looming. Back then, taking the option seemed a no-brainer; today, his recent skid and injury history make it a much more divisive gamble. Without a strong finish to 2026, the Falcons face the harsh reality of declining Penix’s option and turning 2027 into a make-or-break prove-it year. What the option costs for Atlanta Exercising Penix’s option fully guarantees his 2028 salary, whereas declining it puts him on track for unrestricted free agency after 2027. OverTheCap currently projects the base-tier quarterback option at roughly $25.7 million, an average of the third- through 25th-highest-paid passers over the past five seasons, since Penix can no longer reach the playing-time and Pro Bowl escalators required for higher tiers. Fortunately for Atlanta, the early-May deadline comes after both free agency and the 2027 NFL Draft, allowing head coach Kevin Stefanski and GM Ian Cunningham time to explore all their quarterback options before committing to Penix. The case for: Bryce Young’s blueprint Atlanta’s division rival Carolina has already paved the way by exercising Bryce Young’s $25.9 million option this past spring. Young showed year-over-year improvement, even if modest, giving Carolina reason to think the trend would continue with more time. Penix’s trendline isn’t as neat, thanks to his recent struggles , but if you remove his awful monsoon performance in Tampa , his numbers have improved slightly in several efficiency metrics, including completion rate and passer rating, compared to last year. There’s also significant financial advantage to picking up the option. If the Falcons decline Penix’s option and he plays well in 2027, they’d have to extend or use a franchise tag, set to increase from the $50 million projection in 2027. Picking up Penix’s option could save Atlanta roughly $25 million in cap space for 2028, giving Stefanski and Cunningham greater flexibility entering a pivotal third year. The case against: Anthony Richardson’s risk However, the decision isn’t as neat and tidy due to the complications of Penix’s injury history. Five season-ending injuries over the last eight years, dating back to his freshman year at Indiana, invite risk. If Penix suffers another serious injury setback in 2027 after exercising the option, the team would be on the hook for his full 2028 salary. Atlanta only needs to look at Young’s 2023 draft companion, Anthony Richardson, as a cautionary tale. The Indianapolis Colts declined Richardson’s option because frequent injuries kept the team from fully evaluating him. Richardson missed over 50 percent of games in his first two years, and another injury derailed his 2025 camp competition against Daniel Jones. Injuries have kept Penix out of 37 percent of the Falcons’ games over the past two seasons, impeding his development. Neither Atlanta nor its quarterback can afford another health setback. No middle ground left If Penix finishes 2026 healthy and sharp, trending up on the field, the Falcons will likely throw caution to the wind and pick up the option. Anything short of an emphatic finish, however, pushes the Falcons toward declining and using their projected $100 million in 2027 cap space to aggressively pursue competition, if not an outright replacement at quarterback this offseason. Right now, the decision feels like a coin flip. Over the next seven weeks, Penix will decide which side it lands on.
