title: Chicago Bears week 12 game preview: Detroit Lions Thanksgiving Day
summary: A clash of 8-2 teams to kick off Thanksgiving Day. This isn’t your run-of-the-mill early mid-2010s Detroit Lions-Chicago Bears matchups anymore. This game has significant weight in the NFC North battle and playoff seeding. Gone are the days of quarterbacks whose mere names elicit groans, first-round busts, offenses that are offensive in the bad way […]
full_text: CHICAGO, ILLINOIS - JANUARY 4: Jared Goff #16 of the Detroit Lions looks to throw during the second half of an NFL football game against the Chicago Bears at Solider Field on January 4, 2026 in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by Todd Rosenberg/Getty Images) | Getty Images A clash of 8-2 teams to kick off Thanksgiving Day. This isn’t your run-of-the-mill early mid-2010s Detroit Lions- Chicago Bears matchups anymore. This game has significant weight in the NFC North battle and playoff seeding. Gone are the days of quarterbacks whose mere names elicit groans, first-round busts, offenses that are offensive in the bad way and defenses that can’t stop a cold. No, this is a meeting of two great coaches and two outstanding quarterbacks, each with a bevvy of weapons lined up around them. This game is why our fanbases have endured all the bad, the jokes, the frustration. We’ve longed for the days when we could sit down and expect the team to win. To be in primetime games that made the collective NFL world say, “I can’t wait to watch the Lions-Bears game.” Thursday is that day. Now the Cowboys game is when you want to eat, because the games on the other side of it are the good ones. Enjoy this one. Win or lose, it should be a good one. The Bears badly need a division win. Detroit Lions SB Nation site: Pride of Detroit Record: 8-2, first in the NFC North Last week: 31-21 win against the Buccaneers Game day, time, TV: Thursday, noon CT, FOX Spread: Bears -1.5 Bears all-time record against: 105-82-5 Historical meetings: Sunday, Nov. 26, 1933, the 6-2-1 Bears hosted the 6-3 Portsmouth Spartans at Wrigley Field. Jack Manders kicked things off with a first-quarter field goal. Later in the quarter, Bill Hewitt threw a 34-yard pass to Bill Karr for a touchdown. The Spartans came back with Glenn Presnell hitting Ernie Caddel twice for touchdowns in the second quarter and again in the fourth. But the Bears would finish it off with a 29-yard Bronko Nagurski run to win 17-14. Last meeting: Week 18 last season. In a slugfest game, the Lions took a 16-0 lead on three field goals and a Jared Goff-to-Jahmyr Gibbs touchdown pass. The Bears woke up in the fourth quarter, with Caleb Williams hitting Jahdae Walker for a 25-yard score and converting a 2-point conversion on a Kyle Monangai run. Then, Williams hit Colston Loveland for another TD and converted the game-tying 2-point conversion with a pass to Cole Kmet. Kevin Byard picked off Goff on the next Lions’ drive, but the Bears took an intentional grounding penalty that set them back to third and 20. They ended up punting back to Detroit. The Lions moved the ball down the field and Jake Bates hit a walk-off 42-yard field goal for a 19-16 Detroit win. Injury report: The Lions listed four players on their estimated injury report for Tuesday. (The full game day report will be out later today, so stay tuned and we’ll share it later.) Limited S Chuck Clark (hamstring) Did not participate DT Skyler Gill-Howard (knee) – announced out for the season CB Ennis Rakestraw Jr. (shoulder) DE DJ Wonnum (back) Offense: The Lions offense comes in ranked fifth in points and third in yards. Detroit’s passing offense ranks fifth and their rushing offense ranks eighth. Jared Goff (67.8 pct cmp/2,716 yds/20 TD/4 INT) should probably be higher in MVP conversation than he is currently. He’s playing as well as Joe Burrow, Brock Purdy and Josh Allen. And he still has a great group of talent around him. Amon-Ra St. Brown (70 rec/792 yds./8 TD), TE Sam LaPorta (39/477/3), Jameson Williams (36/611/6) and Isaac TeSlaa (13/225/1) are making plays up and down the field. But the main weapon is Jahmyr Gibbs (222 att./1,098 yds./13 TD on the ground and 45/404/2 as a receiver). Gibbs leads the league in rushing attempts, yards, touchdowns and first downs. And in total touches and yards from scrimmage. He’s averaging 109.8 rushing yards per game and his 15 total TDs leads the league as well. Defense: Detroit’s defense has improved drastically throughout the season and enters the week 14th in points and 15th in yards allowed. Their passing defense ranks 27th, while their rushing defense ranks sixth. Without Aidan Hutchinson, D.J. Wonnum (7 sk/7 TFL10 QB hits/2 PD) is now the pass-rushing leader for Detroit. Alim McNeill (6.5 sk/7 TFL/12 QB hits/1 PD) and Derrick Moore (4.5 sk/4 TFL/8 QB hits) are just behind. Chuck Clark (61 tkls/2 TFL/4 PD/2 INT/2 FF) is their leading tackler and ballhawk. LB Derrick Barnes (49 tkls/6 TFL/4 QB hits/3 sk/1 INT/2 PD) is making plays all over the field. In the secondary Roger McCreary (42 tkls/11 PD/1 FF/1 INT/1 sk) and D.J. Reed (42 tkls/3 TFL/7 PD/1 INT) are trying to slow down opposing receivers. Key match ups: This is going to be a great game between two 8-2 teams and it’s really anyone’s guess what’s going to happen. The Bears have been playing like they’ve been waiting for this moment. The Lions have just become a rock-solid team, checking off opponents. This game is likely going to come down to the trenches. Can the Bears DL slow down Gibbs and pressure Goff? Can the Bears OL open running lanes for Swift and Monangai? Which QB will make the fewest mistakes? Chicago’s secondary is going to have its hands full with Amon-Ra St. Brown and Jameson Williams. If those guys get free, it could be a long afternoon. This game could be 45-43 or it could be 17-14, I really don’t know. Key stats Since their week six bye, the Lions defense has improved significantly. They allowed 404 yards per game over the first five games, but have allowed just 249 yards per game in the five games since. But the competition has shifted too. The first five game stretch included the Bills, Jacoby Brissett Cardinals and Panthers. Since the bye it’s been the pre-Kirk Vikings, Dolphins, Patriots (who lost Maye in the game) and Bucs. The Lions rank 28th in defensive takeaways with nine on the season. They have just two fumble recoveries and seven interceptions. Their offense has only turned the ball over seven times, which is the second fewest giveaways. The Bears have 19 giveaways, which is the fifth-most in the league. That includes nine lost fumbles by the offense, which is the third-most in the NFL. Chicago and Detroit are about even in plays per drive (fourth and third, respectively) at 6.3 (CHI) and 6.4 (DET). They are also about even in average drive time (3 minutes even for CHI, 2:58 for DET). The Bears have run the third-most plays in the league (714), while the Lions are 13th with 668. Despite having the league’s leading rusher and averaging nearly 110 yards per game by himself, the Lions rank 10th with 132.2 rushing yards per game, while the Bears are third with 142.4 yards per game as a team. Will the Bears win their first division game of season and get Ben Johnson a win over his mentor? What’s it going to take for Chicago to get the W?

title: Reviewing the Bears’ defensive PFN grades from Week 11 vs. Saints
summary: The Chicago Bears picked up a key win on Sunday, beating the Saints 21-13 to improve their record to 8-2. It wasn’t always pretty, but when you’re competing for a playoff spot in a loaded division like the NFC North, every win counts. As has been the case since the Bears traded for All-Pro defensive […]
full_text: CHICAGO, ILLINOIS - NOVEMBER 22: Tyler Shough #6 of the New Orleans Saints is pressured by Jeffery Simmons #99 of the Chicago Bears during the fourth quarter at Soldier Field on November 22, 2026 in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by Geoff Stellfox/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Chicago Bears picked up a key win on Sunday, beating the Saints 21-13 to improve their record to 8-2. It wasn’t always pretty, but when you’re competing for a playoff spot in a loaded division like the NFC North, every win counts. As has been the case since the Bears traded for All-Pro defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons, their defense was efficient yet again in their victory over New Orleans on Sunday. Any time you can hold an NFL team to just one touchdown over the course of an afternoon, it should be considered a good day, and Chicago got home against quarterback Tyler Shough to the tune of six sacks. Each week, I’ll review how Chicago’s eligible performers graded by Pro Football Network’s Impact Scoring model. Coming out of the bye week and picking up its fifth win in a row, here’s how Week 11 looked for the team by the numbers for the defense and special teams. Defense Montez Sweat: 85.2 (9th of 82 EDGEs) Austin Booker: 75.4 (23rd of 82 EDGEs) Jeffery Simmons: 93.1 (2nd of 86 DTs) Grady Jarrett: 70.0 (36th of 86 DTs) Neville Gallimore: 60.5 (63rd of 86 DTs) Jordan van den Berg: 60.4 (64th of 86 DTs) T.J. Edwards: 75.8 (30th of 74 LBs) Noah Sewell: 75.0 (32nd of 74 LBs) Devin Bush: 73.8 (37th of 74 LBs) Clark Phillips III: 83.8 (10th of 86 CBs) Tyrique Stevenson: 76.5 (33rd of 86 CBs) Jaylon Johnson: 69.2 (70th of 86 CBs) Dillon Thieneman: 93.3 (2nd of 71 SAFs) Cam Lewis: 76.7 (30th of 71 SAFs) As a unit, the Bears finished fifth among all 26 NFL teams that played in Week 11 with an 82.7 PFN Defense Impact grade. In particular, they finished in the top ten in such categories as takeaways, sacks, fewest explosive plays allowed, success rate allowed, EPA per play allowed, and drives allowed involving points scored. Finishing the game with four tackles and 3.0 sacks, it’s no surprise that Jeffery Simmons was a top performer by PFN Impact grading in Week 11. His 93.1 grade marked the second-highest grade he’s had all year, as well as the best grade he’s had in his three games with Chicago thus far. Alongside him on the defensive line, Montez Sweat had his most efficient game of the season with an 85.2 PFN EDGE Impact grade, two tackles for loss, and a sack. He has had three of his top four performances of the season after the Bears acquired Simmons, his former defensive line running mate at Mississippi State. The top performer on either side of the ball for the Bears was Dillon Thieneman, however. He finished Sunday off with seven tackles, one of which going for a loss, and an interception on the only pass that Saints quarterback Tyler Shough threw his way. Shough had more success throwing against Jaylon Johnson, who fell back down to Earth in Week 11 after leading the NFL in PFN CB Impact grading in Week 9 against the Buccaneers. Another notable top performer for the Bears’ defense against New Orleans was Clark Phillips III. The cornerback, whom Chicago acquired in the Gervon Dexter trade with the Falcons, had a sack and a forced fumble on Sunday. He also allowed just two catches for eight receiving yards in coverage, having been targeted four times, with an allowed passer rating of just 56.2. The Bears’ defensive tackle room was pretty thin outside of Simmons’ performance on Sunday, but a handful of starters performed at a solid enough level to keep the defense afloat. Special teams (for the sickos) Cairo Santos: 79.1 (12th of 23 Ks) Tory Taylor: 77.8 (14th of 23 Ps) Cairo Santos missed one of his two extra point attempts, but he nailed both of his field goal tries. He ended the game with +0.3 field goals over expected, hitting kicks from 41 and 35 yards out. Tory Taylor was also pretty average with his three punts against New Orleans, ranking No. 16 with 40.0 net yards per punt and No. 15 with +1.8 net yards per punt above expected.

title: Chicago Bears @ Detroit Lions: Week 12 Players to Watch
summary: As healthy as they’ve been all season, the Chicago Bears travel to Detroit for a Thanksgiving Day duel against the Lions in Week 12 for a chance to secure control of the NFC North and position themselves to compete for the NFC’s #1 seed. Some are calling it the biggest clash between these two rivals […]
full_text: DETROIT, MICHIGAN - NOVEMBER 22: A rear view of Jameson Williams #1, Jahmyr Gibbs #0 and Amon-Ra St. Brown #14 of the Detroit Lions after a touchdown against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers at Ford Field on November 22, 2026 in Detroit, Michigan. (Photo by Nic Antaya/Getty Images) | Getty Images As healthy as they’ve been all season, the Chicago Bears travel to Detroit for a Thanksgiving Day duel against the Lions in Week 12 for a chance to secure control of the NFC North and position themselves to compete for the NFC’s #1 seed. Some are calling it the biggest clash between these two rivals ever. Count me amongst that group! Both teams enter this week with an identical 8-2 record where Detroit has won 6 straight and Chicago 5 straight including 5 straight games played without trailing for a single minute since Caleb Williams has returned from injury. When you consider Ben Johnson has yet to beat his former team and his record against NFC North rivals, I am not sure there is a bigger game on the schedule than this week’s 1 p.m. EST Turkey Day slot. Let’s get to which players on both sides of the ball for Detroit that I will be keying in on at Ford Field. Offense: Jameson Williams, #0 – WR If you have been following this weekly series all season, I tend to highlight the oppositions deep threat as Chicago’s secondary has proven to be susceptible to such weapons. Both unheralded but blazing WRs in Tez Johnson for Tampa and Jahan Dotson for Atlanta proved to be big-play weapons against Chicago’s secondary earlier this season, and neither is as lethal as Jameson Williams for Detroit. Averaging 17 yards per reception throughout his career, Williams average against Chicago in his seven games against them is at 19.9 yards per reception. The speedster out of Alabama is the perfect complement to the dominant Jahmyr Gibbs at RB (leading the league in scrimmage yards), and the consistently productive Amon-Ra St. Brown (top 5 in catches and TDs and top 10 in yards) as offenses are forced to focus on those two. All it takes is for one miscommunication on the backend for Williams to find himself behind the secondary for a backbreaking play. I expect rookie Dillon Thieneman and his 4.35 forty time to be responsible for the deep ball this week, but if Detroit can scheme up a play or two where Thieneman is sucked up into the fray, watch out for Williams to break free deep as there is not a single cornerback on the Bears roster that can run with him. If Chicago can stymie Williams at the line and keep contain over the top, they should keep this game within reach for Caleb Williams and Co. to keep pace. If not, the Bears defense will struggle to stop anything as the deep ball will just open things up for Gibbs and ARSB. Defense: Chuck Clark, #36 – S Truth be told, I am typically drawn to the MLB position and have even highlighted Lions MLB Jack Campbell on this article series multiple times in the past. That said, I am a huge fan of his replacement, Malcolm Rodriguez, and absolutely feel he can make an impact on this game. But the more I study Detroit’s team this year, the more I am drawn to the veteran Clark in his first season with the team. Clark has recently been awarded as team captain and has continued to see the lions share of snaps at Safety even with the return of former All-Pros and/or Pro Bowlers Brian Branch and Kerby Joseph. Yes , Clark’s heady presence has absolutely been rock-steady for Detroit, but the 10th year pro is having a career year from a production standpoint as well. In 10 games, Clark has already matched or exceeded career highs in interceptions, sacks and forced fumbles. If Clark continues to play sound, dependable, and impactful play from his safety spot, the Chicago passing game won’t have as much room to operate and will struggle to keep pace with the Lions offense. But if Chicago can get their players the ball in space to allow the team speed to shine, Clark and the Detroit defense will have a hard time slowing down the Bears. What about you? Which players for Detroit outside of Gibbs and Amon-Ra will you be focused on this week? Or does it all come down to slowing Gibbs for you?

title: Reviewing the Bears’ offensive PFN grades from Week 11 vs. Saints
summary: The Chicago Bears picked up a key victory on Sunday, defeating the Saints 21-13 to improve their record to 8-2 for the year. It wasn’t always pretty, but when you’re competing for a playoff spot in a loaded division like the NFC North, every win counts. After their bye week, the Bears had the luxury […]
full_text: CHICAGO, ILLINOIS - NOVEMBER 22: Zavion Thomas #13 of the Chicago Bears reacts after a 30 yard run in the second quarter of the game against the New Orleans Saints at Soldier Field on November 22, 2026 in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by John Fisher/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Chicago Bears picked up a key victory on Sunday, defeating the Saints 21-13 to improve their record to 8-2 for the year. It wasn’t always pretty, but when you’re competing for a playoff spot in a loaded division like the NFC North, every win counts. After their bye week, the Bears had the luxury of having running back Kyle Monangai return healthy to the lineup in Week 11, though their run game was still plenty lackluster. A very strong start to the game helped them create a lead that proved to be insurmountable, even though their second half performance felt at times like they wanted to be surmounted. Each week, I’ll review how Chicago’s eligible performers graded by Pro Football Network’s Impact Scoring model. Coming out of the bye week and picking up its fifth win in a row, here’s how Week 11 looked for the team by the numbers. Offense Caleb Williams: 76.7 (10th of 26 QBs) D’Andre Swift: 72.0 (28th of 37 RBs) Kyle Monangai: 67.6 (35th of 37 RBs) Zavion Thomas: 76.5 (17th of 62 WRs) Rome Odunze: 74.0 (25th of 62 WRs) Luther Burden III: 66.9 (57th of 62 WRs) Kalif Raymond: 66.9 (58th of 62 WRs) Colston Loveland: 75.6 (11th of 31 TEs) Theo Benedet: 78.6 (21st of 54 OTs) Joe Thuney: 79.7 (14th of 56 OGs) Garrett Bradbury: 79.7 (16th of 26 Cs) Jonah Jackson: 74.2 (40th of 56 OGs) Darnell Wright: 89.2 (2nd of 54 OTs) Based solely off of Week 11 production, the Bears finished with the No. 16 offense in the NFL among the 26 teams that played, tallying a 72.4 PFN Offense Impact grade as a unit. Their -0.05 EPA per play also ranked No. 16 in the league this past week, while their explosive play rate of 6.8% came in No. 19 overall. It wasn’t a bad performance from Caleb Williams, who still graded as an above-average starter in the win over the Saints. His solid 65.2% completion percentage certainly surpassed expectations given the circumstances he faced from a pressure and separation perspective, as his +8.0 completion percentage over expected ranked fifth in the NFL this past week. It wasn’t his best game by any stretch, but he still was efficient operating Chicago’s offense, all things considered. Big plays from Zavion Thomas helped get the Bears into favorable situations, as the rookie wide receiver had a 40-yard catch and a 30-yard run against New Orleans. He and Rome Odunze graded particularly well, as Odunze caught all four of his targeted passes for 45 yards. Colston Loveland also had a good grade, catching three passes for 29 yards and a touchdown, as well as placing in the top 12 among tight ends with a 75.3 blocking grade. From a receiving EPA perspective, though, both Kalif Raymond and Luther Burden finished in the bottom six among 62 qualified wide receivers with -2.56 EPA and -2.04 EPA, respectively. Inconsistency in the run game hurt the Bears, as D’Andre Swift and Kyle Monangai each averaged just 3.9 and 2.3 yards per carry, respectively. Garrett Bradbury finished with a relatively average ranking among centers in Week 11, while Jonah Jackson finished with his third-lowest grade in a single game this year in the ten games he has played. However, Joe Thuney and Theo Benedet both ended the Saints game with rankings reflecting that of above-average starters, while Darnell Wright continued playing at his All-Pro level.

summary: Yesterday, someone shared on social media (no, I won’t elevate their account here) that the Chicago Bears had a dire salary cap situation looming in 2027. It’s not the biggest account, and it’s not even a sports-related account, but it picked up a bunch of traction as others shared it. Some believed the erroneous content […]
full_text: CHICAGO, ILLINOIS - SEPTEMBER 28: General manager Ryan Poles of the Chicago Bears walks the field prior to the game against the Philadelphia Eagles at Soldier Field on September 28, 2026 in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by Patrick McDermott/Getty Images) | Getty Images Yesterday, someone shared on social media (no, I won’t elevate their account here) that the Chicago Bears had a dire salary cap situation looming in 2027. It’s not the biggest account, and it’s not even a sports-related account, but it picked up a bunch of traction as others shared it. Some believed the erroneous content and complained the Bears were screwed or wanted to lol at the stupid Bears, while others wanted to dunk on how wrong the take was. A prominent gambling account (I won’t elevate this account either) picked up on the narrative and, to gain clicks and engagement, shared their own version of the “oh no, the Bears are in cap Hell in 2027!” tweet to all their followers too. For those not on social media, Bears fans are an easy mark. And that’s not meant negatively; our fanbase is very, very active and passionate, and if you want to bait us or troll us, you’re going to get a reaction. ESPN’s Field Yates, who knows a thing or two about the NFL and the salary cap, came across that above-referenced tweet and shared , “I don’t know why this notion that the Bears are facing salary cap straits in 2027 has generated traction recently, but it’s… not true. There are so many pathways for this team to easily clear cap room next year. And extend Caleb Williams.” Nick Korte, who is a contributor at Over the Cap and one of the best follows for salary cap and comp pick info, responded to Yates with this . Simple restructures of the 5 players who the Bears have already devoted guaranteed salaries to in 2027 gets them in salary cap compliance without doing anything else. And the Bears have the 2nd highest availability in cap dollars in 2028 right now. Stay chill, Bears fans. So even though Chicago’s cap looks tight in 2027, and Caleb’s extension will be a big one , there’s nothing to worry about. “Stay chill, Bears fans.”

title: Are you confident in the Chicago Bears’ offense?
summary: Welcome to SB Nation Reacts, a survey of fans across the NFL. Throughout the year, we ask questions of the most plugged-in Bears fans and fans across the country. When you have a goal to be the most prolific offense of all time — which just about every team does, even if they don’t say […]
full_text: CHICAGO, IL - NOVEMBER 22: Chicago Bears head coach Ben Johnson looks on during the NFL game between the New Orleans Saints and the Chicago Bears on November 22, 2026, at Soldier Field in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by Michael Allio/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Welcome to SB Nation Reacts, a survey of fans across the NFL. Throughout the year, we ask questions of the most plugged-in Bears fans and fans across the country. When you have a goal to be the most prolific offense of all time — which just about every team does, even if they don’t say it out loud — you’re bound to be criticized when the offense isn’t hitting on all cylinders, but even if the Chicago Bears’ offense isn’t reaching that lofty standard they strive for, it’s still been pretty good. Yes, despite what you may think, Chicago’s offense has been pretty good; still top 10 in many metrics. However, it hasn’t been as good as most expected at this point in the season. Head coach Ben Johnson isn’t satisfied with his offense’s efficiency or production either. He’s particularly down on his running game, something he again said is a point of emphasis this week. “It’s a commitment to the principles that we have,” he said today when asked how they get better. “There is a lot that can happen in a season. The more you emphasize it, the better it gets.” In Sunday’s win over the Saints, the Bears had 146 yards on the ground, their third-most in a game this season and their best since Week 4. It wasn’t as efficient as he’d like, but it’s a start in the right direction. The offense has plenty of room to improve, but any narrative that it’s been bad is just doom-and-gloom negativity for the sake of being negative. The Bears are tenth in offensive DVOA (Defense-adjusted Value Over Average), and just outside the top 10 in EPA (Expected Points Added), at number 11. Chicago’s offense is eighth in scoring, eighth in yards, first in plays, first in average time per drive, seventh in average points per drive, and seventh in average yards per drive, but the inconsistency shows up in the percentage of drives ending in a score, where the Bears rank 26th, and in the percentage of drives ending with a turnover, where the Bears are 19th. title: Bengals Film Room: Joe Burrow has an uneven performance on MNF
summary: The Cincinnati Bengals lost 22-20 against the Washington Commanders on Monday Night Football this week. Joe Burrow made some special Joe Burrow plays during the game, throwing for 300 receiving yards with 2 touchdowns and 0 interceptions. However, Burrow was also sacked 3 times, had several near interceptions, and missed some wide-open targets that we […]
full_text: The Cincinnati Bengals lost 22-20 against the Washington Commanders on Monday Night Football this week. Joe Burrow made some special Joe Burrow plays during the game, throwing for 300 receiving yards with 2 touchdowns and 0 interceptions. However, Burrow was also sacked 3 times, had several near interceptions, and missed some wide-open targets that we are accustomed to seeing him find. It is hard to criticize a talent like Burrow, but if you are going to tout someone as an MVP candidate, you expect them to play like one. It isn’t just the fans that have placed high expectations on Burrow and the Bengals, but it is Joe Burrow himself. When Burrow made the statement that this team reminded him of his National Championship season with LSU, that set the expectations for what this team is hoping to achieve. If they want that to happen, they need Joe Burrow to make the big plays in the biggest moments. Unfortunately, we did not see enough of that during the Bengals’ last few possessions of the game. Let’s take a look at some of the good and bad from Joe Burrow’s performance. Early in the game, it felt like Washington was bringing pressure that the Bengals and Burrow were not prepared to handle. After taking the ball early, the Bengals could not get anything going. They went 3-and-out on their opening series. The very first play of the game was a sack, which was an ominous sign of things to come on this night. Burrow sacked on the first play of the game was an ominous sign of things to come offensively. pic.twitter.com/K5KfoyRleZ — Bengals & Brews (@BengalsBrews) November 24, 2026 Good thing we took the ball first pic.twitter.com/i17SycjfGZ — Bengals & Brews (@BengalsBrews) November 24, 2026 The Bengals’ second drive of the game didn’t go much better than the first one. Burrow threw a couple of near interceptions before the Bengals ultimately were forced to punt the ball back to Washington. This drive ended up going -6 yards. So after two series, the offense had -6 yards after electing to take the ball first in a downpour. I don’t quite understand that decision still. One of a few Burrow passes that could have been picked off pic.twitter.com/StxP3wYvvg — Bengals & Brews (@BengalsBrews) November 24, 2026 Another one https://t.co/b7PE5lRK34 pic.twitter.com/F15x3Wg0HA — Bengals & Brews (@BengalsBrews) November 24, 2026 The Bengals started to find a little success on their third drive of the game. They got the ball near midfield after gaining 27 yards, 17 of which came on a good scramble by Joe Burrow before finding Samaje Perine out in the flat. The drive would ultimately stall out after the Bengals went for it on 4th down. It looked like Burrow was the one who decided to take the ball to the outside, but Frankie Luvu stoned him for no gain on the play, forcing a turnover on downs. Perine would have an even bigger gain here if he doesn’t fumble the ball pic.twitter.com/9WtqZZZWcK — Bengals & Brews (@BengalsBrews) November 24, 2026 Frankie Luvu stops Joe Burrow on 4th down for the turnover on downs pic.twitter.com/KNF6c9GGLE — Bengals & Brews (@BengalsBrews) November 24, 2026 After the defense forced a three-and-out, the Bengals offense were able to finally put together a drive. They marched 71 yards that included some key receptions by tight ends Jack Endries and Mike Gesicki. The drive was kept alive with a phenomenal 4th down pass from Joe Burrow to Mike Gesicki. The Bengals ultimately settled for a field goal on the drive. Jack Endries with his first of four catches on the night for Cincinnati pic.twitter.com/tlUdfuYUjr — Bengals & Brews (@BengalsBrews) November 24, 2026 Hell of a 4th down conversion from Joe Burrow to Mike Gesicki pic.twitter.com/vpKFS9gFS3 — Bengals & Brews (@BengalsBrews) November 24, 2026 Burrow was sacked three times on the night, but I thought he had pretty good protection overall. The Commanders sent a lot of blitzes throughout the game, and those were handled well for the most part. Some of the sacks were just Joe Burrow holding on to the ball way too long. Burrow was sacked 3 times, and there is no blaming the offensive line on this one. pic.twitter.com/yeUI0to6xp — Bengals & Brews (@BengalsBrews) November 24, 2026 The Bengals were able to overcome that sack, though, because they hit Samaje Perine for a big gain on 3rd down. Burrow did a great job stepping up in the pocket and extending the play long enough for Perine to break up across the middle. Perine was able to do the rest on a 44-yard gain. Two plays later, Burrow hit Tee Higgins down the sideline for the Bengals’ first touchdown of the night, going up 10-0. Joe Burrow to Samaje Perine for the big gain to help setup the Bengals first touchdown of the night. pic.twitter.com/o2utrGeEy2 — Bengals & Brews (@BengalsBrews) November 24, 2026 Burrow to Higgins for the touchdown pic.twitter.com/MUMGMtkOrF — Bengals & Brews (@BengalsBrews) November 24, 2026 I thought Burrow’s best throw of the night came on the Bengals opening series of the second half. After the Commanders had tied things up at 10-10, the Bengals put together a 66-yard drive of their own. That included the aforementioned throw of the night from Joe Burrow to Mike Gesicki for 19 yards. It later ended with Colbie Young getting his first career touchdown. Now this is the good stuff from Joe Burrow. Phenomenal play to avoid the pressure, step up in the pocket, and layer the throw perfectly to Mike Gesicki. pic.twitter.com/xHf3HxQ0Uo — Bengals & Brews (@BengalsBrews) November 24, 2026 Joe Burrow extending the play and finding Colbie Young in the end zone for his first career touchdown reception in the NFL. pic.twitter.com/LVab2j2UZO — Bengals & Brews (@BengalsBrews) November 24, 2026 While there were plays that Joe missed, there were also plays where his teammates let him down. Chase Brown had multiple drops, while Tee Higgins had one of his own. After the Commanders cut the lead to 17-13, Burrow was unable to connect with Ja’Marr Chase deep. This put the Bengals defense right back on the field after going three-and-out. The Bengals had 3 drops. 2 by Chase Brown and this one by Tee Higgins. pic.twitter.com/rp9bYK9Lcl — Bengals & Brews (@BengalsBrews) November 24, 2026 Burrow unable to connect with Chase on the deep ball and the Bengals go 3-and-out with a 17-13 lead. pic.twitter.com/6vBdpKQk4Y — Bengals & Brews (@BengalsBrews) November 24, 2026 On the Bengals’ next drive, they managed to only get one first down. They put the defense once again right back on the field against a Commanders defense they were struggling to stop. This drive featured a Burrow miss to Chase Brown, and then a Chase Brown drop. The final play of the drive was an offense that seemed to be losing some confidence, as they threw a screen for just 3 yards to Ja’Marr Chase on 3rd and 10. The Bengals would punt the football and come back on the field next down 19-17. Burrow with the inaccurate pass to Chase Brown, Chase Brown with the drop, and a screen to Ja’Marr Chase that only goes 3 yards forces the Bengals to punt with now just a 17-16 lead. pic.twitter.com/XI8qs2g2JS — Bengals & Brews (@BengalsBrews) November 24, 2026 On the Bengals’ final possession, things started out really well. First, Burrow hit Tee Higgins for a 12-yard completion before the 2-minute warning. On the other side of the two-minute warning, Burrow was able to find Mike Gesicki for a 32-yard reception. Burrow to Gesicki for 32 yards on the Bengals final drive of the game. pic.twitter.com/HmDk9KVE5v — Bengals & Brews (@BengalsBrews) November 24, 2026 Then, we almost saw an unthinkable turnover while in field goal range on a pass from Joe Burrow to Ja’Marr Chase. The Bengals got another attempt, and this time Joe Burrow held the football too long and took a sack to make the field goal much more difficult. Ultimately, the field goal was made from 56 yards by Evan McPherson, but the defense crapped their pants once again in allowing another field goal to end it for the Washington…

title: 3 Bengals legends still alive in Pro Football Hall of Fame race for Class of 2027
summary: It’s that time of year again, Cincinnati Bengals fans. The turkey’s thawing, the Bengals are in the thick of the stretch run, and we’re once again refreshing our feeds to see if Canton is finally ready to give Cincinnati its due. On Tuesday, the Pro Football Hall of Fame trimmed its Class of 2027 player […]
full_text: It’s that time of year again, Cincinnati Bengals fans. The turkey’s thawing, the Bengals are in the thick of the stretch run, and we’re once again refreshing our feeds to see if Canton is finally ready to give Cincinnati its due. On Tuesday, the Pro Football Hall of Fame trimmed its Class of 2027 player pool down to 52 names, and three familiar stripes are still on the board: quarterback Ken Anderson, offensive tackle Willie Anderson, and defensive tackle Geno Atkins. If you’re wondering why Ken Anderson’s name is showing up on the same list as Ben Roethlisberger and Rob Gronkowski, it’s because this is a whole new ballgame. Back in September, the Hall announced the biggest overhaul of its selection process in its history. The separate seniors category is gone, so every eligible player, no matter when he retired, is now in one pool. The selection committee was cut roughly in half, to 25 voters plus three non-voting participants. And the final ballot now has room for only 13 players, joining one coach and one contributor. Those two spots already belong to Bill Belichick and Robert Kraft, by the way. Fifty-two players advanced in the voting process for the Pro Football Hall of Fame Class of 2027. pic.twitter.com/D9ghxinYTu — Adam Schefter (@AdamSchefter) November 24, 2026 The 52 will be cut to 25 in about two weeks. The final 13 will then go into the room ahead of Super Bowl LXI, with the class revealed at NFL Honors in February. For the Bengals, the stakes are pretty simple. This franchise still has just two career players enshrined in Canton: Anthony Muñoz and Ken Riley. That’s the fewest in the league. Let’s look at the three men trying to change that. Ken Anderson: The wait that won’t end The résumé hasn’t changed, and it never needed to. Anderson spent all 16 of his NFL seasons in Cincinnati. He won four NFL passing titles, was the 1975 NFL Man of the Year, and took home league MVP honors in 1981 while leading the Bengals to their first Super Bowl. He’s still the franchise’s all-time leader in passing yards, and he remains the only eligible quarterback with four passing titles who isn’t in the Hall. The path to Canton has been a long, winding, and frankly maddening one. Anderson was a finalist back in 1996 and 1998, then fell into the seniors pool, where he reached the semifinals four straight years. Last cycle, he finally broke through as one of three senior finalists for the Class of 2026, only to come up short in a year when voters were also weighing Belichick and Kraft. Now, with the seniors category scrapped, Anderson doesn’t have to wait for a small committee to pick him. But he also has to beat out every modern-era candidate on the list for one of those 13 spots. There’s real momentum behind him, though. Even Joe Montana, the guy who beat him in Super Bowl XVI, has publicly said Anderson’s call is long overdue. Kenny for Canton, folks. Willie Anderson: Knocking on the door, again “Big Willie” was the anchor of the Bengals’ offensive line for 12 seasons (1996-2007) before a final year in Baltimore. He made 184 career starts and earned three first-team All-Pro nods, and he did it at right tackle, at a time when that position rarely got that kind of recognition. He was one of the most dominant run-blockers of his era, and he did it for a lot of bad Bengals teams. The frustrating part is that Willie has been about as close as you can get without walking through the door. He’s been a finalist five years in a row and made the final seven for the Class of 2026. Under the old bylaws, that would have made him an automatic finalist for 2027. The new rules wiped that safety net away, so he has to earn his way back to the final 13 from scratch, alongside a loaded crop of first-time eligibles. If there’s any silver lining, it’s that voters clearly already know his case. Getting back into the room is the hurdle. Getting the votes once he’s there feels like it’s been a matter of when, not if. Geno Atkins: The newest name in the mix This is the one that should get Bengals fans excited, because it’s new. Atkins was a fourth-round pick (No. 120 overall) out of Georgia in the 2010 NFL Draft, and he turned into one of the best interior pass rushers of his generation. Over 11 seasons, all in Cincinnati, he piled up 75.5 sacks from the defensive tackle spot. He made eight Pro Bowls, earned two first-team All-Pro selections, and was named to the Hall of Fame’s All-Decade Team of the 2010s. That last one matters, because All-Decade nods tend to carry real weight with voters. Along with Aaron Donald, Fletcher Cox, and Gerald McCoy in a similar era, Atkins helped redefine the interior defensive line position and its importance to franchise success. At his peak, Atkins was a nightmare. He was undersized by traditional standards, but his first step and leverage made him nearly unblockable from the 3-technique. He posted a monster 12.5-sack season in 2012 before a torn ACL in 2013 derailed things for a stretch, and he came roaring back to re-establish himself as one of the league’s most disruptive interior linemen through the back half of the decade. For a good chunk of the 2010s, Geno and Aaron Donald were the conversation at defensive tackle. Atkins last played in 2020, which made him eligible for the first time with the Class of 2026. Eligible and noticed aren’t the same thing, though. Last year he didn’t make the Hall’s initial cut to 52, let alone the semifinals. Plenty of folks, including longtime voter Rick Gosselin, have pointed to the lack of postseason success and a ring as the biggest knock on his case. So simply making the 52 this time around is a genuine step forward. Atkins may have a tough time getting into Canton this year, but his resume is definitely Canton-worthy. The bottom line Three Bengals in the final 52 is a good day. The next cut to 25 is where things get real, and the new single-pool format makes it tougher than ever to predict who survives. Ken has the momentum, Willie has the familiarity, and Geno finally has his foot in the door.

title: Bengals News: Playoff projections for Cincinnati
summary: The Cincinnati Bengals are still more likely to host a playoff game than not, but their chances at earning home-field advantage in the AFC throughout the playoffs took a hit after they lost by a score of 22-20 to the Washington Commanders on Monday Night Football. Still, were you to tell me before the season […]
full_text: The Cincinnati Bengals are still more likely to host a playoff game than not, but their chances at earning home-field advantage in the AFC throughout the playoffs took a hit after they lost by a score of 22-20 to the Washington Commanders on Monday Night Football. Still, were you to tell me before the season started the Bengals would be 7-3 heading into Thanksgiving weekend, I would have been thrilled. The Bengals’ current odds to make the playoffs sit at 97%, and their odds of hosting a playoff game and winning the AFC North are still at 82%, according to A to Z Sports’ John Sheeran . Their odds of earning the top seed in the conference, though, fell to 6%. Hopefully the Bengals can bounce back against the Saints on Sunday. Here’s what else is going on: Zac Taylor’s controversial final-drive call in Bengals’ loss to Commanders was right no matter the outcome “Trying to get a first down to win it,” Taylor told reporters. “That way the walk-off field goal would win the game for us, make them use their timeouts, go get that last first down so we can walk off with a field goal. That was the objective.” Bengals-Commanders clock error brings back memories of Steelers-Chargers clock error in 2015 “The game clock is not subject to instant replay review unless there is a timing issue on the last play of the first half or the last play of the game. title: 3 things we learned from the Bengals’ upset loss to the Commanders
summary: There are two ways of looking at the Cincinnati Bengals’ upset loss to the Washington Commanders: 1. it was a nightmare of a game where everything that could go wrong did; 2. it was a wakeup call for a team that isn’t quite the contender many thought it was. For the sake of education, we’ll […]
full_text: Photo by Patrick Smith/Getty Images | Getty Images There are two ways of looking at the Cincinnati Bengals’ upset loss to the Washington Commanders: 1. it was a nightmare of a game where everything that could go wrong did; 2. it was a wakeup call for a team that isn’t quite the contender many thought it was. For the sake of education, we’ll go with the second one. Here’s what we learned: The Bengals’ offense isn’t playoff-ready yet The postseason is physical, gritty, and nasty. It’s when high-powered offenses look mortal because of bad weather, higher stakes, and greater familiarity with playbooks and tendencies. Well, the Bengals got a glimpse of what their team looks like when things aren’t going their way, on the road against a flawed roster with a losing record. And they failed the test miserably. Zac Taylor wasn’t prepared to shift his focus to the running game or get his players’ heads back into the game when they looked shell-shocked from the Commanders’ energy and ferocity. Worst of all, Taylor completely botched the end of the game, when he decided to continue passing, even after the Bengals were easily in field goal range, thus leaving time on the clock for Washington. But Joe Burrow doesn’t get off the hook. He threw multiple passes that could’ve been picked off early and a near pick on that final drive. The Bengals were the classic example of the team that has everything going its way and forgets that winning football games requires a sense of urgency and intense focus every single week, despite the disparity in talent with the opponent. The d-line can only cover for the secondary for so long Boye Mafe, Dexter Lawrence, and the Bengals d-line was amazing early in the game and solid against the pass throughout. It seemed like the secondary was shutting down Jayden Daniels as well. But the reality was that they didn’t get much of a fight from Washington’s offense until late in the first half. When Cincinnati needed a stop in the defensive backfield on the Commanders’ final drive with under a minute left, the secondary caved completely, allowing 64 yards on two pass plays. The o-line still needs to work on blitz pickup Washington blitzed more than 80 percent of the time using a sophisticated scheme, and it caught Cincinnati’s o-line off guard. This after a week in which even the national media started to recognize that the Bengals’ o-line is top tier. Burrow commented , “They were sending it, for sure.” And Ted Karras said that the first quarter was a problem for them. “We were a bit exasperated,” the center said . The breakthrough, just like in that first AFC Championship game against the Kansas City Chiefs, came on a short pass to Samaje Perine that the big running back took a long distance. The Bengals need to figure that stuff out early and not stick to their guns when Burrow isn’t getting the kind of pockets he needs to pick apart defenses.

title: AFC North’s changing of the guard from Steelers/Ravens to Bengals/Browns happening fast
summary: For years- really, decades- the AFC North has seen the Cleveland Browns in the basement, with the Baltimore Ravens and Pittsburgh Steelers running the show. The Cincinnati Bengals have had windows of time when they join the top two, but they haven’t had the kind of consistency that the others have. The Browns have been […]
full_text: For years- really, decades- the AFC North has seen the Cleveland Browns in the basement, with the Baltimore Ravens and Pittsburgh Steelers running the show. The Cincinnati Bengals have had windows of time when they join the top two, but they haven’t had the kind of consistency that the others have. The Browns have been consistently bad, with just a couple of playoff appearances and no AFC North titles . Things have started to change during the 2026 NFL season, with Cincinnati and Cleveland at the top of the division, even if Pittsburgh had the same 6-4 record as the second-place team. Baltimore has fallen off without Lamar Jackson . Now, with the news of the Steelers benching Aaron Rodgers late on Tuesday night, after he practiced as the team’s starter the first two days of the week, the bloom seems to be off in Mike McCarthy’s first year. As our Producer at Behind the Steel Curtain said, Pittsburgh needs to reset everything in order to rebuild: It’s easy to say now, but they should have gotten rid of all the Tomlin guys. They were always going to have that “well Mike T wouldn’t have done this” about them. It’s a spoiled group. https://t.co/Q8MtftMykE — Jarrett Bailey (@JBaileyNFL) November 25, 2026 The Ravens may be looking at a similar turnover with Jackson’s contract at a point where the team either needs to try to extend him (something they’ve tried and failed to do), trade him, or release him this offseason. Given Jackson’s price tag, injury history, and limited playoff success, Baltimore’s future may not include their MVP-winning quarterback. There are many around Baltimore and Pittsburgh’s fanbases who are hoping that Jesse Minter and McCarthy are one-and-done coaches, whereas Cincinnati’s Zac Taylor was the one holdover in the division, and Todd Monken has had a positive start to his tenure in Cleveland. With the Bengals having stability at quarterback, an offensive line coming together well, great weapons on offense, and a defense coming together well, Cincinnati might be the cream of the crop in the AFC North for a few seasons. The Browns could be close behind, with a young, exciting roster of talented players all over the roster, extra draft picks over the next couple of years, and a coach who is making everything work ahead of schedule. By the time the next decade starts, we could be looking back at the 2026 NFL season as the time that the changing of the guard in the AFC North was fast-tracked, with the State of Ohio on top for a number of years. When you look at the AFC North, do you think the Bengals and Browns will takeover in the same way the Ravens and Steelers have for so many years? title: Browns’ home-field advantage could be on display on Sunday Night Football vs. the Raiders
summary: The dedication of the Cleveland Browns fan base has been a huge advantage for the players on the field throughout the team’s history. The fans do a great job of cheering the team on while also making it a challenging environment for opposing teams.  The Browns are 4-0 at home so far this season, and […]
full_text: The dedication of the Cleveland Browns fan base has been a huge advantage for the players on the field throughout the team’s history. The fans do a great job of cheering the team on while also making it a challenging environment for opposing teams. The Browns are 4-0 at home so far this season, and the team had a game-winning fourth-quarter drive in each of those victories. While on-field performance is certainly the main factor in these wins, it cannot be overlooked that the atmosphere at Huntington Bank Field played a role in the team’s ability to finish these games strong. Consistency at home can build confidence too and help to establish a winning culture. When fans recognize that the atmosphere makes a difference and players are confident that it gives them an extra edge, it can have a positive impact on the team’s performance on the field. With four home games left against the Las Vegas Raiders, Cincinnati Bengals, Atlanta Falcons, and Indianapolis Colts, Cleveland hopes to finish out the season 8-0 in front of the home crowd. title: Browns vs. Raiders: Week 12’s SNF is a chance for CLE to prove who they are
summary: Going into the season, the Cleveland Browns had only one primetime game. One. Granted, rebuilding teams are not going to get multiple primetime games. A few Thursday night games, but no Sunday or Monday night games. Early this season, the Browns played their division rival, the Pittsburgh Steelers, on Thursday night, and it was somewhat […]
full_text: Going into the season, the Cleveland Browns had only one primetime game. One. Granted, rebuilding teams are not going to get multiple primetime games. A few Thursday night games, but no Sunday or Monday night games. Early this season, the Browns played their division rival, the Pittsburgh Steelers, on Thursday night , and it was somewhat of a statement win for the team. The final score didn’t indicate how the game actually went, but for the first time in a long time, Cleveland played on a national stage, and the moment didn’t seem too bright for them. However, it didn’t stop the constant doubt the team faced. Whether it was people questioning how the Browns were winning or not giving credit where it’s due, no one was moved. Weeks have passed, and Cleveland has another primetime game coming up against the Las Vegas Raiders . Originally, this game was scheduled for a 1 pm kickoff. However, things changed. The NFL chose to flex out the original Sunday night game between the New England Patriots and the Los Angeles Chargers. Considering how most of the Week 12 slate has major games that are being played earlier this week, Raiders-Browns felt like an appropriate choice. Both teams are still in the playoff race, and they are the biggest surprises in the NFL. Raiders rookie quarterback Fernando Mendoza will be making his primetime debut after being handed the reins after the Las Vegas traded away quarterback Kirk Cousins. For the Browns, this is another rare opportunity for them. Another primetime game, another chance to impress a national audience. Last time Cleveland was on Sunday Night Football? 2021. Last time the team played a Sunday night game at home? 2019. It’s been a while, but the team should be looking to prove a point on Sunday. Lost in the conversation is that many believe this could be the game that Mendoza announces that he has arrived. For the Browns, it should be about proving a point. The Raiders aren’t a bad team by any means. However, if you want to get eyes focused on you and have the respect of the national media, it all starts with having a dominant win. Sunday night should be a game that Cleveland is looking to prove a point. What is that point? Announcing that these aren’t the same old Cleveland Browns. Announcing that the Cleveland Browns have arrived and that the entire league should recognize. How big of a game do you think Sunday Night Football is for the Browns to prove something to themselves, the fans, and the NFL world? Join the conversation! title: Street free agents the Browns could consider as they push for a postseason berth
summary: The 2026 season for the Cleveland Browns isn’t one that their fanbase has experienced as of late. Cleveland is just one game out of first place in the division, and they also hold the #6 seed if the playoffs began today. Not that this franchise hasn’t had its share of success. The franchise has won […]
full_text: The 2026 season for the Cleveland Browns isn’t one that their fanbase has experienced as of late. Cleveland is just one game out of first place in the division, and they also hold the #6 seed if the playoffs began today . Not that this franchise hasn’t had its share of success. The franchise has won eight pro football titles, tied for third most with the New York Football Giants behind the Green Bay Packers (13) and the Chicago Bears (9). RELATED: 3 THREATS THAT COULD PREVENT THE BROWNS FROM REACHING PLAYOFFS The Browns are the only pro team that has won five consecutive championships from 1946 to 1950. This franchise is also the lone club to go to 10 consecutive title games, winning seven. The very last “NFL Championship Game” before the merger with the American Football League that sent the winner to Super Bowl 4 was in 1969 between the Browns and the Minnesota Vikings. In the 1980s, Cleveland went to and lost three “AFC Championship Games.” But all of this was so long ago. Yes, titles from way back count and look good in the trophy case, but the last NFL championship that the Browns won was the 1964 crown. 62 years without a new title is such a long time. The Super Bowl is simply the new name for the league’s title game, but Cleveland has yet to make an appearance. The Browns are 6-4-0 this year. They lost two games to bad opponents: the 3-8-0 New York Jets and the 3-7-0 New Orleans Saints. Think about an 8-2-0 record if this team had beaten who they should have. At this juncture, Cleveland has a real shot at the postseason tournament . Now, whether they have any success is another question, but getting there is a difficult task. Do the Browns have any holes? How has the injury bug affected this roster? How is their depth? Are there any players currently on IR that will be available later? The NFL trade deadline has come and gone . Teams like the Browns still have likely needs to fill as they hit the bottom half of the schedule. The last thing any playoff club wants is for untimely injuries to take away valuable athletes, with very little on the depth chart to solve the issue. Can’t trade for anyone. What now? The free agent pool, aka street free agents. It’s not like there aren’t players available. There are. Plenty of bodies , but limited on talent. The big questions are: can they still compete at a high level? Have they been faithful with workouts and nutrition? These are players that have been released during this season, or weren’t ever signed after being a late-day cut from training camp. Let’s earmark the depth holes for the Browns, and who is available to sign. OT Taylor Decker (6’-7”, 324 pounds) Age: 33 The Browns seem to be content with rookie Spencer Fano and Tytus Howard on their offensive line corners. Despite being the newbie, Fano has started all 10 games and played every offensive snap. Howard has also started all 10 games with 91% of snaps. That isn’t the concern. The issue is a matter of depth. Coming in this late in the season, Decker would realize that he isn’t being pegged as a starting offensive tackle unless the starter has been sent to IR. Cleveland should want an experienced body at the ready in case this does happen. Currently, that swing tackle option is Dawand Jones. He plays like a roller coaster in that he can dominate with those long arms, yet is a sucker for an inside move. He struggles with speed rushers, and a variety of rushers were able to win around his edge. Decker is a 10-year veteran with 140 NFL starts on his resume. Last year, with the Detroit Lions, he allowed just two sacks over 551 pass-blocking snaps. He did end the 2025 season with some injury issues, including a surgically repaired shoulder. The Lions did not cut Decker, but there was a salary dispute when the team asked him to take a pay cut, and he declined. He asked for his release, and they obliged him. It has been reported that Decker is now healthy, in good shape, and has an interest. However, he has been waiting for the right fit for a playoff contender, which the Browns are. Which means he isn’t interested in signing just any deal. EDGE Hassan Reddick (6’-1”, 240 pounds) Age: 32 The Browns pass rusher has been hit or miss this year. The leading sack meister are DT Mason Graham and DE Isaiah McGuire with just four. The defensive tackle position is responsible for 14 sacks. McGuire’s four are the bulk of sack stats from a defensive end. Jared Verse: 0, Derek Barnett: 0, Sam Williams: 1, and Jamree Kromah: 0. Reddick would give the outside pass-rushing position a much-needed boost. He has played nine seasons with 61.5 sacks, 108 QB hits, 77 tackles for loss, 455 total tackles, 18 forced fumbles, 174 pressures, 64 hurries, 43 knockdowns, and 45 missed tackles. Reddick can fill a void in the Browns’ pass rush by being their rotation. He is a good run defender and can also strengthen the contain against the run. Cleveland’s defense is allowing 4.6 yards per carry and are ranked #25 on allowing first downs on run plays. The Browns should be looking to the free-agent market to add an EDGE rusher. Reddick is perhaps their best option. OG Daniel Brunskill (6’-5, 260 pounds) Age: 32 Another weak spot on the Browns roster is depth at offensive guard. Currently, only Zak Zinter is the backup for both Zion Williams and Austin Barber. Teven Jenkins, the Week 1 projected starter, is now on IR. Brunskill was recently released by the Los Angeles Chargers. He can play all five offensive line positions, so this versatility might be helpful at some juncture. He has played in 110 NFL games with 71 starts over his eight-year career. He allowed zero pressures this year with one penalty flag and zero sacks in limited action plus work on the practice squad. Last year he played in 16 games, while the two seasons before that he was their starter. He isn’t a road grader, but has positive marks in pass protection. When a wide-zone team is able to reach wide zone and threaten defenses like that, the defenses now have to think about the run more, and Brunskill has the tools. A little older now, he isn’t the quick puller he once was but can provide the Browns will an experienced backup going down the stretch. full_text: CLEVELAND, OHIO - NOVEMBER 15: Running back Quinshon Judkins #10 of the Cleveland Browns celebrates after the game against the Houston Texans at Huntington Bank Field on November 15, 2026 in Cleveland, Ohio. The Browns defeated the Texans 27-24. (Photo by Jason Miller/Getty Images) | Getty Images It is Week 12 of the 2026 NFL season, and the Cleveland Browns watched all three of their AFC North foes lose this past week, while they were resting on the bye. Life is good, for the moment. Overall, the Browns basically stayed flat, but dropped by 0.2 spots from week-to-week to have an overall ranking of 13.9 . Every site kept them flat, except for one that dropped them down by one spot. Meanwhile, the Bengals and Steelers both dropped about two to three spots, with Pittsburgh’s fall making them go behind Cleveland. Here is a summary of how the Cleveland Browns are viewed across mainstream media outlets in NFL Power Rankings heading into Week 12 of the 2026 NFL season. CBS Sports – No. 14 (no change) Coming off their bye, they would be in the playoffs if they started today. They are also playing in prime time this week after their game was flexed. Who saw this all coming? ESPN – No. 14 (no change) Extension candidate: Edge Isaiah McGuire A 2023 fourth-round pick, McGuire was pushed into a full-time starting role after Alex Wright’s season-ending Achilles injury in training camp. McGuire has put together his most productive season in a contract year. His career-high four sacks are tied for the team lead, and his pressure rate (9.2%) is in line with his career average despite facing increased attention (career-high 35.2% double team rate). Wright’s injury and edge rusher Jared Verse’s struggles should make McGuire more of a priority in free agency. NFL.com – No. 13 (down 1 spot) The Browns entered their bye awash in the glow of a comeback victory that could prove to be transformative because of how they earned it, overcoming a Houston haymaker that would have floored lesser teams and returning the favor to the Texans over the final three quarters. Will that inspire a second-half run that propels Cleveland to the playoffs? Stay tuned. Sporting News – No. 14 (no change) The Browns improved their playoff position a little during the bye with the Steelers losing. But now they can expect to get a full-on challenge for their wild-card spot, with the Raiders, Bengals and Giants among the opponents over the next month. Yahoo Sports – No. 14 (no change) Seeing the Raiders’ upset bid fall short was good news for the Browns. Their game against Las Vegas in Week 12, which got flexed to Sunday night, would have been much more interesting in the wild-card race had the Raiders been 5-6 instead of 4-7. It also wasn’t bad for Cleveland to see the Steelers slip back to 6-4 with a bad loss at Philadelphia. The Browns aren’t a lock to make the playoffs but the path is very clear. They have two games left against the Bengals and one against the Giants, but the other four are against teams with losing records. Bleacher Report – No. 14 (no change) The Cleveland Browns are earning their respect by winning close games. All six of their wins are by four points or fewer. While those contests could’ve gone the other way, they’re battle-tested and won’t flinch in coin-flip contests down the stretch. To crack the top 10 in these power rankings, the Browns need to be more productive on offense. They’re 18th in passing and 24th in rushing. Cleveland doesn’t do anything particularly well on that side of the ball and must improve in both areas. USA Today – No. 14 (no change) Since they last played on Nov. 15, they’ve picked up playoff positioning and got shifted by the league into the post-Thanksgiving Sunday night slot. A pretty bountiful bye week. title: Browns can’t give away a QB, even if they tried
summary: In the 1983 classic Eddie Murphy comedy Trading Places, the fictional characters of Randolph and Mortimer Duke owned Duke & Duke, a commodities brokerage firm in Philadelphia. A key plot point in the movie centers on the Dukes trying to corner the frozen concentrated orange juice market through an ill-advised scheme to manipulate it, which […]
full_text: BEREA, OHIO - JUNE 11: Shedeur Sanders #2, Dillon Gabriel #6 and Taylen Green #15 of the Cleveland Browns look on during the Cleveland Browns Mandatory Minicamp at CrossCountry Mortgage Campus on June 11, 2026 in Berea, Ohio. (Photo by Nick Cammett/Diamond Images via Getty Images) | Diamond Images/Getty Images In the 1983 classic Eddie Murphy comedy Trading Places , the fictional characters of Randolph and Mortimer Duke owned Duke & Duke, a commodities brokerage firm in Philadelphia. A key plot point in the movie centers on the Dukes trying to corner the frozen concentrated orange juice market through an ill-advised scheme to manipulate it, which ultimately fails. The Cleveland Browns are not interested in frozen concentrated orange juice, at least as far as anyone knows, but they have spent the 2026 season cornering the market on quarterbacks that no other team really wants. Cleveland’s quarterback room currently consists of: Deshaun Watson, champion of the six fourth-quarter comebacks that have been needed because of his poor play in the first three quarters of games. Backup Shedeur Sanders, who followed Watson’s script in his lone start of the season, only he forgot the part about actually winning the game. Backup to the backup Dillon Gabriel, whose biggest contribution so far this season was to come down with a back injury and go on injured reserve when the final rosters needed to be set. Rounding out the room is Taylen Green, an unpolished developmental quarterback who presents the always exciting prospects of a player who the Browns could “build a package of plays” around, if only they were not busy having the starters practice each week. General manager Andrew Berry had an opportunity to get a jump on cleaning out the room in anticipation of 2027’s new group at the trade deadline earlier this month, only there was one small problem. No one was interested in what Berry had on display in the shop window. That must certainly be hard to believe for some, especially given that the Browns have the greatest unpolished gem in NFL history just waiting to be unleashed, but it appears to be the truth, according to cleveland.com’s Mary Kay Cabot : The Browns received no trade calls on backup quarterbacks Shedeur Sanders or Dillon Gabriel at or before the Nov. 10 trade deadline, league sources told cleveland.com. A report circulated on Monday that the Vikings offered the Browns a third-round pick for Sanders and that they turned it down. The report was untrue … Ah, but we can hear the gears turning in the heads of armchair GMs everywhere. There is no way that Berry will jeopardize a potential playoff run by relying on Watson and a room full of unproven quarterbacks. Surely he would be interested in another veteran insurance policy like … Daniel Jones? Thankfully, the Berry and head coach Todd Monken reportedly have zero interest in checking out Jones, who was released last week by the Indianapolis Colts, according to Cabot . So there it is. The Browns are going to ride out the rest of the season with their current crop of quarterbacks and hope Watson plays well enough to get the Browns into the playoffs. Then, once the season is done, Berry will get to work on rebuilding the quarterback room in 2027. Because if no one else wants one of the quarterbacks, why would the Browns? full_text: As the Cleveland Browns begin their preparations for Week 12’s Sunday Night Football matchup with the Las Vegas Raiders, their roster continues to have news and, potentially, is in flux . Not only could the 53-man roster see RB Raheim Sanders return from injured reserve, but GM Andrew Berry continues to look at ways to improve different units. On Tuesday, the Browns had four players in for workouts in Berea: DT Derrick Nnadi DT Khalen Saunders DT Jalen Hunt DT Ben Stille Nnadi and Saunders were both third-round picks, playing multiple years for the Kansas City Chiefs, including Super Bowl victories. Nnadi played 130 games, including 98 starts, with the Chiefs, accumulating 249 tackles, nine QB hits, seven tackles for loss, and five sacks. Saunders spent four years with Kansas City, two with the New Orleans Saints, and split last year between the New York Jets and Jacksonville Jaguars. In seven seasons, Saunders has 193 tackles, 18 QB hits, eight tackles for loss, and 7.5 sacks. Stille has spent four seasons with five teams, including six games with the Browns in 2022. In 19 games, the former undrafted free agent has had 17 tackles, three QB hits, two sacks, and one tackle for loss. Hunt has not played in an NFL contest after going undrafted this year. Cleveland currently has just two teams (three games) against teams with winning records: Twice versus the Cincinnati Bengals and a road clash with John Harbaugh’s New York Giants. That Week 15 game was also CB Greg Newsome II’s chance at revenge against the team that traded him away last year . The key word there is “was,” as Newsome injured his ankle a few weeks after signing a big extension with the Giants, and now is out at least four weeks: Sources: #Giants CB Greg Newsome will undergo tightrope surgery this week for a high-ankle sprain and will be out roughly 4–6 weeks. A big loss, as Newsome has been a top corner for the Giants this season and recently inked a 3-year, $46M extension. pic.twitter.com/6XW9uxXYn4 — Jordan Schultz (@Schultz_Report) November 24, 2026 Newsome didn’t play well for the Jacksonville Jaguars after the trade, but has had a solid season in New York this year, with eight passes defended and one interception. Cleveland fans will always remember Newsome for his regular celebrations, no matter the score, but the former first-round pick didn’t live up to his draft status while with the Browns.

title: 2026 Week 12 rooting guide for Cowboys fans
summary: Thanksgiving week is always a big one for the Cowboys and the NFL as a whole. Beyond any special halftime shows or other extra production, it’s also generally when the regular season heats up as playoff scenarios begin to take clearer form. Despite all of their tribulations so far this year, the Cowboys are still […]
full_text: Photo by Matthew Pearce/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Thanksgiving week is always a big one for the Cowboys and the NFL as a whole. Beyond any special halftime shows or other extra production, it’s also generally when the regular season heats up as playoff scenarios begin to take clearer form. Despite all of their tribulations so far this year, the Cowboys are still just a couple of games away from both a division title and the NFC’s last wild card spot. Let’s check out the current standings, and then see how the entire Week 12 slate could help or hurt Dallas. Current 2026 NFC Playoff Standings 1. San Francisco 49ers 9-1 (6-1 vs NFC) 2. Detroit Lions 8-2 (5-1) 3. New York Giants 6-3-1 (3-3-1) 4. Carolina Panthers 5-5 (4-3) 5. Chicago Bears 8-2 (6-2) 6. Minnesota Vikings 7-3 (5-2) 7. Green Bay Packers 6-4 (4-4) _______________________________ 8. Seattle Seahawks 6-4 (2-3) 9. Los Angeles Rams 6-4 (4-2) 10. Dallas Cowboys 5-6 (2-5) With the Packers, Rams, and Seahawks all on a bye last week, Dallas was able to inch closer in the wild card race. It’s hard to see the Cowboys leapfrogging all three of those teams into the seventh seed, but at least it’s still on the table. Even winning the NFC East isn’t solely up to the Cowboys at this point. They‘ll need help for either lane to get into the playoffs. How might some help come from the Week 12 schedule? NFC East teams Cowboys d. Eagles Colts d. Giants Cardinals d. Commanders The Jaguars let us down last week, allowing New York to pull off yet another surprise win. We may have to stop calling them upsets soon, as John Harbaugh has the Giants consistently performing above expectations. This week, the G-Men are anything but underdogs. The Colts appear to be in full tank mode now, and even a 3-3 home record doesn’t give much room for confidence. If anything, we have to hope that New York is the team that’s feeling itself and allows Indy to catch them by surprise. You can go either way on Washington at this point. On the one hand, you’d like them to keep winning and hurt their draft position. On the other, you don’t want them suddenly having something to play for when they meet Dallas in Week 18. A loss to Arizona would certainly take the wind out of their sails, and keep the NFC East feeling like a two-horse race. That feels like the better option this week, but it’s truly a 50/50 proposition. NFC vs. NFC Rams d. Packers Bears d. Lions Vikings d. Falcons 49ers d. Seahawks Bucs d. Panthers Los Angeles winning the Wednesday night game is doubly good for Dallas. It pulls Green Bay down a peg, who is currently our biggest concern of those 6-4 teams with a head-to-head advantage. It also helps the value of the 2027 first-round pick they owe us. If someone’s going to get that seventh seed aside from the Cowboys, we definitely don’t want it to be Green Bay. Speaking of NFC North teams, the best thing for Dallas is that the Bears, Lions, and Vikings all stay jumbled at the top and lock the Packers out of a possible division win. The Packers have division games left against the Bears and Lions, and we want to see their rivals motivated in those contests. The NFC West is a different story, with the Niners looking ready to run right on through the Super Bowl. They can have the division, at least, and help the Cowboys by putting losses on our wild card competition like the Seahawks and Rams along the way. In the one division that makes the NFC East look competent this year, the NFC South “winner” is guaranteed to be at least the fourth seed in the playoffs. If the Cowboys do slide into the tournament as NFC East champions, they’d rather be the third seed if possible. So whoever wins the South, may they have the worst record possible. NFC vs. AFC Bengals d. Saints This week’s only interconference game is a real nothing burger for Cowboys fans. The best thing we can say about a Saints loss is that it pushes them further up the draft order and helps block the Eagles. So there’s that. AFC vs. AFC Broncos d. Steelers Chargers d. Patriots For purely draft-related reasons: Dallas is owed the Steelers’ 4th-round pick and the Patriots’ 7th-rounder in 2027. So the worse their records are, the better.

title: What the numbers say about Cowboys vs Eagles
summary: Every week, we’ll examine the numbers behind the next opponent on the schedule. Looking at the recent numbers and trends for each team, we’ll add it all up to see which squad may have the edge. This week, the 5-6 Dallas Cowboys look to get back to .500 against the 3-7 Joe Milton-led Philadelphia Eagles. […]
full_text: Mandatory Credit: Kevin Jairaj-Imagn Images Every week, we’ll examine the numbers behind the next opponent on the schedule. Looking at the recent numbers and trends for each team, we’ll add it all up to see which squad may have the edge. This week, the 5-6 Dallas Cowboys look to get back to .500 against the 3-7 Joe Milton-led Philadelphia Eagles. Cowboys key stats from last week Dak Prescott continued his recent hot streak, completing 28/33 passes for 325 yards and four touchdowns. He’d also cash in with his legs, scoring once on the ground. Prescott currently ranks second in the NFL in pass yards and passing touchdowns, just behind Joe Burrow in both categories. Over the last two weeks, the Cowboys quarterback has put up ten touchdowns, 668 passing yards, and a passer rating of 123.5 . CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens each crossed the century mark on the day, recording 132 and 102 yards respectively. Each finished with a touchdown against the Titans. Quinnen Williams and James Houston each recorded two sacks and had a combined five tackles for loss. The defense played their best game of the season against a Titans team that came in averaging 27 points per week over the last three games. Eagles key stats from last week The Eagles snapped a seven-game losing streak with former Cowboys quarterback Joe Milton leading the team. Milton finished the day 11/21 for 141 yards and a 73.7 passer rating. He did not score. Saquon Barkley scored the only Eagles touchdown on the day. He totaled 17 carries for 75 yards against the Steelers. Philadelphia’s biggest weapon was the right leg of Jake Elliot who went 4/4 , the longest coming from 55 yards out. The defense recorded five sacks and held the Steelers to just 255 total yards and 16 points. Stack up points early We’ve seen Joe Milton’s cannon arm here in Dallas. The power he possesses is truly amazing. And while his accuracy has improved since last year, he still is not a starting-caliber NFL quarterback at this point in his career. He’ll overthrow balls at times and his decision making isn’t the best. The Cowboys can take advantage of Milton’s vulnerabilities by playing complementary football for the second straight week. Dallas held the Titans to just three field goals in the first half last week while putting up four touchdowns of their own. If the offense and defense are synced up like that again on Thanksgiving, this could be another big game for this team. If Dallas allows Saquon Barkley to get going and doesn’t force Milton into mistakes while simultaneously struggling on offense, you’ll see a close game that goes down to the wire. While Dallas may not be a good team, the Eagles are exponentially worse. Force them to play keep up with a Cowboys offense that’s firing on all cylinders and this will be a fun Thanksgiving day for the Dallas players and fans alike. What do the numbers mean? Containing a banged up Saquon Barkley will be the biggest key for Dallas in this game. If the defense forces Joe Milton to win through the air, the Cowboys win this game by multiple scores. If Barkley consistently gives the Eagles third and short while keeping the offense on track, Dallas will have a game on their hands. They simply cannot allow that to happen. Brian Schottenheimer needs to ride the hot hand and allow Dak Prescott and his receivers to cook while also utilizing the running game in a complementary capacity. The offensive line has been hot as well, playing their best game of the year last week against the Titans. Play the game with points on the brain and forget about time of possession. This week, quick scoring drives benefits the Cowboys more than long, methodical drives. The Eagles will try and shorten the game while Dallas needs to focus on quick strikes and explosives to run up the score. Notably, the offensive motion rate has dramatically increased over the past few weeks. This should continue again this week, helping Prescott diagnose the defense pre-snap and creating mismatch opportunities. Watch for big plays from the Cowboys receivers this week with Quinyon Mitchell likely out and Tariq Woolen filling in. We’ve seen Lamb beat Woolen earlier this season, so finding that matchup will be key again this time around. Last week was the first time we saw it all come together for Dallas, blowing out a team they were meant to walk over. Take care of business early and we’ll see opportunities for turnovers from Joe Milton pressing to play keep up in a game where Dallas is likely put up another huge point total. If all goes to plan, the Cowboys should win this game handily on Thanksgiving.

full_text: Photo by Norm Hall/Getty Images | Getty Images The Dallas Cowboys annihilated the Tennessee Titans last Sunday by a score of 51-30. It was a complete game by the offense, elite really, but even the defense has a ‘decent’ day by their standards. The Cowboys are at home for this week’s Thanksgiving game against the 3-7 Philadelphia Eagles, and are 8.5-point favorites according to our friends at FanDuel. The over/under is 48.5 points. CeeDee Lamb did turn out to be the star and he did get a touchdown, but only had 132 receiving yards, not the 150 predicted. Here are this week’s bold predictions. Joe Milton scores a rushing touchdown on a planned play Former Cowboys QB Joe Milton returns to Dallas as the starting signal-caller for the Eagles. We know his M.O. from his Dallas days – dangerous runner with a rocket arm, struggles with consistency and accuracy.
