The Cowboys call up Jashaun Corbin again, and he scores this week When the Cowboys lost Tyler Goodson, the position of RB2 appeared to be an issue. title: Cowboys roundtable discussion: Eagles, playoffs and Thanksgiving
summary: Every week, we gather to discuss the latest news about the Dallas Cowboys and seek our writer’s perspective on each headline. Welcome back to the roundtable. This week we have Jorge Guajardo, Dyllan Rivers, Tom Ryle, RJ Ochoa and Sean Martin.  What did the win against the Tennessee Titans tell us about the Dallas Cowboys? Mike – It told us that […]
full_text: Photo by Richard Rodriguez/Getty Images Every week, we gather to discuss the latest news about the Dallas Cowboys and seek our writer’s perspective on each headline. Welcome back to the roundtable. This week we have Jorge Guajardo , Dyllan Rivers , Tom Ryle, RJ Ochoa and Sean Martin. What did the win against the Tennessee Titans tell us about the Dallas Cowboys? Mike – It told us that Dallas has an offense capable of competing with anybody, but a defense that still has plenty to prove. Scoring 51 points, with touchdowns on the opening six possessions, was an outstanding offensive performance. The offensive line controlled the trenches, the receivers were causing problems everywhere, and Dallas looked almost unstoppable. Defensively, there were encouraging signs under Mike Pettine, particularly better communication, a more unified approach and five sacks, but conceding 30 points to a one-win Tennessee team shows the problems are far from gone. Tom – The one takeaway for me is that they are good enough to dominate a clearly inferior team. I’m not sure that is enough going forward, because there just aren’t any more teams that are going to be that easy to beat. And there were still some significant warts, like the two long plays that led to the first two Titans touchdowns, letting Tony Pollard get over 100 yards, and those seemingly endless penalties. That last one is particularly concerning to me, because it indicates a real lack of discipline. Dyllan – The offense played about as well as one could hope, scoring touchdowns on every drive but one (which still resulted in a field goal). Defensively, the 30 points allowed isn’t indicative of how well they played. I expect the offense to continue to play at a high level. I believe they’ve unlocked something, especially with George Pickens more involved. The defense, however, will scare me for the remainder of the season. That’ll continue to be the Achilles heel for this team. Jorge – This offense is clearly one of the best units in the league. Schotty didn’t let up in the second half, and they really left little doubt about the result, even when the Titans started scoring touchdowns. The defense, however, is still a huge question mark, and the penalties are killing the Cowboys to Tom’s point. Still, I fear this team will give us, and themselves, hope for actually making a run at the Giants. The offense is that good. RJ – Ultimately the takeaway for me is that the Cowboys won a game. I think it can be that simple. Obviously if they win on Thanksgiving then things become a little bit more legitimate. Things have been so chaotic that I am fine with taking things for what they are and this was just a win against a bad team. I’m happy, but we all need to see more. Sean – That the Cowboys will make their layups. They’ve outplayed and outcoached Robert Saleh teams a lot before, and they did it again Sunday. They’ve made a point under Brian Schottenheimer to beat weaker AFC teams along with NFC East teams as the bulk of the wins in their W-L records, and they did it again Sunday. They’ve played solid defense against Brian Daboll-coordinated offenses, and in some ways but not all, they did that again Sunday too. If Dallas defeats the Philadelphia Eagles, what chance do you give that the Cowboys will win the NFC East? Mike – If Dallas beats Philadelphia on Thanksgiving, I’d give the Cowboys around a 50% chance of winning the NFC East. That might sound optimistic considering how this season has unfolded, but the division is still there for the taking. A victory would move Dallas to 6-6 and complete the season sweep over Philadelphia, which is important for divisional positioning. The biggest obstacle isn’t the Eagles, it’s themselves. If the team can come together now, find a sudden surge and become consistent, then it’s game on. The concern remains the defense, which simply cannot keep surrendering huge scores, and until I start seeing that happening, I remain down the middle on certainty on where Dallas finish. Tom – That sadly depends on how the New York Giants do the rest of the way. Dallas is chasing them, and after the Giants just beat the Jacksonville Jaguars, they are going to be hard to catch. I think Dallas still has less than a 50% chance of making it to the playoffs, probably more like 25% or so. They have to duplicate their success in several games the rest of the way. That is a tall order given the inconsistency they have shown this year. And there were still plenty of vulnerabilities on display on Sunday for better teams to try and exploit. Even with the hopefuls sign in the 51-30 win, there seem to be more issues that are yet to be resolved. Dyllan – How many games will the Giants lose? The majority assumption was that Dallas needed to win the games they’re favored in as well as steal one of the big three versus Jacksonville, Seattle, or LA. Depending on the Giants, the Cowboys may need to win two or more of those. I don’t like those odds. If the Giants falter, losing two or more games, Dallas is in business. Jorge – So the probability of Dallas pulling it off and winning the division is around 20% right now, and that seems accurate. The thing is, with this team, there are a lot of what-ifs, and for them to make the comeback and catch the Giants, we have to assume they are going to pull off some huge wins, including beating the Giants, and assuming that this team will do what it takes to pull something like that off is just a bad bet. This is still not a good team as a whole, and every real test they’ve faced this year, they have faltered. RJ – At this point for me it isn’t even about what the Cowboys do. I can’t trust them to take care of all business right now, but even if they do they need help. Many people believed the Giants would lose to Jacksonville and that obviously didn’t happen. If New York keeps surprising us then all of what Dallas may or may not do would be for not. Sean – Especially after Sunday where the Giants really did well to hold off the Jaguars and look like they belong in the playoffs, I just can’t have a ton of hope for them dropping games that are supposed traps or whatever term you want to call them. I’ve even been saying since previewing the week one matchup that the Giants would be a threat in the division. I think the Cowboys will remain a threat in their rear view mirror the whole way, but catching them seems difficult. What do you feel is the most realistic path for Dallas to get into the Wild Card race? Mike – For me, the most realistic path is simple, Dallas needs to win at least five of its remaining six games and hope the teams above them start slipping up. At 5-6, the Cowboys have almost no margin for error, and reaching 10-7 should be the minimum target. That means every game from now is a must-win, and the biggest opportunities come against Seattle and the Rams, two teams directly ahead of Dallas in the Wild Card race. Beat them both, and suddenly the picture looks very different. The remaining divisional games against the Giants and Commanders are equally important. Tom – I just don’t think there is a likely one. Basically they have to win most of their remaining games while several teams currently ahead of them have to stumble. That is possible with the way so many of those teams are dealing with injuries, particularly at quarterback. I just don’t think it is probable. Dyllan – The wild card seems quite unrealistic. But if there was a path, the Cowboys would most likely need to win every remaining game on their schedule but one. They’d also count on the Packers, Seahawks and Rams to falter. Ten wins probably locks in a wild card spot, but that’s a steep hill to climb with the remaining schedule. Dallas would love to have the Cardinals and Buccaneers games back – those losses against lesser teams always come back to haunt them and this season is no different. All things considered, a wild card spot is far less likely than just winning the division. Jorge – The…

title: Cowboys vs. Eagles: Offensive, defensive impact players in Week 12
summary: With a victory over the Philadelphia Eagles this week the Dallas Cowboys have a chance to get back to .500 on the season. They’ve already beaten them once the season, and this time around they are the ones with the home-field advantage. To secure the victory this week the Cowboys are going to need some […]
full_text: Photo by Matthew Pearce/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images With a victory over the Philadelphia Eagles this week the Dallas Cowboys have a chance to get back to .500 on the season. They’ve already beaten them once the season, and this time around they are the ones with the home-field advantage. To secure the victory this week the Cowboys are going to need some impact plays on both sides of the ball. Today, we identified one offensive and defensive player we believe will make such an impact, helping to sway the game in Dallas’ favor. Offense – WR George Pickens The Cowboys aerial attack has been lethal the past two games and a lot of that probably has to do with George Pickens’ uptick in production. He’s coming off back-to-back 100+ receiving yard games and has been much more involved in Dallas’ passing game during that time. In the last two weeks alone he’s caught 18 passes for 247 yards and four touchdowns. We believe we will see more of the same in the Thanksgiving Day matchup with the Eagles. The Eagles are currently ranked 17 th in the league allowing 222.8 receiving yards per game. They held George Pickens to just four catches for 57 yards in Week 7, but did allow him to score a touchdown in that matchup. That was then and this is now. No. 3 is playing his best football right now and QB Dak Prescott is looking his way more often because of it. Another 100-yard receiving game isn’t out of the question. Defense – LB Justin Barron Dee Winters exited the game early with a knee injury last week against the Titans and didn’t return. The Cowboys surprisingly chose to replace him in the starting lineup with LB Justin Barron, who they signed as an undrafted free agent out of Syracuse last year. He’s predominantly been a special teams player thus far in his young career with the Cowboys, but ended up leading the team in tackles last week with nine as an injury fill-in. With it being a short week, No. 45 has a good chance to get his first NFL career start on Thanksgiving against the Eagles. He was impressive last week while filling in for Dee Winters and could get rewarded because of it. He seems to have the coaching staffs trust and has been productive when given the opportunity. He could have a big impact on the game helping to contain Saquon Barkley as both the run and receiver this week.
author: Brian Martin

title: Cowboys point/counterpoint: Eagles are going to be much more of a test
summary: At least all hope is not lost. After the Dallas Cowboys delivered a dominating victory over the Tennessee Titans, there is still a path to the playoffs. But there were some warts that still emerged in the game. Now the Thanksgiving Day game against the Philadelphia Eagles has become one more crucial step if Dallas […]
full_text: Photo by Terence Lewis/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images At least all hope is not lost. After the Dallas Cowboys delivered a dominating victory over the Tennessee Titans, there is still a path to the playoffs. But there were some warts that still emerged in the game. Now the Thanksgiving Day game against the Philadelphia Eagles has become one more crucial step if Dallas hopes to overtake the surging New York Giants, who took down the Jacksonville Jaguars, one of the top teams in the leagues. Our Tom Ryle and Sean Martin cast their skeptical eyes on things. Tom – Normally, you take a 21-point win without quibbles. Sadly, I am unable to do that. There was too much in that game that points to potential problems on Thursday. Let’s start with something obvious. Tennessee is in any conversation about the worst franchise in the league this year. And for the most part, that’s exactly how they played. Outside of a few rather freaky plays, their offense was mostly impotent, especially their passing game. Cam Ward managed to deliver a respectable 248 yards passing and two touchdowns without an interception, but his offensive line failed him. He was sacked five times for 28 yards lost, and endured eight QB hits. Kudos to the Cowboys’ pass rush, but you have to look at what they were up against. This game was just too easy for them to penetrate and get to Ward. Flipping it around, Dak Prescott saw very little pressure, with no sacks and only one hit. That is the main reason he had such a magnificent performance. He just had all the time he needed to keep leading the team down the field and into the end zone. Both CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens eclipsed 100 yard receiving and scored a touchdown, showing that not only was the Titans’ pass rush not much of a threat, their secondary was badly overmatched. Prescott set records in the game. We have to expect that the Eagles are going to present much more of a challenge. And this season, Prescott has been significantly less effective when pressured. Don’t forget that Philly is coming off their own win, a close one over the Pittsburgh Steelers. Sean – As unrealistic as it is, obviously in some sense the offense showed they can do what it takes to win every game. Can we expect a scoring drive on every possession though? Of course not. The defense however played much more like the type of defense that should be supporting a high powered offense. The splash plays like five more sacks and the fumble nearly returned for a touchdown are exactly what they should be after – instant drive-killers that get the ball back in Dak Prescott’s hands. Mike Pettine seemed to understand this, and I’m not discounting the fact that maybe Schottenheimer’s splendid day calling plays had something to do with less pressure in the week of game prep worrying about the defense because of Pettine’s steady hand. Is the most realistic, grounded, and likely outcome still that this team has dropped too many winnable games early to parlay another November run into a playoff berth? Unfortunately, yes. But the ultimate gift of this lousy division is one the Cowboys are going to firmly stay in the hunt for, and the Giants are far from locks to win it just yet. Also, we were so starved for even average defense last year that when the team won these November games, Quinnen Williams making a few plays here and there was seen as enough to get excited about. Now, we’re seeing more and more each week that Williams will be someone to build this defense around in the offseason. That’s still a tough consolation prize should this team actually miss the playoffs for a third straight year, but building blocks need to be put in place on defense at some point, and there’s enough runway left for that to happen through December I hope. Tom – At least the defense seemed to be more consistent. That pressure speaks for itself. The secondary held up most of the game, with just a few notable breakdowns. One was a pass interference call the announcers were not so sure about, and the other just a bit of being asleep at the wheel when they failed to make sure the receiver was actually on the ground when they touched him. I think those are more related to the discipline issue than anything, but take some hope from how things looked outside those plays and the wild touchdown throw against the second-stringers at the end. Now it comes down to stringing together two at least acceptable defensive performances paired with the offense not slowing down. Again, this should be a much harder task against our beloved NFC East rival from Philadelphia. The key here may just be something that is applicable far beyond the football field. Take care of the things that are in your control and don’t get distracted by what isn’t. Dallas can’t do a thing about the Giants until the penultimate game of the season. They need to keep improving and just win as many as they can over the final six contests, and things should work out. Sean – The Eagles are coming to Arlington off a win that looks to be something of the polar opposite of how yet another fairly wild Cowboys home game played out on Sunday. A game where both teams score less than 20 points is a super rarity these days, but when the Eagles had lost seven straight coming in, that’s probably the fluky type of game they needed. The most concrete take to have is probably that old friend Mike McCarthy’s offense is sputtering badly in Pittsburgh, but given how the Cowboys have dropped every chance to show us fans they can string together wins, another strong Eagles defensive performance to make Thanksgiving a nail-biter can’t be ruled out either. Then there’s the fact Joe Milton will know this defense well, and is a hard QB to bring to the ground in pass rush. If that element of the defense which Mike Pettine has working is neutralized at all, anything can happen on a short week for these rivals. Anyway, here’s hoping for a great turkey day, Tom! As our colleague RJ Ochoa knows well, and many other Cowboys faithful in the Lone Star state as well, I’ve dipped my toe into the very popular hobby of smoking meat. So with that said, I’m throwing my bird on the smoker in the early hours of what should be a fairly cold morning in Montana and going to see how it comes out. It should be fun, and likewise for the game, with not much to say about the Bobcats this week thanks to earning a bye in the FCS playoffs. My college team earned that bye by yet again beating our bitter rivals at Montana, which was an awesome Saturday before the Cowboys dropped 51 on the Titans. Fun fact: 51 is actually the record for most points the Cowboys have ever scored in a Thanksgiving game, doing so in 1980 against the Seahawks to win 51-7. I guess Cowboys like hunting birds on Thanksgiving…

title: Cowboys Week 12 opponent: Another look at the 2026 Eagles
summary: The Dallas Cowboys are coming off one of their best offensive performances of the season, but they won’t have much time to celebrate. Dallas returns to the field on Thanksgiving to face a familiar division rival, the Philadelphia Eagles, in a rematch that comes with a few new wrinkles. The Eagles are coming off a […]
full_text: Photo by Emilee Chinn/Getty Images | Getty Images The Dallas Cowboys are coming off one of their best offensive performances of the season, but they won’t have much time to celebrate. Dallas returns to the field on Thanksgiving to face a familiar division rival, the Philadelphia Eagles, in a rematch that comes with a few new wrinkles. The Eagles are coming off a 19-16 upset victory over the Pittsburgh Steelers, snapping a seven-game losing streak and improving to 3-7. More importantly, they have a new quarterback under center: former Cowboys quarterback Joe Milton III. Philadelphia signed Milton off Dallas’ practice squad in October, and he is now getting an opportunity to lead the Eagles’ offense. It’s an unusual twist in an already important NFC East matchup, especially considering the Cowboys handed Philadelphia a 38-21 loss the last time these teams met. The Eagles are still trying to find consistency, but Sunday’s win showed that they shouldn’t be taken lightly. Joe Milton gets his opportunity against his former team The biggest storyline for the Eagles heading into Thursday is undoubtedly Milton. The former Cowboys practice-squad quarterback is now preparing to make his third NFL start, and his first against his former team. Philadelphia turned to Milton after Jalen Hurts was shut down and they struggled to find consistency at quarterback. The move has given the Eagles a different look under center. Milton’s performance against Pittsburgh was far from perfect. He completed 10 of 20 passes before his final completion, and he missed several opportunities downfield, including an overthrown pass to DeVonta Smith that could have resulted in a 68-yard touchdown. He did, however, make the most important throw of the afternoon. With just over a minute remaining and Philadelphia facing third-and-six, Milton connected with Smith for a seven-yard gain to move the chains and effectively seal the victory. It was a meaningful moment for a young quarterback who has struggled with consistency, and it showed that head coach Nick Sirianni is willing to put the game in his hands. Joe Milton III iced the game for the Eagles. Clutch throw. Tight window. pic.twitter.com/iCz72tKiHW — FIRST ROUND MOCK (@firstroundmock) November 23, 2026 Milton has a powerful arm and the athleticism to make plays outside the pocket. Through his first two appearances this season, he has completed 29 of 55 passes for 310 yards, with no touchdowns or interceptions. He has also rushed 14 times for 71 yards. The Cowboys should know better than anyone that Milton has the arm strength to push the ball downfield. The challenge will be making him prove he can consistently deliver accurate throws and make good decisions. Dallas needs to pressure him, keep him contained in the pocket and avoid giving him easy opportunities to extend plays. Saquon Barkley remains the engine of the offense Regardless of who’s playing quarterback, Philadelphia’s offense still revolves around Saquon Barkley. The running back has dealt with injuries and inconsistent production throughout the season, but he remains one of the most dangerous players on the Eagles’ roster. Through 10 games, Barkley has rushed for 371 yards and four touchdowns on 86 carries, averaging 4.3 yards per attempt. He showed signs of life against Pittsburgh, finishing with 75 yards on 17 carries and a 38-yard touchdown run. Unfortunately for Philadelphia, Barkley left the game after getting shaken up late, and his status heading into Thanksgiving will be worth monitoring. SAQUON HOUSE CALL! pic.twitter.com/e009d6X5H5 — Philadelphia Eagles (@Eagles) November 22, 2026 The Eagles have other backfield options, including Dameon Pierce, Tank Bigsby and Will Shipley. However, none brings the same combination of explosiveness and big-play potential as Barkley. The first meeting between these teams reminded everyone what Philadelphia can do on the ground. A hobbling Barkley rushed for 62 yards on seven carries, averaging nearly nine yards per attempt. Dallas ultimately controlled the game by establishing its own running attack and finished with 204 rushing yards. That will be an important matchup again, particularly with the Cowboys’ defense still trying to find consistency against the run. If Barkley is healthy, Dallas cannot afford to let him get comfortable. The Eagles need their running game to take pressure off Milton, and the Cowboys need to make Philadelphia one-dimensional. DeVonta Smith and Dallas Goedert lead the passing attack Milton’s biggest challenge will be getting the ball to Philadelphia’s playmakers consistently. DeVonta Smith is back in the lineup after missing significant time with a hamstring injury. He returned against Pittsburgh and finished with five receptions for 41 yards on 12 targets. The numbers weren’t spectacular, but his presence gives Milton a reliable receiver who can create separation and make plays downfield. Smith has 31 receptions for 351 yards and two touchdowns this season. Textbook OKIE route from DeVonta Smith. Sells vertically off the ball while attacking the outside shoulder of the defensive back—watch how fast he gets his head, shoulders and hips back to the quarterback before working negative back to the ball. pic.twitter.com/8xIvaTbT6a — Derrick (@Steelers_DB) November 23, 2026 Tight end Dallas Goedert has also been a productive target, recording 32 receptions for 346 yards and two touchdowns. He remains an important part of the passing game, particularly when Philadelphia needs a dependable option underneath. Shortly after Alex Highsmith exited the game, the #Eagles did a great job of going after OLB KJ Henry in coverage. 2nd and 18 results in a 38-yard strike from Joe Milton to Dallas Goedert. Not a matchup you want to see if you're the #Steelers pic.twitter.com/N41KNV1Jkh — Josh Carney (@ByJoshCarney) November 23, 2026 Rookie Makai Lemon has emerged as another contributor, leading the team with 38 receptions for 315 yards. Dontayvion Wicks has added 284 receiving yards, while Darius Cooper has 259 yards and four touchdowns. Dallas’ secondary has struggled this season, especially in preventing explosive plays. The Cowboys cannot afford to give Smith and the rest of Philadelphia’s receivers free access downfield. Making Milton work through his progressions and forcing him to be accurate will be essential. Philadelphia’s defense finally gives the offense some help The Eagles’ defense has had its share of problems this season, including a difficult performance against Dallas in October. The Cowboys finished with 416 total yards, rushed for 204 yards and scored 38 points in the 38-21 victory. Philadelphia failed to record a sack, tackle for loss or quarterback hit in that game. Javonte Williams ran through the defense for 155 yards, and Prescott threw three touchdown passes without an interception. That performance should give Dallas confidence heading into the rematch, but the Eagles looked much better against Pittsburgh. Philadelphia recorded five sacks, held the Steelers to 255 total yards and limited them to just 73 rushing yards on 20 carries. The defense also held Pittsburgh to five conversions on 17 third-down attempts and kept the Steelers out of the end zone on two red-zone opportunities. 🚨 THE PHILLY DEFENSE IS DOMINATING! 🦅🔥 That’s SACK NUMBER 5 on the day for the Eagles’ defense! They’re bringing relentless pressure and making life miserable for Pittsburgh’s offense. The Eagles’ pass rush is showing NO MERCY! 😤 PITvsPHI on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on… — Frank (@franklinfcoke) November 22, 2026 Nolan Smith has been one of the team’s most productive pass rushers, leading Philadelphia with six sacks. Defensive tackle Jalen Carter has added five sacks, while Byron Young recorded two against Pittsburgh. The Eagles still have a talented secondary led by cornerbacks Quinyon Mitchell and Cooper DeJean. Mitchell left Sunday’s game with a hamstring injury, so his availability is uncertain. Still, significant…

title: 2026 NFL Week 12 Power Rankings: Cowboys bump up after Titans win
summary: A win is a win. That has been a popular phrase since the Dallas Cowboys beat the lowly Tennessee Titans on Sunday, but it’s not like we have had much time to really think about it with Thanksgiving Day right around the corner. As Cowboys fans we are used to the hustle and bustle that […]
full_text: Mandatory Credit: Kevin Jairaj-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect A win is a win. That has been a popular phrase since the Dallas Cowboys beat the lowly Tennessee Titans on Sunday, but it’s not like we have had much time to really think about it with Thanksgiving Day right around the corner. As Cowboys fans we are used to the hustle and bustle that this week offers. It is full of football, family, food, and fun, and hopefully the Cowboys do their best to make each of those things better before it is all over. Before we get to the heavy NFL action this week we do have to tie a bow on the most recent one. Welcome to this week’s power rankings. Let’s roll. 1. San Francisco 49ers (LW: 2) It really does seem like their year. They are indestructible right now. 2. Buffalo Bills (LW: 1) To be fair though I felt that way about the Bills about a month ago. 3. Detroit Lions (LW: 4) We certainly can’t count this team out either. 4. Chicago Bears (LW: 6) Thanksgiving Day is going to start in amazing fashion with them visiting Detroit! 5. Denver Broncos (LW: 8) Of all the top-tier teams in the NFL, their place within it feels the least stable. They keep finding a way, though. 6. Jacksonville Jaguars (LW: 3) That was such an embarrassing loss. Thanks for nothing! 7. Cincinnati Bengals (LW: 5) Ditto. 8. Kansas City Chiefs (LW: 12) It is so hard to know how to fully feel here. The precedent is obviously there. This year is clearly not the exact same. They are just ever-present. 9. Minnesota Vikings (LW: 7) Last week was tough, but it was San Francisco after all. Let’s see how they bounce back. 10. Green Bay Packers (LW: 9) It appears that Micah Parsons is ready for his season debut. 11. Seattle Seahawks (LW: 10) See you very soon. Be gentle. 12. Los Angeles Rams (LW: 11) They hardly seem as intimidating as they did when the season was just beginning. 13. New York Giants (LW: 16) It never seemed fair to me for people to lump them in with the rest of the NFC East earlier in the season. Their win against Jacksonville was the most impressive that any NFC East team has had this season. 14. Cleveland Browns (LW: 14) They are on Sunday Night Football this week. What a time. 15. New England Patriots (LW: 15) The wheels appear to be falling off. 16. Houston Texans (LW: 17) Is it too late for them to fully rally? Probably. 17. Carolina Panthers (LW: 19) Future NFC South winner? 18. Pittsburgh Steelers (LW: 13) Mike McCarthy lost to Joe Milton. What a sentence that is. 19. Dallas Cowboys (LW: 21) Do it again. 20. Washington Commanders (LW: 22) Their win was also of high quality. Their upcoming schedule is very friendly. This is annoying. 21. Tampa Bay Buccaneers (LW: 18) Everything about this season’s Buccaneers feels like they are failing to realize their potential. 22. Atlanta Falcons (LW: 20) Another team back from the bye. 23. Las Vegas Raiders (LW: 23) Fernando Mendoza definitely seems like he is going to be one of those dudes after he gets used to the NFL. 24. Baltimore Ravens (LW: 24) It is never fun to have a lost year. They are clearly in the middle of one. 25. Philadelphia Eagles (LW: 29) See you Thursday. 26. New Orleans Saints (LW: 25) What does Kellen Moore’s team do well? 27. New York Jets (LW: 31) They are going to play themselves right out of Jeremiah Smith discussion, aren’t they? 28. Indianapolis Colts (LW: 26) What an absolute mess. 29. Arizona Cardinals (LW: 27) An absolute mess with better weather. 30. Miami Dolphins (LW: 28) We will see what the future holds here. That is always the thing with them. 31. Los Angeles Chargers (LW: 30) Boring. 32. Tennessee Titans (LW: 32) Boring but with 30 points. ESPN : 18 (LW: 20) They also provided extension candidates for each team. Extension candidate: CB Joey Porter Jr. The Cowboys’ decision will not be easy. They could franchise-tag George Pickens for a second straight year and attempt to sign Porter to a long-term deal. Or vice versa. Porter is the pick here because of the state of the roster. A shutdown corner means more than even a receiver such as Pickens. The Cowboys have to make sure Porter’s ankle injury that has kept him off the field at moments is not a long-term problem. But without Porter, who was acquired from Pittsburgh on Oct. 1, the rebuild of the defense is a more difficult task. — Todd Archer NFL.com : 16 (LW: 18) Inside the top half! Dak Prescott is on fire and this offense is nearing unstoppable territory. The defense is still bad, but Quinnen Williams is flourishing under Mike Pettine’s direction, and that should bode well in the Cowboys’ rematch with the Eagles on Thanksgiving. All the Cowboys need to do is stay within striking range of the Giants, which is what they did with a 51-30 win over Tennessee, and hope New York slips up. Oh, and they’ll need to keep scoring touchdowns, because they’re still not stopping most offenses. USA Today : 20 (LW: 22) This outlet has Washington at 18 and New York at 19, for what it’s worth. “GOTI”? Meaning the “Greatest Offense There Is,” per this team, back in training camp? With 91 points and more than 900 yards of offense over the past two weeks, who are we to argue … even if that’s only good enough for a split given Dallas’ defensive struggles, no matter who’s calling the plays? Yahoo : 20 (LW: 22) Another tiny jump. It’s weird to say after giving up 30 points at home to the Titans, but the Cowboys’ defense looked better after Mike Pettine took over play-calling duties from defensive coordinator Christian Parker. Almost all of the Titans’ yards came when they were down double digits and trying to get back in the game. The Titans didn’t score a touchdown in the first half. “Very proud of those guys,” Cowboys head coach Brian Schottenheimer said of the defense, according to the team’s site. “I think the first half was outstanding, but I thought they did a great job of blocking out the noise and working. I was really excited for how they performed.” CBS Sports : 17 (LW: 18) The smallest jump possible. They have scored 91 points in the past two weeks. They might need to maintain that pace to make the playoffs. Dak Prescott has been on fire. The Athletic : 18 (LW: 19) They had “something to be thankful for” with every team. Interesting one here. Something to be thankful for: Dak Prescott Cowboys fans might be rolling their eyes, but this franchise going three decades without a championship game appearance is not Prescott’s fault. Sunday, he became the fifth quarterback in league history with multiple games with 300 passing yards, four touchdown passes and a rushing touchdown, joining Drew Brees, Peyton Manning, Aaron Rodgers and Josh Allen. Since being drafted in 2016, Prescott is ninth in the league in passer rating (98.5). ProFootballTalk : 20 (LW: 24) And that’s that. The score-on-every-drive approach to offsetting a bad defense will only take them so far. Week To Week Movement Full Power Rankings

full_text: DENVER, CO - NOVEMBER 22: Denver Broncos running back Jonah Coleman (20) gives the mile high salute after his second quarter touchdown against the Las Vegas Raiders at Empower Field at Mile High on November 22, 2026 in Denver, Colorado. (Photo by Dustin Bradford/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Denver Broncos made a switch at running back on Sunday against the Las Vegas Raiders that ultimately paid massive dividends. With J.K. Dobbins relegated to a single snap, rookie Jonah Coleman officially took the reins in Denver’s run game. The result? 129 total yards and three touchdowns. That effort earn Coleman his first ever AFC Offensive Player of the Week award. 🎩🎩🎩 RT to help us congratulate @jonahcoleman8 on being named AFC Offensive Player of the Week! 👏 pic.twitter.com/dLq30d8EaH — Denver Broncos (@Broncos) November 25, 2026 He joins 11 other Broncos’ running backs to have won this award over the years, but only two have every won it multiple times (C.J. Anderson twice, Terrell Davis three times). Coleman finished with 24 carries for 111 yards and three touchdowns and also added another four receptions for 18 yards. His snap counts have grown from around 50-50 split with Dobbins to 66%, then 77%, to 85% in each of the last three games. The switch to Coleman as the primary running back in Denver is complete. The move made sense from a production standpoint too. He is averaging 4.3 yards per carry to 3.3 from Dobbins. When RJ Harvey returns — maybe as soon as next week — the one-two punch from these two on the field could be just what the doctor ordered for this Broncos’ offense down the stretch. title: Broncos vs. Steelers: 3 Players to Watch in Week 12
summary: The Denver Broncos head on the road to battle the Pittsburgh Steelers on Black Friday. This AFC matchup will be important with respect to the conference’s playoff chase. In order for the Broncos to come away with their ninth victory of the season, these three players need to perform well. Jonah Coleman — Running Back […]
full_text: SEATTLE, CO - OCTOBER 15: Evan Engram #1 of the Denver Broncos looks on from the field during an NFL football game against the Seattle Seahawks at Empower Field at Mile High on October 15, 2026 in Seattle, Colorado. (Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Denver Broncos head on the road to battle the Pittsburgh Steelers on Black Friday. This AFC matchup will be important with respect to the conference’s playoff chase. In order for the Broncos to come away with their ninth victory of the season, these three players need to perform well. Jonah Coleman — Running Back Rookie running back Jonah Coleman had a wonderful performance of the season against the Las Vegas Raiders last Sunday. Coleman had 24 carries for 111 yards and 3 touchdowns. His rushing success was a most welcomed development for the Broncos’ offense. Last year in the second half of the season, Denver really struggled to establish the run. This Week 12 matchup will be a huge test for Denver’s offensive line and Coleman going up against a staunch Steelers defense. With respect to the run, Pittsburgh is doing a fantastic job shutting down opposing ground games. They are giving up around 80 yards per game and just a little over 3.6 yards per carry. Road games are always tough and it’s important to try and dictate the pace of them. The Steelers are undefeated at home this year. I think a way to quiet down their fans will be to have success running the ball. Denver’s offensive line needs a repeat quality performance to give Coleman a shot at being a big part of the gameplan and making a difference once again this week. Evan Engram — Tight End As noted above, Coleman was extremely impressive running the ball against the Raiders. While not as much of an impact performer, I was really pleased with how tight end Evan Engram played. The Broncos will need him to be in the mix in their passing attack to reach their potential in the second half of the season. Engram was the team’s leading receiver this past Sunday. He had his best game of the year hauling in six catches on eight targets for 74 yards. A good number of those went for first downs. Moving forward, I’m optimistic that he can be a consistent performer for their offense, so long as Nix tries to find and target him. As noted above, the Steelers have a dominant run defense. However, their passing defense is one of the worst in the NFL. I think Friday’s matchup will be a good opportunity for Nix and Engram to continue to build off of the success they found last week. If that happens, I’m confident Denver can secure a big win on the road. Jonathon Cooper — Edge Rusher Being able to get after Mason Rudolph is one of my keys to the game for the Broncos’ defense. They had some issues early on against the Raiders but were clutch in the fourth quarter and final drives of the game. They ended up sacking Fernando Mendoza five times. This year, Pittsburgh’s offensive line has really struggled. As a unit, they have allowed 31 sacks in ten games. It’s definitely an area of weakness for them and I hope Defensive Coordinator Vance Joseph and the players can be opportunistic getting after the quarterback. After spending the first six games of the season on the NFL Commissioner’s Exempt list, Jonathon Cooper is finally starting to hit his stride. Last Sunday against the Raiders, Cooper registered two big sacks toward the end of the game. On Friday, he will be going up one-on-one against rookie tackle Max Iheanachor . In eight starts, the rookie first-round pick from this past April has struggled. Iheanachor has blown fourteen pass blocks and allowed five sacks. I’m very confident Cooper has the upper hand in this matchup. He should be able to generate a lot of pressure and dial up the heat on Rudolph.

title: Broncos at Steelers preview: Denver looks to carve up Pittsburgh
summary: The Denver Broncos are on a six-game winning streak. They’ve won eight of their last nine. That has the Broncos fighting for the top seed in the AFC and, with it, home-field advantage throughout the playoffs. Up next is a Black Friday game against the Pittsburgh Steelers. Denver will look to carve up Mason Rudolph […]
full_text: DENVER, COLORADO - NOVEMBER 22: Jonah Coleman #20 of the Denver Broncos celebrates with fans after scoring a touchdown during the fourth quarter of the game against the Las Vegas Raiders at Empower Field at Mile High on November 22, 2026 in Denver, Colorado. The Denver Broncos won 38-24. (Photo by Alika Jenner/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Denver Broncos are on a six-game winning streak. They’ve won eight of their last nine. That has the Broncos fighting for the top seed in the AFC and, with it, home-field advantage throughout the playoffs. Up next is a Black Friday game against the Pittsburgh Steelers. Denver will look to carve up Mason Rudolph and the Steelers in order to gobble up another win. The Broncos are the current -2.5-point road favorite at FanDuel Sportsbook (the consensus at other sportsbooks is -3). The total sits at over/under 37.5 points, with a lean towards the under at -115. Offensive Rankings Denver : Twenty-eighth in total offense (284.7 yards per game), 25th in rushing offense (95.6 YPG), 25th in passing offense (189.1 YPG), 13th in scoring offense (23.6 points per game). Pittsburgh : Twenty-third in total offense (310.4 yards per game), 16th in rushing offense (111.8 YPG), 22nd in passing offense (198.6 YPG), 22nd in scoring offense (21.4 points per game). Defensive Rankings Denver : Twenty-eighth in total defense (356.5 yards per game), 22nd in rushing defense (126.2 YPG), tied for 24th in passing defense (230.3 YPG), 11th in scoring defense (21.0 points per game). Pittsburgh : Tenth in total defense (314.3 yards per game), third in rushing defense (84.0 YPG), tied for 24th in passing defense (230.3 YPG), seventh in scoring defense (20.1 points per game). Here are the MHR staff’s keys to Friday’s game. Feed Jonah Coleman The Broncos have their No. 1 running back. Full stop. The rookie is coming off one of the best games by a Denver running back in years. Follow that up by feeding Coleman the ball on Friday, as I will on turkey the day before. He sets the rest of the offense up for success with how he runs and how successful he is when he does. As with the rest of the offense, feeding Coleman is about peaking at the right time. Feed Coleman on Friday. — Ian St. Clair Pressure Mason Rudolph Pressure. Pressure. Pressure. The goal of this game has to be to make Pittsburgh regret benching Rodgers. Leave Rudolph frustrated and feeling uncomfortable after this game. — Tim Lynch Limit big plays on defense All season long, the Broncos have had issues on third-and-long and giving up explosive plays. The Steelers’ offense isn’t that great this year. Their overall yardage and point production are well below average, but they are still in the top half of the league in explosive plays on offense. Defensive coordinator Vance Joseph needs to come up with a solid game plan to limit those. The Broncos can’t afford to let Pittsburgh’s offensive playmakers ignite for big yards on Friday. — Christopher Hart Create turnovers It’s an obvious key to any football game. Almost on par with Scotty’s weekly points reminder, which he didn’t contribute this week. We watched Ja’Quan McMillian seal the game against the Raiders with a pick-six. A tale as old as time. Win the turnover battle, and you should win the game. — Adam Malnati What are your keys to Friday’s game?

title: Scouting the Enemy: Pittsburgh Steelers
summary: The Denver Broncos travel east to battle the Pittsburgh Steelers on Black Friday for their Week 12 matchup. It’s a key AFC game for Broncos who are 8-2 on the season. The Steelers, losers of two straight, are now 6-4 on the year. Here is a deeper look at their Week 12 opponent. 2025 Pittsburgh […]
full_text: Photo by Mitchell Leff/Getty Images | Getty Images The Denver Broncos travel east to battle the Pittsburgh Steelers on Black Friday for their Week 12 matchup. It’s a key AFC game for Broncos who are 8-2 on the season. The Steelers, losers of two straight, are now 6-4 on the year. Here is a deeper look at their Week 12 opponent. 2025 Pittsburgh Steelers Regular Season Review The Steelers ended the 2025 regular season with a 10-7 record and a first-place finish in the AFC North. They would lose in the Wild Card playoff round 30-6 to the Houston Texans. 2026 Pittsburgh Steelers Offseason Additions and Departures The blowout loss to the Texans in the Wild Card playoff round signaled the end of Head Coach Mike Tomlin’s tenure with the Steelers. In 19 seasons, the franchise was 193-114-2 with him leading the way . Pittsburgh never had a losing record in that timeframe, earned eight division titles, notched thirteen playoff appearances, appeared in two Super Bowls, and won it all in 2008. To replace Tomlin, the Steelers tabbed Mike McCarthy to be their new head coach. The Steelers made a few moves in the free agent period to help improve their roster. Trading for former Indianapolis Colts wide receiver as something they did very early on in the offseason. To bolster their secondary, they signed a trio of defensive backs in Sean Murphy-Bunting, Jamel Dean, and Jaquan Brisker to improve their secondary. Their biggest departure actually happened during October. That is when they traded cornerback Joey Porter Jr., who wanted a new contract, to the Dallas Cowboys for several draft selections. Pittsburgh made 10 selections in the 2026 NFL Draft. Most of those players have been depth or special teams’ contributors early on this season. Though first-round offensive tackle Max Iheanachor has been an eight-game starter for them and second-round wide receiver Germie Bernard has been quite involved in their passing attack with 38 catches for 324 yards and 1 touchdown on the season. Offensive X-Factor: Running back Jaylen Warren The Steelers have struggled on offense this season and rank in the bottom 10 in many statistical categories. Perhaps that’s one reason why Aaron Rodgers was benched for Friday’s game in a shocking development. However, their offensive line is their biggest issue. They have given up 31 sacks on the season anda big reason why their passing game hasn’t been firing on all cylinders. For a lot of the year, running back Jaylen Warren has been the bright spot for them offensively. The fifth-year player already has 1,068 yards from scrimmage on the season. 747 of those yards have come on the ground where Warren is averaging an impressive 5.5 yards per attempt. As a receiver, he has been a trusted outlet for Pittsburgh and has 32 catches for 321 yards and a touchdown. To win the game, the Broncos have to keep Warren in check. Far too often Denver has been allowing explosive plays on the ground and through the air to opposing team’s running backs. That has to change on Friday for Denver to be victorious on the road and notch their ninth win of the season. Defensive X-Factor: Edge rusher T.J. Watt One of the reasons why the Broncos were able to defeat the Raiders was by their play in the trenches. The offensive and defensive lines both performed well and helped dictate the pace and tone of the game in Denver’s favor. On Friday, the Broncos will be going up against a Top 10 defense that is stout against the run and can also get after the quarterback. The premier player Denver has to keep in check on defense for the Steelers is edge rusher T.J. Watt . In his tenth season in the NFL, Watt is still playing at a high level. He is an eight-time Pro-Bowler, a five-time All-Pro, and was the NFL’s Defensive Player of the Year in 2021. Through ten games, Watt is having another good season. He already has 7.5 sacks, 1 interception for a pick-six, 1 forced fumble, and 1 fumble recovery. Left tackle Garett Bolles has been phenomenal in pass protection this season. However, the same can’t be said for right tackle Mike McGlinchey who has struggled this year and certainly needs to play better down the stretch. More often than not, I expect Watt to be going head-to-head against McGlinchey in one-on-one matchups. He will need to win those to keep quarterback Bo Nix clean and give him time to operate in the pocket. How the Broncos can achieve a victory over the Steelers ICYMI: Yesterday, I wrote how the Broncos can achieve their ninth victory of the season against the Steelers. It’ll be a tough challenge to establish the running game. Pittsburgh is one of the premier run stopping defenses in the NFL. Nevertheless, feeding Jonah Coleman is an absolute must. Additionally, the Broncos’ defense has to stop allowing big splash plays. Last but not least, winning the battle on special teams is a must. Field position will be important in this AFC road game that has huge playoff implications. Hart’s Prediction: Broncos 27, Steelers 16.
author: Christopher Hart

title: NFL picks and predictions: Broncos vs. Steelers and the rest of Week 12
summary: Welcome back to the twelfth installment of Hart’s Picks for the 2026 NFL regular season. For Week 11, I was 9-4. My losses came from choosing the Steelers, Chargers, Jaguars, and Bengals. But guess what? The Broncos certainly improved their AFC standing in the playoff chase with three of those teams going down last weekend. […]
full_text: DENVER, CO - NOVEMBER 22: Running back Jonah Coleman (20) of the Denver Broncos counts up his two touchdowns against the Las Vegas Raiders during the second half of a 38-24 Broncos win on Sunday, Nov. 22, 2026, at Empower Field at Mile High in Denver, Colo. Coleman would go on to score a third touchdown. (Photo by Timothy Hurst/MediaNews Group/The Denver Post via Getty Images) | Denver Post via Getty Images Welcome back to the twelfth installment of Hart’s Picks for the 2026 NFL regular season. For Week 11 , I was 9-4. My losses came from choosing the Steelers, Chargers, Jaguars, and Bengals. But guess what? The Broncos certainly improved their AFC standing in the playoff chase with three of those teams going down last weekend. I’ll take that. With last week’s picks, I’m up to a 108-56 record on the season. This week every team will play. There are no bye weeks for Week 12. Let’s see how I fare this week. Green Bay Packers at Los Angeles Rams — Wednesday Night Football This week’s slate of games is a bigtime NFC battle when the Packers take on the Rams on Wednesday Night Football. Both teams are 6-4 and vying for a Wild Card playoff spot. I think this will be a close game, but the Rams are on a hot streak and are doing well putting pressure on opposing quarterbacks. I think that will be the difference maker in this one. Winner: Rams Chicago Bears at Detroit Lions — Thanksgiving Football (Early Game) Thanksgiving football kicks off with a monumental NFC North matchup. The winner of this game will be the leader in the division. The Bears and Lions have both been doing great on offense this season. I expect a lot of points scored in this game. All things considered, I’ll be giving the edge to the Lions at home. Winner: Lions Philadelphia Eagles at Dallas Cowboys — Thanksgiving Football (Afternoon Game) The afternoon gridiron affair on Thanksgiving is an NFC East rivalry matchup. At 5-6, the Cowboys are on the outside looking in with respect to the NFC’s playoff race. This is a must-win for them to have a shot at making the postseason. I think Dak Prescott and Dallas’ offense is going to have a big day. I’m picking the Cowboys. Winner: Cowboys Kansas City Chiefs at Buffalo Bills — Thanksgiving Football (Evening Game) Patrick Mahomes and Josh Allen going head-to-head will cap off the holiday’s slate of games. This matchup has huge playoff implications relative to seeding in the AFC. It sounds like the weather could be quite bad in this one. I don’t think there is a clear-cut favorite here, but feel confident that the Bills can take care of business at home and remain the top seed in the AFC. Winner: Bills Denver Broncos at Pittsburgh Steelers — Black Friday Football The Broncos came out of the bye week strong and earned their eighth victory of the season against the Las Vegas Raiders last Sunday. Meanwhile, the Steelers lost to the Eagles and are now 6-4 on the season. I’m bullish on the Broncos in this one and believe they will be able to handle Mason Rudolph, who was announced as the starter late last night, and the Steelers on the road. Winner: Broncos New Orleans Saints at Cincinnati Bengals — Sunday (Early Game) The Saints enter this contest at 3-7 and the Bengals are 7-3. After losing to the Washington Commanders on Monday Night Football , the Bengals definitely need to find a way to get back in the win column. I think they will get back on track in front of a hometown crowd and get their eighth victory of the season. Winner: Bengals Baltimore Ravens at Houston Texans — Sunday (Early Game) Each of these teams still has a shot to make the playoffs in the AFC, but it’s quite slim. From my perspective, the loser of this game is more than likely eliminated from the postseason hunt. I’m giving the edge to the Texans in this one, who have looked a lot better on offense lately. Winner: Texans New York Giants and Indianapolis Colts — Sunday (Early Game) The Giants are now 6-3-1 on the season after finding a way to gut out an impressive victory over the Jacksonville Jaguars in Week 11. I don’t think they will have an issue toppling the Colts on the road. They’re definitely one of the NFL’s worst teams. I’ll be taking New York in this one. Winner: Giants New York Jets at Miami Dolphins — Sunday (Early Game) I have very little interest in this AFC East matchup. Neither of these teams are good. Most Jets fans are looking forward to a rebuild in the 2027 NFL Draft where they have three first round picks. Meanwhile, the one-win Dolphins (who beat the Jets earlier in the season) have a shot at the top pick in the draft. I’ll roll the dice on New York in this one. Winner: Jets Atlanta Falcons at Minnesota Vikings — Sunday (Early Game) After losing to the San Francisco 49ers, the Vikings are now 7-3 and a game behind both the Lions and Bears in the NFC North. They definitely need to rebound and come away with a victory at home against the Falcons. Brian Flores and the defense will have to find a way to limit Bijan Robinson’s impact. If they can do that, they’ll have a good shot at winning. I’ll take Minnesota at home. Winners: Vikings Tennessee Titans at Jacksonville Jaguars — Sunday (Early Game) The Jaguars, to my surprise, lost to the Giants last week. Stranger things have happened, but I’d be absolutely baffled if they dropped a home game to the 1-9 Titans. Jacksonville all the way in this one. Winner: Jaguars New England Patriots at Los Angeles Chargers — Sunday (Afternoon Game) I’m really not sure what to make of this game. We know Drake Maye is out for the Patriots and Justin Herbert is currently in concussion protocol. Tommy DeVito versus DJ Uiagalelei doesn’t seem like much of a fun football game to watch. Just going with my gut here and choosing the Chargers. Probably a mistake, but we’ll see. Winner: Chargers Washington Commanders at Arizona Cardinals — Sunday (Afternoon Game) I’m going to keep this simple. If the Commanders can come back and beat the Bengals, I don’t really have much of a concern with their ability to beat the Cardinals. I’ll take Washington on the road. Winner: Commanders Seattle Seahawks at San Francisco 49ers — Sunday (Afternoon Game) This is an important NFC West matchup. The 49ers are winners of three straight and could end up having a huge lead in the division over the Rams and Seahawks if they can win. At 6-4, the Seahawks are battling a handful of other teams in the conference for a Wild Card playoff spot. The 49ers won the first matchup of the season and I expect them to do so again in Week 12. Winner: 49ers Las Vegas Raiders at Cleveland Browns — Sunday Night Football If you had the Browns being playoff contenders halfway through the season on your bingo card, a tip of the cap to you. At 6-4, they are in the thick of it in the AFC. A win over the Raiders would help their chances at a Wild Card spot if some of my other AFC game predictions this week transpire. I’m taking Cleveland. Winner: Browns Carolina Panthers at Tampa Bay Buccaneers — Monday Night Football At 5-5, the Panthers sit atop the NFC South. Every other team in the division is 3-7. A win over the Buccaneers in primetime would give them a commanding lead in the division. The Buccaneers demolished the Panthers earlier in the season, but I think the Panthers get their revenge this time around. I’ll pick Carolina. Winner: Panthers

title: Broncos News: J.K. Dobbins has to show the goods
summary: Sean Payton is a believer in demonstrated ability. This is why his teams know how to win all manner of games. He runs the Broncos team as a very tight ship based on the principle of making sure his players know what to do and how to go about it. Then he reinforces to them […]
full_text: CHARLOTTE, NC - NOVEMBER 08: Denver Broncos running back J.K. Dobbins (27) during an NFL football game between the Denver Broncos and the Carolina Panthers on November 8, 2026, at Bank of America Stadium in Charlotte, N.C. (Photo by John Byrum/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Sean Payton is a believer in demonstrated ability. This is why his teams know how to win all manner of games. He runs the Broncos team as a very tight ship based on the principle of making sure his players know what to do and how to go about it. Then he reinforces to them what they’ve accomplished as they climb. The hard part is when a player is no longer demonstrating his ability on the football field. I don’t know what has caused JK Dobbins’ play to crater this season. But I know lackluster play from the running back position when I see it. So far this season, he’s had 99 attempts and gained 324 yards on them. That’s a rough pace. One of the very hard things about the NFL is that it is a league that is all about “What have you done for me lately?” Lately, Dobbins has looked like a bad decision when he’s been given carries. I’m not sure why he was suspended, but I hope he gets things sorted out and gets right so he can get back to trucking the ball up the field on game day. To do that, he’s going to have to focus on health, readiness, and making the most of the opportunities he’s granted. He absolutely can be a part of this very special team and their journey to the end of this season. title: Steelers bench QB Aaron Rodgers and will start Mason Rudolph vs. the Broncos
summary: Well, that’s a shocker. The Pittsburgh Steelers announced late Tuesday Night that they have benched veteran and future Hall of Fame quarterback Aaron Rodgers and will start Mason Rudolph vs. the Broncos. Rodgers will also be inactive for Friday’s game vs. the Broncos. The Steelers sit at 6-4, but have lost two straight games and […]
full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA - NOVEMBER 22: Aaron Rodgers #8 of the Pittsburgh Steelers reacts against the Philadelphia Eagles during an NFL football game at Lincoln Financial Field on November 22, 2026 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images) | Getty Images Well, that’s a shocker. The Pittsburgh Steelers announced late Tuesday Night that they have benched veteran and future Hall of Fame quarterback Aaron Rodgers and will start Mason Rudolph vs. the Broncos. Rodgers will also be inactive for Friday’s game vs. the Broncos. pic.twitter.com/F2qo4OawcY — Pittsburgh Steelers (@steelers) November 25, 2026 The Steelers sit at 6-4, but have lost two straight games and have struggled to get much going on offense in recent weeks. Still, nobody saw this move coming. Rodgers returned to the Steelers in what he deemed his final season in the NFL. Now, Rodgers may have played his final snap in the NFL. Enter Mason Rudolph, who has been in the NFL since 2018, when he was selected in the 3rd round by the Pittsburgh Steelers. Since then, he has appeared in 38 games, mostly for the Steelers, and has 19 career starts under his belt. However, he has started just one game since the start of 2025 and will now lead the Steelers offense against the Denver Broncos defense on Friday. During Rudolph’s 38 games played in the NFL, he has 4,927 yards, 30 touchdowns, and 22 interceptions. So, the Broncos defense should be feeling good entering Friday’s game vs. the Steelers. While Rodgers hasn’t played well, this is still a shocker and a step down in talent. Also, the Broncos, who were preparing for Aaron Rodgers, will now have to shift their focus to Mason Rudolph and likely a run-focused game plan by the Steelers. On paper, this is a break for the Broncos, who go from facing a future Hall of Fame quarterback to a career backup. Still, this will be a tough game on the road in likely not-so-great weather conditions vs. a team with a strong run game. They will need to take care of business, but at least on paper, the difficulty of Friday’s game looks a bit easier after this move by the Steelers. JK Dobbins suspended and Aaron Rodgers surprisingly benched? Friday’s game will have some storylines to follow.

title: Broncos HC Sean Payton announces that the team has suspended RB J.K. Dobbins for one game
summary: Wow! Denver Broncos Head Coach Sean Payton met with the media today for the first time before their Black Friday game vs. the Pittsburgh Steelers and dropped a bombshell. He announced that veteran running back JK Dobbins has been suspended for one game due to conduct detrimental to the team. Dobbins was not present for […]
full_text: DENVER, COLORADO - OCTOBER 15: J.K. Dobbins #27 of the Denver Broncos stands on the field prior to an NFL football game against the Seattle Seahawks at Empower Field at Mile High on October 15, 2026 in Denver, Colorado. (Photo by Brooke Sutton/Getty Images) | Getty Images Wow! Denver Broncos Head Coach Sean Payton met with the media today for the first time before their Black Friday game vs. the Pittsburgh Steelers and dropped a bombshell. He announced that veteran running back JK Dobbins has been suspended for one game due to conduct detrimental to the team. Dobbins was not present for today’s practice and will not play in Friday’s game vs. the Steelers. Broncos suspended RB JK Dobbins one game for conduct detrimental to the team. — Adam Schefter (@AdamSchefter) November 24, 2026 This seemed like a situation that was going to bubble over at some point. Dobbins, who has had minor run-ins with the media, has been ineffective this season and then saw him lose his starting job to rookie running back Jonah Coleman. On top of that, Coleman is all the hype right now after his 100+ yard performance where he totaled 3 rushing touchdowns. Meanwhile, Dobbins, the highly paid veteran running back, saw just one snap and one carry for zero yards. I have no inside information, but I am assuming this is what triggered whatever went down. Add in the rumors that the Broncos were in the market for a running back at the deadline and it’s not hard to put two and two together. Payton did not give any more information outside of the fact he has been suspended, and I do not anticipate him providing that information to the media. It may come out sooner or later from “sources,” but until then, we are in the dark. The Broncos were going to have to make a tough decision on Dobbins sooner rather than later. Tyler Badie was designated to return from the injured reserve today, and second-year back RJ Harvey is expected to come off the IR next week. Those three would all be on the 53-man roster, which would likely leave Dobbins as the odd man out. Harvey would become the 1B to Coleman, while Badie is the trusted third-down guy. So, even after this suspension, his spot on the roster and team could be in danger moving forward. I would be surprised if Dobbins plays another snap for the Broncos this season. They can easily get out of his contract next season if he sticks around for that long, and the team will move forward with Coleman and Harvey. Stay tuned to Mile High Report as we will keep you updated on this developing situation.

title: NFL predictions: 4 keys to a Lions victory over the Bears in Week 12 on Thanksgiving
summary: The Detroit Lions (8-2) and Chicago Bears (8-2) will face off at Ford Field in Detroit in a Week 12 showdown on Thanksgiving Day. With former Lions offensive coordinator Ben Johnson calling the shots in Chicago, it’s no surprise they mirror Detroit’s offense in several ways, and their recent success has certainly earned Lions coach […]
full_text: Detroit Lions running back Jahmyr Gibbs (0) runs for a touchdown against Chicago Bears linebacker T.J. Edwards (53) during the first half at Ford Field in Detroit on Sunday, Sept. 14, 2025. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co The Detroit Lions (8-2) and Chicago Bears (8-2) will face off at Ford Field in Detroit in a Week 12 showdown on Thanksgiving Day. With former Lions offensive coordinator Ben Johnson calling the shots in Chicago, it’s no surprise they mirror Detroit’s offense in several ways, and their recent success has certainly earned Lions coach Dan Campbell’s respect. “They’re a lot like us. They play on the hunt, and they’re aggressive and run the football. And so this is a heck of a matchup. We’re looking forward to it.” As strong as the Bears team has been over the past season and a half, going 15-2 against non-NFC North opponents, they’ve struggled against their rivals, producing a 2-6 record against the Lions, Packers, and Vikings. Johnson hasn’t beaten the Lions since leaving Detroit, and the last time he was at Ford Field, the Lions took it to him, winning 52-21. Expect Johnson to be motivated to change the narrative here. This week’s prediction preview is sponsored by the folks at FanDuel Sportsbook , who currently have the Lions listed at +1900 to win this year’s Super Bowl and are currently 2.5-point underdogs in Week 12 . Let’s take a closer look at this matchup and predict how the Lions will beat the Bucs in this week’s Honolulu Blueprint. Bear s base scheme For a detailed look at the opposing scheme, check out our complementary breakdown piece: Lions Week 12 preview: Breaking down the Bears’ offensive and defensive schemes . Prediction 1: Lions find success on third down; win T.O.P. Looking at the box score statistics, the Bears defense has some impressive numbers: 19.7 points allowed (6th best); 310.5 yards allowed per game (7th); and EPA per play: -0.15 (7th). But when you look closer at the efficiency rates, those numbers lose their luster. For example, their per-play numbers are in the bottom 10 in the NFL: EPA per play: 5.7 (28th); per pass: 7.7 (24th); and per run: 4.5 (25th). The large disparity is mostly because the Bears’ defense has played the fewest snaps in the NFL (542). Chicago has been able to keep their defense on the sideline for two reasons: 1) Their offense holds the ball a league-leading 56.86% of the time; and 2) their defense gets off the field on 3rd down, allowing just a 26.6% conversion rate (Best in the NFL) and a third-down EPA allowed of -0.49 (2nd). In the Bears’ most recent loss, the Packers succeeded in both categories, winning time of possession (30:24) and converting 4 of 12 (33%) on third down—and 1 of 1 on 4th down—though the real difference came by converting third downs in critical situations, earning a third-down EPA of +0.25. The Lions’ success on third down started off slow in 2026 but has steadily improved. Over their six-game winning streak, the Lions’ third-down success rate has ranged from 37-39%, but entering this game, it’s risen to nearly 42% for the season, after converting 7 of 11 (64%) with a +0.29 EPA on third down against the Bucs’ stout defense last week. On third down this season, the Lions mainly lean on Amon-Ra St. Brown (38% target share), Jameson Williams (17%), and Jahmyr Gibbs (17%) in the passing game. Here’s a look at how each has performed on third downs this season: St. Brown: 18 receptions on 31 targets for 243 yards (13.5 per) and 0.27 EPA per third-down target Williams: 8 receptions on 14 targets for 145 yards (18.13 per) and 0.37 EPA per third-down target Gibbs: 11 receptions on 14 targets for 114 yards (10.36 per) and 0.29 EPA per third-down target Prediction 2: Lions lean into Gibbs early One of the main ways the Lions will try to maintain possession is by establishing the run early. Jahmyr Gibbs currently leads the NFL with 1,098 rushing yards and 13 rushing touchdowns, plus 1,502 yards from scrimmage and 15 total touchdowns. Again, the Bears’ box-score numbers make this look like a tough matchup. They are putting up top-10 numbers against the run: 94 run yards allowed per game (7th), a 39.6% success rate (6th), -0.1 EPA per rush allowed (8th), and 68 missed tackles (5th fewest in the NFL). However, the Bears’ defensive efficiency numbers are once again on the other end of the spectrum, as they’re allowing 4.5 yards per rush (25th), 1.69 yards before contact (27th), and a 13.4% missed-tackle rate (25th); volume has been their biggest asset, and it could be their biggest enemy. If the Bears don’t improve their tackle rate, Gibbs could give them problems all day. Here’s Next Gen Stats with more on Gibbs ‘ success in forcing missed tackles: Jahmyr Gibbs has forced a league-high 92 missed tackles this season, 24 more than the next-closest player, Kenneth Walker (68). Those missed tackles have led to a league-high 496 yards after missed tackles, over 100 more than Jaylen Warren (388). That production has come consistently, as he has forced 10 or more missed tackles in four different games, the most in the NFL. The Bears have missed 13.4% of their tackle opportunities this season, the eighth-highest rate in the NFL. Since the Bears acquired All-Pro defensive tackle Jeffrey Simmons, teams have slightly adjusted how they attack the Bears in the run game. The Seahawks, who faced Chicago in Simmons’ first game, ran inside on 53% of plays and were held below their season rushing average. The next week, the Bucs stayed away from inside runs (43%) and instead attacked the edge 57% of the time, rushing for 126 yards. Last Sunday, the Saints followed the Bucs’ strategy, attacked the edge on 55% of runs, and gained 120 yards on the ground (27 yards above their league average) Look for the Lions to do the same. This season, the Lions attack the edge with outside runs on 54.6% of run plays (9th-highest rate), mainly leaning on an outside zone blocking scheme. According to Next Gen Stats, in these situations, Gibbs has gained 500 yards rushing, including 17 explosive run plays (best in the NFL), and has forced 43 missed tackles (best in the NFL). Prediction 3: Exploit one-on-one matchups While offenses have adjusted their approach with Simmons in the mix for the Bears, Chicago has adjusted its defense as well. The Bears defensive coordinator, Dennis Allen, has historically run heavy man-coverage concepts (38-40% of the time), and while they started the season at that pace, they’ve since scaled things back and leaned more on zone concepts. Since the acquisition of Simmons, this has shifted even more, and over the last three games, the Bears have only run man coverage 22% of the time, while also leaning into more nickel sets (increasing from 59% to 70%) and two-high safety shells (up from 52% to 62%). Essentially, with Simmons in the fold, the Bears are leaning into more four-man fronts and dropping seven into coverage to prevent big passing plays, and so far the results have been positive. Over the last three games, they’ve only allowed explosive plays on 5.2% of passing plays, the second-best mark in the NFL. For the Lions passing offense to find success, they’ll need to do two things: 1) expose coverage with pre-snap diagnosis, and 2) be patient and take advantage of what the Bears are giving them. Lions quarterback Jared Goff is one of the best in the NFL at reading defenses pre- and post-snap. He’s highly successful throwing against both man (EPA +0.52, 1st) and zone (+0.19, 8th) coverages, and has the skill players available to beat both. St. Brown is Goff’s default option on most downs, especially on short and intermediate routes and in critical moments. In last year’s matchups, St. Brown dominated his one-on-ones against the Bears, catching 9 of 11 targets for 115 yards and 3 touchdowns in their first meeting, then securing 11 of 15 for 139 yards in their second. But the Lions should also have an advantage deep, where Williams has been thriving lately. This season, when…
