title: How much better is the Texans offense than last season?
summary: Thursday night games throw off the schedule a little. The rearview mirror feature comes on the previous Friday which opens up a hole in the Value of Things week. However, these holes provide us with a unique opportunity to finish a thought we started on Monday. The big question was whether the offense or defense […]
full_text: HOUSTON, TEXAS - NOVEMBER 19: Marlin Klein #83 celebrates with C.J. Stroud #7 of the Houston Texans after scoring a touchdown during the third quarter of an NFL football game against the Indianapolis Colts at NRG Stadium on November 19, 2026 in Houston, Texas. (Photo by Kevin Sabitus/Getty Images) | Getty Images Thursday night games throw off the schedule a little. The rearview mirror feature comes on the previous Friday which opens up a hole in the Value of Things week. However, these holes provide us with a unique opportunity to finish a thought we started on Monday. The big question was whether the offense or defense was more responsible for the team’s struggles in the early going? As you might imagine, there is no single answer to that question. These answers come in a game by game basis and the basic numbers say something different than the more advanced analytics. We will look at both in this go around. The general idea is to look at the basic numbers on a game by game and aggregate basis. Those would include points, total yards, passing yards, rushing yards, and turnovers. Once we have established ourselves there we can move onto the more possession by possession statistics that we looked at for the defense last time around. Let’s start with the basics. Points Total Yards Rush Yards Pass Yards Turnovers Bills 31 381 124 257 2 Bengals 6 374 60 314 0 Colts 17 223 70 153 0 Cowboys 30 397 62 335 0 Titans 26 329 79 250 0 Jaguars 34 426 114 312 1 Giants 21 237 84 153 0 Chargers 44 485 104 381 1 Browns 24 290 88 202 1 Colts 26 354 167 187 1 Total 25.9 349.6 95.2 254.4 0.6 As in most things, this becomes a good news/bad news kind of deal. The good news is that the team in general is much better at putting points on the board than they were a year ago. The Texans set the record for field goals in 2025. They aren’t going to get there this season at their current pace. They have scored far more touchdowns than they did a season ago. So, their points per game average is higher and is in the top ten in the league in that department. They are generally gaining yards as well and limiting turnovers. So, in the grand scheme of things, when you are scoring points, gaining yards, and limiting turnovers it seems foolish to suggest that the offense is the problem. This is the natural difference when we view the world through the aggregate and when we view it at game level. Like with the defense, the offense has coasted on several huge offensive games to make the whole seem greater than the sum of the parts. Six of the ten games have seen 350 or more total yards and four of the ten games have seen 30 or more points. Let’s see what happens when we break it down by possession. Possessions YPP Punts TO 4th PCT Bills 11 34.6 4 2 0 45.5 Bengals 11 34.0 5 0 4 18.2 Colts 9 24.8 5 0 1 33.3 Cowboys 10 39.7 4 0 0 60.0 Titans 8 41.1 2 0 0 75.0 Jaguars 10 42.6 3 1 0 60.0 Giants 10 23.7 6 0 0 40.0 Chargers 12 40.4 3 1 0 66.7 Browns 13 22.3 7 1 1 30.8 Colts 9 39.3 3 1 1 44.4 Total 10.3 33.9 4.2 0.6 0.7 46.6 A couple of points come forward that should be explored. The Texans have surrendered points on a higher percentage of possessions than they have scored. Yet. they have scored more points than they have surrendered. That means that their defense is doing a better job of holding their opponents to field goals. The offense is also doing a good job of putting the ball in the end zone. So, no set of numbers is going to be all good or all bad. It is always going to cut both ways. On four occasions, the Texans offense has scored on more than half of their possessions. Compare that with the defense that allowed a 50 percent rate or higher four times. What is interesting is that the Texans are 3-1 in games where they scored on 50 percent or more times. They were 0-4 when they allowed a 50 percent or higher rate. They are sixth in the NFL with 42 points. So, while they haven’t turned it over when you combine their punts with the fact that they are 31st in fourth down conversions. So, the Texans offense is a tale of two teams. On the one hand, they are scoring more points and gaining more yards than they did a season ago. On the other hand, there are definite situations where they get bogged down and those situations have contributed to the problems on defense. Bill O’Brien always talked about complimentary football. It got to be annoying after awhile, but he wasn’t wrong. When you punt more often and go three and out in particular you are putting more pressure on your defense. We have seen this play out often in the last two years. It would be instructive to look at the basic and more advanced numbers from the last two seasons along with the situational ones. PPG TYPG RYPG PYPG TO/G 2025 23.8 327.0 108.9 218.1 0.7 2026 25.9 349.6 95.2 254.4 0.6 Is this a better offense? On balance you would have to say so based on these numbers. They are scoring more points, gaining more yards, and turning the ball over fewer times. What’s not to like? Obviously, the rushing attack is the one thing that is not to like. There is more than one way to look at those numbers though. We could say the running attack is worse or we could say they are leaning into the passing attack more. That by itself would be a sign of progress. Still, are they scoring on the same number of a possessions. This time we are altering the numbers slightly to include missed field goals in the failed possessions. It will also change the number of yards per possession. Let’s see what happens when we break things down on a per possession basis. Are the Texans actually any better than they were a season ago? Possessions Points YPP Punts TO 4th PCT 2025 177 81 31.4 72 12 8 45.8 2026 104 48 33.6 42 6 7 46.2 So, the 2026 Texans are slightly better, but some would consider the difference to be statistical noise. So, the main difference in this year’s team is simply that they are better at scoring touchdowns. That’s not nothing, but when the final epitaph on this season and this offense is told, we should report the facts and give them the weight they deserve. This is a better offense, but it might be tough to call it a good one all things considered.

title: Colts announce tough injury update on promising rookie edge Caden Curry
summary: On Wednesday, Indianapolis Colts head coach Shane Steichen announced that rookie defensive end Caden Curry will be out for the remainder of the 2026 season because of his recently surgically repaired wrist: The local Center Grove product had a promising rookie debut, fighting his way as a 6th round pick out of Ohio State, through […]

(Photo by Kevin Sabitus/Getty Images) | Getty Images On Wednesday, Indianapolis Colts head coach Shane Steichen announced that rookie defensive end Caden Curry will be out for the remainder of the 2026 season because of his recently surgically repaired wrist: #Colts rookie DE Caden Curry landed on IR due to a wrist injury and is out for the rest of the season, per HC Shane Steichen. Curry recently underwent surgery on his wrist. "Really unfortunate situation for him. He was playing at a really high level defensively, special teams." — James Boyd (@RomeovilleKid) November 25, 2026 The local Center Grove product had a promising rookie debut, fighting his way as a 6th round pick out of Ohio State, through his encouraging training camp and preseason performances onto the Colts active 53-man roster. Unfortunately, Curry his finished his rookie campaign prematurely, having recorded 26 tackles (14 solo), a tackle for loss, a sack, 3 QB pressures, and 2 fumble recoveries during 11 games. He had played on 62% of the Colts special teams snaps so far this season, and his 12 total special teams tackles currently lead Indianapolis. Along with fellow rookie George Gumbs Jr., Curry had seen an uptick in playing time during veteran Arden Key’s absence at defensive end—although the latter had recently returned back to the Colts first-team defensive lineup. For a late ‘Day 3’ pick, even though it was cut short, Curry was impressive during his first year with the Colts. His energy, hustle, and toughness immediately stood out, as well as his solid arsenal of natural pass rushing moves.

title: Is there anything to be thankful for with the Colts?
summary: I’m struggling. I am struggling to find a silver lining in the 2026 Indianapolis Colts season. It’s understandable that fans don’t always want a negative take, but honestly, what are we excited for? Since Berlin, the team is 3-15. 3-15… That is beyond dreadful, but it’s in the past. With Thanksgiving upon us, let’s hunker […]
full_text: HOUSTON, TEXAS - NOVEMBER 19: Will Anderson Jr. #51 of the Houston Texans sacks Daniel Jones #17 of the Indianapolis Colts in the end zone for a safety during the third quarter of the game at Reliant Stadium on November 19, 2026 in Houston, Texas. (Photo by Tim Warner/Getty Images) | Getty Images I’m struggling. I am struggling to find a silver lining in the 2026 Indianapolis Colts season. It’s understandable that fans don’t always want a negative take, but honestly, what are we excited for? Since Berlin, the team is 3-15. 3-15 … That is beyond dreadful, but it’s in the past. With Thanksgiving upon us, let’s hunker down and try to find things to be thankful for regarding the Colts. A change at quarterback is a start. Fans couldn’t stomach many more Daniel Jones starts, and while Anthony Richardson might not set things on fire, he will be a welcome change of pace. If nothing else, it will provide a reason to tune in for at least a few more games. How about the team keeping Jonathan Taylor? It would have been nice to get a huge draft haul for him, but there is something about holding onto franchise players, creating and keeping legends of the team. Let’s look at the draft. It’s unfortunate that the Colts don’t have a first-round pick. What they do have is a lot of ammo and a good place to reload, starting in the second round. They hold at least ten picks and will be at the top of most rounds. That allows them to move in the draft and restock the roster. Who will be drafting those players? No idea, but we know it won’t be Chris Ballard. That is yet another reason to be thankful in 2026. It isn’t rosy. The prospects are dim, but there are a couple of bright spots. A refresh at quarterback and GM are the obvious positives. There is way too much work to do to get this franchise back on track, but a bevy of draft picks is a good place to start. I’m struggling to find the positives for the Colts right now. I guess we will have to be thankful for anything we can.

title: Colts coaches weigh in on Anthony Richardson’s abrupt return to the starting lineup
summary: After the surprising release of starting quarterback Daniel Jones, Indianapolis Colts quarterback Anthony Richardson Sr. now receives one last opportunity to prove he’s a viable QB1 for the franchise going forward. As long as he can stay healthy, he projects to start these dismantled 3-8 Colts’ final six games down the stretch of the 2026 […]
full_text: NASHVILLE, TENNESSEE - SEPTEMBER 21: Indianapolis Colts running back Jonathan Taylor #28 celebrates after scoring a touchdown during the third quarter with teammate Anthony Richardson #5 and Head coach Shane Steichen against the Tennessee Titans at Nissan Stadium — September 21, 2025 in Nashville, Tennessee. (Photo by Dylan Buell/Getty Images) | Getty Images After the surprising release of starting quarterback Daniel Jones, Indianapolis Colts quarterback Anthony Richardson Sr. now receives one last opportunity to prove he’s a viable QB1 for the franchise going forward. As long as he can stay healthy, he projects to start these dismantled 3-8 Colts’ final six games down the stretch of the 2026 campaign. The former 4th overall pick of the 2023 NFL Draft has only started 15 games since being selected by Indianapolis, and his last start for the Colts occurred on December 22, 2024, against the Tennessee Titans. The reason being because of both lengthy injury recovery timelines and a demotion in favor of Jones, until the latter’s surprising recent release. When asked about his rumored “rocky” relationship with Richardson Sr., and his thoughts on Richardson’s long awaited return to the starting lineup, Steichen downplayed any lingering issues and told the local media on Monday ( via The Athletic’s James Boyd ): “I think we’re in a really good place,” Steichen said recently. “I know there is a lot of stuff out there, but me and him, we still talk regularly, and I’m excited for his opportunity. He’s matured over these years. He puts in good work, and now he gets another opportunity, and I’m really looking forward to seeing him go out and compete.” Meanwhile, Colts offensive coordinator Jim Bob Cooter commented on Richardson Sr.’s last four seasons with Indianapolis, noting that being able to reflect and watch from afar could help him take another step forward: #Colts OC Jim Bob Cooter on Anthony Richardson Sr.: "We've obviously had an interesting four years at (QB). But Anthony's got to watch a lot of different guys go through their weekly process … of preparing for an opponent." "It can be nice to have that 10,000 foot view. …" — James Boyd (@RomeovilleKid) November 24, 2026 That being said, Richardson Sr. may have to rely on his still elite athleticism, dual-threat mobility, and improvisation more than ever because he’ll be returning to the first-team offense in less than an ideal situation. He won’t exactly be placed in a position to succeed, as the Colts have been stripped to the studs following early November’s trade deadline. Along the offensive line, the Colts traded All-Pro left guard Quenton Nelson and now have a rookie starting in his place, with both starting left tackles out because of injuries during last Thursday night’s blowout loss in Houston. Meanwhile, this isn’t Hall of Famers Marvin Harrison and Reggie Wayne that he’ll be throwing to, as Indianapolis’ starting receiving corps more closely resembles a patchwork positional group you’d find in preseason. The group has recently struggled to separate, get open, and create any sort of big plays downfield. Perhaps, Richardson with his ability to run, create plays outside the pocket, and willingness to throw downfield can provide a spark for this stagnant Colts offense, which mustered just 3 points last Thursday night. If nothing else, he should be more exciting on offense, as the prior disastrous Daniel Jones led offense in 2026 had clearly run its course this season, and a change at the position was long overdue.
author: Luke Schultheis

title: Colts sign Shane Buechele and Wanya Morris in flurry of roster moves, place Caden Curry on IR
summary: The Indianapolis Colts made a series of roster moves Tuesday, signing quarterback Shane Buechele from the Buffalo Bills’ practice squad, promoting defensive end Carl Lawson to the 53-man roster and placing rookie defensive end Caden Curry on injured reserve. The organization also waived offensive tackle Charlie Heck while adding tight end Sean McKeon and defensive […]
full_text: ORCHARD PARK, NEW YORK - AUGUST 27: Shane Buechele #6 of the Buffalo Bills throws a pass during the first half of a preseason game against the Pittsburgh Steelers at Highmark Stadium on August 27, 2026 in Orchard Park, New York. (Photo by Timothy T Ludwig/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Indianapolis Colts made a series of roster moves Tuesday, signing quarterback Shane Buechele from the Buffalo Bills’ practice squad, promoting defensive end Carl Lawson to the 53-man roster and placing rookie defensive end Caden Curry on injured reserve. The organization also waived offensive tackle Charlie Heck while adding tight end Sean McKeon and defensive end Cam Sample to the practice squad, according to the team’s official announcement. We have signed QB Shane Buechele off of the Bills practice squad and signed DE Carl Lawson to the 53-man roster from the practice squad. We have placed DE Caden Curry on IR. We have waived T Charlie Heck and signed TE Sean McKeon and DE Cam Sample to the practice squad. — Indianapolis Colts (@Colts) November 24, 2026 Indianapolis wasn’t finished there, as ESPN’s Adam Schefter also reported that the Colts are signing offensive tackle Wanya Morris from the Dallas Cowboys’ practice squad to their active roster, providing additional help to an offensive line that has been severely affected by injuries throughout the season. Colts are signing OT Wanya Morris off the Cowboys practice squad. — Adam Schefter (@AdamSchefter) November 24, 2026 The addition of Buechele comes just days after Indianapolis released Daniel Jones and announced that Anthony Richardson would return as the starting quarterback for the remainder of the 2026 season. With Richardson now receiving another opportunity to prove himself and Riley Leonard also on the roster, Buechele provides additional depth and experience in a quarterback room that has undergone considerable changes. Buechele entered the NFL as an undrafted free agent with the Kansas City Chiefs in 2021 after playing collegiately at Texas and SMU. He spent several seasons developing behind Patrick Mahomes before joining Buffalo in 2023, where he spent time on both the active roster and practice squad. His only regular-season appearance came with Kansas City in 2025, when he completed seven of 14 passes for 88 yards. While he is unlikely to challenge Richardson for the starting job, his familiarity with NFL systems gives Indianapolis another option as it navigates the final six games of the season. Morris, meanwhile, represents an interesting addition given the current state of the Colts’ offensive line. The 26-year-old was selected in the third round of the 2023 NFL Draft by Kansas City and appeared in 43 games, making 16 starts during his three seasons with the Chiefs. He was traded to Atlanta during the offseason before being released in August, eventually joining Dallas’ practice squad. Indianapolis has been forced to make significant adjustments at offensive tackle following injuries to Bernhard Raimann and Jalen Travis. With Raimann dealing with a concussion and Travis sidelined by a knee injury, the Colts started Luke Tenuta at left tackle and moved Matt Goncalves to right tackle against Houston. Morris provides another experienced option at a position where the team has struggled to maintain continuity, while Heck’s departure ends a brief stint in Indianapolis after signing with the organization on October 29. On the defensive side, the promotion of Lawson comes at the expense of losing another promising young contributor. Curry, a sixth-round selection in the 2026 NFL Draft, has appeared in all 11 games this season, recording 14 tackles, one sack, two fumble recoveries and 12 special teams stops. The former Ohio State defensive end has provided useful depth along the defensive line while establishing himself as a dependable contributor on special teams. His placement on injured reserve means he will be required to miss at least four games, a disappointing development for a rookie who had begun carving out a role within the organization. Lawson should help compensate for that absence, providing Indianapolis with an experienced pass rusher who has recorded 32 sacks across his NFL career. The former Cincinnati Bengals fourth-round pick joined the Colts’ practice squad in October and was previously elevated for the team’s matchup against Jacksonville, recording one tackle. Although he is no longer the player who consistently generated pressure earlier in his career, he offers additional experience to a defensive front that has already undergone considerable changes following DeForest Buckner’s departure. The Colts also added two familiar NFL veterans to their practice squad in McKeon and Sample. McKeon returns to Indianapolis after previously spending time with the organization during the 2024 and 2025 seasons, as well as participating in this year’s offseason program and training camp. His addition provides additional tight end depth following Mo Alie-Cox’s placement on injured reserve earlier this month. Sample, meanwhile, was originally selected by Cincinnati in the fourth round of the 2021 NFL Draft and has appeared in 61 career games, recording seven sacks. The veteran defensive end has spent time with the Bengals, 49ers and Falcons, and could provide another option for Indianapolis should additional injuries occur along the defensive line. With the Colts sitting at 3-8 and preparing to face the New York Giants on Sunday, the latest moves reflect an organization attempting to manage mounting injuries while continuing to evaluate its roster for the future. Richardson’s return has already brought significant changes to the offense, and the additions of Buechele and Morris provide some much-needed depth at two important positions. While none of these transactions is likely to dramatically change the team’s outlook over the final six games, they should help Indianapolis navigate the remainder of an increasingly difficult season while giving several players an opportunity to demonstrate whether they deserve a role moving forward.
author: Andrew Aziz

title: Thoughts on The Daniel Jones Saga
summary: The Colts made the decision to release Daniel Jones last Friday following yet another rough offensive performance. The decision certainly raised some eyebrows, not necessarily because of how Jones has performed this season, but because Indianapolis had an opportunity to trade him at the deadline and was seemingly steadfast in their decision to keep him. […]
full_text: HOUSTON, TEXAS - NOVEMBER 19: Daniel Jones #17 of the Indianapolis Colts looks on against the Houston Texans following an NFL football game at NRG Stadium on November 19, 2026 in Houston, Texas. (Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Colts made the decision to release Daniel Jones last Friday following yet another rough offensive performance. The decision certainly raised some eyebrows, not necessarily because of how Jones has performed this season, but because Indianapolis had an opportunity to trade him at the deadline and was seemingly steadfast in their decision to keep him. Some will call it “organizational malpractice,” while others believe it’s really not that big of a deal. I fall somewhere in the middle, with a slight lean toward organizational malpractice, just not to the dramatic extent some have suggested. The net loss of releasing Jones rather than trading him was never going to materially change the outlook or trajectory of the Colts’ future. And for that reason alone, many have dismissed the situation. But when you consider the timeline of events and sifting through the various reporting, the Colts are telling the NFL they simply have no plan. Here’s my rough interpretation of how we got here: – October 31st: Tom Pelissero puts out a report that the Colts have not discussed benching Daniel Jones but his 10.5M injury guarantee could be a factor if they are out of playoff contention – November 4: Adam Schefter and Jeremy Fowler floated Daniel Jones as a potential trade candidate, with Baltimore and Minnesota emerging as possible destinations. – November 6: Fowler expands on his report that Daniel Jones would potentially want out of Indy and that people inside the building think he should want out as well. – November 7: Adam Schefter and Ian Rapoport reported that multiple teams had contacted Indianapolis about Jones and that the Colts were listening to offers. – November 7: Tom Pelissero reported that the Colts were telling interested teams they had no intention of trading Jones. – November 8: Pelissero reported that Indianapolis had informed Jones he would not be traded before the deadline. – November 10: The NFL trade deadline passed with Jones remaining in Indianapolis. – November 22: Adam Schefter reported that Baltimore had offered a fourth-round pick for Jones, along with a conditional fifth-round pick that would return to Indianapolis if the Ravens made the playoffs. – November 20: The Colts released Jones, 10 days after the trade deadline, receiving no compensation in return. Ok, now that we got that out of the way. The Colts had to have known that Daniel Jones was unhappy with the firesale that was occurring, unhappy with the organization seemingly giving up on the team early in the season, and unhappy with the weekly questions (fair or not fair, think there was a bit of both) of him being benched every week. He obviously did not want to QB a rebuild here. They also had floated the idea of him being benched more than a week before the deadline because of the injury guarantees. That is the exact situation to what had played out in New York. This was not a situation the Colts couldn’t have seen coming. In my opinion, the Colts had three options that were acceptable in this situation and somehow chose neither: The first option is to trade Daniel Jones. Many people will argue that the Ravens’ offer is not worth it. I would argue that the Ravens’ offer was one offer in a snapshot in time. The Colts essentially shut down negotiations and never took any of that seriously. It was also reported that the Vikings had called about Jones and the Colts were “unsure of what they wanted” so they pivoted to Cousins. The second option would be to keep Daniel Jones because you wanted to keep him and genuinely did not want to trade him. You believe that he needs a reset for this season and can be on the roster a year removed from the Achilles as a bridge or someone who could compete for the job. The third option is that if you didn’t like the trade compensation you were getting and you also didn’t want to keep him. Don’t cut him! He signed the contract. He can sit on the bench. Nobody made you do that. Let the new GM decide if they want him or not. The Colts essentially did Daniel Jones a favor just to be nice I guess? To make matters worse they made their supposed lame duck HC announce the move at his press conference on a Friday. They could have made this move on a Monday. I should repeat myself here. Will any of this materially change the trajectory or future of the Colts? Not on paper, no. But I find it hard to convince myself that the process here was worth dismissing . Things in the NFL can change quickly. The Colts may not have a first round pick, which obviously is what the national media will point to. But it’s not a bad consolation prize to get a head start on completely tearing down an era of Colts football that was never good enough to compete for anything meaningful and was hanging on for dear life just to be on the “in the hunt” graphic.

title: Stampede Blue Reacts Survey (Week 12): Can Anthony Richardson turn things around for the Colts?
summary: Welcome to SB Nation Reacts, a survey of fans across the NFL. Throughout the year we ask questions of the most plugged-in Colts fans and fans across the country. What record will Anthony Richardson have? The Indianapolis Colts have officially made another change at quarterback, releasing Daniel Jones following Thursday’s embarrassing 26-3 loss to the […]
full_text: HOUSTON, TEXAS - NOVEMBER 19: Anthony Richardson #5 of the Indianapolis Colts runs off the field during an NFL football game against the Houston Texans at Reliant Stadium on November 19, 2026 in Houston, Texas. (Photo by Kevin Sabitus/Getty Images) | Getty Images Welcome to SB Nation Reacts, a survey of fans across the NFL. Throughout the year we ask questions of the most plugged-in Colts fans and fans across the country. What record will Anthony Richardson have? The Indianapolis Colts have officially made another change at quarterback, releasing Daniel Jones following Thursday’s embarrassing 26-3 loss to the Houston Texans and naming Anthony Richardson the starter for the remainder of the 2026 season. Jones’ departure brings an end to a disappointing tenure in Indianapolis, particularly after his encouraging performances in 2025 and the substantial contract extension he received during the offseason. With the Colts sitting at 3-8 and their playoff hopes effectively gone, the organization will now turn back to the former fourth-overall pick in hopes of evaluating whether he has any future with the franchise. Richardson hasn’t started a regular-season game since December 2024 and has struggled with accuracy, decision-making and consistency throughout his young career. However, he remains only 24 years old and possesses exceptional athletic ability, providing Shane Steichen with an opportunity to experiment with a more mobile quarterback and potentially reshape an offense that has become increasingly ineffective. With six games remaining, Richardson will have an opportunity to demonstrate whether he has made meaningful progress since losing his starting job. The question is whether his return can produce additional victories or whether the Colts’ struggles will continue through the end of the season. Are you confident in the Colts? The situation in Indianapolis continues to deteriorate following another embarrassing performance, this time against the Houston Texans on Thursday Night Football. The Colts managed just 167 total yards, eight first downs and three points in a 26-3 defeat, dropping to 3-8 on the season. The offense was ineffective throughout the evening, with Daniel Jones struggling once again before being replaced by Anthony Richardson, while the defense also had difficulty containing C.J. Stroud and Houston’s passing attack. The loss reinforced how far Indianapolis remains from becoming a competitive team, particularly with several important veterans having already departed at the trade deadline. Last week’s Reacts survey revealed that only 12 percent of Colts fans believed the franchise was headed in the right direction, continuing a remarkable decline from 47 percent just over a month ago. However, the decision to release Jones and give Richardson another opportunity could provide some renewed optimism, even if there is considerable skepticism about whether he can become a dependable NFL starter. With a new general manager expected to take over during the offseason and several younger players receiving opportunities to establish themselves, the final six games should provide valuable information about the organization’s future. Whether those developments are enough to restore any confidence among Colts fans remains to be seen. Sign up here to participate in the weekly emailed surveys:

title: Jaguars Open Patrick Mekari’s 21-Day Practice Window
summary: The Jacksonville Jaguars took a major step toward getting a starting offensive lineman back on Wednesday, as the team announced it has opened the 21-day practice period for 2025 starting guard Patrick Mekari, who has been on injured reserve since the start of the season. Under NFL rules, a player placed on injured reserve with […]
full_text: JACKSONVILLE, FLORIDA - NOVEMBER 16: Patrick Mekari #65 of the Jacksonville Jaguars looks on at the end of a game against the Los Angeles Chargersat EverBank Stadium on November 16, 2025 in Jacksonville, Florida. (Photo by Rich Storry/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Jacksonville Jaguars took a major step toward getting a starting offensive lineman back on Wednesday, as the team announced it has opened the 21-day practice period for 2025 starting guard Patrick Mekari, who has been on injured reserve since the start of the season. Under NFL rules, a player placed on injured reserve with a designation to return can resume practicing once he is eligible. That begins a 21-day clock. Within it, the team must either activate him to the 53-man roster or leave him on IR for the rest of the season. Counting from today, that clock runs into mid-December. Similarly, defensive end BJ Green’s 21-day window was also recently opened, with his hopeful activation still looming from injured reserve. How We Got Here Jacksonville signed Mekari as a free agent to a three-year, $37.5 million contract with $20 million guaranteed during the 2025 offseason. The money alone makes his return to the lineup a notable one for an interior line still struggling for an identity. With left tackle Anton Harrison on IR, center Robert Hainsey reportedly week to week, and swing tackle Walker Little exiting the Week 11 matchup with injury, Mekari’s versatility, if healthy, could be a boon to this Jacksonville offensive line. With an ability to play center and either guard or tackle position, Patrick would allow a variety of starting line combinations, or at minimum, functional depth at all five spots. Also, should the team decide that Cleveland or rookie Emmanuel Pregnon needs more time, they could plug Mekari there. Offensive Penalty Yard Leaders 1. JAX Emmanuel Pregnon: 82 yards (11 penalties) 2. PIT DK Metcalf: 76 (8) 3. BAL Ronnie Stanley: 69 (9) Brock Purdy being #5 with his FOUR intentional grounding penalties is hilarious. pic.twitter.com/UGinFtWNy7 — SFdata9ers🏈📊 (@sfdata9ers) November 25, 2026 A Timely Return Mekari started at right guard in all 14 games he appeared in for Jacksonville last season. He was part of an offensive line that did not allow a sack in five games, tied for the most in the league. It also allowed no QB hit in two games, the most in the NFL in 2025. He has played 102 career games (67 starts) with Baltimore (2019-24) and Jacksonville (2025-present). However, Mekari has consistently struggled with back issues since signing in Jacksonville. This culminated in the veteran OL undergoing back surgery in mid-August. He was placed on injured reserve with a designation to return, with Ezra Cleveland starting at right guard in his absence. After being listed on the injury report throughout 2025 with the back injury, Mekari’s final injury came in Week 16 against the Denver Broncos, which kept him out of the Week 17 game against the Colts. He was later cleared to play in the wild-card game against the Bills, with the offseason surgery to follow. It’s easy to say that Jacksonville fans have yet to see a consistently healthy Patrick Mekari. If healthy currently, the benefit for the recently struggling offensive line may be right on time. Head Coach Liam Coen noted on Wednesday that it was great to get Mekari going, stating that the 305-pound lineman has “worked his tail off to get back,” as another experienced veteran in the fold to give the team depth and competition. He stated Mekari is “as strong as he’s been in a long time.” What’s next Opening the window doesn’t guarantee he plays, as there is no guarantee that a player will be activated from injured reserve simply because their practice window is opened. During the 2025 season, then rookie defensive end Jalen McLeod 21-day window was opened on December 16th and subsequently expired on January 7th with the rookie unable to make it back. Once the 21-day window expires the player is required to spend the remainder of the season on IR with no ability to return during that season. The coaching staff will watch how his back responds to practice before deciding on activation. Any updates on his status will likely come through the weekly injury reports. Stay tuned.

title: Chiefs-Bills Week 12 game and score predictions from Arrowhead Pride
summary: It’s time for the Arrowhead Pride staff to put their opinions to the test. Before the Kansas City Chiefs travel to face the Buffalo Bills on Thanksgiving night, our writers predicted the final score and result. The NFL’s marquee rivalry for the last half-decade sees the Chiefs entering with a 8-2 record, having already exceeded […]
full_text: (Photo by Al Bello/Getty Images) | Getty Images It’s time for the Arrowhead Pride staff to put their opinions to the test. Before the Kansas City Chiefs travel to face the Buffalo Bills on Thanksgiving night, our writers predicted the final score and result. The NFL’s marquee rivalry for the last half-decade sees the Chiefs entering with a 8-2 record, having already exceeded last season’s disappointing win total by two victories. At 9-1, the Bills are tied for the best record in the NFL. Both teams face major questions after facing some of the league’s worst teams over the past month. Thursday night is an opportunity for each team to prove their record to be legitimate. FanDuel Sportsbook currently lists the Bills as slight 2.5-point home favorites. The Chiefs are coming off of a dominant 34-7 blowout of the Arizona Cardinals in Week 11, while the Bills defeated the Miami Dolphins by a 26-9 margin. Both teams faced off against backup quarterbacks last week. Chiefs Kingdom, bring the noise to the SB Nation app! Join fellow Chiefs fans to react to every explosive play and game-changing moment in real time. Chat live throughout the game Browse with fewer ads Easily jump between communities Enjoy faster commenting and posting Download the SB Nation app on iOS or Android . We also want to know your score prediction! Vote in the poll on The Feed and share your score prediction ! Jared Sapp ( @TrumanChief ) For most of the season, I’ve assumed that I would be picking Buffalo to win this one. And the Chiefs have some major questions to answer about how good they are after a trio of dominant wins over minimal competition. However, the same can be true for Buffalo, who has faced a laughable stretch of opposing quarterbacks since their Week 7 bye. Based on expected rainy and cold weather, I am going to pick the Chiefs to come out on top in a game where pounding the rock will prove crucial. This would have been a nice game to have Kenneth Walker available to alternate with Emmett Johnson. But Johnson has been as hot as any player in the league this month and will have a nice chance to make a Rookie of the Year case before a national audience. Chiefs 24, Bills 20 Caleb James ( @CJScoobs ) Ding, Ding. The best rivalry in the NFL will pit two of the top contenders in football against one another this week. While the Chiefs and Bills both won in blowout fashion on Sunday, it should be noted that a poor performance from Josh Allen caused Buffalo to have to scrap all the way to the finish line. Meanwhile, Patrick Mahomes and company played mostly backups in the second half. As usual, this game will come down to Mahomes or Allen holding the ball in critical situations. The Chiefs must find answers for stopping the Bills pass rush, but a well-balanced running game will be needed for a Chiefs win. The two teams mirror each other, and the game will come down to who can win late. Bills 28, Chiefs 24 Maurice Elston ( @MrMauriceElston ) Chiefs-Bills has become one of the defining rivalries of the Patrick Mahomes era, and this Thanksgiving matchup has me torn. Buffalo has James Cook to complement Josh Allen, but I think Kansas City’s running game can make the difference this time. The Chiefs have found ways to run against Buffalo before, but this backfield gives them a stronger opportunity to sustain drives without asking Mahomes to do everything. In a game that could come down to the final possession, being able to grind out first downs late in the fourth quarter and keep Allen on the sideline could be the deciding factor. Defensively, I trust the Chiefs’ cornerbacks to compete with Buffalo’s receivers and limit explosive plays. Containing Allen is another challenge entirely, and Kansas City will need to finish possessions without letting him escape pressure and create something out of nothing. I expect another tense game between these two teams, but I’m betting on the Chiefs’ ground game helping them close it out. My mind says Buffalo, but my heart says Kansas City—and I’m following my heart. Chiefs 28, Bills 24 Mark Gunnels ( @MarkAGunnels ) The Chiefs will beat Buffalo because they have Patrick Mahomes, and there’s nobody I trust more when the stakes are elevated. As great as Josh Allen is, Mahomes’ ability to manipulate defenses, extend plays and deliver in the biggest moments is what separates him from every other quarterback in football. He’s thrown 13 touchdowns without a single interception over his last four games, and I expect the best player on the planet to remind everybody why the AFC still runs through him. Chiefs 22, Bills 20 Matt Stagner ( @stagdsp ) The regular season game of the year, and the Super Bowl of this and every Bills season is on Thanksgiving night. It should be the most-watched, highest scoring game of 2026. But, with the weather looking cold and wet, it could be the team with the best running game and defense that holds up– and this season, that’s your Kansas City Chiefs. Josh Allen is a problem for both teams at times– his ability to run can move the chains in big moments, but he’ll also give the Chiefs defense a chance at a couple turnovers. Spagnuolo’s crew is quietly among the best in the NFL, but don’t expect a flurry of sacks this week, they’ll need to focus on stopping Cook and containing Allen. It’s weird to say, but I like Emmett Johnson over James Cook on Thanksgiving. I also suspect Mahomes’ competitive nature can overcome mother nature. Chiefs 24, Bills 21 Dakota Watson ( @D_Watson56 ) I’ve talked myself into it. This is the year. The Bills can’t ever make it to the Super Bowl, and so each regular season matchup against the Chiefs becomes their Super Bowl. This is the year they lose their Super Bowl. Patrick Mahomes is quietly playing at an MVP level and the Bills’ defense can be had. I love the matchup of the Chiefs’ rushing attack against the Bills. Our defense has played better the last few weeks, but I’m really curious to see how they play against a more quality opponent. This is always one of the best games of the year, and a potential AFC Championship preview. The Chiefs win and remain competitive in the race for the AFC West crown and home field advantage. Chiefs 27, Bills 24 Rocky Magana ( @RockyMagana ) The Kansas City Chiefs are coming in hot off beating three terrible teams in a row. Now it’s time to get back into the deep end and swim with the sharks. This game is by far the biggest of the Chiefs’ season. A victory on Thanksgiving night changes the complexion of this entire season. Luckily, the Bills’ defense is nothing to write home about. This is the team that gave up 31 points to the Houston Texans and 30 points to the Las Vegas Raiders. The issue is, they have scored over 30 points in five games this year. So the defense will have their hands full playing on the road at the new Highmark Stadium, but to heck with it, I’m riding with my team, and I believe in these boys. Chiefs 28, Bills 24 Nate Christensen The Chiefs have not beat the Bills in the regular season since 2020. The Bills have typically come off a heartbreaking loss to the Chiefs in the playoffs and get revenge for it in the regular season. This year, I do think the Chiefs get the win. I think the Chiefs are able to slow this game down with a run game Buffalo won’t be able to stop. The defense will give up some points and yards, but I think they create more stops that let the Chiefs win. Chiefs 27, Bills 24 Ron Kopp Jr. ( @RonOnChiefs ) After an afternoon loss on Thanksgiving last year that ruined my favorite holiday, I am fired up for the Chiefs to be the nightcap, after I can enjoy my mother’s cooking all day and not have my appetite ruined by a potential loss. But I see myself and the rest of Chiefs Kingdom eating their pies in happiness through the night, celebrating with family and friends that Kansas City looks to be back in control of the AFC. The Chiefs have built themselves to beat the Bills, whether intentional or not, and it starts with one of…

title: Chiefs-Bills Week 12 Final injury report: Kenneth Walker ruled out
summary: Each practice day this season, the Kansas City Chiefs release an official injury report ahead of the next game. In Week 12, the Chiefs play the Buffalo Bills on Thanksgiving night. Here is the Chiefs’ final official injury report of the week, courtesy of the team’s official website. After Monday’s practice estimates, Tuesday’s report showed the […]
full_text: (Photo by Alika Jenner/Getty Images) | Getty Images Each practice day this season, the Kansas City Chiefs release an official injury report ahead of the next game. In Week 12, the Chiefs play the Buffalo Bills on Thanksgiving night. Here is the Chiefs’ final official injury report of the week, courtesy of the team’s official website . After Monday’s practice estimates, Tuesday’s report showed the teams on the field preparing for the game. Chiefs Running back Kenneth Walker (groin) was ruled out after being upgraded to a limited participant and practiced Tuesday for the first time since injuring his groin before the Week 10 game against the Atlanta Falcons . Starting right tackle Jaylon Moore (ankle) was ruled out after he did not participate in practice again and hasn’t since leaving the Week 9 game against the New York Jets in the third quarter with an ankle injury. Second-year defensive tackle Omarr Norman-Lott (knee) was ruled out after he was a limited participant in practice all week for the third consecutive week. He was activated from the Reserve/Physically-Unable-to-Perform list last week. Tight end Noah Gray (rib) is questionable after he was upgraded to a full participant in practice after missing on Monday after leaving the game against the Arizona Cardinals late with the injury. Right guard Trey Smith (concussion) has no game designation after he was a full participant in practice again; he appears set to return after entering concussion protocol during the first quarter of the Week 10 game. Rookie defensive tackle Peter Woods (neck) is questionable to play for the first time since leaving the game injured against the Denver Broncos in Week 8. Bills The following information is from Tuesday’s injury report. Check back in for Buffalo’s final injury designations. Starting cornerback Christian Benford (groin) was upgraded to a limited participant after he was estimated to not participate in practice on Monday and missed last week’s game. In eight games played this season, Benford has 33 tackles and eight passes defended. In his career against Kansas City, Benford has 2 passes defended, one sack and a forced fumble. Starting right tackle Spencer Brown (back) was upgraded to a full participant in practice after being estimated as limited on Monday. He missed time earlier this year, but has played in the last two games. Starting tight end Dalton Kincaid (thumb/ankle) was a limited participant in practice on Tuesday after being estimated as limited on Monday. He missed last week’s game and has been banged up for a few weeks. This season, Kincaid has seen the second-most catches on the team (32) and has 487 yards and two touchdowns; Kincaid has one touchdown in his career against the Chiefs. Starting right guard O’Cyrus Torrence (ankle) has been a limited participant in practice this week; he has not missed a start this year. Starting linebacker Dorian Williams (calf) has been a limited participant in practice this week after missing last week’s game. This season, Williams has 61 tackles (5 for loss), one sack, two interceptions and four passes defended.

title: Chiefs-Bills Madden Simulation Week 12: Happy Thanksgiving
summary: On Thursday, the (8-2) Kansas City Chiefs are on the road to New York to take on the (9-1) Buffalo Bills. Let’s see how the game plays out in Madden NFL 27. Note: Madden simulation is 8-2 this season, predicting the outcome. First quarter The Chiefs opened with the ball but managed just one first […]
full_text: On Thursday, the (8-2) Kansas City Chiefs are on the road to New York to take on the (9-1) Buffalo Bills . Let’s see how the game plays out in Madden NFL 2 7. Note: Madden simulation is 8-2 this season, predicting the outcome. STOP! If you want to watch the simulation without spoilers, start this video — or if you can’t see it, click here . First quarter The Chiefs opened with the ball but managed just one first down, coming on an 18-yard pass to Xavier Worthy. The drive stalled after Deone Walker sacked Mahomes on third down, forcing Kansas City to punt. James Cook flipped the field with a 33-yard gain, followed by a 22-yard run that moved the Bills to the Chiefs’ 20-yard line. Kansas City’s defense stood tall, forcing Buffalo to settle for a field goal on its opening drive. Tyler Bass put the Bills on the board. Trey Smith exited the game with an apparent injury. Emmett Johnson caught a Texas route near midfield and turned it into a 21-yard gain to the Bills’ 26-yard line. End of first quarter: Bills 3, Chiefs 0 Second quarter On third-and-10, Patrick Mahomes tossed a pass to Travis Kelce on a tight end screen gaining eight yards. Opting to go for it on fourth-and-two, Mahomes went back to Kelce, but the pass was knocked down, and the Chiefs turned the ball over on downs. The Bills quickly went three-and-out. Kansas City then connected on a 20-yard catch-and-run to Rashee Rice, reaching the Bills’ 47-yard line. However, the drive stalled, and the Chiefs punted the ball back to Buffalo. The Bills picked up a first down on a 19-yard pass to Dalton Kincaid before crossing midfield and facing fourth-and-six. Josh Allen rifled a pass to a streaking James Cook, who picked up the first down and more, reaching the Chiefs’ 20-yard line. Kincaid snagged a pass in the end zone for the game’s first touchdown with less than two minutes remaining in the quarter. The Chiefs managed to steal some points before halftime, as Harrison Butker drilled a field goal. End of second quarter: Bills 10, Chiefs 3 Third quarter Wide receiver Khalil Shakir caught a corner route for 25 yards before being stopped at the Chiefs’ 23-yard line. Shakir followed that up with another catch to move Buffalo to the 12. James Cook found the end zone on a comeback route along the goal line for a receiving touchdown. Patrick Mahomes took off for a first-down run, gaining 18 yards to reach the Chiefs’ 45-yard line. Mahomes then connected with Josh Downs on a streak route to move Kansas City to the Bills’ 35. A Bills defender knocked away another third-down pass intended for Kelce. Butker then missed a 52-yard field goal attempt. Shakir caught a wide-open pass over the middle for a 29-yard gain, setting up another scoring opportunity for Buffalo. Cook reached the end zone once again, this time on the ground, with a 19-yard run to the right side for another touchdown. End of third quarter: Bills 24, Chiefs 3 Fourth quarter The Chiefs started the quarter with the ball at the Bills’ 40-yard line. Ed Oliver got to Mahomes for a seven-yard loss, but Mahomes responded by finding a streaking Worthy behind the Bills’ secondary for a 47-yard touchdown in the back of the end zone. James Cook continued to take over the game, gaining 36 yards on the drive, including a 10-yard touchdown run for his third touchdown of the game. Coming out of the two-minute warning, Jalen Royals caught a slant from Mahomes and reached the Bills’ four-yard line. The Chiefs couldn’t capitalize, failing to score a touchdown and turning the ball over on downs. Final score: Bills 31, Chiefs 10 Notable stats Patrick Mahomes: 29 for 42 passing, 316 yards, 1 touchdown, 2 rushing attempts, 20 yards Emmett Johnson: 4 rushing attempts, -1 yard, 6 receptions, 50 yards. Josh Downs: 9 receptions, 81 yards. Xavier Worthy: 5 receptions, 84 yards, 1 touchdown. Rashee Rice: 3 receptions, 47 yards. Travis Kelce: 3 receptions, 29 yards George Karlaftis: 4 tackles for loss, .5 sack. Chris Jones: 2 tackles for loss, .5 sack. Felix Anudike-Uzomah: .5 sack Josh Allen: 16 for 22 passing, 187 yards, 2 touchdowns James Cook III: 15 rushing attempts, 135 yards, 2 touchdowns, 3 receptions, 38 yards, 1 touchdown. Khalil Shakir: 7 receptions, 87 yards. Dalton Kincaid: 5 receptions, 57 yards, 1 touchdown Ed Oliver: 1 sack Deon Walker: 1 sack Joe Andreessen: 1 sack Next week, the Chiefs are once again playing Thursday Night Football, this time taking on the Los Angeles Rams. Until then, we will see how it plays out inside the EA Universe.

title: Week 12 AP NFL Power Rankings: Chiefs climb to Top 3 ahead of Thanksgiving matchup
summary: Somehow, it’s already Thanksgiving. I don’t know how we got here, but here we are. It’s almost 2027, folks. In my opinion, Thanksgiving weekend is the second-best weekend of football after the Divisional Playoff weekend. This Thanksgiving is shaping up to be no different. Each game scheduled for Wednesday-Friday could have major playoff implications. Yes, […]
full_text: (Photo by Scott Winters/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Somehow, it’s already Thanksgiving. I don’t know how we got here, but here we are. It’s almost 2027, folks. In my opinion, Thanksgiving weekend is the second-best weekend of football after the Divisional Playoff weekend. This Thanksgiving is shaping up to be no different. Each game scheduled for Wednesday-Friday could have major playoff implications. Yes, we are being treated to a Thanksgiving appetizer with a “Thanksgiving Eve” game on Wednesday night between the Packers and Rams. This is followed by a huge NFC North matchup between the Bears and Lions on Thanksgiving, an NFC East battle between the Eagles and Cowboys that afternoon, leading up to the nightcap of the AFC rivals Chiefs and Bills. Finally, Black Friday will bring us the Broncos versus Steelers as both teams are fighting to maintain their playoff positions. Before this feast of football on Thanksgiving week, let’s take a look back at Week 11 and where each team stands in this week’s edition of the Arrowhead Pride Power Rankings. In honor of Thanksgiving, and to perhaps stir up even more debate, we’ll tier-rank the teams according to the best Thanksgiving side dishes. As I think we can all agree—the best food on the Thanksgiving table, and what makes a Thanksgiving dinner worth having—are the side dishes. Biggest riser: New York Giants +4 Biggest fallers: Cincinnati Bengals and Arizona Cardinals -4 This week, along with myself, staff voters were: Maurice Elston, Caleb James, Ron Kopp Jr., Rocky Magana, and Jared Sapp . Turkey stuffing tier The Thanksgiving plate is not complete without it, and it’s so good you go back for seconds. 1. San Francisco 49ers (1st) Right now, they’re the class of the NFL. The unanimous number one overall team by the AP staff. 2. Buffalo Bills (2nd) This team remains high in the power rankings, but Josh Allen continues to try and give the ball away to his opponents. 3. Kansas City Chiefs (6th) They took care of business in the three-game stretch against inferior opponents. Now we find out what the Chiefs are truly made of. 4. Chicago Bears (5th) A win on the road in Detroit on Turkey Day would give the Bears the definitive edge in the NFC North. Huge game upcoming. 5. Denver Broncos (8th) Running back Jonah Coleman adds a whole other dimension to this offense. 6. Jacksonville Jaguars (3rd) They looked like the Jaguars of old on Sunday. 7. Detroit Lions (9th) The quietest 8-2 record of any team—ever? 8. Cincinnati Bengals (4th) Their lack of a rushing attack could be a major problem in January. Potatoes Tier Mashed, sweet, baked, au gratin—these teams are quality but can look vastly different from week to week. 9. Minnesota Vikings (7th) Outclassed in Mexico City in all phases. Kirk Cousins was great last week, but didn’t do much to help this team against the current top-ranked team. 10. New York Giants (14th) Well coached, great pass rush, serviceable play from the quarterback position. Cam Skattebo could blow it at any moment. 11. Seattle Seahawks (10th) They desperately need to figure out a way to win in San Francisco on Thanksgiving weekend. They will have the rest advantage coming off their bye week, while the 49ers are returning from their second international trip of the season in Mexico 12. Los Angeles Rams (11th) Now is the time for the offseason champs to turn it on and make their postseason run. As it stands currently, they’ll be in Cancun come January. 13. Green Bay Packers (12th) This offensive line has looked porous, and a matchup against Myles Garrett and Aaron Donald is not the Thanksgiving appetizer they were surely hoping for. Rolls tier At times, great and can be game-changing. But if not homemade, it’s not worth having on the table. 14. Cleveland Browns (13th) With the Bengals bungling their Monday night contest, the Browns only sit one game back for the AFC North crown. 15. Houston Texans (15th) Their hopes at a postseason berth hinge on the continued collapse of the Steelers. 16. Pittsburgh Steelers (16th) 4-0 at home and 2-4 on the road. Black Friday at home against the Broncos…so there’s a chance? Casseroles tier The “mid” tier. It can fill you up, but you don’t always know what you’re eating. 17. Carolina Panthers (18th) One week Bryce Young will look like an MVP candidate, and the next he’ll look like that confused rookie we once knew. 18. New England Patriots (17th) Is Daniel Jones a future New England Patriot? 19. Dallas Cowboys (21st) The only team in the NFC East to not have a win against a team with a winning record. 20. Tampa Bay Buccaneers (20th) This roster seems more talented than the product on the field we are seeing. Todd Bowles’ days in Tampa seem numbered. 21. Las Vegas Raiders (19th) Fernando Mendoza may be the real deal. But they are currently only an average football team. 22. Washington Commanders (23rd) Huge win on Monday night. They avenge some of their own late-game management blunders. 23. Atlanta Falcons (22nd) We’ll see if the bye week is the reset this team clearly needed. Bijan, my fantasy team needs you. 24. New Orleans Saints (24th) Jordyn Tyson cooled off, while Chris Olive had a big day receiving. Alas, it still was not enough. Cranberry sauce tier This can be left off the Thanksgiving menu. 25. Baltimore Ravens (25th) The Ravens are in the midst of a six-game losing streak. Their point differential in those six games? 96 points for and 175 points against. 26. Philadelphia Eagles (28th) They won the Pennsylvania Bowl but still sit in last place in the NFC East after all four teams won this week. Mathematically, they are still in the running for the NFC East with their third quarterback of the season. 27. New York Jets (26th) Playing the Los Angeles Chargers is like passing go and collecting $200 in Monopoly. 28. Tennessee Titans (29th) 30 points against the Cowboys’ defense is nothing to write home about. Head coach Robert Saleh still called it “disgusting football.” 29. Indianapolis Colts (30th) This franchise makes no sense…offered a fourth-round draft pick for Daniel Jones, only to decline the offer and then release him for peanuts a week later. 30. Miami Dolphins (32nd) Did the Dolphins’ defense actually expose Josh Allen? 31. Arizona Cardinals (27th) Seeing Trey McBride battling on such a poor roster reminded me of the days of Tony Gonzalez with the Chiefs. 32. Los Angeles Chargers (31st) Jim Harbaugh looks totally lost and confused—on the sidelines and in his press conferences.

title: Josh Downs and Cyrus Allen providing a boost to Chiefs’ wide receiver corps
summary: The Kansas City Chiefs landed wideout Josh Downs in a deal with the Indianapolis Colts just before the NFL’s November 10 trade deadline expired. The move quickly paid dividends. In two games with his new team — while seeing only 28 total offensive snaps — Downs has racked up eight catches from quarterback Patrick Mahomes […]
full_text: Credit: Brett Davis-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Kansas City Chiefs landed wideout Josh Downs in a deal with the Indianapolis Colts just before the NFL’s November 10 trade deadline expired. The move quickly paid dividends. In two games with his new team — while seeing only 28 total offensive snaps — Downs has racked up eight catches from quarterback Patrick Mahomes for 112 yards and a touchdown. Speaking before Tuesday’s practice, Mahomes noted how quickly he’s been able to figure out what Downs does to put his own spin on routes. “He just has excellent body language when he runs routes,” the superstar observed. “He has conviction with how he runs routes, and so I understand what he’s thinking by the way he’s running and setting things up. So, that makes my job easier. Then, I’ve trusted him in a couple of these scenarios, and he’s made big plays and got himself open, and so he understands it. He understands coverages. He understands how to run routes. That’s why he gets himself open so much.” Patrick Mahomes hitting an RPO Slant to an outside aligned Josh Downs pic.twitter.com/WqBX3Wm2xE — Nate Tice (@Nate_Tice) November 22, 2026 Even with the Chiefs facing a short week ahead of Thursday’s showdown with the Buffalo Bills , head coach Andy Reid anticipates Downs’ role growing for his third game with Kansas City. “He’s done a great job,” Reid remarked of his newest receiver. “He’s a retainer; every week, we’ve given him a little bit more. He’s got a little bit more this week on a short week, but he seems to be able to digest all of it and I’ve been happy with what I’ve seen. I think Patrick’s happy with it, and he’s great in the room. It’s not one of these where the guys are looking at him cross-eyed, all that. He’s handled all that, and he’s a good guy and smart. So, the guys respect him — which, that helps.” Downs’ arrival with the Chiefs appears to have benefited rookie wide receiver Cyrus Allen, who has reeled in a spectacular catch in each of the past two games. “He’s feeling more comfortable within the offense,” Mahomes noted of Allen. “It’s hard when you’re a rookie coming into a new scheme and going through the combine stuff and getting to a team and learning a completely new language. So, I think we’ve always seen the talent that he has. It’s about him getting more and more comfortable. Now that he’s more comfortable, you start seeing those catches and stuff that you’ve seen since training camp because he has a better understanding of where he is within the offense.” The @cyrusallen_ catch that set us up for our fourth TD 👀 pic.twitter.com/VZYR036XSq — Kansas City Chiefs (@Chiefs) November 23, 2026 Mahomes broke down his best connection of Week 10 with Allen against the Arizona Cardinals that saw the rookie come back on a deep route and perfectly navigate a tight sideline to stay in bounds. “It was out and up,” Mahomes explained, “and you’ve just got to try to throw it to your best matchup. Obviously, the corner actually covered it really well. Just throughout practice and work with him, I know that he can make those back shoulder catches, and I just gave him a chance one-on-one, and he stopped on a dime and made a catch on the sideline.” As Downs and Allen have trended up, many fans have soured on third-year pro Xavier Worthy in the passing game. If anything, Mahomes expects their presence to boost Worthy’s prospects, such as when he got free for a catch and run touchdown against Arizona on Sunday. “I think more than anything,” Mahomes offered, “he’s just been staying with the work and progressing each and every week. Obviously, he wants to go out there and play his best football every single week, and I feel like he’s done a good job whenever we’ve given him opportunities, too. You saw the tough catch over the middle last week and then the catch and being able to explode down the sideline and make a touchdown. Not many guys in this league would have been able to score on that play, and so we understand how talented he is. We’ll continue to give him more and more opportunities, and I think his speed will be able to help out even other guys within the offense when he can stretch the field vertically and horizontally as well.”

The latest Kansas City Chiefs news “I Have to Be Careful”: Andy Reid Remains Tight-Lipped Over Pablo Torre’s ‘Investigation’ Into Chiefs HC’s Mysterious Mac & Cheese Case | EssentiallySports In March 2018, during a press conference, Reid declared that “five [cheeses] should be good,” but seven cheeses make the recipe even better. That prompted Torre to kickstart an investigation into the recipe, and he revealed the name of the seventh cheese on his talk show, Pablo Torre Finds Out. The missing piece to the puzzle was revealed by former Chiefs offensive tackle, Mitchell Schwartz. “We got some good news and bad news regarding the seventh cheese,” he told Torre. “The recipe I was given and the instruction I was given as an option to make the sauce smooth, provide a little flavor, some richness: a few chunks of Velveeta. That is the seventh missing cheese.” Chiefs have a growing X-factor in Josh Downs ahead of Bills showdown | The Kansas City Star “He’s done a great job retaining,” Reid said. “Every week we’ve given him a little bit more. He’s got a little bit more this week on a short week. But he seems to be able to digest all of it, and I’ve been happy with what I’ve seen. “He’s great in the room. It’s not one of these where the guys are looking at him cross-eyed and all that. He’s handled all that, and he’s a good guy and smart. So the guys respect him, which helps.” There is probably no better evidence of Downs’ comfort in the offense than the production he’s managed despite limited snaps. Bills’ Josh Allen didn’t retire (as requested). So Chiefs are preparing for his best | The Athletic “I don’t want to play you anymore,” Spagnuolo said with a smile, as caught by NFL Films cameras. “I want you to retire.” Spagnuolo laughed during a news conference Monday when he was reminded that the 30-year-old Allen had not decided to give up football this offseason after that conversation. “I wish he had,” Spagnuolo said with a grin. “He didn’t listen to me, though. He didn’t listen to me.” Seven things Solak thinks for NFL Week 12: Takes on Chiefs-Bills, Giants, Lions | ESPN The Chiefs’ offense is undergoing a smaller but still significant revolution of its own. Early in the season, it was the running game. The free agent acquisition of Kenneth Walker III and commitment to an under-center rushing attack brought newfound balance and explosiveness to a Chiefs offense in desperate need of both. But as the season has gone along, the Chiefs have begun tilting their offense back to a pass-heavy approach, just as the Bills have tinkered with their coverages. In Weeks 1-7, the Chiefs were fifth in pass rate over expectation at plus-1.5%, per NFL Next Gen Stats. Since Week 8, they’re second to only the Bengals at plus-6.2%. Chiefs Stock Watch: Separation Sunday in Week 11’s Big Win vs. Cardinals? | Sports Illustrated Jalen Royals At one stage of this campaign, it appeared that 2025 fourth-round pick Jalen Royals was settling into a bit of a groove as a rotational receiver option for KC. From Weeks 4-9, the former Utah State prospect averaged 32.4 offensive snaps and 2.2 targets per game. Since then, he’s combined for 43 snaps, good for a per-game ledger of 21.5. That span’s accompanied by just one lonely target in blowout wins over the Cardinals and Atlanta Falcons. Quarterback Patrick Mahomes missed Royals on his only opportunity in Week 11, underscoring the possibility that the sophomore wideout may be the odd man out in the aftermath of the Josh Downs trade . Around the NF L Aaron Rodgers will be inactive for Steelers Friday vs. Broncos; Mason Rudolph to start | NFL.com The statement, issued by longtime Steelers director of communications Burt Lauten, simply read: “The Pittsburgh Steelers have named Mason Rudolph the starting quarterback for the game this Friday against the Denver Broncos. “Aaron Rodgers will be inactive for the game on Friday.” NFL Network’s Cameron Wolfe reported that Rodgers, who was not listed on the team’s Tuesday injury report, has been benched. Dobbins for this weekend’s game, conduct detrimental, that’s all I’m going to say about it,” Payton said after Tuesday’s practice. “Head coach’s decision.” Asked if he wanted to elaborate on any of the circumstances that surrounded the decision, Payton said no and added “think it’s better that way.” Dobbins was in the Broncos’ facility earlier Tuesday and then left, multiple team sources said. title: Kingdom Keys: 3 Keys to a Chiefs victory over the Bills in Week 12
summary: The Kansas City Chiefs and Buffalo Bills will bring one of the NFL’s most intense modern rivalries to Thanksgiving night. The rivalry has been defined by a strange split during the Patrick Mahomes and Josh Allen era. Buffalo has won five consecutive regular-season meetings and owns a 5-1 overall advantage before January. Kansas City, however, […]
full_text: (Photo by Peter Aiken/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Kansas City Chiefs and Buffalo Bills will bring one of the NFL’s most intense modern rivalries to Thanksgiving night. The rivalry has been defined by a strange split during the Patrick Mahomes and Josh Allen era. Buffalo has won five consecutive regular-season meetings and owns a 5-1 overall advantage before January. Kansas City, however, is 4-0 against Buffalo in the postseason. That leaves Mahomes and Allen tied at five wins apiece heading into their 11th head-to-head matchup. The games have typically been close, regardless of when they have been played. Five of the past six meetings have been decided by one possession. Buffalo won the most recent matchup 28-21 during the 2025 regular season, when the Chiefs ultimately missed the playoffs. Their most recent postseason meeting came in the AFC Championship Game after the 2024 season, when Kansas City won 32-29 to advance to the Super Bowl. Another close finish should be expected Thursday. The Bills enter at 9-1 and hold a one-game advantage over the 8-2 Chiefs in the AFC standings. Buffalo has won six consecutive games, while Kansas City has responded to its loss against the Seattle Seahawks with three straight victories by at least 22 points. Here are three Kingdom Keys to a Chiefs victory. Offensive key: Run the football in the fourth quarter It will not be enough for the Chiefs to establish the run early. They must be able to lean on it when the game reaches the fourth quarter. Previous matchups between these teams have often turned into late shootouts, with Mahomes and Allen trading possessions until the final minutes. Kansas City now has a running game that can change that formula. The Chiefs rank sixth in total rushing yards (1,342), second in yards per carry (4.9) and sixth in runs of 10 or more yards (37). Kenneth Walker III has led that improvement with 872 rushing yards, seven touchdowns and an average of 5.5 yards per attempt. Walker’s availability remains uncertain after missing the past two games with a groin injury, although he was upgraded to limited participation in Tuesday’s practice. If Walker cannot play, Emmett Johnson has shown he can handle the responsibility. The rookie has rushed for more than 100 yards in consecutive games, totaling 314 yards from scrimmage and three touchdowns during Walker’s absence. Whether Walker returns or Johnson receives another start, Kansas City must remain committed to the ground game. If the Chiefs carry a lead into the fourth quarter, they need to produce a clock-draining drive that forces Buffalo to use its timeouts and keeps Allen on the sideline. Defensive key: Keep Josh Allen in the pocket Keeping Josh Allen in the pocket is not simply about limiting his rushing total. It is about preventing him from extending plays and creating explosive passes after the original play has broken down. Allen is most dangerous when he escapes pressure and forces defensive backs to cover for several more seconds. A play that initially appears to be defended can quickly become a scramble, a deep completion or a touchdown once Allen gets outside the pocket. That is why Kansas City’s pass rush must be disciplined. The Chiefs cannot allow their defensive ends to rush too far upfield and create open escape lanes. The interior rush must also prevent Allen from stepping forward, breaking contain and buying his receivers additional time to uncover. Kansas City has recorded 11 sacks during its three-game winning streak, but pressure alone will not be enough Thursday night. The Chiefs must finish sacks when they reach Allen. A missed opportunity in the backfield cannot turn into an off-schedule completion downfield. Steve Spagnuolo can selectively use a quarterback spy, particularly on third down and in other obvious passing situations. The secondary must also stay disciplined when Allen starts scrambling, rather than abandoning coverage too early. Limiting his rushing yards would certainly help. The larger objective, however, is to force Allen to operate on schedule from inside the pocket. If the Chiefs can prevent him from extending plays and producing the explosive passes that often follow, they’ll have a much better chance of slowing down Buffalo’s offense. X-factor: Turn Buffalo’s mistakes into touchdowns The Bills are 9-1, but they have not always protected the football like a team with one of the NFL’s best records. Buffalo has committed 16 turnovers and enters Thursday with a -1 turnover differential. Allen has thrown nine interceptions, including five over his past four games. Kansas City, meanwhile, ranks fourth in the NFL with a +6 turnover margin. The Bills have shown that they can overcome their mistakes, which makes Kansas City’s response to those opportunities even more important. Forcing a turnover will only be half the assignment. The Chiefs cannot intercept Allen or recover a fumble and then settle for a three-and-out. Against a Buffalo offense averaging 31.3 points per game, extra possessions must become points — preferably touchdowns. Kansas City must also capitalize on Buffalo penalties, failed fourth-down attempts and poor punts. Any possession beginning with favorable field position must be treated as an opportunity to take control of the game. Winning the turnover battle would help. Turning one of Buffalo’s mistakes into seven points could decide the outcome. The bottom line The Chiefs do not need to turn Thanksgiving night into another frantic shootout. Kansas City must use its running game to control the fourth quarter and keep Allen on the sideline. Defensively, the Chiefs must contain Allen in the pocket and keep extended plays from turning into explosive completions. When Buffalo makes a mistake, Mahomes and the offense must turn it into points. If the Chiefs accomplish those three things, they will have an excellent opportunity to end Buffalo’s five-game regular-season winning streak in the rivalry and strengthen their position in the race for the AFC’s No. 1 seed.
author: Maurice Elston

title: Chiefs-Bills Week 12 Tuesday injury report: Kenneth Walker returns limited
summary: Each practice day this season, the Kansas City Chiefs release an official injury report ahead of the next game. In Week 12, the Chiefs play the Buffalo Bills on Thanksgiving night. Here is the Chiefs’ second official injury report of the week, courtesy of the team’s official website. After practice estimations on Monday’s report, Tuesday featured […]
full_text: (Photo by Kevin Sabitus/Getty Images) | Getty Images Each practice day this season, the Kansas City Chiefs release an official injury report ahead of the next game. In Week 12, the Chiefs play the Buffalo Bills on Thanksgiving night. Here is the Chiefs’ second official injury report of the week, courtesy of the team’s official website . After practice estimations on Monday’s report, Tuesday featured the teams actually on the practice field preparing for the game. Chiefs Running back Kenneth Walker (groin) was upgraded to a limited participant and practiced on Tuesday for the first time since injuring his groin prior to the Week 10 game against the Atlanta Falcons . This is what head coach Andy Reid said during his press conference on Tuesday about Walker potentially playing this week. “Let’s see how he does today,” Reid said. “I just want to get him out there and see—really, he wants to get out there and see, but we’ll see how he moves around. He’s feeling pretty good though.” Starting right tackle Jaylon Moore (ankle) did not participate in practice again and hasn’t since leaving the Week 9 game against the New York Jets in the third quarter with an ankle injury. Right guard Trey Smith (concussion) was a full participant in practice again and appears to be set to return after entering concussion protocol during the first quarter of the Week 10 game. Andy Reid Smith “will probably be in” the game this week on Tuesday. Second-year defensive tackle Omarr Norman-Lott (knee) was a limited participant in practice again. He was activated from the Reserve/Physically-Unable-to-Perform list last week, but was scratched on gameday. Tight end Noah Gray (rib) was upgraded to a full participant in practice after missing on Monday after leaving the game against the Arizona Cardinals late with the injury. Fullback Ben VanSumeren (knee) was placed on the Reserve/Injured list on Tuesday. Bills Starting cornerback Christian Benford (groin) was upgraded to a limited participant after he was estimated to not participate in practice on Monday and missed last week’s game. In eight games played this season, Benford has 33 tackles and eight passes defended. In his career against Kansas City, Benford has 2 passes defended, one sack and a forced fumble. Starting right tackle Spencer Brown (back) was upgraded to a full participant in practice after being estimated as limited on Monday. He missed time earlier this year, but has played in the last two games. Starting tight end Dalton Kincaid (thumb/ankle) was a limited participant in practice on Tuesday after being estimated as limited on Monday. He missed last week’s game and has been banged up for a few weeks. This season, Kincaid has seen the second-most catches on the team (32) and has 487 yards and two touchdowns; Kincaid has one touchdown in his career against the Chiefs. Starting right guard O’Cyrus Torrence (ankle) has been a limited participant in practice this week; he has not missed a start this year. Starting linebacker Dorian Williams (calf) has been a limited participant in practice this week after missing last week’s game. This season, Williams has 61 tackles (5 for loss), one sack, two interceptions and four passes defended.
