title: Chiefs sign tackle Fred Johnson to active roster
summary: Early on Tuesday, NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reported that the Kansas City Chiefs would be signing tackle Fred Johnson — who joined their practice squad last week — to the active roster. Johnson had previously been with the Philadelphia Eagles before being waived on November 13 after seven appearances with the team in 2026. The […]
full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA - AUGUST 28: Fred Johnson #74 of the Philadelphia Eagles drops back to block during an NFL preseason game against the Cincinnati Bengals at Lincoln Financial Field on August 28, 2026 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Perry Knotts/Getty Images) | Getty Images Early on Tuesday, NFL Network ’s Ian Rapoport reported that the Kansas City Chiefs would be signing tackle Fred Johnson — who joined their practice squad last week — to the active roster. Johnson had previously been with the Philadelphia Eagles before being waived on November 13 after seven appearances with the team in 2026. The #Chiefs are moving Fred Johnson to their 53-man roster, source says. https://t.co/OHsT3aU7Uf — Ian Rapoport (@RapSheet) November 24, 2026 The player himself appeared to confirm Rapoport’s scoop later in the morning. CHIEFS KINGDOM!!!!!!!! #LETSGETIT #BTO — Fredrick Johnson (@FredDaDon74) November 24, 2026 Later in the afternoon, the Chiefs made the move official. To create a spot for Johnson on the active roster, fullback Ben VanSumeren was placed on the Reserve/Injured list. VanSumeren left Kansas City’s Week 11 win over the Arizona Cardinals with a knee injury. The Chiefs have navigated uncertainty at the tackle position all season in the absence of 2025 first round selection Josh Simmons. The team also appears set to play on Thursday against the Buffalo Bills without right tackle Jaylon Moore, who is recovering from an ankle injury. Moore has missed the Chiefs’ last two games and has not practiced this week. Kansas City was fortunate to be able to add a veteran lineman with positional versatility who has played in 86 NFL games. Whether Johnson will see playing time against Buffalo after being with the team such a short time remains to be seen. “Fred, he’s had time,” head coach Andy Reid said before Tuesday’s practice. “Enough time? We’ll have to see on that. He seems like a sharp kid. He has a ton of experience. He’s got skills. We’ll see how all that goes as we roll.” Johnson’s short time with the Chiefs has made an impression on their most famous player. “Obviously, he’s played football for a number of years — and played really good football,” observed quarterback Patrick Mahomes. “He can play guard and tackle, so that versatility is going to help out a ton. We’ll continue to try to get him more and more work within our offense and within our scheme. I know one thing — he’s a big guy, and he’s athletic. You see why he’s had success in this league. It’s about getting him more and more accustomed to how we do things here.” With Tuesday’s transactions, the Chiefs will have an opening on their practice squad.

title: Chargers Power Rankings Roundup: Bolts’ positive momentum over before it began
summary: The Chargers unfortunately fell short against the Jets 27-24 on Sunday and dropped to 1-9 on the year with seven games remaining. A miraculous late game run to push for a winning record is now impossible and all of you who held out hope for such a thing can now finally let that one go. […]
full_text: Inglewood, CA - November 22: Los Angeles Chargers quarterback Justin Herbert (10) looks for a pass down field during second quarter of an football game between the New York Jets and Los Angeles Chargers at SoFi Stadium in Inglewood, CA, Sunday, Nov. 22, 2026. (Ronaldo Bolaños / Los Angeles Times via Getty Images) The Chargers unfortunately fell short against the Jets 27-24 on Sunday and dropped to 1-9 on the year with seven games remaining. A miraculous late game run to push for a winning record is now impossible and all of you who held out hope for such a thing can now finally let that one go. Another loss further reinforced the Chargers as one of the league’s worst. With a chance to get out of the bottom three in the league, the defense unfortunately could not find any decent footing as the Jets went the entire game without a single punt. Offensively it was a better day for Justin Herbert and that unit, but overall it wasn’t enough to beat a previously 2-win Jets team. With that said, let’s get into the rankings from Week 12. NFL.com – #29 “ After finally winning a game in Week 10, the Chargers returned to their former selves, minus the crushing turnovers. A remarkably quick game saw just 12 possessions combined between the two teams, and the Chargers didn’t quite value them as much as they should have in Sunday’s loss. A complete lack of urgency while facing a 10-point deficit frustrated everyone taking the time to watch this game and included a sequence of snaps that featured a flea flicker on third-and-2, a speed option run by a quarterback (Justin Herbert) who had already taken too many hits, and a pace that ate up nearly eight minutes of time in the fourth quarter. This is an unserious team that unsurprisingly didn’t regain possession after that marathon scoring drive and might not win another game if it continues operating like this. ” Pro Football Talk – #30 “Will Jim Harbaugh be back for 2027?” – Mike Florio ESPN – #31 “ The best player on the Chargers this season is playing out his rookie deal, so the best candidate for an extension is fairly obvious. According to NFL Next Gen Stats, Tuipulotu leads the team with 37 pressures through Sunday. Are the Chargers willing to pay him top edge money, which could be close to $35 million per year? Only time will tell.” – Aaron Schatz The Athletic – #31 “ The sooner this season ends, the better. And this game lasted only 2 hours, 40 minutes, the shortest of the year. The Chargers and Jets had only six possessions apiece Sunday. New York scored on its first five, marking a rare occasion when the defense let down Los Angeles. The Chargers are now next to last in the league in offensive EPA per drive (minus-0.80).” – Josh Kendall and Chad Graff CBS Sports – #31 “ After winning at Baltimore, they were back to being the Chargers again, losing to the Jets. This team has to make changes. ” Sports Illustrated – #31 “On the MMQB pod, Albert Breer breathlessly details the potential death knell in the Jim Harbaugh era: a long, meandering drive to nowhere with the game on the line.” – Conor Orr Yahoo Sports – #32 “ Good thing the Chargers got that win in Week 10. Losing to the Jets on Sunday at home was a strong indication that Los Angeles might not win again. “ “At least there were a couple of decent performances on offense. title: Aaron Rodgers wishes he had a coach like Sean McVay
summary: We have never seen a player, let alone a Hall of Fame quarterback, go off on a head coach while he’s still on the team like what Aaron Rodgers did to Mike McCarthy on Wednesday. One day before the holiday, Rodgers made it clear that he’s not thankful for McCarthy or the Pittsburgh Steelers after […]
full_text: We have never seen a player, let alone a Hall of Fame quarterback, go off on a head coach while he’s still on the team like what Aaron Rodgers did to Mike McCarthy on Wednesday. One day before the holiday, Rodgers made it clear that he’s not thankful for McCarthy or the Pittsburgh Steelers after the quarterback was benched on Tuesday night and had to find out through teammate Pat Freiermuth. During a surprise appearance on The Pat McAfee Show on Wednesday, Rodgers said that McCarthy has been snoring during meetings, missing walkthroughs, and broke a halftime in the locker room during Sunday’s loss to the Eagles with “1-2-3 Packers”. Rodgers said that he told McCarthy during a “contentious” meeting on Monday that he should do the right thing and give up play calling duties, so the head coach decided to bench him for Mason Rudolph for Friday’s game against the Denver Broncos. The Steelers management and ownership decided to back McCarthy, according to Rodgers, so he says his career with the franchise is definitively over. In the same interview, Rodgers name dropped Sean McVay, among a couple of other head coaches, as the types of play callers who probably get deeply involved with working with the starting quarterback to make a game plan and watch film, which he says McCarthy never does. BREAKING NEWS: @AaronRodgers12 addresses being benched by the Pittsburgh Steelers #PMSLive pic.twitter.com/6rggspWDGX — Pat McAfee (@PatMcAfeeShow) November 25, 2026 There were rumors floating around in previous years that if Matthew Stafford were to retire that Aaron Rodgers would be someone who may be interested in the organization and vice versa. It seems even more obvious now that what Rodgers has really wanted in a head coach is a play caller who seems invested in the game plan, someone like McVay. For all the grief that McVay gets when the Rams don’t win the Super Bowl — and especially during a tumultuous season like this one — that there are qualities to being a head coach that never get appreciated. Like being able to keep a powder keg from exploding. Clearly that’s something that Mike Tomlin was doing for many years, and why Pittsburgh didn’t fire him for so long despite not winning a playoff game in a decade. If McVay is not the head coach next year, or the year after that, whether it’s his choice or the franchise, remember how quickly things can fall apart without a reliable person to steady the ship. Even when the Steelers are 6-4, same record as the Rams, the boat can brake apart overnight. Sometimes even on a Tuesday night.

title: Matthew Stafford has to play well against the Green Bay blitz
summary: Quarterback Matthew Stafford has to beat the blitz if the Los Angeles Rams want to defeat the Green Bay Packers Wednesday night. If he can’t, L.A. is in big trouble. Considering how important this game is for the Rams’ playoff chances, there’s no alternative for finding a way to counter one of the Packers’ best […]
full_text: Quarterback Matthew Stafford has to beat the blitz if the Los Angeles Rams want to defeat the Green Bay Packers Wednesday night. If he can’t, L.A. is in big trouble. Considering how important this game is for the Rams’ playoff chances , there’s no alternative for finding a way to counter one of the Packers’ best weapons. Green Bay has done a good job getting after the quarterback this year. It’s second in the NFL in pressure rate at 40.2% according to Next Gen Stats, only behind the 46.2% clip of the Minnesota Vikings. While the Packers don’t blitz nearly as much as Brian Flores and the Vikings do, their defensive coordinator, Jonathan Gannon, still brings plenty of extra pass rushers. Green Bay has the NFL’s eighth-highest blitz rate at 35.8%. The books expect the Rams to lean pass tonight … Stafford over/under 34.5 pass atts Kyren Williams over/under 12.5 carries Blake Corum over/under 11.5 carries Rams were -11.2% pass rate over expected last time out. 🤔🤔🤔 — Jared Smola (@SmolaDS) November 25, 2026 Meanwhile, this has not been Stafford’s best season against blitzes. For the year, he’s 18th in the NFL in EPA per dropback when blitzed, actually giving away .06 points per dropback in those situations. Considering he has the sixth-most pass attempts when blitz, that’s a lot of ineffective plays over the balance of the season. For comparison’s sake, when not blitzed this year Stafford is ninth in the league in EPA per dropback. The Packers like to blitz. Stafford has struggled against the blitz. You can see where this is headed on Wednesday night. The Rams can find a few ways to mitigate this issue. For one, Stafford is throwing short (0-9 yards) on 49.5% of his dropbacks this season. The Packers have been good at limiting yards after the catch this season, but getting the ball out quickly can help neutralize the extra pressure. Obviously, the offensive line has to play well. That shouldn’t be particularly concerning for the Rams, because they’ve handled pass protection well all season. Pass protection composite ratings pic.twitter.com/L2zSQHURig — Computer Cowboy (@benbbaldwin) November 24, 2026 Los Angeles is ninth in ESPN’s Pass Rush Win Rate metric and they’re seventh in the NFL in PFF’s pass protection grades. There’s also one other potentially interesting wrinkle involved here: Micah Parsons. The three-time first-team All-Pro will make his season debut Wednesday after missing the Packers’ first 10 games due to recovery from a torn ACL. It goes without saying that the Rams would prefer to not face one of the best pass rushers in the league, one of the few other players even in Myles Garrett’s stratosphere. But we also don’t know what the Packers will look like defensively with him on the field. Gannon said earlier this month that he has game planned for Parsons’s return “every day,” but he’s never actually coached him before. Will the Packers continue to blitz at a well above-average rate with him back? Or will they try to win with just four and bank on Parsons adding enough juice to make up for it? Matthew Stafford since joining the Rams: November: 41 TDs, 14 INTs, 97.0 passer rating December: 45 TDs, 11 INTs, 101.5 passer rating 26-11 record in those months combined, 15-3 (!!!!) in December alone. — Sosa Kremenjas (@QBsMVP) November 23, 2026 The Packers want to attack you and they will want to attack the Rams. They have an interception-hungry secondary and want to use their blitz pressures to force quarterbacks into bad throws. If Matthew Stafford can avoid that quagmire, either thanks to his offensive line or his own heroics, the Rams’ offense should be in good shape. If it remains an issue, there will be far more pressure on the Los Angeles defense to carry this game.

title: By the numbers: Rams’ Matthew Stafford in November
summary: Matthew Stafford has developed a reputation for playing some of his best football as the NFL season gets deeper and deeper into the calendar. For the Los Angeles Rams, November has provided plenty of opportunities for the veteran quarterback to showcase his experience, elevate his game and help position the team for a postseason push. […]
full_text: GLENDALE, ARIZONA - NOVEMBER 15: Quarterback Matthew Stafford #9 of the Los Angeles Rams warms up before a game against the Arizona Cardinals at State Farm Stadium on November 15, 2026 in Glendale, Arizona. (Photo by Mike Christy/Getty Images) | Getty Images Matthew Stafford has developed a reputation for playing some of his best football as the NFL season gets deeper and deeper into the calendar. For the Los Angeles Rams, November has provided plenty of opportunities for the veteran quarterback to showcase his experience, elevate his game and help position the team for a postseason push. Since joining the Rams in 2021, Stafford has put together an impressive collection of numbers during the month of November. Through the Rams’ November games in 2026, he has appeared in 19 games during the month, compiling an 11-8 record as the team’s quarterback. Here is a look at Stafford’s November production since arriving in Los Angeles: Matthew Stafford’s November stats (2021–2026): Win-loss record: 11-8 Completions/Attempts: 410-of-642 (63.8%) Passing yards: 4,552 Passing touchdowns: 41 Interceptions: 14 Perhaps the most impressive aspect of Stafford’s November production is his ability to generate touchdowns while limiting turnovers. Across those 19 appearances, he has thrown nearly three touchdowns for every interception, demonstrating his ability to take care of the football while continuing to push the ball downfield. His November numbers have also improved considerably over the years. In 2021, Stafford threw five touchdowns and five interceptions in three November appearances. In 2022, he was limited to two appearances, throwing three touchdowns without an interception. By 2024, he had accumulated 1,129 passing yards and eight touchdowns in four November games. His most productive November as a Ram came in 2025. Stafford completed 106 of 159 passes for 1,207 yards, 15 touchdowns and just two interceptions across five games. That production included four consecutive victories to begin the month. Matthew Stafford since joining the Rams: November: 41 TDs, 14 INTs, 97.0 passer rating December: 45 TDs, 11 INTs, 101.5 passer rating 26-11 record in those months combined, 15-3 (!!!!) in December alone. — Sosa Kremenjas (@QBsMVP) November 23, 2026 Stafford has continued that success in 2026, throwing five touchdowns and three interceptions while completing 64.9% of his passes through three November appearances. As the Rams prepare for the final stretch of the regular season, Stafford’s historical November production offers another reason for optimism. At 38 years old, the veteran quarterback continues to demonstrate that experience matters when the stakes get higher and the season begins to wind down.

title: Which Rams pass catcher will stand out versus Packers?
summary: With Puka Nacua, Davante Adams, and Terrance Ferguson all out for the Los Angeles Rams in a highly anticipated Wednesday night clash against the Green Bay Packers, fans and fantasy players are asking themselves which LA pass catcher will step up for Matthew Stafford. The Rams are about to play an all-important game without the […]
full_text: With Puka Nacua, Davante Adams, and Terrance Ferguson all out for the Los Angeles Rams in a highly anticipated Wednesday night clash against the Green Bay Packers, fans and fantasy players are asking themselves which LA pass catcher will step up for Matthew Stafford. The Rams are about to play an all-important game without the two players (Nacua and Adams) who took the bulk of Matthew Stafford’s targets this season. Nacua and Ferguson aren’t coming back. Adams, at least, won’t return this week. The remaining pure wide receivers—Konata Mumpfield, CJ Daniels, Tutu Atwell, and Xavier Smith—have combined for fewer than 450 receiving yards on the season so far. It’s not an ideal group to ask to carry a 300-yard passing performance if LA ends up needing that from Stafford. The most useful question is not which wideout steps up—it’s whether the most productive pass catcher Wednesday night is even a receiver. In the last game without Nacua and Adams—two weeks ago against the Cardinals—half of Stafford’s passes were aimed at Kyren Williams, Blake Corum, and Tyler Higbee. In other words, the receivers are complimentary pieces. Their contributions are simply value adds. The Rams aren’t relying on them to produce in order to stay afloat. That is to say, of course, if all goes according to plan. You can beat the Cardinals by relying on a strong running game and leaning on backs and tight ends in the passing game. The Rams have spent the last five weeks or so beating up bad teams. As competition tightens, it’s still an open question whether Los Angeles has enough talent to keep pace. Our first answer will come against the Packers, whose offense can get vertical fast and put up points in a hurry. The task at hand isn’t just to hold water until Adams returns. The Rams need to find out whether the existing receiving corps has a playmaker within them. If not, LA stands effectively no chance into the playoffs. So I ask this question to you, Rams fans. Which pass catcher steps up on Wednesday night against the Packers and will it be enough to keep the team relevant this season?

title: Puka Nacua injury details reveal ‘completely torn’ MCL
summary: Puka Nacua may have a hard time trusting Sean McVay after his latest injury. The Los Angeles Rams’ top receiver’s decision to get knee surgery was not a hasty one after all, as Nacua’s MCL was “completely torn” off of his tibia, making it a Grade 3 strain, according to ESPN’s Adam Schefter. Nacua is […]
full_text: Puka Nacua may have a hard time trusting Sean McVay after his latest injury. The Los Angeles Rams’ top receiver’s decision to get knee surgery was not a hasty one after all , as Nacua’s MCL was “completely torn” off of his tibia, making it a Grade 3 strain, according to ESPN’s Adam Schefter. Nacua is expected to be in recovery for at least the next four months, but the decision to get surgery is based on the belief that without it he would have never been the same again. With surgery, Nacua should be able to fully recover and be back to his usual self by Week 1 of 2027, according to most experts. Schefter on Puka: – Rams want to/will try to keep him but we will see (injury/off field) – MCL injury was grade 3. Completely torn off tibia – Also had a “tear off the posterior oblique portion of the MCL as well” – would have been performance limiting/degenerative w/o surgery — A.B. (@FantasyKash) November 24, 2026 It’s hard to believe this catastrophe could have been so easily avoided. The Rams were ready to throw in the towel on their last offensive snap against the Washington Commanders and punt the ball away with a lead, but for some reason McVay called an end-around for Nacua to throw him into the fire at full speed in the middle of the field. The hit on Nacua caused damage to his MCL and PCL, requiring season-ending surgery. Nacua is also dealing with turf toe. Given how poorly injury diagnoses have gone for L.A. this season — from Myles Garrett to Terrance Ferguson to Davante Adams and Nacua — can any players or fans trust a return timeline from McVay ever again? From @BigDayESPN : If the #Rams are going to make a run, they’ll have to do it without WR Puka Nacua and with Davante Adams not quite back yet. pic.twitter.com/0BiMCTp3SQ — Ian Rapoport (@RapSheet) November 24, 2026 With surgery, there’s little skepticism that Nacua will be able to be a top-tier receiver by next season. That’s good news for the Rams, but only if they decide to keep him. It would be ludicrous for L.A. to let Nacua become a free agent ( they almost certainly won’t do that ) but equally foolish for the receiver to play on a franchise tag in 2027. Given the number of injuries he has suffered in an offense practically designed to injure receivers, Nacua must not play for the Rams again without a long-term contract. L.A. should consider how bad their team might look next season without Puka Nacua. This surgery allows Nacua the chance to fully recover in time to participate in OTAs, but only if the Rams have extended him first. Makes sense why Puka Nacua got surgery. Complete MCL plus POL (part of the posteromedial corner that helps add rotational stability to the knee). Should heal up well with low long term impact on knee health. Could be a good buying opp despite team uncertainty in 2027 https://t.co/bkmT9GMpoC — Jeff Mueller, PT, DPT (@jmthrivept) November 24, 2026 An extension for Nacua will be costly, but actually take up less cap space in 2027 than a franchise tag. A lot less. With as many free agency priorities as they have, the Rams should think about extending Nacua as soon as they can. It may also depend on the futures of Matthew Stafford and McVay. If both of those people move on in 2027 to other things in life — retirement or the booth — then the Rams may have other priorities in mind. Nacua might be thinking of moving on too.

title: The Rams have to beat the Packers to control their own destiny
summary: If the Los Angeles Rams want to make the NFL postseason, they’d better find a way to beat the Green Bay Packers on Wednesday night. Otherwise, we’re likely barreling toward one of the biggest single-season flops in modern league history. That’s harsh, to be sure, but it’s also the reality the Rams are currently facing. […]
full_text: If the Los Angeles Rams want to make the NFL postseason, they’d better find a way to beat the Green Bay Packers on Wednesday night. Otherwise, we’re likely barreling toward one of the biggest single-season flops in modern league history. That’s harsh, to be sure, but it’s also the reality the Rams are currently facing. This was the heavy preseason favorite to win the Super Bowl, currently sitting on the outside looking in at the playoff picture as we enter Week 12. If they can’t edge out a team in a similarly precarious position, and one with a devastating weakness, at that , reality will get even more grim. More I think about Packers at Rams, more I think it’s the most consequential game of this regular season. The winner is likely going to the playoffs. The loser very likely isn’t. — DaBearsBlog (@dabearsblog) November 24, 2026 This overall point is fleshed out by the math. There is massive playoff leverage on the line for whichever wins (and, subsequently, whichever one loses). According to RBSDM.com , Los Angeles currently has a 42% chance to make the playoffs. With a win on Thanksgiving Eve, the odds are bumped up to 56%. With a loss? They plummet to merely 20%. Compared to The Athletic’s playoff predictor , RBSDM’s modeling is actually rosy for the Rams. That outlet gives L.A. just a 34% chance of reaching the postseason as things currently stand. It increases to 47% with a win and drops off to 16% with a loss. The obvious storylines and narratives, and simply looking at the upcoming schedule, flesh out what the models are indicating. Packers and Rams both have a bye next week then play on Wednesday the 25th, Thanksgiving eve. That’s basically the season on the line with the way this is all shaking out. That tiebreaker will be HUGE at the end of the year. The Packers being 4-4 in the conference while 1-3 in… pic.twitter.com/v9MKkhVV0J — Kurt Benkert (@KurtBenkert) November 16, 2026 Right now, the Packers are clinging to the No. 7 seed in the NFC playoffs. The Seattle Seahawks are one spot back of them, followed by the Rams and they’re all 6-4 entering this week’s action. The Packers and Seahawks don’t play each other, so that potential tiebreaker is a little more complicated than simply head-to-head results, but Green Bay obviously is in control for the time being. Los Angeles gets at least one crack at both, however, with two meetings against Seattle. Blowing a chance to win the tiebreaker over the Packers would be devastating. Per Tankathon , the Rams have the second-most challenging schedule left in the NFL, only behind that of the Chicago Bears. The Seahawks are fourth in that metric while the Packers are seventh. None of those home stretches are particularly easy, but it’s an especially difficult road for the Rams. Throw in a lost tiebreaker and it gets scary quickly. It isn’t impossible for the Rams to make the playoffs with a loss on Wednesday night, but it becomes exceptionally difficult and it takes their fate out of their hands. Even if Los Angeles sweeps Seattle late in the season, a loss this week means it would need help to crack the top seven in the NFC. This team has already had to battle through so much, and we’re only 2/3 of the way through the season. It’s only getting more difficult with each passing devastating injury . In case there was any doubt Micah Parsons is playing against the Rams, Myles Garrett says the Packers OLB reached out to him asking for extra tickets for Wednesdays game — Adam Grosbard (@AdamGrosbard) November 23, 2026 From an objective viewpoint, that desperation is what makes this week’s matchup such incredible theater, especially considering the Packers are essentially in the same boat. They’re almost certainly toast for the postseason with a loss. The Rams would love to make that their opponents’ reality this week. For their own sake, they have to.

title: Micah Parsons will make 2026 debut against Rams
summary: The Green Bay Packers have activated Micah Parsons in time for Wednesday’s game against the Los Angeles Rams. It will be the star pass rusher’s first game since he tore his ACL almost one year ago in a loss to the Broncos on December 14. Parsons told the media on Monday that he was looking […]
full_text: The Green Bay Packers have activated Micah Parsons in time for Wednesday’s game against the Los Angeles Rams. It will be the star pass rusher’s first game since he tore his ACL almost one year ago in a loss to the Broncos on December 14. Parsons told the media on Monday that he was looking forward to facing the Rams and helping Green Bay make the playoffs if he was cleared to play , which is now the case. “I’m so locked in on what’s ahead of me and I understand what this game Wednesday means to the organization and I myself and what it means for playoffs,” Parsons said. “And if I can be out there, I want to be out there and I’m excited for any time. Because we only got seven more games left, so I want to capitalize on all those if I can.” Parsons had 12.5 sacks in 14 games during his debut season with the Packers after he was traded to Green Bay by the Dallas Cowboys in exchange for two first-round picks. Still only 27, Parsons has been on the Physically Unable to Perform list while rehabbing from a torn ACL. He has never had fewer than 12 sacks in a season. The Packers have the same 6-4 record as the L.A. Rams, meaning that Wednesday’s game is monumental in the hunt for a wild card spot in the NFC. The Rams could at least temporarily move into the 7-seed with a win over Green Bay. They’ll now have to contend with a motivated Micah Parsons in his first game in almost a year.
author: Kenneth Arthur

title: Could Aaron Donald play in 2027?
summary: Could Aaron Donald really return to the NFL in 2027? After stepping away from football following the 2023 season, the former Los Angeles Rams defensive tackle has found himself back around the game in 2026, and the possibility of another season is worth hypothesizing. One of the biggest reasons a return could be appealing is […]
full_text: LAS VEGAS, NEVADA - OCTOBER 25: Aaron Donald #99 of the Los Angeles Rams looks on in the second quarter of a game against the Las Vegas Raiders at Allegiant Stadium on October 25, 2026 in Las Vegas, Nevada. (Photo by Ian Maule/Getty Images) | Getty Images Could Aaron Donald really return to the NFL in 2027? After stepping away from football following the 2023 season, the former Los Angeles Rams defensive tackle has found himself back around the game in 2026, and the possibility of another season is worth hypothesizing. One of the biggest reasons a return could be appealing is that Donald appears to be having fun again. When he originally retired, it wasn’t necessarily because he had lost his love for football. Rather, the grind of an NFL season had taken its toll. Donald spent much of his career dealing with constant double and triple teams, making it increasingly difficult to enjoy the game when opposing offenses built their entire protection schemes around stopping him. “I think we’ve got a good core group, that played with each other, that knows how to play with each other.” 🎙️ Aaron Donald on the Defense pic.twitter.com/XtjotPMMco — Los Angeles Rams (@RamsNFL) November 22, 2026 That could make the idea of returning under different circumstances particularly interesting. For years, Donald was the player opposing offenses had to account for on every snap. Garrett has become one of the league’s most dominant defensive forces in his own right. Putting those two together has created a nightmare for opposing offensive lines. More importantly, Garrett gives Donald something he rarely experienced during his prime: another elite pass rusher demanding attention. Instead of facing constant double teams, Donald is now having opportunities to attack one-on-one matchups while Garrett draws his own share of protection. Next time we see get to the see the dynamic duo of Aaron Donald & Myles Garrett in action is on Thanksgiving Eve 👀 Rams captain @qlakee pulled back the curtain with @brock .vereen & @alex_curry on what it’s really like sharing a locker room with Aaron Donald and Myles Garrett.… pic.twitter.com/BG2wFYzI2t — 97.1 The Fan (@TheFanLA) November 21, 2026 At this stage of his career, Donald knows that he does not have to carry a defense. He gets to pick his spots, create pressure in obvious passing situations and make an impact without having to play every down. Of course, there are significant questions. Donald would be approaching another year away from his original retirement, and the physical demands of playing defensive tackle at the NFL level are enormous. Even for one of the greatest defensive players in league history, returning for 2027 would be a considerable challenge. Still, if Donald is enjoying football again and the opportunity to keep playing alongside Garrett is still available, it’s difficult to completely dismiss the possibility. A 2027 return might be unlikely, but the thought of Donald and Garrett lining up together for a second year is worth discussing.

title: Brock Bowers returns to practice
summary: The Las Vegas Raiders began the practice week to prepare for Sunday night’s crucial game at the Cleveland Browns with some good news. Superstar tight end Brock Bowers was present at the start of practice according to media reports. That is a good sign Bowers, barring a setback should be in line to play at […]
full_text: (Photo by Brooke Sutton/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Las Vegas Raiders began the practice week to prepare for Sunday night’s crucial game at the Cleveland Browns with some good news. Superstar tight end Brock Bowers was present at the start of practice according to media reports. That is a good sign Bowers, barring a setback should be in line to play at the Browns. Bowers missed Sunday’s loss at the Denver Broncos with an ankle injury that kept him to 11 snaps in a home loss to the Seattle Seahawks. He practiced on a limited basis Thursday and Friday last week before being ruled out. Raiders’ head coach Klint Kubiak said after the Denver game that the team was hopeful Bowers could play against the Browns. Meanwhile, defensive tackle Tonka Hemingway (stinger) was back at practice Wednesday after missing the Denver game. The only two Las Vegas players reportedly not present to start practice Wednesday were defensive tackles Tim Keenan (knee) and Adam Butler (concussion). They were both hurt at Denver. Also, defensive end Patrick Johnson was at practice, which begins his 21-day practice window from being removed from the injured reserve. This post will be updated after the injury report is released.

title: Ashton Jeanty, Jack Bech answer the bell
summary: Here is a look at how the Las Vegas Raiders’ 2025 draft class fared in a 38-24 road loss at the Denver Broncos on Sunday and what to look for Sunday at the Cleveland Browns: Ashton Jeanty: The No. 6 overall draft pick played 84 percent of the snaps and had 79 yards rushing on […]
full_text: (Photo by Justin Edmonds/Getty Images) | Getty Images Here is a look at how the Las Vegas Raiders’ 2025 draft class fared in a 38-24 road loss at the Denver Broncos on Sunday and what to look for Sunday at the Cleveland Browns: Ashton Jeanty: The No. 6 overall draft pick played 84 percent of the snaps and had 79 yards rushing on 11 carries, including a 46-yard run. He also had a 68-yard touchdown catch. He needs to keep this explosion going. Jack Bech: The second-round pick played a career 55 snaps and had eight catches for 88 yards on nine targets, also a career high. He has finally made an impact and he was Fernando Mendoza’s security blanket with star tight end Brock Bowers out. With Bowers coming back, Bech needs to find a way to make an impact moving forward. Darien Porter: The third-round pick was a starter as recently as Week 9. At Denver, Porter didn’t play one defensive snap and played just three snaps on special teams. It will be interesting if he plays any cornerback at Cleveland. Caleb Rogers: The benched starter played just four special teams snaps. Charles Grant: The offensive lineman, taken in the third round, played four special teams snaps. Dont’e Thornton: The wide receiver, taken in the fourth round, has been on the 53-man roster for four games and he was inactive for all four games. Tonka Hemingway: The fourth-round pick missed Week 11 due to an injury. The team is hopeful he plays at Cleveland. JJ Pegues: The defensive tackle, taken in the sixth round, was injured in the fourth quarter at Denver. He will be monitored through the week. Cody Lindenberg: The seventh-round pick played 29 snaps on special teams, which is his norm. He has played just three defensive snaps this season.

His last one against the Broncos displayed why he could be the Raiders’ franchise quarterback. His three-touchdown performance after falling behind 17-0 showed toughness and grit. Of course, Mendoza’s leap in throwing downfield was big from Week 10 to 11. Expect Mendoza to keep this going and improve in this area as well.

title: ‘Madden’ exclusive interview: Simms May
summary: I got the opportunity to sit down and interview actor Simms May, who portrays Michael Madden in the Amazon Prime Video “Madden” movie. You can check out the full interview, From the Set to the Silver and Black: Simms May on “Madden.” Here’s the link. It was a great opportunity to see what happens behind […]
full_text: (Photo by Kirby Lee/NFLPhotoLibrary) | Getty Images I got the opportunity to sit down and interview actor Simms May, who portrays Michael Madden in the Amazon Prime Video “Madden” movie. You can check out the full interview, From the Set to the Silver and Black: Simms May on “Madden.” Here’s the link. It was a great opportunity to see what happens behind the scenes of movies and talk about the biggest project of a young career. May nailed his role as a young knucklehead with one of the most recognizable dads in America. The most incredible part about his role was that he was unable to meet with any of the Madden family until the night of the premiere. He ultimately achieved the nod of approval and praise from Mr. Michael Madden himself, which is a big deal for an actor making only his fourth appearance on the big screen. When auditioning for the part, Simms didn’t know what the movie was about. In fact, they used the code name Santa Maria’s BBQ. An interesting caveat for any aspiring actors: you won’t know what you are actually auditioning for until you land the role. Locking in and securing the role became the mission for May and he was extremely excited to know what he was participating in when he landed it. Through some of his research and after the creation of the movie, May showed excellent life-decision-making skills in turning towards the dark side and becoming a part of Raider Nation. Making his hometown team, the Atlanta Falcons, rise up and kick rocks. Why? Because he learned about the previously winningest team in NFL history, the greatest organization, with the greatest coaches and “just win, baby.” Famous co-stars On the set, May worked alongside high-level method actors Nicholas Cage (John Madden) and Christian Bale (Al Davis). Detailing throughout the entire shoot, only three times did he come into contact with Nicholas Cage and not Madden, his movie dad. His favorite co-star was none other than Shane Gillis, their movie neighbor and resident funny man. Gillis was the same guy off-set that he was on it, absolutely hilarious. Regrettably, May had concluded the filming of his role prior to Marshawn BeastMode Lynch arriving on set to film his. However, he did get to see current Raiders superstar Maxx Crosby come in, film his role and got to hang out on set. Joy in exploits May is jubilant about being in the Madden movie, indoctrinating himself into such an outstanding fanbase and being able to further his own career all at once. Getting to work with brilliant actors and being on set with a comedian was like unlocking stairs to the next level of personal greatness. Much like the 2026 Raiders, he started at the bottom, but now he’s here.

title: Fernando Mendoza draws praise in Week 12 NFL Power Rankings for Las Vegas Raiders
summary: Fernando Mendoza is two games into his tenure as the Las Vegas Raiders’ starting quarterback. While he’s 0-2 in those outings, there have been a handful of promising moments, and he’s coming off a three-touchdown performance against a strong Denver Broncos defense. As a result, Mendoza has drawn plenty of praise in the Week 12 […]
full_text: (Photo by Justin Edmonds/Getty Images) | Getty Images Fernando Mendoza is two games into his tenure as the Las Vegas Raiders’ starting quarterback. While he’s 0-2 in those outings, there have been a handful of promising moments, and he’s coming off a three-touchdown performance against a strong Denver Broncos defense . As a result, Mendoza has drawn plenty of praise in the Week 12 NFL Power Rankings across the league’s media. Bleacher Report 21. Las Vegas Raiders Last week: 18 The Las Vegas Raiders have lost both games in which Fernando Mendoza started. Yet, the resiliency seen from this year’s No. 1 overall draft pick has been impressive. The Denver Broncos built a 17-0 lead Sunday. Mendoza is going to have his ups and downs, of course. At the same time, the rookie signal-caller led his team to 17 straight points before everything started to fall apart again. In doing so, he opened some eyes among the Raiders’ division rival. “There certainly was a lot of respect for Fernando Mendoza in the Broncos locker room,” James Palmer reported . “What stood out was how calm he was in the pocket and his feel in the pocket, as well as how unpredictable he is when he starts to move. Most young players have something they do and go to it over and over again. Mendoza scrambles out a variety of ways and scans the field well while doing it.” — Brent Sobleski To be fair, the No. 1 pick did play a role in everything falling apart for the Raiders. After tying the game, he missed Jalen Nailor on an open fourth-down conversion and had the pick-six that sealed the team’s fate. However, the defense was undoubtedly the bigger issue. Denver scored touchdowns on its two possessions after the contest was knotted up at 17 with about five minutes left in the third quarter. Also, it’s hard to win when the other team’s offense scores 31 points and has 350 yards from scrimmage . Granted, the Raiders outgained the Broncos by 19 yards despite running four fewer plays and losing the time of possession battle by about 7.5 minutes. Mendoza has to avoid the big mistake, but he’s far from the biggest reason the Silver and Black lost on Sunday. NFL.com 20. Las Vegas Raiders Last week: 21 I’m fascinated to see what the Raiders can do to improve their defense this offseason because I know this offense can put up points. Fernando Mendoza produced the first strong game of his career, and the Silver and Black delivered an entertaining contest against a superior Broncos squad in Denver, which is a good sign about where Las Vegas is headed in the bigger, multiyear picture. — Nick Shook This picks up right where the section above left off. Las Vegas ranks third-to-last in yards allowed ( 382.0 ) and dead last in points allowed (29.7) per game, signalling big changes are needed on defense in the offseason. Defensive tackle should be the starting point, and it will be interesting to see how the young corners — Jermod McCoy, Hezekiah Masses and Darien Porter — finish the season. Adding another edge-rusher wouldn’t hurt either, but the Raiders will get Keyron Crawford back from injury next season to give the position group a young talent to turn to. The Athletic 22. Las Vegas Raiders Last week: 20 Something to be thankful for: Fernando Mendoza’s learning curve After making his first two starts against Seattle and Denver, the rookie quarterback is a predictable 0-2. The good news is he threw for 267 yards and three touchdowns against the Broncos, and the road gets easier from here. “I was really impressed with (Mendoza’s) off-schedule stuff,” Broncos coach Sean Payton said. “I was more impressed with his size and his escapability than maybe I saw on tape.” — Josh Kendall, Chad Graff It’s funny, being able to make out of structure plays was viewed as one of the Indiana product’s weaknesses coming out of college. But something that stood out about his game during the Mendoza Mania series this summer was his ability to make defenders wrong when scrambling; either using his legs to move the ball or dumping it to receivers when defenders don’t plaster. We’ve seen that pop up a few times in the last two weeks, and, as Payton mentioned, Mendoza’s escapability was much better from start one to start two. ESPN 22. Las Vegas Raiders Last week: 22 Extension candidate: TE Brock Bowers Bowers will be eligible for an extension in the offseason, and Las Vegas shouldn’t waste time locking down a franchise cornerstone. Despite battling knee and ankle injuries this season, he still has been productive, with 50 catches for 676 receiving yards and six touchdowns. Having Bowers around for the early stages of quarterback Fernando Mendoza’s career will be essential for the No. 1 pick’s development. Negotiations between Bowers and the Raiders could get interesting, given the number of times he has lined up on the outside this season. — Ryan McFadden McFadden brings up a point that helps add some context/encouragement about Mendoza’s first two starts: Bowers has only been on the field for 11 snaps in the last two weeks, per Pro Football Focus . That leaves the rookie quarterback with an underwhelming crew of pass-catchers, and he’s still managed to turn heads. The problem is that’s music to Bowers’ agent’s ears, as he’s about to get paid like a ‘WR1’ when the time comes. Luckily, the Raiders can buy themselves some time in the negotiation by picking up his fifth-year option this spring. According to Over The Cap , that will cost $17.35 million for 2028, which would make him the fifth-highest-paid tight end in terms of dollars per year . Seeing as the two-time Pro Bowler will undoubtedly make more than that when his contract is up, exercising the option is a no-brainer. MMQB 23. Las Vegas Raiders Last week: 19 Some coaches spend minutes saying absolutely nothing. Klint Kubiak is the polar opposite in terms of meaningful words per second in pre-halftime interviews . — Conor Orr We’re veering away from the main topic here; Orr is referencing Kubiak’s halftime interview where he said the refs need to call the game both ways when asked about the penalty discrepancy between the two teams last Sunday. The Raiders were flagged nine times for 63 yards , while the Broncos had just two penalties for 10 yards in the contest. Even more interesting, Vegas averages the third-fewest penalties per game (5.7) this season while Denver is tied for 16th (7.1), according to TeamRankings . The one that stood out to me the most was Cody White getting called for offensive pass interference, which wiped away a touchdown, while the play below by Courtland Sutton wasn’t penalized. Then again, this is nothing new for Raider Nation. While the incompletion is a result of Sutton running into Johnson, this is solid coverage from Jermod McCoy on Sutton against the mesh concept #Raiders pic.twitter.com/sXvxZGziFu — Matt Holder (@MHolder95) November 23, 2026

full_text: (Photo by Ian Maule/Getty Images) | Getty Images There is a potential major NFL offseason story looming in Los Angeles. Could superstar wide receiver Puka Nacua really be moved from the Los Angeles Rams? ESPN reporter Jeremy Fowler recently suggested Nacua will be playing elsewhere in 2027. Nacua is a free agent and he doesn’t seem close to signing an extension with the Rams. He has off-field issues and there seems to be some confusion on his season-ending surgery. So, according to Fowler, that could all point to Nacua not being a member of the Rams next year. If that’s the case, there will be no shortage of interested teams. The most likely way of acquiring him would be for the Rams to give him the franchise tag and then trade him. Whatever the way Nacua could be obtained, the Raiders would likely be among the most interested teams in Nacua. They could afford him and he would be a major upgrade at wide receiver. Again, at this point, it is all speculation, but if Fowler is right, this will be a major story to follow. full_text: MIAMI GARDENS, FLORIDA - NOVEMBER 01: Jacob Rodriguez #10 of the Miami Dolphins is introduced prior to a game against the New England Patriots at Hard Rock Stadium on November 01, 2026 in Miami Gardens, Florida. (Photo by Megan Briggs/Getty Images) | Getty Images Great linebacker play has been a staple of the Miami Dolphins throughout the history of the franchise. From Nick Buoniconti, A.J. Duhe, John Offerdahl and Bryan Cox, all the way up to Zach Thomas, Junior Seau, Joey Porter and now Jordyn Brooks, Dolphins fans have been blessed to witness the play of some of the greats of the game. Keeping with tradition, the season that 2026 second-round pick Jacob Rodriguez is having is giving the youngster a chance to possibly etch his name in the record books. During his rookie season in 1996, future Hall-of-Fame linebacker Zach Thomas finished his first campaign as a professional with 154 combined tackles. That mark set a rookie record for Miami — one that has yet to be broken… yet. However, that record is in danger of being surpassed by Rodriguez this season. Through ten games, Rodriguez ranks 8th in the National Football League with 93 combined tackles — 9.3 per game. If Miami’s sensational rookie can avoid injury and the daunting “rookie wall,” he’ll finish the year with roughly 158 tackles — four more than Thomas had in the greatest rookie year a Dolphins’ linebacker has ever had. The accomplishment would be a bright spot in an otherwise difficult year for the South Florida franchise. Now, it’s worth noting that Thomas’ record was set when the NFL played just 16 regular season games before the playoffs started — one less than the 17 games the league currently plays, so if Rodriguez wants to lay claim to the record without an asterisk, he’ll need to average a little over 10 tackles per game from here on out. Can he do it? Absolutely, but the achievement won’t come easy. In a season that has seen the team secure just one single victory, Rodriguez’s development — plus his potential to set a new Dolphins record — is something fans of the franchise can cheer for as the year nears its conclusion.

title: Vikes Views: Thankful for These Vikings
summary: The holidays are upon us, and there likely won’t be many of you bored at work reading this post. I hope you all enjoy some time with family, football, and whatever else makes this time of year special. As we sit two-thirds of the way through the season, here are a few Vikings I’m thankful […]
full_text: Irving Texas Thursday 11/23/00 Minnesota Vikings at Dallas Cowboys----Vikngs Randy Moss celebrated his first touchdown catch over Dallas in the 3rd quarter on Thanksgiving at Texas Stadium(Photo By JERRY HOLT/Star Tribune via Getty Images) | Star Tribune via Getty Images The holidays are upon us, and there likely won’t be many of you bored at work reading this post. I hope you all enjoy some time with family, football, and whatever else makes this time of year special. As we sit two-thirds of the way through the season, here are a few Vikings I’m thankful for this year. Dallas Turner Turner has stepped up into the starting role and thrived this season. He’s playing 80% of the defensive snaps so far and has already tied his career high with eight sacks. Jonathan Greenard was a key part of this defense and Turner was able to fill those shoes perfectly. Brian Flores The architect of the best defense in the NFL had a rough outing this past Sunday. However, I am still very thankful for Flores. The defense is the only reason this team is relevant this season. Harrison Smith I am thankful for Smith’s entire career. He’s been a Viking for every snap of his career. Joining the 40/40 club this year cements him as a first ballot Hall of Famer. This isn’t just a farewell tour, he’s still playing 55% of the defensive snaps this year. He’s no longer “starting”, but he is making an impact in year 15. Jalen Redmond Redmond has been the most consistent player on the Vikings. He has the second-highest run-defense grade amongst Interior Defensive Lineman and fourth-highest overall grade. Much like Flores, Redmond didn’t have the best night against the 49ers. I am convinced he’s going to bounce back strong. Redmond is playing 81% of the defensive snaps on the line. That’s a lot of work I know his teammates are thankful for. Kirk Cousins I think most of us saw the writing on the wall with the QB room prior to Kirk’s return. The team isn’t the best in the NFC right now, but Kirk gives us fans some hope heading into the holidays. It’s never likely any team is going to win the Super Bowl (1 every 32 years is average by my calculation). There is a chance this year, and that’s largely because of the improved quarterback play we expect going forward. I am thankful for so many more. Our cornerbacks are both really good. Andrew Van Ginkel, the rest of the front seven, and all of the backups have stepped up throughout the season. Aaron Jones continues to carry the load on offense week after week. Justin Jefferson, thank you for not being a diva. Will “The Thrill” Reichard is still one of the best kickers in the league. I hope everyone enjoys the holidays, and thank you for reading my posts. To Packers, Bears, and Lions fans: I hope your turkey is dry and your beer is warm.

(Photo by Todd Rosenberg/Getty Images) | Getty Images After a rough outing in Week 11, the Minnesota Vikings will look to get back on the right track when they return to U.S. Bank Stadium in Week 12 when they host the Atlanta Falcons. The Vikings got trounced in their prime time trip to Mexico City in Week 11, falling to the San Francisco 49ers by a score of 35-10 as Brock Purdy sliced and diced the NFL’s top defense. The loss, while disappointing, leaves the Vikings with a 7-3 record, still firmly in the playoff picture in the NFC and in contention in the NFC North. The Falcons are coming off of their bye week, but have lost five of their last six games. . .with their lone win, oddly enough, being the lone blemish on the schedule of the same 49ers team that just pasted the Vikings. Atlanta comes into this game with a record of 3-7, which would leave them at the bottom of most divisions, but has them just two games out of first place in the NFC South with seven weeks left in the regular season. This game will mark Kirk Cousins’ return to U.S. Bank Stadium as a Viking to face the team that he left the Vikings for following the 2023 season. Cousins came back to the Bank as a member of the Falcons in 2024, but was on the wrong end. . .at least for him. . .of a 42-21 Vikings blowout as Sam Darnold threw five touchdown passes, three to Jordan Addison (who will miss Sunday’s game) and two more to Justin Jefferson. This game will mark the start of a stretch that will see the Vikings have a much easier schedule to finish the season. . .at least on paper. . .than the rest of their NFC North counterparts. While the Chicago Bears, Detroit Lions, and Green Bay Packers have slates over the final seven weeks that rank among the top seven in the NFL in terms of strength of schedule, the Vikings’ strength of schedule to close the season is just 16th in the league. That gives the Vikings hope that they can make a run at the division title and a top-2 seed in this year’s NFL playoffs. title: Vikings Debriefing: Daily Norseman Week 11 Postgame Roundtable (A 35-10 loss to the 49ers)
summary: Hello everyone, and welcome to the Week 11 Minnesota Vikings postgame roundtable here at Daily Norseman. The Vikes are coming off getting knocked around by a San Francisco 49ers team that seemed to have all the answers to the questions before the test even started. So where do the Vikings go from here? Let’s talk […]
full_text: MEXICO CITY, MEXICO - NOVEMBER 22: Kirk Cousins #8 of the Minnesota Vikings is hit by Nick Bosa #97 of the San Francisco 49ers as he throws the ball during the first quarter at Estadio Banorte on November 22, 2026 in Mexico City, Mexico. (Photo by Manuel Velasquez/Getty Images) | Getty Images Hello everyone, and welcome to the Week 11 Minnesota Vikings postgame roundtable here at Daily Norseman. The Vikes are coming off getting knocked around by a San Francisco 49ers team that seemed to have all the answers to the questions before the test even started. So where do the Vikings go from here? Let’s talk to it: Question 1: Let’s freestyle for a minute — share your initial thoughts on the Vikings losing to the 49ers in Mexico City, 35-10. Brandon Warne : They laid an egg. It is what it is. Some might say it created a “blueprint of how to beat the Vikings,” but I think it was more along the lines of the boys seeing their vulnerabilities and how to address them moving forward. I can’t imagine too many quarterbacks attacking this defense with the vigor Brock Purdy did. He was exceptional. Christopher Gates : Obviously, it was disappointing. But, sadly, it’s also not atypical of what we’ve gotten used to seeing from the Vikings in the Kevin O’Connell era. Whenever this team has had the opportunity to rise to the occasion in the past few years, they’ve managed to Sideshow Bob themselves onto as many rakes as they can find. They managed to hang with the Niners for about a quarter and a half, but the touchdown/pick-six sequence at the end of the second quarter wound up being too much to overcome. At some point, you have to ask yourselves exactly what the issue is with this football team and why, exactly, they can’t manage to find a way to get things going when they face the best teams in the league. Warren Ludford : Looking again at the game, it wasn’t so much that the Vikings played bad, it’s that the 49ers — and Brock Purdy in particular — was nearly flawless. There were several completions into tight windows that you don’t see often. He was quick, decisive and accurate and it’s difficult for any defense to beat that. The good news should the Vikings face the 49ers in the playoffs is that there are some coverage adjustments the defense could make to slow him down and that performance is very difficult to repeat. There were also a couple coverage busts that need to be corrected. Offensively, the Vikings aren’t there yet and Jefferson’s fumble was really an unforced error that took away the Vikings’ last chance to make a game of it. But there will be more opportunities against the 49ers and other teams downfield as the offense gets into the swing of things with Cousins at the helm. Getting Addison back will help, but Myles Price deserves a bigger role as well. Dave Stefano : Sunday night was a whole lot of “this defense is supposed to be special” getting answered with “not against this offense.” Purdy and Shanahan just… solved it which few are capable of. Quick game, the blitz got neutralized, Kittle ran free twice, Evans looked like he never left, and we were down 28-10 at half after the pick-six. It felt less like a bad game and more like we walked into the wrong weight class and the referee was also on the 49ers’ side. We scored once, then spent the rest of the night watching oxygen masks get passed around like it was a team bonding exercise. Not the primetime statement we wanted. More like a public service announcement that the defense still has a ceiling. Craig Williams : Thoughts are the Vikings got beat by a better team. There are still seven weeks left in the season and a lot can change, but the 49ers are the class of the NFC at this time. They are better than most, but not good enough to contend for a top seed. Shawn C. : I’ll have an article covering it all. But the theme is: bad, but far from the catastrophic narrative I’ve seen everywhere. Kyle Shanahan schemed the Flores defense differently and brilliantly, using condensed formations and other tactics (h/t ESPN’s Ben Solak). Flores will now adjust. It happens. Better now than in the playoffs. The offense will improve each week as chemistry and comfort with Kirk Cousins grow. ————— Question 2: Who was your Vikings MVP? BW : Was there one? All kidding aside, I think PFF got it right this week with T.J. Hockenson securing an 85.1 grade. He was about the only who maintained a level of play for the whole night. Aaron Jones was pretty good too, and Justin Jefferson probably gets consideration if not for his brain cramp fumble on the cutback. Ugly night, however. CG : Honestly, there aren’t a whole lot to choose from…nobody really covered themselves in glory. Justin Jefferson was having a decent night until that completely inexplicable cutback and fumble on the first drive of the third quarter, so I can’t go with him. I suppose I’ll go with Aaron Jones, who gave us one of the real highlights of the night for the Vikings with his touchdown run. He’s not really known as a power guy, but he pretty well flattened somebody on his way to the end zone and capped the team’s only touchdown drive of the evening, so I’ll give him a little recognition for that. WL : Hard to say who was an MVP in a game like that, but I’d go with Cousins despite the pick-six. He had the intensity and was the driving force behind the offense the entire game. He was on his teammates to play better as well. I hope Cousins can help lead an attitude shift among offensive players from ‘we just need to be mediocre’ as Jefferson said in a recent press conference, to we need to be a top unit in the league. DS : Aaron Jones. He actually scored the one touchdown that made it look competitive for about seven minutes. Eight carries, 30 yards, one score, and he didn’t fumble or throw a pick-six. In a game where the highlight reel was mostly red and gold, Jones at least gave us something to point at and say “see, we did a football thing.” Hockenson graded well too, but Jones’ TD is the only moment that didn’t immediately make me want to change the channel. CW : MVP was TJ Hockenson. I believe he kept the team in it during the first half. The team went away from him after a strong first half including a terrific catch on a 3rd and long over a defender. SC : There isn’t much to go with here, as it was a poor performance across the board. But I’ll go with T.J. Hockenson. He made a great, acrobatic catch for a big gain and had some other nice plays. He’s clearly putting together a solid season, which will only be strengthened with Cousins back. ————— Question 3: Who was your Vikings LVP? BW : I’m going with Josh Metellus. He’s been an issue on the back end all year, and this week was no exception. The Vikings have some serious questions to answer at safety, not just next season — but the rest of this one. CG : I’m not going to single out a player in this one. It’s Kevin O’Connell. Every time this team has had an opportunity to rise to the occasion during his tenure. . .the 2022 playoffs, the 2024 regular season finale, the 2024 playoffs, and now on Sunday night. . .they’ve come out looking woefully underprepared and have gotten thoroughly outcoached. Yes, the Niners are a good team. . .probably the best in the NFL right now. But the Miami Dolphins, who are terrible, scored more points against this Niners defense than the Vikings did. The Atlanta Falcons, who are also terrible, beat this Niners team a month ago, their only loss of the year. There is no reason for a team with this much talent to have only scored ten points on Sunday night. The story is how Brian Flores’ defense gave up a lot of points, but I have faith that Flores can make adjustments when it’s all said and done. I have no such faith in Kevin O’Connell, because he hasn’t given me any reason to. WL : Maybe Theo Jackson for his blown coverage on one of the big completions to Mike Evans up the middle. There was nobody else in his coverage zone but he had his eyes elsewhere until it was…

His participation at practice indicates that the Patriots have opened his 21-day window to be activated from injured reserve to the 53-man roster. Doubs, 26, missed […]
full_text: Another member of the New England Patriots starting offense has returned to practice. Two days after left guard Alijah Vera-Tucker , wide receiver Romeo Doubs made his comeback on Wednesday. His participation at practice indicates that the Patriots have opened his 21-day window to be activated from injured reserve to the 53-man roster. WR Romeo Doubs returned to practice Wednesday, opening his 21-day activation window. pic.twitter.com/ZjaoEHDLG5 — Brian Hines (@iambrianhines) November 25, 2026 Doubs, 26, missed the last four games on injured reserve because of a shoulder ailment he suffered on a touchdown catch in Week 6 against the New York Jets. A former member of the Green Bay Packers, Doubs arrived in New England in March on a four-year, $68 million free agency deal. Before hurting his shoulder early in is sixth game, he had caught 14 passes for 261 yards and three touchdowns. He also had been on the field for 68.2% of the Patriots’ offensive snaps by the time he went down. Doubs’ return means that he, like the aforementioned Alijah Vera-Tucker, is now eligible to appear in this week’s game against the Los Angeles Chargers. For that to happen, however, the Patriots would need to create space on what is currently a full 53-man roster. In addition to Doubs, safety Craig Woodson also returned to practice on Wednesday. Patriots get Craig Woodson back at practice today. Still no Drake Maye, A.J. Brown, Carlton Davis and Walter Rouse. pic.twitter.com/P84vjB7TNa — Brian Hines (@iambrianhines) November 25, 2026 The Patriots will release their first injury report of the week later on Wednesday. They will take on the Chargers in Los Angeles on Sunday for a 4:05 p.m. ET kickoff.

title: Patriots don’t want a new Drake Maye. They want Tommy DeVito to be himself.
summary: Following an injury to quarterback Drake Maye, the New England Patriots have committed to Tommy DeVito as their starter moving forward. The coaching staff’s message to the 28-year-old was simple: be yourself. “They want me to be me,” DeVito said. “They want me to be me, no matter how much of that New Jersey ego, […]
full_text: Following an injury to quarterback Drake Maye, the New England Patriots have committed to Tommy DeVito as their starter moving forward. The coaching staff’s message to the 28-year-old was simple: be yourself. “They want me to be me,” DeVito said. “They want me to be me, no matter how much of that New Jersey ego, lingo, whatever I got going on, whatever kind of energy and just how I play. Don’t be somebody that you’re not. I’m not going to try to be Drake Maye. I’m not going to try to be anybody else. I’m going to be myself because ultimately that’s what gave me the opportunity to be in this position.” With the starting job now his, DeVito spent much of the Patriots’ bye week at the facility preparing for the opportunity. He treated Wednesday through Friday like a typical game week, continuing to throw and work out to stay sharp. Since the team rejoined him Monday, DeVito has spent additional time meeting with offensive coordinator Josh McDaniels and quarterbacks coach Ashton Grant. One of the biggest adjustments has come with the starting offensive line, as he works to get familiar with both the cadence and starting center Jared Wilson. Join the conversation! Sign up for a user account and get: Fewer ads Create community posts Comment on articles, community posts Rec comments, community posts New, improved notifications system! Download the SB Nation app on iOS or Android . DeVito, however, already has plenty of familiarity with the pass catchers he’ll be working with. The quarterback joked that he has the best spot in the locker room, with his corner stall situated in the middle of all the wide receivers. He also spent much of training camp and the preseason throwing to players like Mack Hollins, Efton Chism III and Kyle Williams. “I mean, a lot of the guys that are in there right now are guys that I’ve had reps with during training camp, and I think that’s huge,” DeVito said. “Not just for timing and any of that, it’s more about the comfortability in the huddle and guys knowing how I talk, how I operate in the huddle, what my cadence sounds like and then just building off that. So, I mean, the receivers, the running backs, everybody, I’ve had a ton of reps with them.” In relief of Maye back in Week 10, DeVito struggled off the bench completing just 12-of-28 passes for 84 yards with one touchdown and one interception. Head coach Mike Vrabel expects better from his new starter moving forward after his first extensive live reps since August. DeVito, who has eight career starts, holds himself to similar expectations as he prepares for his next opportunity. “Yeah, I think just more reps. Getting reps during practice, getting the actual reps of the game plan,” he said. “And like I said, no excuses. That’s your job to be ready and do all of that. There are no words to really explain the feeling of what that is, knowing you’re going into that week, you’re about to go battle with these guys. Just the extra little attention to detail from everybody and the communication. ‘Hey, I see this this way, I see this that way.’ They speak to me and it’s a good conversation.” The Patriots could have explored other options at quarterback, particularly after the Indianapolis Colts released Daniel Jones last week. Instead, Vrabel has repeatedly expressed confidence in DeVito, a message that has been echoed throughout the locker room. “It’s been awesome. Everybody’s embraced me. Even from the first snap and the first play that I was in there last week, it’s always been the same message over and over again from the guys,” DeVito said. “They have full trust in me, and that’s what I’ve tried to earn throughout OTAs, training camp, preseason and up until now. And that’s every day I come in. I work, I try to put my best foot forward, do everything I can to earn their trust. Because when we’re on the field, that’s all it’s about.”

title: Patriots vs. Chargers preview: Players to watch, stats, more for Week 12
summary: After flying to Germany for their last game, a loss to the Detroit Lions ahead of last weekend’s bye, another long journey awaits the New England Patriots. The team of head coach Mike Vrabel will fly to Los Angeles to take on a Chargers team that has disappointed so far in 2026. One year after […]
full_text: After flying to Germany for their last game, a loss to the Detroit Lions ahead of last weekend’s bye, another long journey awaits the New England Patriots. The team of head coach Mike Vrabel will fly to Los Angeles to take on a Chargers team that has disappointed so far in 2026. One year after qualifying for the playoffs but losing to these very same Patriots in the wild card round, the Chargers have only won one game so far this season. Are they as bad as their 1-9 record suggests, though? Let’s find out. Chargers key stats The Chargers sitting at one win on Thanksgiving weekend is reflected in their statistics. They have been bad — not universally, but in some critical areas that have prevented them from playing productive football this year. Chargers Patriots Record 1-9 (4th AFCW) 5-5 (2nd AFCE) Scoring diff. -98 (31st) -21 (19th) Points /game 16.8 (30th) 22.1 (18th) Points allowed/game 26.6 (25th) 24.2 (19th) Off. yards/game 288.1 (26th) 347.6 (12th) Off. EPA/play -0.118 (32nd) 0.026 (12th) Off. EPA/dropback -0.117 (30th) 0.106 (11th) Off. EPA/run -0.121 (27th) -0.101 (23rd) Def. yards/game 343.4 (20th) 345.1 (23rd) Def. EPA/play 0.046 (22nd) 0.054 (24th) Def. EPA/dropback 0.094 (22nd) 0.123 (25th) Def. EPA/run -0.015 (26th) -0.051 (15th) Turnover diff. -5 (t-26th) -10 (31) Giveaways 19 (t-27th) 20 (t-31st) Takeaways 14 (t-10th) 10 (t-24th) Offensively, this is a team that simply can’t get out of its own way. Whether it’s the third-highest turnover rate in the NFL (16.1%) or the second-worst scoring rate (31.3%), the Chargers simply have proven themselves incapable of playing productive football. While the run game has been okay at times and is ranked 12th in the league in yards per carry (4.3), the pass game has been atrocious despite a talented quarterback and experienced signal caller running the show. If you can’t throw the ball in the NFL of 2026, you are doomed and L.A. is a perfect illustration of that. Defensively, the Chargers have been better especially considering that they are getting little to no help from their own offense. The unit is ranked 10th in takeaways and 13th in turnover rate (11.3%), and is the eighth-best in the league in keeping opponents from scoring (43.5%) — solid, but not good enough to compensate for what the other side of the ball has been producing. So, to get back to that question above. Yes, their record did not happen by accident. The Chargers have struggled, especially on offense. Chargers 2026 season The last team in the NFL to register a win this season, Los Angeles started with eight straight defeats. Those losses actually brought the team’s losing streak to 11 in a row dating back to last year’s regular season. The team did get off. the schneid in Week 10 with a three-point win over a Jacoby Brissett-led Ravens team that currently is in its own six-game losing skid. Week 1: 26-14 loss vs. Arizona Cardinals (0-1) Week 2: 26-14 loss vs. Las Vegas Raiders (0-2) Week 3: 24-16 loss at Buffalo Bills (0-3) Week 4: 30-23 loss at Seattle Seahawks (0-4) Week 5: 23-17 loss vs. Denver Broncos (0-5) Week 6: 22-6 loss at Kansas City Chiefs (0-6) Week 7: Bye Week 8: 24-9 loss at Los Angeles Rams (0-7) Week 9: 44-22 loss vs. Houston Texans (0-8) Week 10: 23-20 win at Baltimore Ravens (1-8) Week 11: 27-24 loss vs. New York Jets (1-9) What does stand out about the Chargers’ defeats is that most of them have come against quality opponents. The Bills, Seahawks, Broncos, Chiefs and Rams are among the better teams in the league, while the Texans have also started hitting their stride. Of course, losing to the lowly Jets last Sunday disproves the theory that Los Angeles’ struggles have been a byproduct of a tough schedule. Chargers active roster Roster up-to-date as of Nov. 25, 5 a.m. ET | *denotes nominal starter Quarterback (2): Justin Herbert* (10), D.J. Uiagalelei (7) Running back (3): Omarion Hampton* (8), Kimani Vidal (28), Keaton Mitchell (34) Fullback (1): Scott Matlock (44) Wide receiver (6): Quentin Johnston* (1), Tre’ Harris* (9), Ladd McConkey* (15), Darius Devis (12 | KR/PR), KeAndre Lambert-Smith (84), Brenen Thompson (89) Tight end (3): Charlie Kolar* (88), Oronde Gadsden II (86), David Njoku (83) Offensive tackle (3): Joe Alt* (76 | LT), Travis Burke* (77 | RT), Trey Pipkins III (79) Interior offensive line (6): Logan Taylor* (65 | LG), Jake Slaughter* (66 | C), Cole Strange* (69 | RG), Kayode Awosika (74), Jacob Spomer (60), Alex Harkey (73) Interior defensive line (5): Dalvin Tomlinson* (94), Teair Tart* (93), Jamaree Caldwell (99), Justin Eboigbe (92), Nick Barrett (91) Defensive edge (5): Tuli Tuipulotu* (45), Khalil Mack* (52), Akheem Mesidor (90), Caleb Murphy (50), Bud Dupree (48) Linebacker (5): Daiyan Henley* (0), Del’Shawn Phillips* (53), Marlowe Wax (58), Troy Dye (43), Denzel Perryman (6) Cornerback (5): Cam Hart* (20), Donte Jackson* (26), Tarheeb Still* (4), Isas Waxter (37), Deane Leonard (33) Safety (5): Tony Jefferson* (23), Elijah Molden* (2), Genesis Smith (22), R.J. Mickens (27), Kendall Williamson (32) Specialists (3): Cameron Dicker (11 | K), J.K. Scott (16 | P/H), Josh Harris (47 | LS) As if the concerns about the team’s overall performance hadn’t been enough already, it also might enter Sunday’s game without its starting quarterback: Justin Herbert was placed in the league’s concussion protocol after the Week 11 loss to the Jets. His status for the Patriots game is unclear at this point in time. This marks the latest chapter in what has been a rough season for the former first-round draft pick. In 10 starts, Herbert has completed 171 of 274 pass attempts (62.4%) for 1,851 yards with eight touchdowns and 11 interceptions; he also was sacked a league-worst 39 times and has fumbled on eight occasions, with two of those going to the defense. Overall, he is ranked 30th among qualifying quarterbacks in expected points added per play (-0.095). Whether or not backup D.J. Uiagalelei would fare any better should he have to replace Herbert will be seen. So far in 2026, the second-year QB has gone 2-for-7 for 24 yards with one touchdown and no sacks. What makes the Chargers’ their quarterback’s offensive struggles so concerning is the fact that his supporting cast is unchanged from 2025. His top three wide receiver targets are in place — Tre Harris (28/376/0), Ladd McConkey (22/323/3), Quentin Johnston (15/275/1) — as are tight end Oronde Gadsden (20/179/1); the team even added Charlie Kolar (16/153/0) on a three-year free agency deal to further bolster the group. It’s top performer, meanwhile, has been running back Omarion Hampton. The 2025 first-round pick is lapping the field with 630 scrimmage yards and has also found the end zone four times; a multi-purpose weapon, he is averaging 4.1 yards per carry. The Chargers’ issues are manifold, but can in part be traced back to the offensive line having lost three starters to injury — including stalwart left tackle Rashawn Slater, an injury that forced right tackle Joe Alt to change sides. Defensively, some familiar faces are leading the unit. Teair Tart and Tuli Tuipulotu, who. both registered sacks in the wild card playoffs, are still vital pieces up front — as is veteran edge Khalil Mack, who is tied with Tuipulotu for the team lead with three sacks and whose 27 quarterback pressures are ranked second behind his teammate’s 34. Odafeh Oweh, who took Drake Maye down three times in January, is no longer with the team. In his place, however, the team brought in Akheem Mesidor in the first round of the draft. The second level is typically led by Daiyan Henley, whose pre-deadline trade to the Broncos fell through due to concerns about his physical. Henley has been dealing with a knee issue, and did not play last week versus the Jets. If Los Angeles’ tackle leader is out, Del’Shawn Phillips will be the main man off the ball with Marlowe Wax the main replacement for Henley. In the secondary, the Chargers are without their best player, do-it-all safety…
