title: Examining the roster ties between Patriots, Chargers ahead of Week 12
summary: Last January’s AFC wild card is a distant memory now. But there’s still some familiarity between the 5-5 New England Patriots and the 1-9 Los Angeles Chargers. Between the active rosters, practice squads and reserve lists, four players in the fold for head coaches Mike Vrabel and Jim Harbaugh have spent time with both organizations […]
full_text: FOXBOROUGH, MASSACHUSETTS - JANUARY 11: Hunter Henry #85 of the New England Patriots carries the ball after a reception for a touchdown defended by Derwin James Jr. #3 of the Los Angeles Chargers during the fourth quarter of the AFC Wild Card Playoff game at Gillette Stadium on January 11, 2026 in Foxborough, Massachusetts. (Photo by Sarah Stier/Getty Images) | Getty Images Last January’s AFC wild card is a distant memory now. But there’s still some familiarity between the 5-5 New England Patriots and the 1-9 Los Angeles Chargers. Between the active rosters, practice squads and reserve lists, four players in the fold for head coaches Mike Vrabel and Jim Harbaugh have spent time with both organizations during their NFL careers. Here’s the list of former Patriots and former Chargers set for Sunday’s flexed-out 4:05 p.m. ET kickoff at SoFi Stadium. LOS ANGELES Tejhaun Palmer, wide receiver — In the early stages of training camp, Palmer landed at Gillette Stadium as a waiver claim. The 26-year-old wide receiver drew nine targets during his preseason audition. He caught three for 33 yards before being let go at the NFL’s cutdown deadline and later landing in Inglewood on the practice squad in October. By way of Snow College and UAB, Palmer entered the NFL in the sixth round of the 2024 draft at No. 191 overall. He spent majority of his initial two campaigns on the practice squad of the Arizona Cardinals and made his debut as a member of the 53-man roster in last January’s finale. Cole Strange, guard — After making 14 starts for the Miami Dolphins last season, Strange followed offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel to the AFC West on a two-year contract in March. The 28-year-old interior lineman has started every game for the Chargers since then while staying in for 84.4 percent of the offensive snaps. Only quarterback Justin Herbert and center Jake Slaughter have logged a higher rate for a one-win team. Originally entering the NFL at pick No. 29 overall in the 2022 draft, Strange saw action in 30 games while in Foxborough between center and guard. The Chattanooga product missed 52 weeks during his tenure due to a torn patellar tendon and had his fifth-year option declined before being waived. He made a stop on the practice squad of the Cleveland Browns soon after. Caleb Murphy, linebacker — Back from the practice squad to the 53-man roster for the Chargers, Murphy appeared in five games for the Patriots after being claimed from Los Angeles in the fall of 2025. The 26-year-old was waived by New England last December to make room for the addition of fellow linebacker Chad Muma. In between those transactions, he totaled 79 snaps on special teams in a core role and had a hand in a pair of tackles. A New York Giants stint followed. Originally entering the NFL as an undrafted free agent with the Tennessee Titans in 2023, Murphy has checked into 26 career games. The two-time Division II national champion via Grand Valley State and Ferris State has totaled 30 tackles, one fumble recovery as well as a pair of split sacks through 218 snaps on defense and 431 snaps on special teams. NEW ENGLAND Hunter Henry, tight end — Last regular season, Henry led the defending AFC Champions with seven touchdown catches and set a career high with 768 receiving yards. The 31-year-old Patriots captain also found the end zone in the 16-3 playoff win against the organization that drafted him. A past recipient of the Ron Burton Community Service Award, his time in Foxborough stretches 91 games as well as a nomination for the Walter Payton NFL Man of the Year Award. The Arkansas product has tallied 293 catches for 3,356 yards and 28 touchdowns since signing as an unrestricted free agent in 2021 and being extended in 2024. The AFC West was where his run began. Selected in the second round of the 2016 class at No. 35 overall, he soon earned All-Rookie honors from the Pro Football Writers of America. And from San Diego to Los Angeles, his Chargers tenure brought 196 catches for 2,322 yards and 22 touchdowns across 55 games.

title: Patriots have no regrets over Stefon Diggs decision
summary: Before the start of this year’s free agency, the New England Patriots decided to part ways with their leading receiver. Despite having caught a combined 99 regular season and playoff passes for 1,123 yards and five touchdowns, Stefon Diggs was released just one year into his tenure with the club. The move was part of […]
full_text: Before the start of this year’s free agency, the New England Patriots decided to part ways with their leading receiver . Despite having caught a combined 99 regular season and playoff passes for 1,123 yards and five touchdowns, Stefon Diggs was released just one year into his tenure with the club. The move was part of a plan to rebuild the supporting cast around quarterback Drake Maye. Signing Romeo Doubs in free agency and acquiring A.J. Brown in a trade with the Philadelphia Eagles were among the next dominoes to fall, but neither move has paid the desired dividends yet: with injuries limiting both, the pairing has played only 16 snaps together this season. Diggs, on the other hand, has been a model of stability and durability for his new team, the Washington Commanders. In nine games so far, he has caught 40 passes for 431 yards and six touchdowns, outperforming Doubs’ and Browns’ combined output in New England (25/389/3). And yet, Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel is not second-guessing how things turned out. “We don’t have any regrets,” he said on Tuesday when asked about Diggs at a press conference at Gillette Stadium. “We don’t get the luxury of having hindsight. Unfortunately, that’s not the business that we’re in. We’ve chosen a profession that you have to make decisions, you have to be decisive, and the decision that we’re going to make moving forward is that we’re going to play good football. We’re going to be a good football team. We’re going to prepare. We’re going to enjoy this process, and we’re going to rally behind the guys that we have right now.” Despite 2025 being a bounceback season for Diggs and his seventh career 1,000-yard campaign, he generated limited interest after his release from the Patriots. An unresolved legal situation contributed to that, but even after being found not guilty of strangulation, assault and battery charges, he remained unsigned for three more months before the Commanders signed him. When they did, they gave the 32-year-old a one-year, $8 million contract. He would have counted $26.5 million against New England’s cap this season had he not been released; the Patriots created $15.8 million in savings by letting him go in March — almost the exact same space needed to fit Doubs ($8.6 million) and Brown ($7.04 million) under the cap in 2026. The financial and on-field aspects were only one part of the equation. Diggs’ leadership was no less important to New England’s success in 2025, and it is something that has not been openly replaced yet. For Vrabel, however, that also is not a concern at the moment. “The biggest thing that we need is people that perform what their duties are, what their jobs are,” he said. “We’ve always said there’s no restrictions on leadership. The guys that do the things the right way, play a certain style of way, I encourage them to lead any way that they possibly can. But some guys are more emotional, some guys talk a lot more. I’ve been around great players that have said a lot and been around great players that haven’t said a whole lot either.”

full_text: Losers of back-to-back games, the Pittsburgh Steelers have decided on a drastic move. Starting quarterback Aaron Rodgers will not be under center for the upcoming game against the Denver Broncos, with backup Mason Rudolph elevated to the top spot on the depth chart. Rodgers, meanwhile, will be inactive. The organization announced the benching of the future Hall of Famer on Tuesday night. pic.twitter.com/F2qo4OawcY — Pittsburgh Steelers (@steelers) November 25, 2026 Rodgers, 42, is in his second season in Pittsburgh and has led the team to a 6-4 record and the current seventh seed in the AFC playoff picture. The Steelers are one game ahead of the closest non-postseason team at the moment, the eighth-seeded New England Patriots. In his 10 starts this year, Rodgers completed 60.9% of his passes for 2,241 yards, 16 touchdowns and six interceptions. He is ranked 29th among qualifying quarterbacks with -0.022 expected points added per play. Head coach Mike McCarthy’s decision comes after Pittsburgh’s offense has scored just three total touchdowns in its last two contest, defeats to the Browns and Eagles. On the year, the unit is ranked 22nd in the league with a scoring average of 20.7 points per game. The Steelers’ AFC rivals will naturally keep a close eye on the situation. The team entered Wednesday with a 73% chance of making the postseason, according to The Athletic’s playoff simulator , but Rodgers’ benching might end. up impacting the team’s outlook. If so, the Patriots — whose own postseason chance is a mere 29% — would be among the first candidates to pounce.

title: Rob Gronkowski headlines ex-Patriots nominated for Pro Football Hall of Fame class 2027
summary: Newly-minted New England Patriots Hall of Famer Rob Gronkowski already has his sights on the next recognition for his legendary career. As was announced on Tuesday, he is one of 52 former NFL players nominated for the Pro Football Hall of Fame class of 2027. A second-round selection by the Patriots in the 2010 NFL […]
full_text: Newly-minted New England Patriots Hall of Famer Rob Gronkowski already has his sights on the next recognition for his legendary career. As was announced on Tuesday, he is one of 52 former NFL players nominated for the Pro Football Hall of Fame class of 2027. A second-round selection by the Patriots in the 2010 NFL Draft, Gronkowski became one of the most productive and decorated tight ends in league history during his nine seasons in New England and two more with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. In total, he appeared in 143 regular season games, catching 621 passes for 9,286 yards and scoring 93 touchdowns. A four-time Super Bowl champion, he also added 98 receptions for 1,389 yards and 15 TDs in 22 playoff games. Gronkowski also was voted a four-time first-team All-Pro and five-time Pro Bowler, is a member of the NFL’s 2010s All-Decade and 100th Anniversary Teams, and, as noted above, was recently inducted into the Patriots Hall of Fame . A cornerstone of the Patriots’ second-era dynasty, Gronkowski is widely regarded as the greatest tight end in NFL history. His induction into Pro Football Hall of Fame as a first-year candidate seems like a foregone conclusion, even though recent developments — i.e. Bill Belichick not making the cut in 2026 — have cast doubt over the integrity of the organization’s voting process. Gronkowski, 37, is one of nine former Patriots nominated for the Hall of Fame this year. Among them are three fellow franchise legends in guard Logan Mankins, defensive tackle Vince Wilfork and safety Rodney Harrison. Mankins was one of the best offensive linemen of his era, while Wilfork and Harrison are both Patriots Hall of Famers and multiple-time world champions. In addition to those three and Gronkowski, five short-term Patriots are on the list as well. Running back Fred Taylor and linebacker James Harrison appeared in 13 and four games for the team, respectively, toward the tail-end of their careers. Wide receiver Antonio Brown played one game for the club before his release amid allegations of sexual misconduct. Fellow wide receivers Torry Holt and Reggie Wayne spent time with the franchise during training camp but never played any regular season or playoff games for the club. In a next round of voting, the current list of 52 nominees will be reduced to 25; those results are expected to be announced in about two weeks. Eventually, 13 players will remain as candidates and join one coach and one contributor among the candidates the full selection committee will vote on ahead of the Super Bowl in February. This year’s coach and contributor candidates are the aforementioned Bill Belichick and Patriots owner Robert Kraft , respectively.
author: Bernd Buchmasser

title: Is it time for the Saints to make a change at the top?
summary: The New Orleans Saints have spent the better part of the last several years trying to find their footing following Sean Payton’s departure, and the results are impossible to ignore. While they have undergone multiple changes at head coach and quarterback, Mickey Loomis remains the man in charge after 25 years, leaving questions about whether […]
full_text: NEW ORLEANS, LOUISIANA - NOVEMBER 18: Executive Vice President/General Manager Mickey Loomis of the New Orleans Saints looks on prior to the start of an NBA game between the New Orleans Pelicans and the Boston Celtics at Smoothie King Center on November 18, 2022 in New Orleans, Louisiana. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and or using this photograph, User is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. (Photo by Sean Gardner/Getty Images) | Getty Images The New Orleans Saints have spent the better part of the last several years trying to find their footing following Sean Payton’s departure, and the results are impossible to ignore. While they have undergone multiple changes at head coach and quarterback, Mickey Loomis remains the man in charge after 25 years, leaving questions about whether the Saints need a fresh and modernized voice to lead the way at general manager. Loomis’ track record with Payton is undeniable. The two helped transform New Orleans into one of the league’s most consistent contenders, including a Super Bowl and NFC South titles. However, the results since Payton left the building have painted a completely different picture. Loomis is now 58-84 (.408) in games without Payton at the helm. That includes Dennis Allen’s 18-25 record and Kellen Moore’s 9-18 record since taking over in New Orleans. The Saints haven’t been to the playoffs since 2020 and it’s only gone downward since. That kind of sustained disappointment raises legitimate questions about how much of the organization’s success was tied to Payton rather than Loomis’ ability to construct and manage a competitive roster, especially considering how Payton has turned the Denver Broncos around. Loomis deserves credit for the success the Saints have had in the past, but eventually, previous accomplishments can’t continue to outweigh present results. New Orleans has spent years attempting to return to their winning ways and simply just can’t get over the hump. With Kellen Moore’s future in jeopardy, it’s fair to question whether Loomis’ seat should be hot as well. If New Orleans wants to change their current trajectory, it may be time to seriously consider significant changes. That starts with the NFL’s longest tenured general manager.
author: Nic Jennings

summary: Former New Orleans Saints offensive lineman Jahri Evans has once again advanced in the voting process for the Pro Football Hall of Fame. full_text: Former New Orleans Saints offensive lineman Jahri Evans has once again advanced in the voting process for the Pro Football Hall of Fame. This marks the fifth consecutive year Evans has been considered for induction. He was named a semifinalist in 2023 before advancing to finalist status in each of the past three years (2024–2026). 52 players remain in the running for the Pro Football Hall of Fame Class of 2027. Next up: the Selection Committee trims the list to 25 nominees. https://t.co/sJlWFk2mdC pic.twitter.com/IqvUhT5SYD — Pro Football Hall of Fame (@ProFootballHOF) November 24, 2026 Evans, one of 52 players eligible for induction into the Pro Football Hall of Fame, was selected by the Saints in the fourth round of the 2006 NFL Draft. He spent 11 seasons in New Orleans (2006–2016), helping lead them to five playoff appearances, including a victory in Super Bowl XLIV. Evans also earned six consecutive Pro Bowl selections from 2009 to 2014. He was inducted into the Saints Hall of Fame in 2020, the Louisiana Sports Hall of Fame in 2022 and the Saints Ring of Honor in 2025. After spending three seasons on the Saints’ coaching staff, Evans joined the Pittsburgh Steelers, where he currently serves as an assistant offensive line coach. The group of 52 candidates will be narrowed to 25 over the next two weeks, with 15 finalists advancing to the Selection Committee’s annual meeting next year. The Pro Football Hall of Fame’s Class of 2027 will be announced at “NFL Honors” in Los Angeles in February, with the official enshrinement ceremony taking place next August in Canton.

title: NY Giants’ Abdul Carter named the NFC Defensive Player Of the Week
summary: New York Giants edge defender Abdul Carter has been named the NFC Defensive Player Of the Week for his incredible performance against the Jacksonville Jaguars. Carter had an absolutely dominant game against the Jaguars, notching 12 quarterback pressures, 6 of which were quick pressures, 2.0 sacks, 5 QB hits, 4 tackles, and 2 tackles for […]
full_text: Abdul Carter rushing the passer Sunday night. | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images New York Giants edge defender Abdul Carter has been named the NFC Defensive Player Of the Week for his incredible performance against the Jacksonville Jaguars. Carter had an absolutely dominant game against the Jaguars, notching 12 quarterback pressures, 6 of which were quick pressures, 2.0 sacks, 5 QB hits, 4 tackles, and 2 tackles for a loss. He was the only player across the NFC with multiple sacks and five quarterback hits in Week 11. Carter is beginning to truly break out and is becoming the player the Giants envisioned when they took him 3rd overall out of Penn State. Carter told doubters to stand back and watch his game against the Jaguars prior to Week 11. He said that he’d have a big game, then backed it up by terrorizing Trevor Lawrence. “He’s been saying the same thing to me,” coach John Harbaugh said after the game. “But more than that, he’s been practicing that way. So to see him break out and get the sack and the quarterback hits, it was great.” “Twelve pressures, did he? Twelve pressures,” Harbaugh added. “Should have given him two game balls, I guess.” Carter said after the game that he and the rest of the defense answered the call to shut down a good Jaguars team. “These are the games that all of our best players got to play their best,” said Carter. “We’ve got a team like that. You are what your record says you are. They’ve got a great record, they’ve got a great team. We proved we’re that, too.” Carter, 23, has already become one of the most feared and disruptive pass rushers in the NFL despite this beeing just his third season at outside linebacker. Per NFL NextGenStats, this was just the fourth time this season a player put up those types of numbers without an unblocked pressure. So far this year, Carter ranks : 1st in the NFL in Time To Pressure (2.17 secondsj) 2nd in Pass Rush Win Rate (28 percent) 1st in Quick Pressure rate (76 percent) After the game, RT Jermaine Eluemunor credited Carter’s elite get-off for his disruptiveness and compared him to truly elite company. “There’s a lot of guys in the NFL that are really talented but don’t have that get-off,” Eluemunor said “Just anticipating the snap count, but then also being able to have that get-off. Because there are a lot of guys that jump the snap count, but they don’t have that first explosive step that he has. That explosive step that he has is really rare in this league. Only a couple of guys have it. Micah Parsons has it, Myles [Garrett] has it, Will Anderson has it, and those are three of the best in the NFL. He can anticipate the snap count, but then he also has that explosiveness to help with that.” “[Abdul] thinks he’s the best and he’s going to start playing like that,” Eluemunor added. “He’s been playing like that, but I think that in this game, you truly got to see the hard work and the film study that he’s been putting in and just the emphasis he’s put on just trying to be that player. I think that’s the first of many games he’s probably going to have like that this season.” It’s also an increasingly common occurrence to see a Giant be recognized for their play. All told, this is the 6th time this year that a Giant has earned Player Of The Week or Month honors. S Jevon Holland was the NFC Defensive Player Of The Month for September. WR Malik Nabers earned NFC Offensive Player Of The Month for October. CB Deonte Banks was named NFC Defensive Player Of The Week for his game Week 4 against the Cardinals. LB Arvell Reese was named NFC Defensive Rookie Of The Week in Week 4 as well. Reese was also named NFC Defensive Player Of The Week for his Week 9 game against the Philadelphia Eagles. Abdul Carter has been named NFC Defensive Player Of The Week for Week 11.

title: Fantasy Football 2026: Week 12 preview — Start/sit and more
summary: Welcome to Week 12 of the NFL season, and Happy Thanksgiving! The NFL is doing its part to keep marriage counselors in business. full_text: Unstoppable! | Getty Images Welcome to Week 12 of the NFL season, and Happy Thanksgiving! The NFL is doing its part to keep marriage counselors in business. Your Thanksgiving weekend schedule: A game on Wednesday night, a triple-header on Thanksgiving Day, a game on Black Friday, and then the usual Sunday-Monday schedule with the remaining slate. Saturday is a day off, but there are wall-to-wall college rivalry games. Eat, drink, and watch football. Then watch more football. What could possibly go wrong? Game of the Week: There are a few good choices but it has to be Chiefs at Bills on Thanksgiving night. Fun fact: It’s only the second time in NFL history that two teams are coming into a game having won three straight contests by 17 or more points. Mahomes! Allen! Enjoy this one with your second piece of pumpkin pie and a nightcap. The line: BUF -3. There are four weeks left before the fantasy playoffs start in most formats. Still time to make a move, so read on! St ats of the Week Every team in the NFC North is over .500, while no team in the NFC South is over .500. The Bills ’ defense has not allowed a touchdown across 43 straight possessions. The flip side: Across Weeks 10 and 11, the Cowboys’ offense had a stretch of nine straight possessions that resulted in a touchdown. Each of the Cowboys’ last two games had more than 80 total points scored. In all three of their games since trading away DT Jeffery Simmons, the Titans have allowed 40+ points. Seven different 49ers players who are 30 or older have caught a TD pass this season, the most in NFL history. In the first half against Philadelphia, Aaron Rodgers averaged one half of an air yard per pass attempt (the lowest total for a half of football since they began tracking air yards in 2006). Rodgers has been benched for Mason Rudolph. Dak Prescott was the No. 1 fantasy QB this past week, and CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens were the No. 1 and No. 2 fantasy wide receivers. Bye Weeks: NONE Week 12 Rides, Fades and Sleepers For those who are familiar with this column, you know the drill. For everyone else: The Rides, Fades, and Sleepers is an analysis of players that I think are primed for an especially strong or poor performance, often as compared to consensus expectations. This isn’t a straight-up Start/Sit exercise. As a general rule, start your studs. I’ll rarely list the most obvious names at a position as “Rides” because those players are almost always expected to have strong performances. You don’t need me or anyone else telling you to start CeeDee Lamb . While this analysis is intended for season-long play, it works for DFS formats too. Half PPR scoring and Expert Consensus Rankings (ECR) are used for the column. Each week, I’m picking a Ride, Fade, and Sleeper of the Week. The rules: The Ride of the Week can’t be a truly elite option, the Fade can’t be someone who nobody is starting anyway, and the Sleeper must be an actual sleeper, from down in the rankings. Last week, my Rides, Fades, and Sleepers did well, with a lot more hits than misses throughout. Ride of the Week Tony Pollard went over 100 yards rushing but didn’t score or do anything in the passing game, so that’s a bit of a miss. Fade of the Week Tyler Warren had one catch. Sleeper of the Week Justin Herbert was the QB4 on the week, with two passing TDs, a rushing TD, and no picks. You can check my work here . *** Ride of the Week: Bucky Irving (vs. CAR). Bucky is on one. He’s recorded six straight games with at least 18 carries and racked up six TDs across his last four outings. For what seems like the hundredth time in the last two seasons, Baker Mayfield is playing hurt – and he can’t do his usual Baker stuff. Plus, without Mike Evans he’s not the same QB. Tampa is pounding the ball and playing solid defense, and this is a home game, in primetime, that they absolutely must have. Irving should once again feast, in a plus matchup. Carolina has allowed the second most fantasy points per game (FPPG) and the most rushing touchdowns (14) to opposing backs. ATop-3 RB finish this week is realistic. Fade of the Week: Jaylen Warren (vs. DEN). Don’t look now, but Warren has reverted to a timeshare back on a sputtering offense. After an epic run before the bye, it’s been back-to-back stinkers (a total of 16 carries for 43 yards). He does have seven catches in those two contests, and that’s the path to success this week – doing a little of what Ashton Jeanty did to the Broncos catching passes out of the backfield a week ago. It’s viable, as Denver has allowed the most receiving yards to opposing backs. I’m not buying it. Mason Rudolph isn’t likely to check it down as much as Aaron Rodgers. It’s getting ugly in Pittsburgh. I’m out. Sleeper of the Week: I’ll preface all sleeper discussions by saying it’s harder to find sleepers this week, with no teams on bye. Managers are less likely to need to reach. With that said, I’ll go with Deshaun Watson (vs. LV), who I think is a good start this week in 2-QB formats. Watson has been OK for fantasy this season (QB19 in FPPG). He’s starting to run a little more and has some very good young weapons to throw to. The Raiders have allowed the fifth most FPPG and the second most TD passes (23) to opposing QBs, and Cleveland is a tough place to visit. Watson is ranked as the QB15 this week and I think a Top-12 (QB1) finish is in play. Quarterback: Elite options this week – Josh Allen , Patrick Mahomes, Dak Prescott, and Joe Burrow ; the analysis starts below them. title: 5 NY Giants-Indianapolis Colts storylines: This is no time for a stumble
summary: The New York Giants travel to face the Indianapolis Colts on Sunday. Here are 5 storylines to watch. NFC East ramifications As I wrote on Tuesday, the Dallas Cowboys and Washington Commanders are heating up and waiting for the NFC East-leading Giants to stumble and open the door. No NFL game is easy to win, […]
full_text: The New York Giants travel to face the Indianapolis Colts on Sunday. Here are 5 storylines to watch. NFC East ramifications As I wrote on Tuesday , the Dallas Cowboys and Washington Commanders are heating up and waiting for the NFC East-leading Giants to stumble and open the door. No NFL game is easy to win, but this is one the Giants should not lose. The Giants should win this game. They need to win this game. The combined record of the Giants’ next four opponents is 24-17. The combined record of Washington’s next four opponents is 11-30. The combined record of Dallas’s next four opponents is 22-18. If the Giants stumble against the woeful Colts, the door to the NFC East title is blown wide open and the chance the Giants land on the wrong side increases dramatically. Daniel Jones revenge game Oh, wait! That’s what this was supposed to be. Only the Colts, after refusing offers to trade Jones before the NFL trade deadline, released the former Giants’ quarterback last week, thus getting nothing in return. Now, it is the Anthony Richardson return game. It is eerie how similar Jones’ fate with the Colts was to what happened to Jones with the Giants in 2024. He led the Giants to the playoffs in 2022, but got released in the middle of a dismal 2024 season. Jones was excellent for the Colts last season before suffering a torn Achilles in Week 14 with the Colts at 8-4. The Giants will see Richardson, whom the Colts drafted No. 4 overall in 2023 and replaced with Jones last season. He will be making his first start since 2024. Richardson has thrown just six passes the past two seasons. Hello, near friend The Giants were aggressive at the trade deadline in their pursuit of Indianapolis running back Jonathan Taylor. Reporting indicated the Giants offered the Colts a second- and fifth-round pick for the talented running back. The Colts, in what seems like a foolish move on their part, declined. Now, rather than handing the ball to Taylor as part of a backfield combination with Cam Skattebo, the Giants have to face him. Taylor is headed toward a 1,100-yard season, which would be the fifth 1,000-yard season in his seven-year career. The 27-year-old, though, is not having his best year. He is averaging career lows in yards per carry (4.0) and yards rushing per game (69.1). He also does not have a 100-yard rushing game yet. The bet here is that it has more to do with how bad the Colts have been than with Taylor beginning to decline. The Giants’ often questionable run defense has been markedly improved in recent weeks. Over the last three games, the Giants have given up just 3.6 yards per rushing attempt, ninth in the league during that stretch. This would be a bad time for the Giants’ run defense to falter and allow Taylor to have the kind of game that reminds everyone why the Giants wanted him so badly at the trade deadline. Depth tested again The Giants have survived the loss of Jaxson Dart because of the play of Jameis Winston and the trade for J.J. McCarthy. They have survived the loss of Brian Burns and Tremaine Edmunds because of Abdul Carter, Kayvon Thibodeaux, and Micah McFadden. They have gotten past the loss of Chauncey Golston because of help from Dawuane Smoot and Trace Ford. Now, the Giants will have to handle the loss of cornerback Greg Newsome for several weeks. In relief of Newsome on Sunday vs. the Jacksonville Jaguars, Paulson Adebo played his best game in two seasons as a Giant. Rookie second-round pick Colton Hood is now the third cornerback. He played three snaps against Jacksonville, the first defensive snaps he had played since Week 3. 3 issues to address The Giants have three central issues that could contribute to their undoing down the stretch. Dominic Zvada’s inconsistency — Zvada is an incredibly talented placekicker. He has shown that by making eight field goals of more than 50 yards this season. He is also incredibly frustrating. He has missed seven kicks already, all from the right hash mark, and two from extra-point distance. There is an argument to be made that the Giants would be cruising to the NFC East title without critical misses from Zvada in both games against the Washington Commanders. The Giants have shown extraordinary patience with the 23-year-old. Can he reward it by winning them a couple of games down the stretch? Ball security — The Giants have 18 fumbles this season. Only the Los Angeles Chargers, with 19, have more. Skattebo’s fifth fumble of the season Sunday might have turned Sunday’s victory over the Jaguars into a bitter defeat without J.J. McCarthy’s open-field tackle. The Giants have lost eight of those fumbles. Only three teams have lost more. I don’t know exactly how it gets fixed, but the Giants have to stop putting the ball on the ground. Inconsistent running game — The Giants are 24th in the league at 3.8 yards per rushing attempt. We have seen over and over this season that the Giants have had difficulty closing out games on offense, largely because they have struggled to run the ball in critical situations. Trying to close out the Jaguars on Sunday after Skattebo’s fumble, the Giants called just one run play in a four-drive, 13-play sequence that netted just one first down. They did manage a first down on two runs late in Sunday’s game, and that is something that good teams must be able to do consistently. You have to be able to chew up the clock with the ground game when you are ahead, and it has been a problem. Again, I don’t have the answer. The Giants have the personnel that they have — both running and blocking. They need to find a way to get it right more often.
author: Ed Valentine

title: NY Giants’ CB Paulson Adebo: ‘I know what kind of player I am’
summary: Entering this season, New York Giants cornerback Paulson Adebo had started all but one of the 64 NFL games in which he had played. Adebo signed a three-year, $54 million contract with the Giants before last season. He started 12 games, missing five with a knee injury. Entering this season, Adebo figured to be the […]
full_text: Paulson Adebo celebrates an interception against the Jaguars. | Getty Images Entering this season, New York Giants cornerback Paulson Adebo had started all but one of the 64 NFL games in which he had played. Adebo signed a three-year, $54 million contract with the Giants before last season. He started 12 games, missing five with a knee injury. Entering this season, Adebo figured to be the Giants’ No. 1 cornerback, with Deonte Banks and Greg Newsome competing for the second starting spot. With a new head coach in John Harbaugh, who has given far more than the usual lip service to the idea of players having to earn their roles, the contract Adebo signed with the Giants before the 2025 season did not matter. Banks and Newsome clearly outplayed Adebo during the spring and summer, and the six-year veteran opened the season as the team’s third cornerback. He played 10 snaps in Week 1 against the Dallas Cowboys, then went on IR with a knee injury. Adebo returned in Week 7 against the Houston Texans. He has now played in four games, with just one start, and suffered the indignity of being inactive in the Week 10 game against the Washington Commanders. Now, though, with Newsome on injured reserve and facing tightrope surgery for a high ankle sprain suffered Sunday against the Jacksonville Jaguars, Adebo will be back in a prominent role for the Giants. Adebo was ready Sunday when Newsome was lost after just four snaps. He had a critical interception, four passes defensed, and allowed just two completions in eight targets with Pro Football Focus giving him a passer rating against of an absurd 13.0. “You just do it,” Adebo said Tuesday when asked how he stayed ready while not playing when healthy for the first time in his career. “You prepare every week like you’re going to play. I mean, if you’re the third guy, you’re one play away from going in every single game, so you owe it to yourself and you owe it to your teammates to be prepared, so that’s really all it’s about.” Adebo did not complain about not playing. “I think we got a lot of great players on the team,” he said. “Obviously, it’s not where I wanted to be going into the season, but kind of was banged up for a number of reasons, but I think just embracing where you are and continuing to practice, continuing to execute, that way when you have an opportunity you can come in and execute.” Adebo was a playmaking cornerback who intercepted seven passes and had 28 passes defensed with the New Orleans Saints over 22 games in 2023 and 2024. That led the cornerback-needy Giants to give him a big free agent contract. The playmaking he showed in New Orleans did not really surface until Sunday against the Jaguars. Adebo’s confidence has not wavered. “I know what type of player I am. I know what I can do on the field. I know what type of person I am,” he said. “I know when I get an opportunity, I’ll be able to go out and show it.” With Newsome gone for at least four games and perhaps longer, the Giants will need more games like he had against Jacksonville from Adebo.

full_text: Good morning, New York Giants fans! Here are the stories you need to as the Giants get set to travel to Indianapolis to play the Colts this Sunday. Seven things Solak thinks for NFL Week 12 | ESPN.com I think … the Giants can win a playoff game. But they are dangerous. Not because John Harbaugh is a good coach (though he is) and not because McCarthy has some gamer in him (he does, but he didn’t even complete a pass over 15 air yards all game). The 6-3-1 Giants are dangerous because they are talented. If the Giants have a top-10 edge and a top-10 corner — I’d argue, just on the back of 2026 performance, they do — then they have the ability to shut down opposing teams. Those are premier players and premium spots that can force opposing teams to play left-handed. How well will Kirk Cousins handle Carter’s pressure if the Vikings draw the Giants in the wild-card round? Can Banks force third-down throws away from Mike Evans if the 49ers play the Giants in January? On offense, the Giants have more game-altering players. Healthy Malik Nabers doesn’t quite have the game-takeover potential that Ja’Marr Chase or Jaxon Smith-Njigba do, but he feels as if he’s in the next tier of uncoverability when he’s fully on. The Giants’ offensive line, anchored by perennial standout Andrew Thomas, who had one of his best games of the season against the Jaguars, has mashing potential against undersized defensive lines. I could see the Giants’ rushing attack dictating the game to Flores’ Vikings defense that has struggled with heavy sets or Nabers running roughshod through a Lions’ secondary that lacks sticky corners. J.J. Watt impressed by Abdul Carter "Abdul Carter was flying off the ball and he was all over the field.. He called his shot during the week and he backed it up with his play.. Abdul Carter, who tallied two of New York’s three sacks, led a pass rush that kept Trevor Lawrence on the run for nearly all four quarters. Offensively, the Giants almost choked this game away in the second half, but J.J. McCarthy threw a big pass late in the fourth quarter that helped New York run out the clock. If the Giants offense starts playing at the same level as the defense, this team can beat anyone. title: NY Giants make move to replace  injured CB Greg Newsome on 53-man roster
summary: As expected, the New York Giants placed cornerback Greg Newsome on injured reserve Tuesday. It has previously been reported that Newsome will undergo tightrope surgery to repair his high ankle sprain, with the hope being that he could return to action before the season is over. To replace Newsome on the 53-man roster, the Giants […]
full_text: Dawuane Smoot vs. Jacksonville. | Getty Images As expected, the New York Giants placed cornerback Greg Newsome on injured reserve Tuesday. It has previously been reported that Newsome will undergo tightrope surgery to repair his high ankle sprain , with the hope being that he could return to action before the season is over. To replace Newsome on the 53-man roster, the Giants have signed edge defender Dawuane Smoot off their practice squad. The 31-year-old Smoot is in his 10th NFL season. He was signed to the Giants’ practice squad in mid-October, and has been elevated to the active roster for each of the past three games. He has a sack, a quarterback hit, and a tackle for loss in 102 snaps over that time. Smoot has played mostly in pass rush situations. The Giants will turn to veteran Paulson Adebo to replace Newsome in the starting lineup. Adebo had an interception and four passes defensed Sunday after Newsome was injured just four snaps into the game against the Jacksonville Jaguars. To fill Smoot’s spot on the practice, the Giants re-signed offensive lineman Geno VanDeMark. VanDeMark had been released from the practice squad last week.

summary: The New York Giants are riding high after — once again — coming up with a win as underdogs. full_text: ﻿The New York Giants offense huddles before a play | Getty Images The New York Giants are riding high after — once again — coming up with a win as underdogs. Very few people thought the Giants would beat the Jacksonville Jaguars, who are widely considered among the best and most complete teams in the NFL. The most optimistic among us believed that there was a path for the Giants to come up with the win, but weren’t sure if they could execute. As it turned out, they did. They were able to do just enough on offense to establish a lead while their defense turned in a dominant performance for most of the game. It was a great game by the Giants, but it wasn’t a complete game. The offense was still inconsistent and plagued by turnovers, miscues, and penalties. And while the defense was able to pick them up, they were gassed by the end of the game because the offense couldn’t sustain a drive after Cam Skattebo’s fumble. The Giants’ win over the Jags is proving to be even bigger than anticipated, with the rest of the NFC East winning as well. That makes the upcoming game against the Indianapolis Colts into much more of a “must win” than it was before the Washington Commanders’ upset win over the Cincinnati Bengals. This is the time for the Giants to begin peaking if they want to be competitive in their upcoming games against the San Francisco 49ers, Seattle Seahawks, Cleveland Browns, and Detroit Lions. So this week we want to ask the Big Blue View community: Can the Giants put it all together and play a complete game against the Colts? Your choices this week are: A) Yes – The Giants’ offense and defense will play a complete 60 minute of football against the Colts. title: CB Greg Newsome II to have surgery on sprained ankle
summary: New York Giants cornerback Greg Newsome II will have surgery to repair the high ankle sprain he suffered against the Jacksonville Jaguars, per a report from Jordan Schultz. Schultz reports that Newsome will undergo tightrope surgery and will miss the next 4-6 weeks. That will sideline him for the Giants games against the Indianapolis Colts, […]
full_text: ﻿New York Giants cornerback Greg Newsome II | Getty Images New York Giants cornerback Greg Newsome II will have surgery to repair the high ankle sprain he suffered against the Jacksonville Jaguars, per a report from Jordan Schultz . Schultz reports that Newsome will undergo tightrope surgery and will miss the next 4-6 weeks. That will sideline him for the Giants games against the Indianapolis Colts, San Francisco 49ers, Seattle Seahawks, and Cleveland Browns. He could also miss the games against the Detroit Lions and Dallas Cowboys, and perhaps the season finale against Philadelphia Eagles at the long end of his timeline. The good news is that the surgery isn’t season-ending, and Newsome should be able to return for the playoffs should the Giants make the postseason. A high ankle sprain happens when a ligament that stabilizes the ankle and lower leg is torn. Tightrope surgery is a relatively new procedure that sees a flexible braided cable be implanted into the injured ankle to stabilize the joint while the ligament heals. The tightrope implant dramatically reduces the recovery time of a high ankle sprain and the player’s return to sport. A high ankle sprain could take months to return from with previous treatments, but tightrope surgery reduces that to the aforementioned timeline. Newsome recently signed a contract extension with the Giants, capitalizing on a great start to the 2026 season. He emerged a key component of one of the best — and most surprising — secondaries in the NFL. Fortunately, the Giants also have depth at the position, and 2025 free agent Paulson Adebo stepped in for Newsome and played well against Parker Washington and the Jaguars.

full_text: Eli Manning | Getty Images New York Giants: Former New York Giants quarterback Eli Manning is among 52 semifinalists in the running towards enshrinement for Canton. Here’s a look at the players that are in the running for the Class of 2027. OFFENSIVE LINEMEN (10): Willie Anderson, Lomas Brown, Jahri Evans, Joe Jacoby, Nick Mangold, Logan Mankins, Maurkice Pouncey, Richmond Webb, Steve Wisniewski, Marshal Yanda. QUARTERBACKS (3): Ken Anderson, Eli Manning, Ben Roethlisberger. RUNNING BACKS (7): Shaun Alexander, Frank Gore, Marshawn Lynch, LeSean McCoy, Adrian Peterson, Fred Taylor, Ricky Watters. WIDE RECEIVERS/ENDS/TIGHT ENDS (10): Anquan Boldin, Antonio Brown, Rob Gronkowski, Torry Holt, Billy “White Shoes” Johnson, Steve Smith Sr., Otis Taylor, Hines Ward, Reggie Wayne, Jason Witten. DEFENSIVE BACKS (8): Rodney Harrison, Lester Hayes, Albert Lewis, Eddie Meador, Richard Sherman, Earl Thomas III, Everson Walls, Darren Woodson. DEFENSIVE LINEMEN (8): John Abraham, Geno Atkins, L.C. Greenwood, Jim Marshall, Robert Mathis, Haloti Ngata, Vince Wilfork, Kevin Williams. LINEBACKERS (6): Maxie Baughan, London Fletcher, James Harrison, Karl Mecklenburg, Tommy Nobis, Terrell Suggs. The next cut the voters will take will narrow this group of 52 down to 25. The next cut will come from 25 to 15, and those candidates will be presented at the selection committee’s meeting before the Super Bowl, where the finalists will learn whether or not they will be part of football’s immortality. Manning is one of three quarterbacks listed alongside Ken Anderson and Ben Roethlisberger, someone who is easy to compare him with, considering that both of them were in the 2004 draft class. Manning and Roethlisberger each have very decorated resumes, and both should be in the Hall of Fame at some point down the line. On paper, Roethlisberger has the stronger numbers over the course of his career, but each of them has won two Super Bowls, which should count for something. This is Roethlisberger’s first year of eligibility on the ballot, while Manning is on his third season. It remains to be seen what kind of support each quarterback gets, but the direct comparisons should make it a challenging decision for the committee. title: New York Jets News: Did Jets win the Aaron Rodgers Debate After Steelers Benching Decision?
summary: Aaron Glenn’s first big decision when he became the New York Jets head coach was Aaron Rodgers’ future. Rodgers was interested in returning, but the feeling wasn’t mutual. AG told Rodgers to hit the road, and they parted ways. Rodgers ended up signing with the Pittsburgh Steelers, and that is where he has been since […]
full_text: Sep 7, 2025; East Rutherford, New Jersey, USA; New York Jets quarterback Justin Fields (7) greets Pittsburgh Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers (8) after the game at MetLife Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Wendell Cruz-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Aaron Glenn’s first big decision when he became the New York Jets head coach was Aaron Rodgers’ future. Rodgers was interested in returning, but the feeling wasn’t mutual. AG told Rodgers to hit the road, and they parted ways. Rodgers ended up signing with the Pittsburgh Steelers, and that is where he has been since 2025. Late on Tuesday, November 24 NFL Insider Tom Pelissero revealed “The Steelers are benching Aaron Rodgers and naming Mason Rudolph the starting quarterback for Friday’s game against the Broncos. Sources say this was a coach’s decision. But Rodgers has struggled and now Mike McCarthy is making a change.” Stunner: The Steelers are benching Aaron Rodgers and naming Mason Rudolph the starting quarterback for Friday's game against the Broncos. Sources say this was a coach's decision. But Rodgers has struggled and now Mike McCarthy is making a change. pic.twitter.com/wPSeMX3lmq — Tom Pelissero (@TomPelissero) November 25, 2026 “Aaron Rodgers will be inactive Friday, and now has potentially played the final snap of his legendary 22-year career,” Pelissero added . Now feels like a perfect time to look back and judge whether the Jets made the right decision. In 2025 the Jets finished with a 3-14 record and Justin Fields delivered an uneven season before getting benched. He started nine games, completed 62.7% of his passes, threw for 1,259 passing yards, and had seven touchdowns to one interception. He also toted the rock 71 times for 383 rushing yards and four touchdowns on the ground. Pittsburgh had a 10-7 record in 2025 and made a trip to the playoffs, but ended up losing in the wildcard round. Aaron Rodgers started 16 games last season. He completed 65.7% of his passes, threw for 3,322 passing yards and had a 24 touchdown to seven interception ratio. It seems pretty obvious that Rodgers would have been a dramatic upgrade over what the Jets trotted out at QB last year. Things in 2026 feel quite the opposite. Before Rodgers got benched he started 10 games this year. He completed 60.9% of his passes, threw for 2,241 passing yards, and had a 16 touchdown to six interception ratio. The Jets are getting much better QB play than that with Geno Smith at the helm. Smith has started all 11 games so far this season. He has completed 68.1% of his passes, has thrown for 2,402 passing yards, and has a 15 touchdown to three interception ratio. Seems like the Jets are better off with Smith in 2026 than Rodgers. title: Eagles vs. Cowboys Game Preview: 5 questions and answers with the Thanksgiving enemy
summary: The Philadelphia Eagles can avoid being some real turkeys by beating the Dallas Cowboys on Thanksgiving. Fans would be very thankful to see a Birds win on Thursday. In order to preview this Week 12 NFC East battle, I reached out to our enemies over at Blogging The Boys. The divine Dave Halprin kindly took […]
full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA - OCTOBER 26: Joe Milton #14 of the Philadelphia Eagles and Dak Prescott #4 of the Dallas Cowboys hug after the game at Lincoln Financial Field on October 26, 2026 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Kathryn Riley/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Philadelphia Eagles can avoid being some real turkeys by beating the Dallas Cowboys on Thanksgiving. Fans would be very thankful to see a Birds win on Thursday. In order to preview this Week 12 NFC East battle, I reached out to our enemies over at Blogging The Boys . The divine Dave Halprin kindly took the time to answer my questions about this upcoming battle. Let’s take a look at the answers. 1 – To what extent do you buy Mike Pettine taking over play-calling making a positive difference for the Cowboys’ defense? I’d say it somewhat made a positive impact. The defense against the Titans on Sunday certainly looked more coherent, especially in their coverage and with players being in proper position. There didn’t seem to be so many busted assignments and guys not knowing what to do at the snap. There are reports they simplified the defensive calls and ran more zone coverage on the back end. The Titans did score three touchdowns, but one came on a questionable pass interference call in the endzone, another on a fluky run-after-catch where the Cowboys defender thought he touched the guy down but didn’t, then a garbage time TD at the end of the game. So the 30 total points kind of seems larger than how it felt in the run of the game. Of course, having an offense score 51 points overwhelms all issues, but it still felt like a little bit better version of the Cowboys defense. 2 – Besides Christian Parker being demoted, what else has significantly changed for the Cowboys since they last played the Eagles? For one, the pass rush, While the Cowboys overall defense still struggles, in the four games since we last played the Eagles, Dallas has accumulated 17 sacks with plenty of other pressure that forces bad plays. Quinnen Williams has really taken his game up a notch and is terrorizing teams from the middle of the line. The defense still struggles against the run, and besides Joey Porter Jr. our cornerbacks can definitely be had on a regular basis. But the pass rush has become the one thing that really works on defense. On offense, it feels like Brian Schottneheimr has re-discovered motion, play-action, bunch sets, cutdown splits and other things that were severely under-used in the earlier part of the season. The Cowboys scored 40 points on a very good 49ers defense, and 51 points over the hapless Titans defense. The last two games have been more reminiscent of how good the offense had been previously rather than the inconsistent bunch we’ve seen at times in 2026. 3 – If the Cowboys lose to Joe Milton at home on Thanksgiving, would that be their most embarrassing possible loss this season? What’s the path to the Cowboys losing this game? While it would be a bitter pill to swallow, we’ve already hit new lows by losing at home to a then-winless Buccaneers squad playing without Baker Mayfield, and allowed the terrible Cardinals to put together a comeback for the ages to win in Dallas. So losing to Joe Milton would make every fan gnash their teeth and then scream about not keeping him, but beating those other losses in the embarrassment category would be a hard thing to do. But, I won’t count the Cowboys out, they just might find a way to out-embarrass themselves. The path to losing the game is kind of the same every week. The Cowboys defense plays horrible football, busting assignments, gathering penalties and basically making a joke out of form tackling. Then the offense goes into one of its inconsistent modes, where the play-calling is bad and penalties, drops or turnovers come home to roost. 4 – Which NFC East team is going to win this division? Who’s going to finish second, third, and fourth? I was really leaning to the Cowboys because I just kept believing that the Giants would start to fall apart with their backup QBs playing. But that Jacksonville game where the Giants held on to victory makes me think that decent coaching (John Harbaugh) really can turn a team around. I’m still holding out hope we can catch them, but if I had to lay my life savings down on it, I’d have to take the Giants. As for the rest, it will probably end up the way it is now – Cowboys second, Commanders third and Eagles fourth. 5 – Who wins this game and why? With the Cowboys currently listed as 8.5-point home favorites, what’s your score prediction? I’m taking the Cowboys because they are at home where the offense usually plays well, and the defense looks like it might just be getting incrementally better. The Eagles are trying to overcome a lot this season including injuries at QB and at other key positions. There just feels like a lot of turmoil over there and the Cowboys might be in the process of starting to play like we expected them to when the season began. I’ll take the Cowboys 31-23.

title: Eagles’ offensive changes produced less than encouraging results
summary: The more things change, the more they stay the same. The Philadelphia Eagles made notable changes to their offense in Sunday’s win over the Pittsburgh Steelers. Less play-action, more pistol. They changed up the basis of Sean Mannion’s offense, as 84% of the Eagles’ offensive snaps were in the shotgun and 64.2% involved motion — […]
full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PA - NOVEMBER 22: Philadelphia Eagles head coach Nick Sirianni looks on during the game between the Philadelphia Eagles and the Pittsburg Steelers on November 22nd, 2026 at Lincoln Financial Field in Philadelphia, PA. (Photo by Terence Lewis/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The more things change, the more they stay the same. The Philadelphia Eagles made notable changes to their offense in Sunday’s win over the Pittsburgh Steelers. Less play-action, more pistol. They changed up the basis of Sean Mannion’s offense, as 84% of the Eagles’ offensive snaps were in the shotgun and 64.2% involved motion — both were season-highs. A season-high 42% of plays were snapped between six and 10 seconds left on the play clock — far above the previous high of 24.2%. Play-action percentage — the basis of Mannion’s offense — was 8.0%. That’s the lowest since Week 1 (5.7%). Shotgun play-action percentage was 14.3%, the highest since Week 1 (14.3%). The Eagles ran “11 personnel” 82.0% of the time, the second-highest percentage in a game this season (Week 6 vs. Panthers, 83.6%). “12 personnel” was 12.0%, the second-lowest percentage this year (Week 9 vs. Giants, 9.1%). The Eagles didn’t run “13 personnel” — three tight ends on the field — at all (despite having five tight ends on the active roster). There were significant changes on how the Eagles ran their offense, from pre-snap motion, to when they snapped the ball, and the formations they used. Since Joe Milton became the starting quarterback, the Eagles were trending in this direction. The results, unfortunately, have been more of the same. The Eagles can’t control the clock, they’ve been unable to stay on the field, and struggle to score points. This was with Saquon Barkley healthier (for a half at least) and DeVonta Smith back. Sean Mannion’s offense still failed to score 20 points and gain 250 yards. This was with the changes made — and how Philadelphia has been trending in that direction — over the last two weeks. There have been some positives with the changes, but the results have been what we’re accustomed to. Final three quarters were abysmal for an NFL offense When looking at the offensive numbers after the first quarter, it’s impressive the Eagles actually won the football game and snapped their losing streak. This also demonstrates how inept the Pittsburgh Steelers offense was on Sunday (or how well the Eagles defense played). The Eagles had 86 yards of total offense over the final three quarters on 36 plays — an average of 2.4 yards per play. On their nine drives, the Eagles averaged 10.8 yards per drive and 0.75 points per possession. The 3-and-out percentage was 50% (the Eagles lead the NFL in 3-and-out percentage). They had zero explosive plays while running 83.3% of the plays in shotgun and 60.5% of plays in motion. Joe Milton was 6-of-15 for 50 yards in the final three quarters, averaging 3.3 yards per attempt and finishing with a 49.3 rating. Milton was 3-of-9 for 31 yards when blitzed (44.2 rating) and 1-of-4 for 10 yards on throws of 10+ air yards. Milton finished 11-of-21 for 141 yards in the game, averaging 6.7 yards per attempt and finishing with a 73.7 rating. He was 4-of-7 for 87 yards on throws of 10+ air yards for the entire game (101.5 rating). Saquon Barkley had 12 carries for 24 yards, 2.0 yards per carry. The Eagles run offense had 20 carries for 37 yards (1.9 yards per carry) with a longest run of seven yards. DeVonta Smith and Darius Cooper were the only two players to catch passes. The Eagles averaged 3.5 yards per carry for the entire game (26 carries for 91 yards). Barkley had 17 carries for 75 yards, 4.4 yards per carry. Dallas Goedert was the only player other than Smith a Cooper to catch a pass (38-yard reception in the first quarter). The numbers in the final three quarters are consistent throughout the year. The Eagles average 184.7 yards and 4.0 yards per play in the final three quarters — last in the NFL. The 12.6 points per game rank 30th in the NFL. The second half numbers are poor as well. The 4.6 points per game in the second half are 32nd in the NFL, same with the 110.1 yards and 3.6 yards per play. The Eagles did up the scoring average, but that was due to 53 and 55-yard field goals by Jake Elliott. They had just 73 yards of offense and averaged just 2.4 yards per play. Hard to get excited about changes when the numbers remain the same — or worse. The offensive line was better This might be the biggest disappointment from Sunday. Throughout the season, the consensus of the offense’s lack of ability to move the ball was due to the inconsistency and lack of communication on the offensive line. The offensive line arguably played its best game all season, and the Eagles still couldn’t move the ball. Philadelphia’s offensive line allowed just five pressures, a pressure rate allowed of 20.8%. The pressure rate allowed was the lowest in the 2026 season (previous low was 38.3% in Week 9 against the Giants). The sack rate was at 12.5%, the lowest since Week 7 against the Dallas Cowboys. The Eagles offensive line also saw the Steelers blitz five-or-more rushers 54.2% of the time, the highest since Week 4 against the Los Angeles Rams (Markel Bell’s first start). As for Bell, he didn’t allow a sack for the second straight game. Bell also allowed a 4.2% pressure rate, far below the 11.6% allowed in Week 8 and 10.5% allowed in Week 7. The rookie is improving. Landon Dickerson allowed a season-low one pressure and a 4.2% pressure rate. Drew Kendall didn’t allow a pressure. The rushing yards per attempt on designed runs was 3.9, the highest since Week 7. This was with a yards before contact average of 0.23. The Eagles still couldn’t move the ball and score points after the first quarter. The Eagles have been trending this way since Joe Milton became the starting QB Milton has only made two starts for the Eagles, but the offense has been tailed to fit his skill set. That involves less play-action and more pistol. The Eagles ran shotgun on 75.8% of the offensive snaps in the Week 9 loss to the Giants, Milton’s first start. That number increased to 84.0% on Sunday. The play-action rate dipped from 13.6% to 8.0%, and the 13.6% rate in Week 9 was the highest since Jalen Hurts was the starting quarterback (Week 5 at Jacksonville Jaguars). Based on the shotgun percentage in Week 9, the Eagles were considering making a switch on offense — or accommodating to Milton’s style. This is a reminder Milton joined the team on October 16, and has only been in the offense for over a month. Over the past three weeks, the Eagles have been in shotgun 79.3% of the time. That only trails the Cincinnati Bengals for highest in the NFL (85.3%). Play-action is only at 11.2%, 26th in the NFL. The Eagles are also running “11 personnel” on 81.0% of the plays, the highest in the league. The Eagles altered their offense, yet are averaging just 15.0 offensive points per game (28th in NFL) and 217.0 yards per game (31st in NFL). The yards per play is at 3.7 (32nd in NFL). No matter the changes, the offense is still bad. Should Eagles fans be encouraged going forward? There isn’t much to get excited about this offense, and Sunday’s win over the Steelers confirmed that. After an exciting first quarter, the Eagles went dormant. They couldn’t stay on the field, and went 3-and-out on 50.0% of the offensive possessions. Yes, they scored six points in the second half — thanks to Jake Elliott and two 50+ yard field goals. They had 73 yards of offense and averaged 2.4 yards per play in that stretch. In the second half of games since Milton become quarterback, the Eagles are 29th in points per game (4.5), 31st in yards per game (86.0), and 32nd in yards per play (2.8). The Eagles are 32nd in the NFL in points (4.6), yards (110.1), and yards per play (3.6) in the second half this season. There are arguments to be made the offense has only gotten worse. The offense is the…

title: Eagles News: Philadelphia ended Aaron Rodgers’ career
summary: Welcome to The Linc, the daily Philadelphia Eagles news and links roundup at Bleeding Green Nation! Days after losing to the Eagles in Philly, Aaron Rodgers has been benched. On one hand, give Vic Fangio and his defense credit for doing their part to make him struggle to reach this point. On the other hand, […]
full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA - NOVEMBER 22: Aaron Rodgers #8 of the Pittsburgh Steelers is sacked by Byron Young #94 of the Philadelphia Eagles during an NFL football game at Lincoln Financial Field on November 22, 2026 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images) | Getty Images Welcome to The Linc, the daily Philadelphia Eagles news and links roundup at Bleeding Green Nation! Days after losing to the Eagles in Philly, Aaron Rodgers has been benched. On one hand, give Vic Fangio and his defense credit for doing their part to make him struggle to reach this point. On the other hand, the Eagles beat a soon-to-be 43-year-old quarterback whose own team came to the conclusion he’s unplayable and washed. Still, a fun footnote to Rodgers’ career that the Eagles effectively put him in retirement. Let’s get to the Philadelphia Eagles news and links … Steelers bench Aaron Rodgers, name Mason Rudolph starting QB vs. Broncos – Behind The Steel Curtain The Pittsburgh Steelers have named Mason Rudolph the starting quarterback vs. the Denver Broncos in their Week 12 game on Black Friday, the team announced in a statement Tuesday night. The Steelers’ passing game took a massive step backward over the last two weeks, with Aaron Rodgers’ play actively hurting the offense. In that span, Rodgers ranks 26th in success rate and the Steelers have failed to score 20 points. On the season, Rodgers ranks 35th in EPA per play (min. 25 dropbacks). He has thrown 16 touchdowns to six interceptions. NFL Mock Draft 2027: Eagles 7-round simulation, Version 2.0 – BGN The Eagles notched their first win in two months on Sunday. However, the game didn’t give much hope to the prospect of actually turning the season around. Unless they beat Dallas on Thursday, Philly is a team that should be looking ahead to the 2027 NFL Draft. Due to their win and Jacksonville’s loss, the Eagles currently own the ninth and 24th pick in the first round. Right now, the biggest determinants of the Eagles’ draft strategy has to do with what is happening at quarterback and head coach. There are many factors that would lead to the Eagles not needing to draft a quarterback, but I am curious what that draft may look like if the position is taken care of ahead of the draft without sacrificing picks… IE, Jalen Hurts returns from his blood clots. Eagles-Cowboys preview: 5 things to watch – PhillyVoice The strength of the Cowboys’ offensive line is on their interior, where Tyler Smith is an All-Pro caliber player, and Tyler Booker is becoming one. Cooper Beebe has also developed into a good center. The notable change from Week 7 to Week 12 is that Booker is likely out. If he can’t go, he’ll be replaced in the lineup by T.J. Bass. If you’ll recall, Jalen Carter got his ass kicked all night by Booker in that first matchup. Carter should theoretically have a matchup advantage over Bass, but he has only decided to try to be menace in sporadic games this season. At tackle, LT Tyler Guyton was the Cowboys’ first-round pick in 2024. He had a bad rookie season, and then an inconsistent season in 2025 before a Week 12 ankle injury ended his season. He has had his best season in 2026, by far. Steele is a replacement-level RT. The Eagles have 11 sacks in the last two games, and have gotten pressure from the interior and from the edge. The #Feastin’ is back, baby. From practice squad to prime time: A look at Milton’s big chance on Thanksgiving – ESPN It’s not like Milton has been lighting it up since taking over for Tanner McKee, who took over for Jalen Hurts. The Eagles have scored a total of 30 points in his two starts. He’s completed 53% of his throws and has been sacked 10 times. The passing offense has a success rate of 27.7%. But it’s also true that he’s brand new to this team and this offense. Milton was signed off the Cowboys’ practice squad on October 16 and was thrust into the starting lineup behind a shaky offensive line three weeks later. He has yet to throw an interception but has fumbled twice. There are areas of his game he is actively trying to improve, including knowing when to take something off his throws. Milton revealed after the Steelers game that to manage his arm strength — especially on deep throws like the one he had to Smith — he will say the name of his one-year-old daughter, Maleia, as he releases the ball “so I can relax a little bit.” “Basically it kind of tells [me] in my mind that I’m throwing the ball to her, so it can’t be as hard. Show a little love,” he said. Why the Eagles once tried to change the Cowboys’ Thanksgiving tradition – The Athletic Players face a physical challenge. It’s hard enough for a player to recover from a game in one week. Three days between games — especially when one is a travel day — offer no favors. The Eagles had stationary bikes and massage tables set up in the locker room in the minutes after last Sunday’s win over the Pittsburgh Steelers. The recovery started immediately. They are not practicing this week, using Tuesday for a walk-through before a Wednesday flight to Dallas. “For us to be able to play in a Thanksgiving game, I’ve been able to do that one time, but that’s something you grow up (watching) as a kid,” Eagles running back Saquon Barkley said. “So I love that opportunity every single time. “But how I feel about Thursday games, if we’re all for what benefits the players’ health, I don’t know how you can make logic of how that helps your players’ health, like the health side of it. But I get it for the business side.” Still, Thursday games are a reality of the NFL. So are Thanksgiving games. It’s long gone beyond the traditional schedule in Detroit and Dallas. The third Thanksgiving primetime timeslot was added in 2006. The NFL added a Black Friday game in 2023. This year, they’ll have a Thanksgiving eve game. (That is not on a short week because the two teams are coming off byes.) Though the Thanksgiving slate evolves, the tradition remains. The Lions and Cowboys host Thanksgiving games. The Eagles once tried to spark discussion about changing the hosting aspect, but it didn’t gain traction. “There wasn’t enough support at this point,” Lurie said in 2019. “But you want to start the conversation somewhere.” NFL Quarterback Rankings: Joe Burrow leads the way, Patrick Mahomes rises – PFF 27) Joe Milton, Philadelphia Eagles (up 1). Milton improved on what was a fairly disastrous first start for the Eagles in Week 9 with a stronger performance in the win over the Pittsburgh Steelers in Week 11. He went 11-for-21 for 141 yards and a 65.6 PFF grade in the win, producing a pair of big-time throws and no turnover-worthy plays as a passer. The switch that flips for Jeremiah Trotter Jr. when he takes the field – NBCSP Jeremiah Trotter Jr. is a soft-spoken guy. He’s normally calm, quiet and reserved. Until he hits the field. That’s when Axe Man Jr. is able to flip a switch. “You guys might talk to him, he seems a little quiet, but once he gets out on that field, he gets louder,” Eagles DB Cooper DeJean said. “You hear him talk some trash every once in a while, which is funny.” Trotter started on Sunday against the Steelers and led the Eagles with 13 tackles in the 19-16 win. He also wore the green dot on his helmet for communication in place of Zack Baun, who is on IR with a back injury. If you’re gonna have that green dot, you’d better speak up, and Trotter did. DeJean and Trotter were both part of the 2024 draft class, but even DeJean was surprised the first time he saw Trotter’s on-field personality take over. “Yeah, definitely,” DeJean said. “I like it, though, when he gets that confidence and that swagger. I feel like it gives everybody else confidence too.” Sean Mannion explains the ‘tweaks’ of the shotgun- and pistol-heavy offense the Eagles ran Sunday – Inquirer Five plays came and went before Joe Milton took his first snap from under center Sunday. It was the first time all season that an Eagles quarterback didn’t line up under…

full_text: ARLINGTON, TX - NOVEMBER 23: Quinyon Mitchell #27 of the Philadelphia Eagles defends in coverage during an NFL football game against the Dallas Cowboys at AT&T Stadium on November 23, 2025 in Arlington, Texas. (Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Philadelphia Eagles issued their second official injury report of the week on Tuesday in advance of their Week 12 game against the Dallas Cowboys on Thanksgiving. Note that this report is an estimation because the team held a walkthrough in lieu of a normal practice. The Eagles listed two players under DID NOT PARTICIPATE: Jonathan Jones and Arnold Ebiketie. Jones and Ebiketie are on track to miss Thursday’s game. Jones might’ve been starting at cornerback if he wasn’t hurt. His likely absence moves Kelee Ringo and Mac McWilliams up the depth chart. Ebiketie’s likely absence means A.J. Epenesa could see playing time as a rotational edge rusher behind Jalyx Hunt, Nolan Smith, and Jonathan Greenard. The Eagles listed three players under LIMITED PARTICIPATION: Quinyon Mitchell, Will Shipley, and Smael Mondon . Mitchell was upgraded from DNP on Monday to limited on Tuesday. Vic Fangio said he thinks Mitchell will be fine enough to play. It doesn’t really seem wise for the Eagles to put him out there with a hammy issue on short rest. Even if Mitchell does suit up, he could be hampered going up against CeeDee Lamb and/or George Pickens. Not really ideal. Shipley was limited for the second day in a row. Guessing he’ll be able to suit up and provide depth behind Saquon Barkley. Mondon was upgraded from DNP to limited. He might be able to play, though the Eagles signing Chance Campbell to the roster indicates they’re prepping to have more linebacker depth. The Eagles listed nine players under FULL PARTICIPATION: Kelee Ringo, Saquon Barkley, Dallas Goedert , Tanner McKee , DeVonta Smith, Jalen Carter, Jonathan Greenard, Michael Carter, and Britain Covey. Ringo is a new addition to the report with a neck injury. The Eagles can’t really afford more cornerback injuries with Mitchell and Jones already banged up. Ringo is also a key special teams contributor. Seems like he’ll be able to play but something to monitor. Barkley, Goedert, and McKee were upgraded from limited on Monday to full on Tuesday. title: Eagles sign practice squad linebacker to roster
summary: The Philadelphia Eagles officially announced two roster moves on Tuesday afternoon. Here’s an overview: Let’s sort through this news on a player-by-player basis. CHANCE CAMPBELL Campbell was once believed to be pushing for a roster spot. Back in training camp, Vic Fangio told reporters to put him on their 53-man projections. Campbell began the season […]
full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PA - AUGUST 28: Philadelphia Eagles linebacker Chance Campbell #59 is shown during the pre season game between the Philadelphia Eagles and the Cincinnati Bengals on August 28th, 2026 at Lincoln Financial Field in Philadelphia, PA. (Photo by Terence Lewis/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Philadelphia Eagles officially announced two roster moves on Tuesday afternoon. Here’s an overview: LB Chance Campbell was signed from the practice squad to the active roster. OL Jake Majors was waived. Let’s sort through this news on a player-by-player basis. CHANCE CAMPBELL Campbell was once believed to be pushing for a roster spot. Back in training camp, Vic Fangio told reporters to put him on their 53-man projections. Campbell began the season on the practice squad, though, before being temporarily elevated for the Eagles’ Week 3 game against the Chicago Bears. Campbell was then placed on the practice squad injured list in early October before the team cut him Campbell returned to the practice squad on November 16. In need off off-ball linebacker depth with Zack Baun going on injured reserve, the Eagles decided to temporarily elevate Anfernee Orji instead of Campbell for their Week 11 game against the Pittsburgh Steelers. But now Campbell is on the roster while Orji remains on the practice squad. It’s possible they’ll temporarily elevate the latter to give the team four linebackers (assuming Smael Mondon can’t play again) for their Week 12 game against the Dallas Cowboys. Chance Campbell and Orji would be the backups behind Jihaad Campbell and Jeremiah Trotter Jr. Or perhaps they’ll just roll with three again, like they did in Week 11. That situation almost got dire with Jihaad Campbell suffering a finger injury that caused Orji to see three defensive snaps before the former player quickly returned. Chance Campbell seems like a solid depth player in addition to being able to help out on special teams. He wears No. 59. JAKE MAJORS With the Eagles trading Cam Jurgens and Drew Kendall getting hurt while Landon Dickerson was on injured reserve, Majors started at center for the eagles in Week 6 and Week 7. His bad snap in the Carolina Panthers game was a big momentum killer that prevented any hopes of a comeback in that game. Majors hasn’t played since Week 7 and has been a healthy scratch in recent weeks. He was understandably deemed expendable. It’s possible the Eagles will bring him back on the practice squad (swapping places with Campbell, then) if/when he clears waivers. Or maybe not. We’ll see.
