title: NFL Playoff Picture: Which team is going to win the NFC East?
summary: If you’re rooting for the Philadelphia Eagles to make the playoffs, the good news is that the Philadelphia Eagles did their part to keep extremely slim postseason hopes alive by beating the Pittsburgh Steelers. The bad news is that every other team in the NFC East won in Week 11. And this despite two of […]
full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA - OCTOBER 26: Saquon Barkley #26 of the Philadelphia Eagles looks on from the field after an NFL football game against the Dallas Cowboys at Lincoln Financial Field on October 26, 2026 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Perry Knotts/Getty Images) | Getty Images If you’re rooting for the Philadelphia Eagles to make the playoffs, the good news is that the Philadelphia Eagles did their part to keep extremely slim postseason hopes alive by beating the Pittsburgh Steelers. The bad news is that every other team in the NFC East won in Week 11. And this despite two of those three being betting underdogs. As such, the division standings now look like this entering Week 12: 1) New York Giants: 6-3-1 2) Dallas Cowboys: 5-6 3) Washington Commanders: 4-5-1 4) Philadelphia Eagles: 3-7 Can the Eagles make up a lot of ground in a short amount of time? Probably not! The betting odds to win the NFC East show that the Birds are massive long shots to threepeat as division champs: Giants -230 Cowboys +410 Commanders +430 Eagles +12500 But if you’re building the case for optimism, it’s that the Eagles’ defense has stabilized over their past two games. Vic Fangio’s group limited the New York Giants to 19 points before holding the Pittsburgh Steelers to 16. It’s difficult (read: nearly impossible) to feel good about the Eagles’ offensive outlook, especially after their lackluster performance against the Stillers. But at least they’re doing some different things stylistically ? Maybe that leads to some positive results? Again, probably not. But if there were a time for that much to happen, it would be against the Dallas Cowboys’ dreadful defense on Thanksgiving. If the Eagles can pull off an upset as 8.5-point road underdogs, they’re much more alive at 4-7 than they’d be at 3-8. If we take the Eagles out of the equation, which is safe to do at this point in time, I’m curious to hear which team you think has the best chance of winning the NFC East. The Giants are in the top spot, yes, but they are set to face the NFL’s eighth-toughest remaining schedule and the Commanders hold a head-to-head tiebreaker over them. Washington also has the NFL’s third-easiest remaining schedule. The Cowboys’ offense is capable of staying hot down the stretch, though they have the ninth-toughest remaining schedule. Which team do you think will win? Vote in our poll: I voted for the Commanders. They have a feel of a team that could go on a run … before losing in the wild card round. summary: Now that Week 11 of the 2026 NFL season is in the books, it’s time for an incredibly meaningful and serious exercise: NFL Power Rankings! full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PA - NOVEMBER 22: Philadelphia Eagles running back Saquon Barkley #26 breaks a tackle during the game between the Philadelphia Eagles and the Pittsburg Steelers on November 22nd, 2026 at Lincoln Financial Field in Philadelphia, PA. (Photo by Terence Lewis/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Now that Week 11 of the 2026 NFL season is in the books, it’s time for an incredibly meaningful and serious exercise: NFL Power Rankings ! What differentiates these rankings from all others is that they’re THE only truly accurate ones in the entire universe. Hard to believe, I know. But it’s true. Let’s take a look at how all 32 teams stack up. ( Here’s a link to last week’s version .) BLG’S WEEK 12 POWER RANKINGS 1 – Chicago Bears (Last Week: 1) – If the Bears are as for real as we think they are, they’ll go out and beat the Lions in Detroit on Thanksgiving. Massive game. If they don’t win, they’ll drop to an 0-3 division record. They haven’t lost when Caleb Williams starts and finishes a game this season, so, let’s see it. 2 – San Francisco 49ers (LW: 2) – Unfortunately, the Niners look like badasses who could very well win the Super Bowl this season. They’re a juggernaut. 3 – Buffalo Bills (LW: 3) – The average margin of victory over the Bills’ last four wins is 19.25 points. They faced some pretty bad quarterbacks during that stretch. But they clobbered them, which is what good teams do to inferior opponents. 4 – Kansas City Chiefs (LW: 4) – The Chiefs followed up a two-game losing streak with decisive wins over NYJ, Atlanta, and Arizona. Despite their 8-2 record, they’re currently the No. 5 seed in the AFC playoff picture. But you would think they’ll eventually overtake Denver. 5 – Detroit Lions (LW: 5) – Six straight wins for the Lions, who have really stabilized after a shaky start to the season. If they can beat the Bears on Thursday, they’ll be 3-0 in division games. They’ll be on a good path to take the NFC North crown at that point. 6 – Seattle Seahawks (LW: 7) – The Seahawks return from their bye to face the 49ers in Santa Clara. They’re three-point underdogs to a dominant Niners team that previously beat them in Week 5. This is their chance to prevent the NFC West from being wrapped up before Week 13. 7 – Jacksonville Jaguars (LW: 6) – The Jags can probably kiss a first-round bye goodbye after losing to the G-Men. 8 – Cincinnati Bengals (LW: 8) – Joe Burrow logged his fourth-worst passer rating of the season in a loss to Washington. That number? 108.3. Bad loss for the Bengals but it was the least valuable game on their schedule (out of conference floating opponent). They’ll bounce back from this. 9 – Denver Broncos (LW: 11) – With one more Broncos win, Sean Payton will clinch a non-losing season in eight out of his last nine seasons as a head coach. And the one losing season was his first year in Denver with an 8-9 record. He’s as good at his job as he is unlikable. 10 – Minnesota Vikings (LW: 9) – The NFL’s best defense got shredded by the NFL’s best offense. Bad look for the Vikes to no-show in a big spot. What value is Kevin O’Connell bringing to the table, exactly? 11 – Los Angeles Rams (LW: 10) – The Rams return from their bye to host the Packers. And they’ll be without Puka Nacua for the rest of the season. LA beat up on some lesser teams to reach a 6-4 record. Now we’ll see what they can do with lots of tough games remaining. Their next three: vs. GB, vs. SF, at KC. 12 – Green Bay Packers (LW: 12) – The Packers return from their bye to play the Rams in LA. They’re listed as standard 2.5-point road underdogs. A win for either team will be very valuable since the head-to-head tiebreaker could determine who makes the postseason or not. GB is currently the No. 7 seed in the NFC playoff picture while LA is on the outside looking in at No. 9. 13 – Dallas Cowboys (LW: 16) – The Cowboys had nine drives against the Titans. They scored seven touchdowns and one field goal before taking a knee on their final possession. The Titans are terrible, yes, scoring 51 points is impressive regardless of the opponent. (For perspective, the most points scored by the Eagles in a game this season is 24.) 14 – New York Giants (LW: 17) – Kudos to the Giants; I didn’t think they were ready to hang with the big boys. Beating the Jags gives them a signature win in John Harbaugh’s first season on the job. The G-Men are 4-2-1 as underdogs this season and they have a real chance to win the NFC East. 15 – Cleveland Browns (LW: 15) – The Browns return from their bye to host the Raiders. They’re in a stretch where they’re playing four straight home games. There’s a chance for them to build some momentum. 16 – Las Vegas Raiders (LW: 13) – After a fun 3-0 start, the Raiders are 1-7 over their last eight games. Their wins this season have come over the Dolphins, Chargers, Saints, and Jets. 17 – Pittsburgh Steelers (LW: 14) – It’s unfathomable that his team has six wins. In a matchup against a really bad Eagles squad, the Steelers clearly looked like the lesser team. Aaron Rodgers is so washed. 18 – Carolina Panthers (LW: 20) – The Panthers narrowly defeated Jacoby Brissett’s Ravens. They just might be the least worst team in a dreadful NFC South. 19 – Washington Commanders (LW: 22) – Washington followed up a must-win game in Week 10 with a big victory over the Bengals on Monday night. Jayden Daniels came up in the clutch once again. With the third-easiest remaining schedule in the NFL, the Commanders could make a real run for the NFC East crown. 20 – Tampa Bay Buccaneers (LW: 19) – Any idea of the Bucs turning a corner is dead after following up two straight wins with two straight losses. That being said, they can clinch a head-to-head tiebreaker over the Panthers if they beat Carolina again in Week 12. 21 – Houston Texans (LW: 24) – The Texans have four wins. They came over the Titans, Jags, Chargers, and Colts. Aside from the Jags, those are three of the four teams at the top of the 2027 NFL Draft order. 22 – New England Patriots (LW: 18) – The Pats’ outlook isn’t great with Drake Maye getting injured. They return from their bye to play the Chargers … and they’re 1.5-point road underdogs. 23 – Baltimore Ravens (LW: 21) – Six straight losses. Tough, too, because the last two were narrow defeats. 24 – New Orleans Saints (LW: 23) – The Saints rank dead last in the NFL’s worst division. 25 – Atlanta Falcons (LW: 25) – The Falcons return from their bye to play the Vikings in Minnesota. Another L incoming. 26 – Arizona Cardinals (LW: 26) – Since beating the Cowboys in Week 8, the Cardinals have been outscored 85 to 16. Brutal. 27 – Philadelphia Eagles (LW: 31) – Kudos to the Eagles’ defense for stepping up to snap a seven-game losing streak. The offense is still terrible, though. 28 – Indianapolis Colts (LW: 27) – The Colts are a mess. But at least they’re making the right decision to evaluate Anthony Richardson instead of wasting time by playing Daniel Jones. 29 – Miami Dolphins (LW: 28) – Kyle McCord has logged a 52.8 passer rating while filling in for Malik Willis. 30 – New York Jets (LW: 30) – Two of the Jets’ three wins this season have come against the two teams ranked directly below. Bad … but not THE worst! 31 – Los Angeles Chargers (LW: 29) – The Bolts failed to build off of a win in Baltimore. Hardly shocking. 32 – Tennessee Titans (LW: 32) – Listless franchise.

full_text: (Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Pittsburgh Steelers made the stunning decision late last night to bench their veteran quarterback Aaron Rodgers. The decision came as a shock to many and is believed to be wildly unpopular in the Steelers locker room. Appearing on The Pat McAfee Show , the legendary quarterback broke his silence on the decision and made a stunning claim about Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy. “Last Wednesday, we were in a quarterback meeting,” Rodgers said. “Mike came in late, sat down, and when the 10 minutes began snoring. Woke up, was rattling his papers. We all looked around. Five minutes later, you hear the snoring again. And less than five minutes after that, he walks out of the room.” Rodgers went on to say that McCarthy constantly misses walkthroughs and had admitted to being behind on film on several occasions. The quarterback admitted that even general manager Omar Khan is aware of McCarthy’s sleeping habits inside the facility. It’s safe to say that Rodgers has played his final down with the Steelers, and quite possibly his career. This situation has been blown wide open and is far from over. The veteran quarterback believes his head coach was out to get him, and McCarthy still believes Rodgers got him fired from the Packers in 2018. The relationship that originally brought Rodgers back to the Steelers for another year is now the reason the Steelers’ season has gone off the rails. Let us know what you think in the comments . full_text: (Photo by Mitchell Leff/Getty Images) Pieces of the puzzle are coming together around the Steelers’ shocking decision to bench Aaron Rodgers. The Steelers released a statement, through their team spokesman Burt Lauten, that Mason Rudolph will start against the Denver Broncos on Black Friday. Rodgers won’t even dress and is already announced as inactive. NFL insider Mike Garafolo said on NFL Network that the Steelers were in the process of changing the delivery of their play calling duties to quarterbacks coach Tom Arth. “There was going to be a change in the process this week,” Garafolo said. “Tom Arth is the quarterbacks coach. He was going to be the one to radio the plays in to Rodgers. That change was that this was going to be how things were going to go for the entire game,” Garafolo said. “They worked through that at practice yesterday. They were also having meetings as late as 5:30- 6 o’clock to figure this stuff out.” “Rodgers was the one that wanted this change to be made and that’s why it was happening as early as the walkthrough yesterday,” Garafolo said. Rodgers took first-team reps on Tuesday and met with the media like any typical week. What happened between Rodgers talking and 11:10 p.m. Tuesday night? “Nobody was talking about Rodgers being benched so I do believe that it was late last night when Mike McCarthy finally made the decision to bench Aaron Rodgers,” Garafolo said. “The question is, why?” Arth was the Steelers quarterbacks coach in 2025 when Rodgers joined the Steelers and was the only assistant coach to stay on staff when Mike McCarthy took over. Arth and Rodgers have had a longstanding relationship. Let us know what you think in the comments . Be sure to bookmark Behind the Steel Curtain for all the latest news, breakdowns, and more! title: Steelers Week 12 power rankings roundup: The terrible tumble continues
summary: The Pittsburgh Steelers suffered their second consecutive loss after another embarrassing loss in Philadelphia at the hands of the Eagles. It was another week of the offense looking largely lifeless until the game was already out of reach. Even with the Cincinnati Bengals’ loss on Monday Night Football, the Steelers still sit a game back […]
full_text: Photo by Mitchell Leff/Getty Images | Getty Images The Pittsburgh Steelers suffered their second consecutive loss after another embarrassing loss in Philadelphia at the hands of the Eagles. It was another week of the offense looking largely lifeless until the game was already out of reach. Even with the Cincinnati Bengals’ loss on Monday Night Football, the Steelers still sit a game back in the AFC North standings. As always, let’s take a look around the internet to see where the Steelers fall in this week’s power rankings roundup. FOX Sports: No. 19 (Last Week No. 15) “Aaron Rodgers has had a Hall of Fame career, but surely everyone in Pittsburgh can see it’s over now. He is dragging this team down with his lack of mobility and his inability to throw accurately and consistently more than 5-10 yards downfield. It would be incredibly gutsy for Mike McCarthy to bench him now, but he has to do it. He just has to. The Steelers are still 6-4, but they’ve looked terrible in two losses after the bye. Maybe Mason Rudolph or rookie Drew Allar aren’t going to be much better, especially with games against the Broncos and Jaguars over the next three weeks. But the way Rodgers is playing, it’s not like they could be much worse.” – Ralph Vacchiano The Athletic: No. 15 (Last Week No.13) “For a while at least, hopefully. The Eagles are on the Steelers’ 2028 schedule, but that game is scheduled for Pittsburgh. Sunday’s loss to the scab-level Eagles was the Steelers’ 12th straight in Philly, where they haven’t won since 1965. “We expected to win this game, especially with some of the challenges and changes our opponent was going through,” coach Mike McCarthy said.“ – Chad Graff and Josh Kendall CBS Sports: No. 15 (Last Week No. 10) “What was that against the Eagles? Two straight losses has their playoff hold in jeopardy.” – Pete Prisco Pro Football Talk: No. 15 (Last Week No. 11) “Playoffs or not, the Steelers aren’t good enough to compete with the best teams in the AFC.” – Mike Florio NFL.com: No. 21 (Last Week No.13) “The Steelers should be embarrassed by what happened Sunday in Philadelphia. Their offense was abysmal for the vast majority of the contest, Aaron Rodgers looked every bit of 42 years old and DK Metcalf got himself ejected after contributing virtually nothing to their effort. This is the most volatile team with a winning record and one that seems headed toward a dark place after losing to the Eagles.” – Nick Shook Yahoo! Sports: No. 16 (Last Week No. 13) “The Steelers were showing improvement but the last two weeks are alarming. They were destroyed by the Bengals, then didn’t threaten an Eagles team that had lost seven in a row and was on its third quarterback this season. The lingering problem from the game is receiver DK Metcalf getting ejected after another unproductive game. The NFL reportedly won’t suspend him , but that doesn’t mean Pittsburgh can rely on a player who hasn’t done much on the field and whose behavior is unreliable too.“ “There are also injury concerns at a key spot. Edge rusher Nick Herbig was inactive Sunday because of rib and hip injuries, then Alex Highsmith left the game against the Eagles early because of an ankle injury. The Steelers get the 8-2 Broncos on Friday and the Texans and Jaguars after that. Pittsburgh was once 6-2. It’s possible it will be under .500 by mid-December.” – Frank Schwab USA Today: No. 13 (Last Week No.13) “Yes, a 6-4 squad is slotted at unlucky No. 13 as its season appears to be bleeding luck … and poise in the case of too-often unhinged WR DK Metcalf. But the Steelers − and the clubs they’re clustered with − also seem a lot closer to, say, No. 24 than No. 10.” – Nate Davis ESPN: No. 15 (Last Week No. 13) “Frazier has shown the makings of a long-term anchor for the group throughout his three seasons as a starter; quarterback Aaron Rodgers has frequently praised the center’s intelligence. Extension eligible for the first time this offseason, the 2024 second-round pick has played a big role in the Steelers’ offensive line renovation. Not only are they likely to prioritize extending him because they believe in building through the trenches, Frazier also figures to be an invaluable resource for the team’s next starting quarterback — a player who will have much less experience than Rodgers.” – Brooke Pryor Last week, the outlets we examined were willing to give the Steelers a pass considering how well the Bengals had been playing as of late. However, this loss to an Eagles team that had lost seven consecutive games entering this game is inexcusable. The consensus among the rankings seems to be that the Steelers may very well make the playoffs, but are nowhere near the top of the line Super Bowl contenders. They will have a chance to get back in the good graces of all of us if they can take down the Denver Broncos on Black Friday, who enter the contest riding a six-game win streak. title: Where the Seahawks’ still elite defense has fallen off from 2025
summary: If you look at some of the major stats for the Seattle Seahawks defense, they’re roughly averaging the same points allowed as last season’s Super Bowl team, they’re once again ranked No. 1 overall by DVOA, No. 1 in EPA/play, No. 1 in fewest pass yards allowed, and tied for first with the San Francisco […]
full_text: (Photo by Steph Chambers/Getty Images) | Getty Images If you look at some of the major stats for the Seattle Seahawks defense, they’re roughly averaging the same points allowed as last season’s Super Bowl team, they’re once again ranked No. 1 overall by DVOA, No. 1 in EPA/play, No. 1 in fewest pass yards allowed, and tied for first with the San Francisco 49ers in fewest yards allowed per carry. And yet, there are times where the Seahawks do not feel like their defense is as great as 2025. We’ve got a few stats to show where things have noticeably dipped. Red zone defense Thanks to the Carolina Panthers , the Seahawks are no longer the worst red zone defense by EPA/play. Holding the Arizona Cardinals and Las Vegas Raiders to just a touchdown on four red zone trips means Seattle has improved it’s red zone TD percentage to 29th, but this is still a perplexingly bad RZ defense until further notice. Last season, the Seahawks were fifth in red zone TD percentage defensively and No. 1 in red zone DVOA. Generally speaking, red zone numbers are smaller sample size and such a huge disparity between Seattle’s RZ and non-RZ defense should signify future positive regression. The Seahawks defense has been put in many unenviable spots due to short-field turnovers, but it wasn’t like short-field turnovers weren’t happening last year. Something is not clicking in the micro structure of Seattle’s red zone defense. 4th down defense Almost the same deal as red zone defense. Seattle was 10th-best at stopping 4th down in 2025, but this year the ‘Hawks have sunk to 31st. Last year’s 4th down defense ranked 2nd in EPA/play, while the 2026 unit is 31st overall and 32nd against the run. Their only two stops on 14 attempts came in garbage time against the Kansas City Chiefs and the goal line stand late in the second Cardinals game. While the Seahawks boast a fantastic 3rd down defense, we live in an era where going for it on 4th down more often is strongly encouraged, and the Seahawks have struggled to slam the door shut on all four downs. Again, small sample size that can normalize as the season progresses, but much like the red zone, it’s not necessarily guaranteed. It’s certainly notable that in both the red zone and 4th down, Seattle’s otherwise airtight run defense is at or near the bottom in EPA, so something is not clicking in the trenches the way it did last year. Defending No. 1 receivers FTN’s DVOA metric has long included metrics for opposing defenses against receivers, running backs, and tight ends. The Seahawks 2025 pass defense was not only the best in the NFL overall, they were the best at defending No. 1 wide receivers. Admittedly, the designation of a No. 1 receiver is “somewhat subjective” by DVOA criteria, but most teams have a clear top wide receiver target. Anyway, the 2026 Seahawks is once again tops by pass defense DVOA, but defending top receivers is a big dropoff to 22nd. The DVOA breakdown includes WR1, WR2, WR3, TE, and RB, and WR1 is the only one for which Seattle is outside the top 10. Seattle’s schedule of opposing offenses is an impressive 8th, with only the Denver Broncos, Arizona Cardinals, and Los Angeles Chargers ranked in the bottom-half in pass offense DVOA. However, when the Seahawks have been tasked with facing what I would assume are top receivers, the results haven’t been overly impressive: Mike Evans had 7 catches for 113 yards and a touchdown in the first 49ers meeting, while Terry McLaurin caught 6 passes (all but one of which went for a first or a touchdown) for 77 yards and a touchdown in the Commanders game. The Bears’ WR1 is presumably Luther Burden, who was shut out in the second half against Seattle but had 7 catches for 56 yards and a score. All but one of Burden’s catches would be classified as a successful play based on yardage gained relative to down and distance. Seattle didn’t have to play Rashee Rice at all, Ladd McConkey checked out early with an injury (and the Chargers offense reeks anyway), and A.J. Brown had 3 catches for 26 yards and a DPI penalty drawn before he left in the second half with his own injury. For the next three weeks, the Seahawks will face Evans again, CeeDee Lamb, and Malik Nabers, so the schedule of wide receiver opposition will not let up in the short term. Make no mistake about it, though: The Seahawks defense is still great and they’re not close to the main reason the team is currently sitting outside of a playoff spot. Seattle’s offense needs to improve significantly to have any shot at contention, but the defense also needs to fix its micro problems that have factored into close games swinging against them.

title: Why Packers vs. Rams could have major Seahawks playoff ramifications
summary: The NFL is getting Thanksgiving week started earlier than ever before, with the Los Angeles Rams hosting the Green Bay Packers on Wednesday night on Netflix. Both teams are 6-4, just like the Seattle Seahawks, who will have their own huge clash with the San Francisco 49ers to focus on this Sunday. The outcome of […]
full_text: (Photo by Brooke Sutton/Getty Images) | Getty Images The NFL is getting Thanksgiving week started earlier than ever before, with the Los Angeles Rams hosting the Green Bay Packers on Wednesday night on Netflix. Both teams are 6-4, just like the Seattle Seahawks, who will have their own huge clash with the San Francisco 49ers to focus on this Sunday. The outcome of Wednesday’s matchup is therefore very relevant to Seattle. The Packers hold the final Wild Card spot over the Seahawks Here’s the relevant portion of the NFC playoff picture for Seattle: 1. San Francisco 49ers (9-1) 2. Detroit Lions (8-2, 2-0 NFCN) 3. New York Giants (6-3-1) 4. Carolina Panthers (5-5) 5. Chicago Bears (8-2, 0-2 NFCN) 6. Minnesota Vikings (7-3) 7. Green Bay Packers (6-4, 4-4 NFC) 8. Seattle Seahawks (6-4, 2-1 NFCW, 2-3 NFC) 9. Los Angeles Rams (6-4, 1-2 NFCW) Seattle is once again tussling with the Packers for a Wild Card spot, just as it did in 2022 (successfully) and 2023 (unsuccessfully). Green Bay currently holds the No. 7 seed over the Seahawks based on the conference record tiebreaker (4-4 for the Packers vs. 2-3 for the Seahawks). Meanwhile, the Seahawks have a superior division record over the Rams (2-1 vs. 1-2). What a Rams win over the Packers means for the Seahawks in Week 12 If the Rams defeat the Packers, they would leapfrog over both Seattle and Green Bay into the last playoff spot. However, the Seahawks could overtake the Rams again by beating the 49ers, therefore assuming the No. 7 seed on the aforementioned division tiebreaker over Los Angeles. What a Packers win over the Rams means for the Seahawks in Week 12 Should the Packers prevail, the Rams would fall to 6-5 and the Seahawks would be guaranteed to stay in the eighth spot in the NFC at the end of Week 12. Either they beat the 49ers and stay behind the Packers on the conference record tiebreaker, or they lose to the 49ers and stay ahead of the Rams on division record tiebreaker. Which outcome results in a higher playoff probability percentage for the Seahawks? If you go through The Athletic/New York Times Playoff Machine, Seattle currently has a 52% chance to make the playoffs. Outside of the Seahawks’ own game, the game on the Week 12 schedule that has the widest playoff probability range is (by a percentage point) Packers-Rams. Folks… you’re not going to like the answer for which team to “root” for. As an aside, I assume the Chicago Bears over the Detroit Lions is preferred for the Seahawks because the Bears getting sucked into the Wild Card chase would hurt Seattle, who don’t hold the head-to-head tiebreaker. I’m not saying “Go Rams!” or anything so sacrilegious, I’m just saying that a Rams win is not the worst thing in the world for the Seahawks. Of course, a Seahawks loss would put them below 50 percent probability regardless of the Packers-Rams result, but a win puts them in the driver’s seat for a Wild Card berth entering December. And if the Rams lose and the Seahawks win this week? Well, there’s a not-so-unrealistic scenario in which the Seahawks could be looking to mathematically eliminate the Rams from postseason contention on Christmas night.

title: Seahawks Week 12 national power rankings: Seattle barely hanging onto top 10 status
summary: Entering Week 11, the Seattle Seahawks slightly moved up power rankings, although the national media still shows skepticism over the team’s offense. Will that skeptic tune change after the bye week? Let’s take a look at five national media sites (NFL.com, CBS Sports, Bleacher Report (B/R), Pro Football Talk (PFT), and ESPN) to see where […]
full_text: (Photo by Steph Chambers/Getty Images) Entering Week 11, the Seattle Seahawks slightly moved up power rankings , although the national media still shows skepticism over the team’s offense. Will that skeptic tune change after the bye week? Let’s take a look at five national media sites (NFL.com, CBS Sports, Bleacher Report (B/R), Pro Football Talk (PFT), and ESPN) to see where they rank Seattle. NFL.com is the lowest on the Seahawks, having them ranked 12th best in the league, one spot down from last week. In their ranking, NFL.com notes that they are on a two game winning streak, although those two wins are against lesser teams. The true test is Week 12 against the San Francisco 49ers. CBS Sports ranks Seattle as the 11th best team in the NFL , one spot up from last week. In their ranking, CBS notes that Seattle comes out of their bye with little room for error if they want to make the playoffs. B/R and ESPN both rank the Seahawks as the 10th best team. BR, in their ranking note the importance of the upcoming game against the 49ers: “ Win, and the NFC West race actually is one down the stretch. Lose, and the division is no longer the priority .” ESPN meanwhile discusses who NFL teams need to prioritize extensions for. For the Seahawks, that player is Byron Murphy II. “ Murphy is one of the NFL’s premier defensive tackles, and he might be the highest-paid player at the position before long .” The highest rank the Seahawks earned in this week’s power rankings are from PFT , who rank Seattle the 9th best. PFT also notes that the season may come down to this upcoming matchup against the 49ers. Overall the national landscape is setting the Seahawks up at a crossroads. Either start winning and defend your Superbowl Title, or continue playing around with lesser teams, and find yourselves out of the playoffs. Entering week 11, the average power rankings between the five polled sites was 10.0. Entering week 12, that average has slightly fallen to 10.4. The Seahawks now prepare for their biggest matchup of the season.

title: NFL rescinds fine for Malik Mustapha’s controversial hit on Jaxon Smith-Njigba
summary: The Seattle Seahawks and San Francisco 49ers will renew their rivalry this Sunday in a game that has massive implications for Seattle’s playoff hopes and San Francisco’s bid for the No. 1 seed in the NFC. San Francisco finds itself in the NFC West driver’s seat in large part due to its 32-29 win at […]
full_text: (Photo by Steph Chambers/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Seattle Seahawks and San Francisco 49ers will renew their rivalry this Sunday in a game that has massive implications for Seattle’s playoff hopes and San Francisco’s bid for the No. 1 seed in the NFC. San Francisco finds itself in the NFC West driver’s seat in large part due to its 32-29 win at Lumen Field back in Week 5, but one play from the closing stages has just been drudged up again. One of the pivotal moments of the game (well, at least after the fact) was Jaxon Smith-Njigba getting rocked on an incomplete pass by 49ers safety Malik Mustapha. No flag was thrown, otherwise Seattle would’ve been in game-tying field goal range. Mustapha was fined $6,998 for a hit on a defenseless receiver , which can be subject to appeal… Wow. The NFL fined 49ers safety Malik Mustapha for a "hit on a defenseless player." More specifically, the hit on JSN on Seattle's final drive. A penalty would've put the Seahawks in game-tying field goal range. pic.twitter.com/1DCt4NiTVs — Mookie Alexander (@mookiealexander) October 17, 2026 …Well, Mustapha won the appeal. Upon appeal, the NFL rescinded the $6,998 fine it assessed to 49ers S Malik Mustapha for this hit earlier in the season on Seahawks WR Jaxon Smith-Njigba. Jordy Nelson was the hearing officer. The 49ers and Seahawks play again Sunday. pic.twitter.com/S0IU2KwFiw — Adam Schefter (@AdamSchefter) November 24, 2026 Rescinding the fine also presumably means rescinding the first of three strikes for Mustapha toward a suspension. Three violations of certain offenses would result in an automatic one-game ban, so Mustapha’s strike is taken off the board. Mustapha also had a heavy collision with Rashid Shaheed which drew neither a flag nor a fine. Anybody else beyond impressed with #49ers S Malik Mustapha yesterday? He reminds me of @thehawk38 & @DonteWhitner ! I believe the reason JSN dropped that ball on 3rd down, is cause Mustapha was laying them out, all damn day 🤣 pic.twitter.com/int1dDMlDw — 49ers & NFL News 24/7 (@49ersSportsTalk) October 12, 2026 That’s one way to stoke some more rage heading into a must-win rivalry game!

full_text: (Photo by Timothy T Ludwig/Getty Images) | Getty Images A day after veteran tackle Bobby Hart was signed to the 53-man roster , the Seattle Seahawks have added another offensive lineman to the roster. The team signed tackle Chase Lundt off the Buffalo Bills’ practice squad, The Ringer ’s Tom Pelissero reported on Tuesday. In a corresponding move, cornerback Avery Smith was waived by the Seahawks. The Seahawks are signing OT Chase Lundt off the Bills practice squad, per source. To make room, Seattle is waiving CB Avery Smith. — Tom Pelissero (@TomPelissero) November 24, 2026 The 26-year-old Lundt was a sixth-round pick of the Bills in the 2025 NFL Draft, and played two games in a rookie season spent on their active roster. After he was waived during roster cuts ahead of the 2026 season, he was signed to their practice squad where he had remained until Tuesday. A four-year starter at UConn, Lundt was a collegiate teammate of former Seattle guard Christian Haynes, now of the Miami Dolphins. Lundt and Hart both joining the roster appear to be insurance for right tackle Abe Lucas, who is dealing with an ankle injury and is a question mark for Week 12 against the San Francisco 49ers. Smith’s departure from the Seahawks comes a day after veteran Trevon Diggs, like Hart, was signed to the active roster off the practice squad. The 22-year-old appeared in six games with Seattle after the team acquired him from the L.A. Chargers for a sixth-round pick ahead of the regular season . After moving a 2027 day-three selection in order to acquire Smith just a few months ago, the Seahawks will presumably be interested in signing him to their practice squad, should he clear waivers.

title: 49ers injury report: Brock Purdy suffered an ankle injury
summary: The San Francisco 49ers have a huge division matchup with the Seattle Seahawks on Sunday, and 49ers head coach Kyle Shanahan took the podium to update the media on injuries and player statuses heading into the game. The obvious news is that right tackle Colton McKivitz is placed on injured reserve, but the big news […]
full_text: (Photo by Manuel Velasquez/Getty Images) | Getty Images The San Francisco 49ers have a huge division matchup with the Seattle Seahawks on Sunday, and 49ers head coach Kyle Shanahan took the podium to update the media on injuries and player statuses heading into the game. The obvious news is that right tackle Colton McKivitz is placed on injured reserve , but the big news is Brock Purdy’s ankle injury, which happened in the second quarter of Sunday night’s win over the Vikings in Mexico City. Shanahan said Purdy won’t practice on Wednesday with the ankle injury, and he was aware of the injury during the game on Sunday night. When asked if there was any concern about the injury moving forward, Shanahan said: “We’ll see.” The injury happened in the second quarter against the Vikings, and Shanahan said it didn’t affect his play in the game and was checked out and deemed “fine.” Shanahan said it’s possible he won’t go on Sunday, but the injury isn’t a high ankle injury, and Purdy will be day-to-day. It’s hard to diagnose how the week will progress or take anything from Shanahan’s statement, which was very matter-of-fact. For now, fans will have to take the news as it comes, but shouldn’t panic that Purdy will miss on Sunday. The other updates were that Deommodore Lenoir, Upton Stout, Austen Pleasants, and Carver Willis were limited today in practice with different ailments. Dre Greenlaw and Siran Neal both missed today’s practice. Shanahan was asked about Vederian Lowe and stated that he will be the new starter at right tackle, and Pleasants has actually been healthy for a few weeks and, with the obvious situation, will be activated to the roster. Lowe was praised by Shanahan, who said he played really well, especially against Minnesota, and this situation is why he was brought in as the swing tackle. Pleasants has a chance to be activated and serve as the swing tackle moving forward. The 49ers are an injury away from rookie Enrique Cruz taking the field. Pleasants would give the team a veteran presence.

full_text: (Photo by Justin Edmonds/Getty Images) | Getty Images The San Francisco 49ers announced a couple of transactions on Wednesday. The 49ers activated cornerback Nate Hobbs from the injured reserve list. The 49ers needed to make the move, or Hobbs’ season would have ended because his practice window had closed. Where Hobbs fits in will be worth monitoring. Throughout his career, Hobbs has rarely played special teams. Unless he’s part of Raheem Morris’s sub packages or rotating with one of the cornerbacks, Hobbs’s main role with the 49ers would be on special teams. The corresponding move was to place right tackle Colton McKivitz on the injured reserve. The 49ers also brought back wide receiver Brandin Cooks to the practice squad. Cooks joins Khadarel Hodge, Will Pauling, and Wesley Grimes on the practice squad at receiver. Given his veteran experience, it makes you wonder whether the 49ers will lean on Cooks come playoff time. Perhaps in an emergency situation, if one of the younger players slips up over the next month and a half.

title: Why the first matchup between the 49ers and Seahawks was so strange
summary: The San Francisco 49ers defeated the Seattle Seahawks in Week 5, 32-29. To say it was a strange game is an understatement. It was also thrilling and exhilarating. Wins are wins in the NFL, but this win was particularly odd given how it played out. The 49ers’ defensive line was excellent. The secondary was exceptional. […]
full_text: (Photo by Steph Chambers/Getty Images) The San Francisco 49ers defeated the Seattle Seahawks in Week 5, 32-29. To say it was a strange game is an understatement. It was also thrilling and exhilarating. Wins are wins in the NFL, but this win was particularly odd given how it played out. The 49ers’ defensive line was excellent. The secondary was exceptional. The offense converted in the red zone, as they have done so effectively this season. So, what made this game so odd? Despite the score, this was the highest-scoring defensive struggle I may have ever seen. How can you call it a defensive struggle with over 60 total points? Let me explain. The 49ers scored a touchdown on a George Holani fumble before halftime. The Seahawks scored points on the back of a Jacob Cowing muffed punt. Deebo Samuel popped his hamstring and fell flat on his face, and the ball came loose for another turnover on the plus side of the field for Seattle. In fact, the initial touchdown for the 49ers started with a Renardo Green interception deep in Seattle’s territory. Now, the reason I point this out is that turnovers were the story of this game. Seattle’s offense likely doesn’t score much without turnovers. The 49ers certainly capitalized on their turnovers, and the biggest drive of the game was a drive that started from the Seattle 26 in the fourth quarter, which was punctuated by a seven-yard touchdown catch by Brandin Cooks. The reason I point all these things out is that it’s hard to expect this type of scenario and, at times, sloppiness from both teams again. Turnovers will be a major part of the story on Sunday as Sam Darnold returns, and if he continues the trend of turning the football over, it will hinder Seattle’s chances. With Darnold as the quarterback, the only stretch of football he has played without turning the football over was from Week 18 (against SF) through the playoffs with a Super Bowl win. That’s a four-game stretch. I’m willing to bet he’s going to make some mistakes on Sunday. Seattle’s defense is still elite, in a much different way than Minnesota is, but if turnovers happen and Seattle is backed up defending their own end zone, that’s a recipe for success for the 49ers. Week 5 was filled with chaos and jaw-dropping scenarios. I expect Sunday to be far more composed and just as tight a matchup.

title: Brandon Aiyuk joins the Commanders’ practice squad
summary: The least surprising transaction to happen on Tuesday was former San Francisco 49ers wide receiver Brandon Aiyuk visiting the Washington Commanders. While Aiyuk has yet to sign officially, it was a move that was the most predictable outcome. The Commanders need a wideout. Former 49ers general manager Adam Peters now runs the show in Washington. […]
full_text: (Photo by Brooke Sutton/Getty Images) | Getty Images The least surprising transaction to happen on Tuesday was former San Francisco 49ers wide receiver Brandon Aiyuk visiting the Washington Commanders. While Aiyuk has yet to sign officially, it was a move that was the most predictable outcome. The Commanders need a wideout. Former 49ers general manager Adam Peters now runs the show in Washington. Aiyuk’s college quarterback, Jayden Daniels, just so happens to be under center in DC. During a radio appearance on Wednesday, Peters called Aiyuk one of the “hardest workers on the team” when he was with the 49ers. “One of the things that I don’t think anyone can dispute is his work ethic. That’s how he became an All-Pro-type player. He was a true No. 1 receiver at the time. He’s a guy who’s a tough cover; he’s great after the catch. There’s a lot of great things about him on the field. It wasn’t just that he was the most gifted guy; he’s self-made too. There’s a lot of positives.” The caveat “on the field” is doing a lot of work here. While the 49ers may have had some buyer’s remorse after his injury, Aiyuk put on a clinic of what not to do for the past year and a half. That’s why he was released . Peters, who hasn’t spoken to Aiyuk in “a couple years,” continued. “I can’t speak on all what happened between him and the 49ers. What I do remember is he’s a very motivated player.” Maybe there was no resolution to be had. But you’d think if Aiyuk had any kind of motivation left, he would’ve swallowed his pride and gone to work for the team with the best record in the conference. Doesn’t winning on the big stage have to mean something? Again, there was likely no coming back from whatever the “situation” was, but Aiyuk had every reason to be motivated last year, when we saw him running routes in August in a preseason game with the team. Then, as the year went along, a No. 1 receiver never emerged. Aiyuk could’ve been the top target for a playoff team. The motivation is different now. It’s been two years since Aiyuk played in the NFL. Unless he’s training against NFL defensive backs on the side, he hasn’t gone against the best competition in the world since a season-ending knee injury. Expecting anything close to the 1,300-yard receiver feels like a long shot. We’ll keep a close eye on whether Aiyuk signs to Washington’s practice squad and where the two sides go from there, but this story is far from over. Kyle’s update, 10:00 am PT : ESPN’s Adam Schefter tweeted that Aiyuk finished up his visit with the Commanders, but there won’t be a deal today. Here’s Schefter’s quote from Drew Rosenhaus: “Discussions are ongoing and positive. Probably no decision today.” Aka, we could not agree on terms today. Kyle’s update, 10:20 am PT: So much for that. About twenty minutes later, Aiyuk is joining the Commanders’ practice squad. Free-agent WR Brandon Aiyuk is signing with the Washington Commanders practice squad, per his agent Drew Rosenhaus. Aiyuk once again becomes teammates with his Commanders QB Jayden Daniels. pic.twitter.com/jt8diY95o3 — Adam Schefter (@AdamSchefter) November 25, 2026
author: Kyle Posey

title: Malik Mustapha wins his appeal; NFL rescinds fine for hit on Jaxon Smith-Njigba
summary: Over a month ago, when the San Francisco 49ers were in Seattle, the NFL fined safety Malik Mustapha for a “hit on a defenseless player.” It was on the final drive of the game that Mustapha hit Jaxon-Smith Njigba. Raheem Morris calls it the “strike zone,” which is above the belt and below the neck. […]
full_text: (Photo by Stacy Revere/Getty Images) | Getty Images Over a month ago, when the San Francisco 49ers were in Seattle, the NFL fined safety Malik Mustapha for a “hit on a defenseless player.” It was on the final drive of the game that Mustapha hit Jaxon-Smith Njigba. Raheem Morris calls it the “strike zone,” which is above the belt and below the neck. That’s where Mustapha hit JSN, yet the NFL still felt the need to step in. The league fined Mustapha $6,998. Mustapha will be happy to get those funds back. More importantly, from the 49ers’ perspective, it means Mustapha no longer has one strike to his name. This year, three violations of specific offenses equal a one-game suspension. Upon appeal, the NFL rescinded the $6,998 fine it assessed to 49ers S Malik Mustapha for this hit earlier in the season on Seahawks WR Jaxon Smith-Njigba. Jordy Nelson was the hearing officer. The 49ers and Seahawks play again Sunday. pic.twitter.com/S0IU2KwFiw — Adam Schefter (@AdamSchefter) November 24, 2026 Mustapha came close against the Cowboys. The kind of force Mustapha plays with, he’ll always come close to what’s deemed “unnecessary” in today’s NFL. So, getting one strike back could pay dividends in the second half of the season. Back in Week 5, Mustapha had another collision where he de-cleated Rashid Shaheed. It was clean and in the strike zone, but a lot of these flags, and eventually penalties, stem from the result or how a player peels himself off the turf. There were a couple of those in Week 5. Malik should not change who he is. He made a difference the last time these two teams met. Hopefully, he won’t be fined for tackling again.

title: Cut the Grass: After Mexico City, the 49ers Get Back to Work in the NFC West
summary: On December 1, 2001, my Bowie High School team beat Eleanor Roosevelt 23-6 at Byrd Stadium for the first state championship in school history. We were the sixth seed. Roosevelt was undefeated and had beaten us in September. They had won nine straight against us, going back to 1994. We scored the first 23 points. […]
full_text: On December 1, 2001, my Bowie High School team beat Eleanor Roosevelt 23-6 at Byrd Stadium for the first state championship in school history. We were the sixth seed. Roosevelt was undefeated and had beaten us in September. They had won nine straight against us, going back to 1994. We scored the first 23 points. When it was over, one of my teammates walked off that field with a plastic bag full of grass—a souvenir. I got home late that night. My parents were proud, but they kept it simple: Be safe, and be home when we wake up. The next morning, I was in church. I even got a shout-out from the pulpit. And that afternoon, I was in the yard cutting the grass, because the playoff run had put me behind on my chores. Took me years to understand it, but the trophy and the lawnmower were the same lesson. The habits that won the championship were the same ones that had me cutting grass the next day. Sunday night in Mexico City was the 49ers’ championship night. A 35-10 win over the best defense in football, in prime time, on an international stage. By Monday, they were Super Bowl favorites, and Brock Purdy’s MVP odds had jumped from +400 to +210. Then Kyle Shanahan was asked if this is the best team he’s coached in San Francisco. “No, but it’s still early,” he said. “We’ve got to earn that.” Now it’s back to the yard. It’s been 49 days since the 49ers played a division game, and the last one took just about everything they had. Seven turnovers between the two teams. Six lead changes. The 49ers hadn’t scored a touchdown against Seattle in more than eight quarters until Mike Evans caught a 2-yarder less than four minutes in. Renardo Green picked off Sam Darnold twice. Fred Warner punched a ball loose, Malik Mustapha fell on it, and Christian McCaffrey scored on the next snap. With 13 seconds left in the half, G-Baby, rookie Gracen Halton, stripped George Holani and recovered it in the end zone. Then Seattle scored 13 straight in the third quarter, and the 49ers had to go get it. Down 26-21, they went 74 yards in 12 plays, and Evans caught a 28-yarder on second-and-21 to set up the go-ahead touchdown. The winning field goal came at the end of a drive built on five runs for 36 yards, and Seattle’s last shot died when Cooper Kupp came up short on fourth-and-10 at midfield. That’s what the division looks like. Ugly, physical, and decided by inches. And the 49ers walking into Levi’s on Sunday aren’t the same team that left Seattle. G-Baby broke his ankle against the Raiders. Right tackle Colton McKivitz is out for the year, and Vederian Lowe, who has played 1,415 career snaps at left tackle and only 276 on the right, takes his place. Nick Bosa missed that first meeting, and DeForest Buckner was still a Colt. Both are back. Purdy has gone 43-for-54 with six touchdowns and no interceptions in his last two games, and the offense has averaged 32.4 points since that trip to Seattle. The Seahawks are different, too. They’re 3-2 since they held Kansas City and Arizona to three points apiece, and they’re coming off a bye. They also ended the 49ers’ season twice last year, 13-3 in Week 18 and 41-6 in the playoffs. “Everyone knows how good of a team we have ahead of us coming off a bye,” Shanahan said. This team has climbed to the Super Bowl twice under Shanahan and come home empty both times. They know what a championship night is worth when you don’t finish the job. Mexico City was the championship night. Sunday is the morning after, and the yard’s waiting.
author: The Coach

title: Brandon Aiyuk clears waivers, to visit Commanders on Wednesday
summary: Former San Francisco 49ers wide receiver Brandon Aiyuk cleared waivers on Tuesday morning after being waived by the team this weekend, and it looks like he’s already got his eyes on his next destination. Aiyuk is now scheduled to visit with the Washington Commanders this Wednesday, per ESPN’s Adam Schefter, as he looks to find […]
full_text: Former San Francisco 49ers wide receiver Brandon Aiyuk cleared waivers on Tuesday morning after being waived by the team this weekend, and it looks like he’s already got his eyes on his next destination. Aiyuk is now scheduled to visit with the Washington Commanders this Wednesday, per ESPN’s Adam Schefter, as he looks to find a new home soon. The Commanders have long been the destination linked to Aiyuk the most, given his relationship with quarterback Jayden Daniels stemming from their time at Arizona State. There is a clear void there for him to fill, as the Commanders, who beat the Cincinnati Bengals on Monday night to improve to 4-5-1, will be without star receiver Terry McLaurin for the rest of the season. If all pans out, Aiyuk could potentially be the team’s ‘X’ wide receiver opposite Antonio Williams, with Stefon Diggs in the slot. However, the Commanders aren’t the only team interested in Aiyuk, according to Schefter, who tweeted that the wide receiver “is expected to draw interest from a few teams, including the Washington Commanders, and would like to sign soon.” Aiyuk has bought a home in the Washington area, so the Commanders obviously seem like the clearest fit. Other potential teams that could logically make sense also include the Pittsburgh Steelers or even the Seattle Seahawks. The 49ers saga with Aiyuk is now officially over, and it looks like he’s going to play this season on another team.

title: Week 12 NFL Power Rankings: Did the Vikings blowout move the 49ers up to No. 1?
summary: The San Francisco 49ers routed the Minnesota Vikings 35-10 on Sunday Night Football in Mexico City, improving to 9-1 as they retained control of the No. 1 seed in the NFC. In a battle between the No. 1 offense and the No. 1 defense in the NFL, the 49ers were well-prepared and came out firing […]
full_text: The San Francisco 49ers routed the Minnesota Vikings 35-10 on Sunday Night Football in Mexico City, improving to 9-1 as they retained control of the No. 1 seed in the NFC. In a battle between the No. 1 offense and the No. 1 defense in the NFL, the 49ers were well-prepared and came out firing in one of their most complete performances of the season. Last week, in the Week 11 NFL Power Rankings, the 49ers were between No. 1 and No. 2 on most major outlets with the Buffalo Bills, who won once again this week, beating the Miami Dolphins 26-9 to improve to 9-1 as well. Buffalo had beaten Minnesota 23-6 earlier this month on primetime. Will the 49ers dominant win sway opinions this week, or will the status quo remain the same? Let’s see where San Francisco falls in the Week 12 power rankings. ESPN: No. 1 The 49ers moved up to No. 1 in last week’s ESPN NFL power rankings, as they beat the Cowboys while the Bills were on bye. They remained there this week, while the Bills stayed at No. 2. Behind them, the Kansas City Chiefs jumped from No. 5 to No. 3 after their beatdown of the Arizona Cardinals. The Chicago Bears stayed at No. 4 on their bye week, while the Denver Broncos jumped from No. 7 to No. 5 with a 14-point win over the Raiders. Just missing out on the top five were the Detroit Lions, who jumped four spots from No. 10 to No. 6 after beating the Tampa Bay Buccaneers by 10. NFL.com: No. 1 The 49ers moved up to No. 1 last week in the NFL’s Week 11 power rankings and stayed there this week following the win over the Vikings. “Of the 49ers’ nine victories in 10 games, this rout of the Vikings was undoubtedly their most impressive,” NFL.com’s Nick Shook wrote. “Brock Purdy knew when to get rid of the ball and where to throw it against a Minnesota defense that had caused problems for every other quarterback it faced, delivering a pristine performance on the Sunday night stage in Mexico City. “Mike Evans’ return upgraded this offense and came at the perfect time, and San Francisco’s defense is quietly becoming a bit of a monster up front thanks to the return of some previously injured members and the deadline addition of DeForest Buckner. This is unquestionably the best team in football through 11 weeks.” The Bills remained at No. 2, followed by the Broncos (who jumped up four spots), the Chiefs (who jumped up five spots), and the Lions (who jumped up three spots). Yahoo Sports: No. 1 The 49ers jumped up from No. 2 to No. 1 on these power rankings after their win over the Vikings, as the Jacksonville Jaguars fell from No. 1 to No. 4. “The 49ers have faced the No. 1 defense in DVOA (Seattle) and the No. 1 defense in EPA allowed per play (Minnesota),” Yahoo’s Frank Schwab wrote. “They scored 32 points against the Seahawks and 35 against the Vikings. They got a defensive touchdown in each game but it seems like no defense can hold down the 49ers this season. “While the offense has been fantastic, the 49ers wouldn’t be the best team in football through Week 11 without their defense, which has excelled despite Nick Bosa not having a sack all season (he did have two quarterback hits on Sunday night). The 49ers have given up 17 or fewer points in six of their 10 games. They have given up fewer than 300 yards in six games too. Defensive coordinator Raheem Morris, who replaced Robert Saleh, is doing an excellent job.” Following the 49ers were the Bills, Bears, Jaguars, and Chiefs in the top five. CBS Sports: No. 2 There was no movement on Pete Prisco’s power rankings once again, as the Bills stayed at No. 1, while the No. 2 remained at No. 2. “They are clearly the team to beat in the NFC and maybe the league. They get better each and every week. The loss of right tackle Colton McKivitz will be felt,” Prisco wrote. The Bears, Broncos, and Chiefs rounded out the top five, with each moving up one spot as the Jaguars fell from No. 3 to No. 8. Bleacher Report: No. 1 The Vikings win moved the 49ers up from No. 2 to No. 1 here, with the Bills falling. “Sunday night’s Mexico City beatdown was a statement win in every way—chief among them the statement that the 49ers are the NFL’s best team,” Bleacher Report’s Gary Davenport wrote. “This was supposed to be a titanic showdown between two of the NFC’s top teams. The Niners apparently didn’t get that memo, because they took control immediately and never gave Minnesota a chance to recover. On the first drive of the game, it took San Francisco less than four minutes to drive the length of the field on one of the NFL’s best defenses. Just before halftime a pick-six by the 49ers defense put the game on ice. “Brock Purdy is the NFL’s MVP after 11 weeks. Given all the injuries the team has had to endure on both sides of the ball, Kyle Shanahan is the Coach of the Year.” Here, the Bears, Broncos, and Chiefs rounded out the top five as well.

title: 49ers vs. Seahawks odds: Points could be at a premium  in this game
summary: Good teams win. Great teams cover. The San Francisco 49ers have won and covered with relative ease in the three games since the bye. No victory was more impressive than dropping 35 points against the NFL’s best defense. After riding high on three straight victories, the Niners host their rivals, the Seattle Seahawks, off a […]
full_text: Photo by Robin Alam/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Good teams win. Great teams cover. The San Francisco 49ers have won and covered with relative ease in the three games since the bye. No victory was more impressive than dropping 35 points against the NFL’s best defense. Faithful, take 49ers game day wherever you go! Stay connected to the action and share every reaction with fellow 49ers fans on the SB Nation app. Join the live game-day chat Browse with fewer ads Seamlessly jump between communities Enjoy faster commenting and posting Download the SB Nation app on iOS or Android . After riding high on three straight victories, the Niners host their rivals, the Seattle Seahawks, off a bye. Head coach Mike Macdonald said he expects Sam Darnold to start. Darnold hasn’t played since Week 8. Seattle covered in back-to-back games with Drew Lock under center. The defense did the heavy lifting, allowing three and 13 points against the Cardinals and Raiders, respectively. Going back to the Week 5 matchup between these two teams, Seattle was a three-point favorite, and the game total was set at 47. That game went over the total by two touchdowns. Plenty of people will expect a higher-scoring affair, but a 32-29 score couldn’t be further from what transpired defensively in that game. The 49ers had their worst offensive performance of the season. They finished with an EPA per play in the 27th percentile, a success rate in the 47th percentile, a yards per play in the 32nd percentile, an explosive play rate in the 41st percentile, and a third-down success rate in the 26th percentile. And they were still the best offense in that game. Darnold and the Seahawks had a fifth-percentile EPA per play and a fourth-percentile success rate. They didn’t generate big plays or convert on third downs. So, despite a 62-point outburst in Week 5 and the Niners scoring in recent weeks, the total is lower than it was the last time these two teams met. FanDuel Sportsbook has set the total at 45.5, with the Niners favored by 3 points. The Vikings have a reputation for having the best defense in the league, but we still think it’s the Seahawks. They have the best success rate and are fourth in EPA per play. It’s the talent and where they can hurt you that make it a difficult matchup for San Francisco. Their stout defensive line and legitimate first-rounders across the board mean every offensive lineman will be tested. Right tackle Vederian Lowe will make his first start. In Week 5, Colton McKivitz led the offensive line with five impact plays. He has a pass-block win rate of 97% and only missed two blocks all game. Lowe has big shoes to fill. Seattle had zero answers for Mike Evans. Josh Jobe probably feels the variance battle will go his way this time. Even if Evans doesn’t have another superhero drive, weapons like Keenan Allen and Jordan Watkins exist. On the other side of the ball, Nick Bosa and DeForest Buckner didn’t play in Week 5. Buckner gets to face his old teammate, Quenton Nelson, while Bosa gets an advantageous matchup against Seattle’s tackles. In the first contest, the Niners defensive line created 13 havoc plays, sacked Darnold five times, hit him eight times, and broke up five of his passes while intercepting two. We’re not sure if the forced fumbles are repeatable, but the pressure should lead to turnovers and negative plays. Last week was supposed to be the “game of the year.” Week 5 was, and this will be the sequel.

title: Grading the Titans’ rookie class vs. Cowboys in Week 11
summary: Three rookies played extensively for the Tennessee Titans versus the Dallas Cowboys in Week 11. They were Mike Borgonzi’s first three picks in the 2026 NFL Draft: WR Carnell Tate, DE Keldric Faulk, and LB Anthony Hill Jr. After reviewing the tape, we’re grading how they performed in Sunday’s embarrassing 51-30 loss. WR Carnell Tate […]
full_text: NASHVILLE, TENNESSEE - AUGUST 23: Carnell Tate #14 of the Tennessee Titans warms up prior to Week 2 of the preseason game against the Seattle Seahawks at Nissan Stadium on August 23, 2026 in Nashville, Tennessee. (Photo by Johnnie Izquierdo/Getty Images) | Getty Images Three rookies played extensively for the Tennessee Titans versus the Dallas Cowboys in Week 11 . They were Mike Borgonzi’s first three picks in the 2026 NFL Draft: WR Carnell Tate, DE Keldric Faulk, and LB Anthony Hill Jr. After reviewing the tape, we’re grading how they performed in Sunday’s embarrassing 51-30 loss. WR Carnell Tate Titans rookie receiver Carnell Tate returned to the lineup following a two-game absence due to a shoulder injury. The fourth overall pick recorded two receptions for 58 yards and a touchdown. What’s even funnier is that his TD was a 59-yard catch. Tate’s touchdown was an excellent example of situational awareness. He realized he went untouched on a short slant route from Cam Ward, stood up and rumbled 40+ yards for a TD. Tate also had 1-2 drops, but overall it was a positive performance in his return. GRADE: B- DE Keldric Faulk Titans head coach Robert Saleh wanted to play rookie defensive end Keldric Faulk in an expanded role versus the Cowboys. That didn’t necessarily happen, and for good reason. Faulk ended up matching his 24 snaps from the previous week (Jacksonville Jaguars, Week 10). Faulk was flagged for being offside twice against the Cowboys. The former Auburn standout didn’t register a single quarterback pressure, had one assisted tackle, and wasn’t credited with a run-game stop either. It continues being an extremely frustrating rookie season for Faulk, who was rightfully described as raw coming out of Auburn. GRADE: F LB Anthony Hill Jr. Rookie linebacker Anthony Hill Jr. also returned to the lineup following a one-week absence due to a neck injury. Sunday’s performance versus the Cowboys wasn’t his finest showing. Hill only had six combined tackles, his second-fewest of the season. Cowboys quarterback Dak Prescott also routinely abused Hill (and Cedric Gray) in pass coverage. Pro Football Focus credited Hill with allowing three receptions (on three targets) for 63 yards. The rookie linebacker is still a building block for Saleh’s defense, but his Cowboys showing was forgettable. GRADE: C-

full_text: It’s a short week for the Washington Commanders after Monday night’s big home win over the Cincinnati Bengals. They’re also traveling to Arizona this week to take on the Cardinals, making the week even more condensed for players, coaches, and the media. Dan Quinn held a virtual call with reporters for Victory Tuesday, and is back in front of the microphones today for his weekly Wednesday presser before the team hits the practice fields. The big news of the day was former 49ers WR Brandon Aiyuk visiting the team and reportedly signing to the team’s practice squad. Its been a long, strange trip for Aiyuk to get freed from the Niners to reunite with his college QB Jayden Daniels. Quinn is excited to add a talented player, and he’s looking forward to getting to know his new receiver. Aiyuk has not played in the NFL since 2023 when he suffered a serious knee injury. title: Washington Commanders reportedly sign Brandon Aiyuk to practice squad
summary: The Commanders have signed receiver Brandon Aiyuk to their practice squad, ESPN’s Adam Schefter reported on Wednesday.   The free agent, who was released by the San Francisco 49ers and formally cleared waivers, met with the Commanders at the team’s complex on Wednesday. Per Schefter, Aiyuk signed contract to join the team’s practice squad.   This move […]
full_text: The Commanders have signed receiver Brandon Aiyuk to their practice squad, ESPN’s Adam Schefter reported on Wednesday. The free agent, who was released by the San Francisco 49ers and formally cleared waivers, met with the Commanders at the team’s complex on Wednesday . Per Schefter, Aiyuk signed contract to join the team’s practice squad. Free-agent WR Brandon Aiyuk is signing with the Washington Commanders practice squad, per his agent Drew Rosenhaus. Aiyuk once again becomes teammates with his Commanders QB Jayden Daniels. pic.twitter.com/jt8diY95o3 — Adam Schefter (@AdamSchefter) November 25, 2026 This move was telegraphed somewhat, with the Tuesday release of running back Craig Reynolds to open up a spot. Aiyuk will have an opportunity to work himself back into game shape after more than two years on the shelf. The Commanders can elevate him when ready, or they can sign him to the active roster at a time of their choosing. He can be elevated three times before Washington has to formally activate him. Washington has been Aiyuk’s preferred destination, a point that was clear when he started wearing Commanders gear in social media posts over the summer. Some quick background: The 49ers drafted Aiyuk in the first round back in 2020 and then inked him to a four-year, $120-million contract in 2024. Then things got messy. Aiyuk suffered a serious knee injury during the 2024 campaign and didn’t play after that. The 49ers took issue with Aiyuk’s choice to rehab away from their facility, and it created a schism and a rift that was never repaired. The 49ers voided Aiyuk’s guarantees and placed him on the exempt/did not report list. Then Aiyuk went on a social media tirade, torching 49ers GM John Lynch and head coach Kyle Shanahan. He also took some shots at Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels – Aiyuk and Daniels were good friends and teammates at Arizona State – and his mother. They have reportedly mended fences, which set the stage for this signing. Commanders GM Adam Peters was also involved in the Aiyuk draft pick when he was in San Francisco. Aiyuk had 75 catches for 1,342 yards and seven touchdowns in 2023, shockingly his last full season in the NFL. There’s no doubting Aiyuk’s talent, though it has been some time since that has led to production. How long it takes for Aiyuk to get ready is to be determined, but Washington needs him to get prepared fast to keep this good thing going. It’s hard to imagine he’ll be ready for Sunday’s road game against the Arizona Cardinals, especially with his need to catch up learning the Commanders system. And there’s great shape and football shape, which are two totally different things. Let us know your thoughts about this Brandon Aiyuk signing in the article comments below:

title: For the first time in years, it’s fun to watch the Commanders play defense
summary: The Daily Slop – 25 November Editor’s note: Each day, Hogs Haven compiles a collection of articles, podcasts & tweets from around the web to keep you in touch with the Commanders, the NFC East, the NFL and sports in general, with a sprinkling of other stuff. full_text: The Daily Slop – 25 November Editor’s note: Each day, Hogs Haven compiles a collection of articles, podcasts & tweets from around the web to keep you in touch with the Commanders, the NFC East, the NFL and sports in general, with a sprinkling of other stuff. Enjoy! Commanders links Hail = Raised @SeatGeek | #RaiseHail pic.twitter.com/VS4c8jPbmU — Washington Commanders (@Commanders) November 24, 2026 Articles Bullock’s Film Room (subscription) Commanders Film Review: Defense vs Bengals This was a new Cover-0 look that I don’t recall seeing from Jones so far this season. Traditional Cover-0 is pure man-to-man coverage against all eligible receivers and no safety help in the middle, but this is almost like a three-deep zone variation of Cover-0. The Commanders put eight defenders on the line of scrimmage this time and all eight of them blitz. That leaves just three defenders in coverage as they effectively play the deep zones of Cover-3 behind the blitz. Burrow again looks to his top receiver in Ja’Marr Chase, but this time Chase is in the slot and spotting up as a hot route option. Burrow immediately pulls the trigger to avoid a sack and throws hot to Chase, but cornerback Rasul Douglas plays this perfectly. Douglas sits at the first down marker knowing the ball has to come out quick against the blitz. He knows Chase is Burrow’s go-to target and he spots Chase beginning to slow down and spot up underneath. So before Burrow even delivers the throw, Douglas begins breaking on the pass. This enables Douglas to arrive at Chase before the ball does and he goes over the top of him to nearly intercept the pass. The Commanders defense had an outstanding performance against the Bengals on Monday night. Daronte Jones stuck to his identity of aggressive blitzing and it paid off against one of the top offenses in the NFL. I broke it all down: https://t.co/Ro4PSrO3As pic.twitter.com/OuHITh0WH9 — Mark Bullock (@MarkBullockNFL) November 25, 2026 Unfortunately, Douglas drops the interception on what would have been an outstanding play by him. It goes back to what I said on the previous play, the Commanders biggest issue defensively is finishing plays when they have the opportunity. Douglas dropped three interceptions in this game and this was one of them. It was still a terrific read and great play by Douglas, but it could have been so much better had he come up with the ball. It’s a fun variation of Cover-0 because it’s not really Cover-0 when you have three zone defenders deep, but it also is Cover-0 because the Commanders only have three defenders in coverage. The Bengals had four receivers running routes so the Commanders were outnumbered in coverage, but that’s the risk you sometimes take to commit to the blitz and force a hurried throw underneath that can lead to interception opportunities. Jones stayed aggressive throughout the game, dialing up various blitzes that were all fairly effective. But it was Cover-0 that he came back to in the most critical moment. The Athletic (paywall) The Commanders defense was like a new language; they’re getting more fluent This mini-Commanders renaissance — three wins in four games, consecutive victories for the first time in 22 months — is due in no small part to a defense that was tasked with learning a new language in the offseason, and is only now able to think in that language without clumsily running it through a translator in their brains. The pauses are fewer. The flow is better. The results are coming. Witness: This is a defense that just held Joe Burrow and the absolutely steamrolling Cincinnati Bengals to an output below their season averages across the board. Early in the season, when Washington started 1-3-1, the Commanders allowed chunk plays in bunches —ranking 16th in the percentage of plays that went for at least 20 yards — and couldn’t sustain efforts through the second half. In this quasi-revival — a 3-2 stretch that includes an understandable, competitive loss at San Francisco — they have tackled better, gotten more consistent pressure on the quarterback and limited gash plays. What’s happening is clear. First-year coordinator Daronte Jones arrived in Washington from Minnesota — and you should check out the body of work by his old Vikings boss Brian Flores — with the task of building a new, more aggressive system from the ground up. The build takes time. But it’s happening. To read more of this article, CLICK HERE From Commanders Roundtable: Cincinnati entered Monday night converting an NFL second-best 51.9% on third down, yet Washington held them to just 4-of-12 (33.3%) on the night. Against an offense averaging 29.8 points per game, keeping the Bengals off the scoreboard for the first 21 minutes was a clear statement. Aside from two isolated explosive plays—a 44-yard catch-and-run by Samaje Perine late in the second quarter and a 31-yard touchdown strike to Higgins right before halftime—the Commanders kept a tight lid on every big-play threat Cincinnati threw at them. What looked like an outlier a month ago is rapidly becoming Washington’s identity. The Commanders have now held four consecutive opponents to 21 points or fewer—and they haven’t padded those numbers against bottom-feeders. That stretch includes offensive heavyweights in San Francisco, a healthy Los Angeles Rams squad, and now Cincinnati. Against a Cardinals offense ranked 29th in scoring (17.3 points per game), 25th in total yards, and carrying a steep -132 point differential, Jones’ group has a golden chance to keep rolling. To read more of this Commanders Roundtable article, CLICK HERE My SC4U video on the Commanders blitzing success vs Burrow. “Hey what does John look like on 3 hours sleep? oof. Get some beauty rest dude.” https://t.co/WGwK5JL1Qy — John Keim (@john_keim) November 25, 2026 Athlon Sports How Did Jayden Daniels Do in Week 11 vs. Bengals? Jayden Daniels spent most of Monday’s first half dodging Boye Mafe in the rain at Northwest Stadium, and the Washington Commanders went into the locker room trailing a Cincinnati Bengals team that had won five straight . By the end of the night, he had thrown for 289 yards, run for 55 more and needed only two throws to Antonio Williams to set up Drew Stevens’ winning kick in a 22-20 win . So how did he do? Slow start, strong finish. Daniels went 23 of 35 with no touchdown passes and no interceptions, a 91.2 passer rating and a 58.6 QBR, per ESPN’s box score . Those numbers undersell the second half, when Washington scored on six straight possessions for the first time in 48 years, according to ESPN’s John Keim . title: Commanders rookie Drew Stevens wins NFC Special Teams Player of the Week
summary: When the Washington Commanders lined up for a 26-yard field goal as time expired on Monday Night Football against the Cincinnati Bengals, I didn’t feel the usual knot in my stomach that has defined white-knuckle football in Washington for the better part of a decade. Watching undrafted rookie Drew Stevens line up his fifth kick […]
full_text: LANDOVER, MARYLAND- NOVEMBER 23: Drew Stevens #19 of the Washington Commanders celebrates kicking a game winning field goal after an NFL football game against the Cincinnati Bengals at Northwest Stadium on November 23, 2026 in Landover, Maryland. (Photo by Logan Bowles/Getty Images | Getty Images When the Washington Commanders lined up for a 26-yard field goal as time expired on Monday Night Football against the Cincinnati Bengals, I didn’t feel the usual knot in my stomach that has defined white-knuckle football in Washington for the better part of a decade. Watching undrafted rookie Drew Stevens line up his fifth kick of the night, I had total confidence he was going to split the uprights. As it turned out, my confidence was well-placed. Stevens drilled the game-winner to seal a 22-20 Week 11 victory, and the NFL officially recognized his primetime clinic by naming him the NFC Special Teams Player of the Week . K Drew Stevens has been named NFC Special Teams Player of the Week after going 5-for-5 on field goals and 1-for-1 on extra point attempts in Monday Night's win over the Bengals. Stevens becomes the first rookie kicker in franchise history to earn NFC Player of the Week honors. pic.twitter.com/tdMLhL00S8 — Commanders PR (@Wash_PR) November 25, 2026 Stevens’ honor is the first of his young NFL career and makes him the first Washington player to take home the weekly award since Austin Seibert did it back in Week 2 of the 2024 season. More importantly, it validates what we saw on the field Monday night: a rookie who simply refuses to blink when the lights are brightest. Against Cincinnati, Washington’s offense moved the ball well—piling up 428 total yards—but repeatedly stalled once it crossed into Bengals territory, going just 1-for-4 in the red zone. Whenever a drive bogged down, Dan Quinn called on Stevens, and the 22-year-old out of Iowa answered every single time. He finished a perfect 5-for-5 on field goals (connecting from 36, 40, 25, 41, and 26 yards) and 1-for-1 on extra points, accounting for 16 of Washington’s 22 points. His 41-yarder tested his nerve against swirling wind, while his final 26-yard chip shot carried all the pressure of a walk-off winner after rookie receiver Antonio Williams made two clutch late catches to set up the attempt. With that performance, Stevens etched his name into the franchise record books twice in one night: Single-Game Rookie Record: He became the first rookie in Washington history to make five or more field goals in a single game. Season Milestone: He became the first rookie kicker in franchise history to reach 22 made field goals in a season since Charlie Gogolak in 1966—and Stevens did it in just 10 games. To truly appreciate how refreshing this is, you have to remember the seemingly endless kicking carousel Washington fans have endured. Since moving on from Dustin Hopkins, the franchise has cycled through roughly a dozen kickers—from Joey Slye and Cade York to Austin Seibert, Zane Gonzalez, Greg Joseph, Matt Gay, and Jake Moody. Whether it was Seibert’s 2024 hip and hamstring injuries derailing a promising start, Gay’s struggles in 2025, or persistent inconsistency on long-range kicks, special teams stability at the position remained elusive. Even entering training camp this summer, the job was up for grabs until Stevens decisively outkicked Moody (going 43-of-48 in camp compared to Moody’s 36-of-47) to claim the spot. After starting his NFL career 3-of-5 through his first two games—with all three of his season’s misses coming from 50-plus yards—Stevens has caught fire. He has now connected on 19 of his last 20 field goal attempts, bringing his season mark to an impressive 22-of-25 (88%) with a long of 57 yards. For years, every fourth-down decision inside the opponent’s 35-yard line felt like a roll of the dice in Ashburn. Now, with a poised, big-legged rookie who already owns franchise records and a Player of the Week trophy ( and a Rookie of the Week nomination ) before Thanksgiving, Washington finally appears to have found its long-term answer at kicker. Next up for Stevens and the 4-5-1 Commanders is a Week 12 road trip to face the Arizona Cardinals—and for the first time in a long time, fans can watch field goal units jog onto the field without holding their breath.
