title: Commanders’ Antonio Williams, Drew Stevens up for Rookie of the Week
summary: If you watched Monday night’s wild 22–20 upset over the Cincinnati Bengals — and who didn’t? — you already know about the two rookies who carried the Washington Commanders to victory with contributions throughout the game, and in particular, on the final drive. Now, the rest of the league is officially recognizing it too. On […]
full_text: If you watched Monday night’s wild 22–20 upset over the Cincinnati Bengals — and who didn’t? — you already know about the two rookies who carried the Washington Commanders to victory with contributions throughout the game, and in particular, on the final drive. Now, the rest of the league is officially recognizing it too. On Wednesday, the NFL announced the four nominees for the Week 11 Pepsi NFL Rookie of the Week award, and half the ballot belongs to the burgundy and gold. Wide receiver Antonio Williams and kicker Drew Stevens both earned nods alongside Denver Broncos running back Jonah Coleman and Kansas City Chiefs running back Emmett Johnson. For a franchise that spent far too many years wondering where its next wave of young playmakers would come from, having two rookies headline a primetime Monday Night Football victory—and immediately land on the league’s weekly ballot—is about as encouraging as it gets! Who should be the @pepsi Rookie of the Week for Week 11? Vote in the poll below! pic.twitter.com/pf82HR075i — NFL (@NFL) November 24, 2026 @Broncos | @Chiefs | @Commanders | @pepsi — NFL (@NFL) November 24, 2026 A familiar spotlight for Antonio Williams If Williams’ name looks familiar on the Pepsi ballot, that is because he has already taken home the hardware once this season. Back in Week 1 against the Philadelphia Eagles, the third-round draft pick introduced himself to the NFL by catching all four of his targets for 64 yards and a fourth-quarter touchdown, winning the fan vote right out of the gate. Ten weeks later, with Terry McLaurin sidelined for the season and Washington desperately needing someone to step into the void, Williams delivered what head coach Dan Quinn called his best performance yet. Against Cincinnati on Monday night, the 22-year-old led all receivers with nine catches for 122 yards—setting new franchise rookie records for both receptions and receiving yards on a Monday night. None of those yards mattered more than the final 64. After Evan McPherson’s 56-yard field goal gave Cincinnati a 20–19 lead with just 39 seconds remaining and Washington out of timeouts, Jayden Daniels turned straight to Williams. First came a 22-yard strike over the middle to jump-start the drive, followed immediately after a spike by a 42-yard catch-and-run that put the Commanders on the Bengals’ eight-yard line with five seconds left. In 34 seconds of pure chaos, Williams essentially handed the game to his fellow rookie. . @Bengals @Commanders @JayD__5 to the rookie @a_williams2022 Antonio Williams…the 2 most important catches of the season for 64 yards and in a blink of an eye the Commanders are off life support and in the thick of a division race #BaldysBreakdowns pic.twitter.com/GznG06YZ3X — Brian Baldinger (@BaldyNFL) November 24, 2026 Drew Stevens makes franchise history under pressure While Williams provided the fireworks, Drew Stevens provided the steady heartbeat that kept Washington alive all night. Offensive coordinator David Blough’s unit moved the ball effectively between the 20s against Cincinnati, but red-zone stalls meant the Commanders repeatedly had to settle for 3 points. Stevens answered the call every single time. The rookie kicker went a perfect 5-for-5 on field goals—drilling attempts from 36, 40, 25, 41, and finally the 26-yard walk-off winner as time expired— also adding his lone extra point for a 16-point night. With that fifth made field goal, Stevens became the first rookie in Washington franchise history to convert five or more field goals in a single game. That 41-yarder in particular was no chip shot given the swirling wind at Northwest Stadium, yet Stevens never flinched. Across his first 10 NFL games, he has now connected on 22 of 25 field goal attempts (88%), including four makes from 50 yards or beyond. Considering how much white-knuckle kicking trauma Washington fans have endured over the years, watching a rookie calmly visualize telling his future kids about drilling a walk-off kick on Monday Night Football is a welcome change of pace. happened before our very eyes pic.twitter.com/000Ki5yItm — Washington Commanders (@Commanders) November 25, 2026 Young Commanders talent leads to a bright future Monday night’s win pushed Washington to 4-5-1 and injected real life back into the season. More importantly, it underscored that general manager Adam Peters’ 2026 rookie class is already carrying real weight when the lights are brightest. Between Williams emerging as a legitimate go-to target for Daniels, Stevens locking down the kicking job, and fellow rookies like linebacker Sonny Styles already earning NFC Defensive Player of the Week honors earlier this fall, the youth movement in Ashburn is ahead of schedule. Now it is up to Commanders fans to stuff the ballot box.

title: NFL Power Rankings Week 12: Commanders on the rise after back-to-back wins
summary: The Washington Commanders are 4-5-1 and coming off their biggest win of the season, defeating the Cincinnati Bengals on Monday Night Football. They did that by pressuring Joe Burrow and limiting his two biggest weapons, WRs Ja’Marr Chase/Tee Higgins, to under 80 yards receiving. Jayden Daniels also had to perform a little magic on the […]
full_text: LANDOVER, MARYLAND - NOVEMBER 23: Jayden Daniels #5 of the Washington Commanders celebrates after defeating the Cincinnati Bengals in the game at Northwest Stadium on November 23, 2026 in Landover, Maryland. (Photo by Scott Taetsch/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Washington Commanders are 4-5-1 and coming off their biggest win of the season, defeating the Cincinnati Bengals on Monday Night Football. They did that by pressuring Joe Burrow and limiting his two biggest weapons, WRs Ja’Marr Chase/Tee Higgins, to under 80 yards receiving. Jayden Daniels also had to perform a little magic on the final drive along with rookie of the week nominees Antonio Williams and Drew Stevens. The Commanders were big home underdogs, and took care of business to stay alive in an NFC East division that saw all it’s teams win in Week 11. The power rankers loved what they saw on Monday Night Football, and Washington’s average jumped up accordingly. The Commanders highest ranking is all the way up to 13, while the low still sits at 23. Washington climbed an average of 2 spots, but they’re now sitting inside the top 20. The massive win over the Bengals, paired with last week’s win over the Giants has put a new coat of paint on the Commanders. Back-to-back primetime wins over division leaders gets people’s attention. Now the team travels to the desert to take on the lowly Arizona Cardinals as they look to extend their first win streak since the 2024 season. Let’s just get the win and keep moving towards the top of the division! High: 13 Low: 23 Average: 18.5 #13 Walter Football The Redskins are +430 to win the division on DraftKings in the wake of their win over the Bengals. That doesn’t seem like a bad bet, considering that Washington is the most balanced team in the division. The Redskins have a better quarterback than the Giants do and a better defense than the Cowboys. They’re not great anywhere, but they’re at least not incompetent on either side of the ball. Last week: 16 Real GM Last week: 14 #15 Sports Illustrated (Orr) Unbelievable. Gutsy. Freeing. A win against one of the best teams remaining on their schedule, in prime time, where they had to manage the clock and spike the ball with seconds to play. This is a poetic way for the season to completely hinge on a moment. Last week: 16 Big Blue View (Falato) What a game by the Washington Commanders, who pulled off the 22-20 upset of the Cincinnati Bengals. Jayden Daniels had less than a minute to drive down the field for a field goal, and he made two HUGE throws to Antonio Williams that allowed for an easy field goal. Dan Quinn’s team was prepared and kept the game close, which makes the NFC East that much more interesting. Last week: 17 #17 NFL.com (Shook) Two gutsy performances in crunch time by Jayden Daniels and Co. — plus a strong defensive showing against a high-powered Bengals offense — led the Commanders to two straight wins in prime time , uplifting Washington from a 2-5-1 hole to a 4-5-1 record that preserves its chance of staying in the race to win the NFC East. Perhaps even more importantly (from a morale-focused perspective), Dan Quinn’s seat has cooled after the last two outings. That’s a nice development for a franchise that could use some good news. By the way, Daniels’ steady improvement is also rather encouraging. Last week: 20 Pro Football Talk For the second time in three years, Jayden Daniels outdueled Joe Burrow in prime time. Last week: 21 #18 Yahoo Sports (Schwab) Jayden Daniels is still capable of looking like a superstar at quarterback. When the Commanders looked like they had lost to the Bengals on a field goal with 46 seconds left, Daniels hit two passes to rookie Antonio Williams for a total of 64 yards, which set up a game-winning field goal as time expired. They were two great throws from Daniels and a great job by Williams to get open. Daniels finished with 289 yards, 122 of which went to Williams. The Commanders remain two games behind the Giants in the NFC East. But Daniels and Williams kept the Commanders’ season alive with two great plays in the final minute on Monday night. Last week: 20 USA Today (Davis) Look who’s playing stout defense all of a sudden, getting major contributions from its rookies and managing the clock. And with the NFC East’s most forgiving schedule down the stretch, the division is very much in play. Last week: 20 Fox Sports (Vacchiano) Super Bowl odds: +12500 (20th) Give the embattled Dan Quinn a lot of credit. His team was staring at yet another lost season, but the Commanders kept playing like they were alive. In fact, they’ve been playing hard and reasonably well for most of the last six games, and on Monday night they really got something to show for it with a huge upset over the high-flying Bengals. Their defense did some number on Joe Burrow and that passing attack, and Jayden Daniels took care of the rest with yet. They are now 3-2-1 in their last six, which keeps them within striking distance of the NFC East-leading Giants. Yeah, they’re two games back, but they own the tie-breaker. And they can make up a lot of ground over the next four weeks when they play the Cardinals, Titans, Texans and Falcons. Stat To Know : The Commanders won in prime time in back-to-back weeks for the first time since 2007. Download the SB Nation app on iOS or Android . #19 ESPN Extension candidate: LB Frankie Luvu Luvu has rebounded after a tough 2025 season, when injuries to others forced him to rush more off the edge. In new coordinator Daronte Jones ‘ defense, Luvu plays inside and has been an effective blitzer. He has also improved as a tackler compared to last season, averaging a career-high 8.4 tackles per game. And Luvu’s pass rush rate entering Monday is the second highest of his career (25.6%). The main issue that could prevent an extension is Luvu’s age, as he will be 31 at the start of next season. — John Keim Last week: 21 The Athletic (Graff/Kendall) Something to be thankful for: Jayden Daniels is back The Commanders quarterback played only seven games last year due to multiple injuries. He played game No. 8 of this season on Monday night and led the Commanders in both passing (225) and rushing yards (55) on the way to an upset of the Bengals via a game-winning drive that went 64 yards in 46 seconds. Daniels is 11th in the league in passer rating (96.1) and leads all quarterbacks with 335 rushing yards. Last week: 22 CBS Sports (Prisco) That’s a big-time victory over the Bengals. Jayden Daniels really made the plays in the moment, which keeps this team’s playoff hopes alive. Last week: 23 Bleacher Report The Washington Commanders have their signature win of the season, knocking off the Cincinnati Bengals with a game-winning field goal. Jayden Daniels has a new favorite target in rookie third-rounder Antonio Williams, whose big fourth-quarter catch put the Commanders in position to win. Washington is riding a high after winning back-to-back outings for the first time since 2024. Looking ahead to Sunday, the Commanders could reach .500 with a win over the Arizona Cardinals. If that happens, the NFC East would be a three-team race, and Washington has the tiebreaker over the division-leading New York Giants. They are still in the NFC East race. Last week: 22 Bleeding Green Nation…

title: Future Hogs Week 12: College football players who could help the Commanders
summary: Week 12 was rough for a number of teams in the Big 10. UCLA is no longer undefeated after being stifled by Michigan’s defense in an overtime loss in Ann Arbor. Meanwhile in Seattle, Indiana suffered their second loss of the season at the hands of Washington. Nebraska ended its streak of 31 losses to […]
full_text: SOUTH BEND, INDIANA - NOVEMBER 21: Leonard Moore #15 of Notre Dame looks down the field during a game between SMU v Notre Dame at Notre Dame Stadium on November 21, 2026 in South Bend, Indiana. (Photo by Michael Miller/ISI Photos/ISI Photos via Getty Images) | ISI Photos via Getty Images Week 12 was rough for a number of teams in the Big 10. UCLA is no longer undefeated after being stifled by Michigan’s defense in an overtime loss in Ann Arbor. Meanwhile in Seattle, Indiana suffered their second loss of the season at the hands of Washington. Nebraska ended its streak of 31 losses to ranked teams by handing Ohio State their fourth loss of the season. There were fewer upsets outside the Big 10. The Georgia Bulldogs remain the top team in the country and punched their ticket to the SEC Championship Game after beating South Carolina. Utah is in the Big 12 Championship after beating TCU to stay undefeated. Miami started slow but rallied late to beat Virginia Tech. Week 13, Rivalry Week, the final week of the college football season is here, and there are matchups that could go a long way to setting up the postseason. Alabama, Texas, and Tennessee all have a chance to face Georgia in the SEC Championship. Alabama will face Auburn in the Iron Bowl, Texas will take on Texas A&M, and Tennessee will play Vanderbilt. If Texas Tech beats TCU, they’ll face Utah in the Big 12 Championship. If they lose, it’ll open the door for BYU if they can beat Cincinnati. UCLA and Oregon and win and get into the Big 10 Championship, but they’ll have to get past USC and Washington, respectively. If they lose, it’ll open the door for Iowa and Indiana. The ACC Championship game is set to be Miami versus Wake Forest, but if Miami loses to Boston College or Wake Forest loses to Duke, it will affect playoff rankings. Here are a few players who had a good week and might be able to help out the Commanders. Let me know what you think about these prospects and feel free to post players that stood out to you: Devon Dampier | QB | Senior | Utah Utah is now the only undefeated team in the country and it starts with their quarterback Devon Dampier . He’s a dual-threat QB that is hard to defend because he is so talented as a runner and passer. Dampier, like many of the quarterbacks in this class, is short for an NFL QB. Dampier is only 5’11”, but he’s put together at 210 pounds. Dampier’s threat to run opens up space downfield in the passing game. He possesses the accuracy and touch to exploit these areas of the field for big gains. Although this is the case, his arm looks to be average at best as he rarely drives throws into tight windows. As a runner, Dampier’s penchant for gaining positive yards puts pressure on a defense. He’s not the fastest player, but he is the Utes’ active career leader for QB rushing yards with nearly 3,000 yards. Dampier led Utah to a win over TCU by going 18 of 28 for 278 yards and two touchdowns. On the ground, he added 62 yards and two touchdowns. Messiah Burch | RB | Senior | Buffalo If you would like the Commanders backfield to have more juice, consider Messiah Burch . He’s a smaller back at only 5’9”, 195 pounds, but Burch’s acceleration stands out. On zone runs, he demonstrates vision to find holes and the quickness to get through them. Once he gets in the open field, Burch appears to have the long speed to take a play the distance. While his acceleration is a fantastic trait, Burch also exhibits patience to let blocks develop. Then he uses his vision to pick his way through the line of scrimmage. While he isn’t trucking defenders regularly at his size, he fights to get as much as he can out of each run. Burch and the Bulls beat Central Michigan behind his 200 yards and two touchdowns on 24 attempts. It was his second game in a row with at least 200 yards. Buffalo's Messiah Burch rushed for 200 yards and two touchdowns, including a 75-yard score, to lead the Bulls to their sixth consecutive victory. It marked his second straight 200-yard rushing performance. @UBuffaloFB | #MACtion pic.twitter.com/wf5BpcihOg — MACtion (@MACSports) November 23, 2026 Reed Harris | WR | Senior | Arizona State There are ton of things to like about Reed Harris . A quarterback in high school, Harris has grown into a prolific wide receiver. And when I say grown, I mean it. He’s 6’5”, 220 pounds. You might think that means he’s just a contested catch receiver at that size. Harris, however, uses his long strides to eat up space against off coverage and has the speed to beat defenses deep. Teams respect his speed, so he sees a lot of off coverage. How he handles press coverage will be a big part of his evaluation. While he runs a lot of go routes, he has shown the ability to run the entire route tree thanks to great agility at his size. He has 11 TDs and over 1,100 yards, but would’ve been more productive if he had more consistent quarterback play throughout the season. In a close loss to Oklahoma State, Harris made 11 catches for 172 yards and two touchdowns. Jake Fette to Reed Harris for 6 pic.twitter.com/QRMBvPTQwa — Jake Estes (@dynasty_jake) November 22, 2026 Arizona State’s Reed Harris has been unstoppable in the first half against Oklahoma State. Finds the end zone again on this circus catch. Harris continues to look like a first-round pick https://t.co/0umGXJom6U pic.twitter.com/VlBlUonK5a — Bobby Football (@Rob__Paul) November 22, 2026 Arizona State’s Reed Harris is such a freak. Moves so well for a 6-foot-5, 220-pound WR. Harris is top 10 nationally in receiving yards + TDs and is a potential first-round pick in April. pic.twitter.com/GnQRrlj606 — Bobby Football (@Rob__Paul) November 22, 2026 Willie Rodriguez | TE | Junior | Kentucky Kentucky has cooled off after a hot start to the season as evidenced by their most recent loss to Missouri. One player that has played well all season is Willie Rodriguez . Standing 6’4” and weighing 249 pounds, Rodriguez is built like a receiving tight end. Yes, he is very capable in the passing game. He uses nuance like varying the speed of his routes to create separation. He can be trusted in contested catch situations thanks to reliable hands. For all of his talents as a receiver, Rodriguez is a talented blocker. Whether inline, as a lead blocker, or blocking in space, Rodriguez can hold the point of attack and stay attached to defenders. He looks like the complete package at tight end. Rodriguez made eight catches for 93 yards in the loss to the Tigers. #Kentucky TE Willie Rodriguez really caught my eye against Florida with his run blocking and ability to win in the vertical passing game matched one-on-one with LBs and safeties. Finished with 5 catches for 62 yards and has 60 or more receiving yards in his last 3 games. pic.twitter.com/hN3waswUgj — Devin Jackson (@RealD_Jackson) November 17, 2026 Greg Johnson | OG/C | Senior | Minnesota Alex Rowsey put Greg Johnson on my radar recently. After watching him, he’s almost tailor-made to address the Commanders offensive line issues. Johnson has played every position on the offensive line with most of his experience at center and left guard. For center, he’s tall at 6’6”, and he has the necessary mass to anchor the middle of the line at 325 pounds. Johnson typically plays with excellent leverage, and while there are times defenders get under his pads, he is strong enough to anchor to prevent them from going through them. He can move people in the run game and plays through the whistle. While he generally has good balance, he can end up on the ground because he looks to finish blocks so emphatically. He mirrors pass rushers well because he has good lateral quickness and agility. If Johnson makes it to the second day of the NFL draft, the Commanders need to give him consideration. summary: The Commanders will meet with receiver Brandon Aiyuk on Wednesday, according to a report from ESPN’s Adam Schefter. This meeting comes after the 49ers released him on Monday, and Aiyuk then cleared waivers on Tuesday. A long dispute […]
full_text: The Commanders will meet with receiver Brandon Aiyuk on Wednesday, according to a report from ESPN’s Adam Schefter. Citing the information from agent Drew Rosenhaus, Schefter says Aiyuk will meet with Washington brass on Wednesday. Free-agent WR Brandon Aiyuk is scheduled to visit Wednesday with the Washington Commanders, per his agent Drew Rosenhaus. Aiyuk and Commanders QB Jayden Daniels played together at Arizona State during the 2019 season. https://t.co/5GZRgm9P1D — Adam Schefter (@AdamSchefter) November 24, 2026 This meeting comes after the 49ers released him on Monday, and Aiyuk then cleared waivers on Tuesday. A long dispute with the 49ers had previously been resolved when he reported to the team after months on the team’s exempt-did not report list . At that time, the NFL gave San Francisco a two-week roster exemption, which expired this week, and which they took advantage of before finally parting ways. Explaining everything that went wrong between Aiyuk and the 49ers would involve thousands of words, but we can sum it up by saying there was a disagreement about his rehab plans that devolved into a messy situation that left the player and team at odds. Then there was a rash of social media post by Aiyuk slamming 49ers brass, including general manager John Lynch and head coach Kyle Shanahan. Aiyuk also took shots at good friend, former Arizona State teammate and current Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels, but Aiyuk reached out to Daniels and they reportedly squashed their friction . The fact he was even given a meeting with the Commanders supports that claim. Aiyuk has made it clear for months that he wants to sign with Washington — he regularly wears Commanders gear in social media posts — who could use some receiver help with Terry McLaurin done for the year with a torn patellar tendon. Aiyuk is expected to draw interest from a few teams, with a practice squad signing as his likeliest path back to NFL action. title: Washington Commanders Whiteboard: Notes, observations from MNF Week 11
summary: Before the advent of media devices, football coaches at all levels used simple whiteboards to outline plays, map out player positions and explain schemes in real time. Nowadays digital playbooks and tablets have taken over, but coaches still use whiteboards on occasion to impart information quickly and effectively. The following are some quick notes and […]
full_text: Before the advent of media devices, football coaches at all levels used simple whiteboards to outline plays, map out player positions and explain schemes in real time. Nowadays digital playbooks and tablets have taken over, but coaches still use whiteboards on occasion to impart information quickly and effectively. The following are some quick notes and observations from the Washington Commanders ‘ 22-20 cardiac win over the Cincinnati Bengals on Monday Night Football. Daronte Jones and the Commanders defense came up big Headed into Monday night’s matchup with the Bengals, the odds of the Washington Commanders’ defense slowing down Joe Burrow and the NFL’s top-ranked passing attack seemed long and, in truth, the Bengals quarterback did throw for 300 yards and 2 touchdowns. The key, however, was that Commanders defensive coordinator Daronte Jones found a way to pressure Burrow from the opening whistle. And while the secondary allowed some plays, they were made by players like Samajae Perine and Mike Gesicki and not Ja’Marr Chase and Tee Higgins. After getting absolutely torched by Puka Nacua in Week 9, the Washington Commanders took away not one, but two star wide receivers in Monday night’s matchup. In fact, Perine’s 71 receiving yards almost surpassed both Ja’Marr Chase and Tee Higgins’ combined total of 74, their lowest since Week 1 against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. Jones crafted a blitz-heavy attack that was effective early and Washington blitzed on 19 dropbacks and caused a 26.3% drop back success rate in those spots. Cornerback Trey Amos and backup Rasul Douglas played plenty of Cover 0 behind their blitz packages but Daronte also switched up the looks, playing both Cover 4 and Cover 6 about half the time . The Commanders utilized plenty of three safety looks in the first half, with Quan Martin playing well in a deep zone. While the cornerbacks had some lapses, they did a good job overall. First two plays of the game Darontae Jones showing out! 1st play: Show 6 send 5, SACK! 2nd play: Show 7 send 7! Sets up 3rd and 16 (Reaves took the stiff arm like it was Josh Allen not Joe Burrow 😵‍💫) pic.twitter.com/XSSVKdP4Wa — Jerome A. Coleman (@YungRome22) November 24, 2026 Rasul Douglas vs Ja’Marr Chase • 3 targets • 1 reception • 8 yards • 1 PBU pic.twitter.com/rWvQkYcIDC — brandon (@JayDanielsMVP) November 24, 2026 Interestingly, free agent addition Odafe Oweh played a season-low 31 snaps , and once again was missing in action, recording no statistics in the prime time matchup. Instead, Dorance Armstrong played more defensive snaps (34) and Joshua Josephs played a career-high 24 snaps while recording two quarterback hits. Defensive tackle Tim Settle led the team with 1.5 sacks, 1 TFL and seven tackles (five solo) despite only playing 23 snaps. When the clock struck zero, the Washington Commanders had held the Bengals’ offense to twenty points, the fifth straight game in which the defense limited the opposing offense to 23 points or less. Even without starting DTs Daron Payne and Javon Kinlaw, Daronte Jones’ squad is starting to mesh, and the Washington Commanders’ 18.8 PPG allowed ranks 7th in the league during that same stretch. That includes matchups with two of the NFL’s best offenses in San Francisco and Cincinnati and, perhaps not coincidentally, also coincides with the arrival of defensive advisor Steve Wilks. David Blough and the Commanders offense continue to start slow On the opposite side of the ball, David Blough still does not appear to have an advisor of his own and, unfortunately, the Commanders’ offense showed it in the first half. Following a game in which Washington established the run versus the Giants, the rookie offensive coordinator chose to move away from the rushing attack against a defense that was susceptible to it. The offense looked disjointed coming off a 10-day prep period or “mini-bye,” and started off the game with four consecutive punts with 28 net yards of offense right around the two-minute warning. While their performance in the second half was record-breaking , the Commanders’ offense can’t continue to start slow in every matchup and expect to win going forward. On the plus side, fans should have been happy to see the Commanders finally use a goal line package with Andrew Wylie, Nick Allegretti, and Ben Sinnott at fullback to end the first half. Commanders running Power at the goal line from Offset-I. Ben Sinnott playing the fullback spot the way the Good Lord intended. 🗣️ @HogsHaven pic.twitter.com/vmC9kahkJN — Last of the Fullbacks (@TheLastFullback) November 24, 2026 Blough did call a better game in the second half. Jacory Croskey-Merritt and Austin Ekeler combined for 20 rushing attempts with Ekeler finishing with an impressive 5.9 yards per carry. Jayden Daniels chipped in with the longest run of his career on a 47-yard burst up the middle, and while the game was won on the back of No. 5’s heroics, Blough deserves credit for calling the right pass concept not once, but twice. Make sure to note Stefon Diggs “helping” his teammate to get down to preserve the clock. Commanders called the same play twice and went 64 yards in 34 seconds. Two different, perfect throws from Jayden Daniels. Two different, perfect routes from Antonio Williams. What a win. pic.twitter.com/QC4KqJqBZH — Benjamin Solak (@BenjaminSolak) November 24, 2026 Two rookies breakout in primetime The Week 8 edition of Whiteboard lamented that Antonio Williams’ breakout game hadn’t happened yet, but speculated it might be coming in the near future. While his usage has been up, the statistical production hadn’t followed. On Monday night the rookie wide receiver cemented his breakout, finishing with nine receptions for 122 yards. Williams was the first Washington rookie with 120-plus receiving yards since Terry McLaurin in Dec. 2019, and his 93 yards receiving in the fourth quarter were the most by a rookie in the fourth quarter of a game since Week 17 of 2020. Most importantly, Williams has won the trust of Jayden Daniels, as evidenced by the anticipation in the game’s final throw. That new JD5 just dropped. Normal breakdown film otw but you gotta see this. pic.twitter.com/yzds311IOt — Kurt Benkert (@KurtBenkert) November 24, 2026 Trust is one of the things Daniels’ prioritizes most in his wide receivers and, with that bond established, Williams should start to cash in with his separation and precise route running. The other rookie to establish trust and confidence is kicker Drew Stevens. After missing two field goals and three extra points in the first five weeks , the undrafted free agent has established himself as the answer to Washington’s kicker woes. While he may have an unorthodox style, Stevens is a player the team will trust after his five field goal performance in prime time. Drew Stevens has some unique motivation before he kicks. pic.twitter.com/TLppfKgGhc — COMMANDERS FOOTBALL (@HogsHaven) November 24, 2026 How about Drew Stevens!? 🦵🏻 • 1st player with 5 FG’s in a half since 2017. • First-ever Commanders rookie to make 5 FG’s in a game. • 22-for-25 on the season. • He’s perfect on kicks inside 50 yards and has made 21 of his last 22 kicks. #RaiseHail pic.twitter.com/9fdoZdA45g — Nick Kerns (@nicktkerns) November 24, 2026 What does Monday night’s win mean for the Washington Commanders? We asked this same closing question last week, but Monday night’s win deserves a repeat inquiry. Following a surprising win by the New York Giants and a dominating one by the Cowboys over the weekend, many Washington fans were discouraged about the chances of the Commanders winning their division. Functionally, Monday night’s win helps the team keep pace in the NFC East and keep their hold on a 16% chance to make the playoffs, but last night’s performance also tells fans something else. Dan Quinn has his players believing in their ability to play any opponent and keep winning. Anybody. Anywhere. Anytime. The Washington Commanders are 4-5-1 now with a 16%…

title: How upsets in the 2026 NFL season have upended survivor pools
summary: Why spend up to nearly $80,000 in order to win a survivor contest over halfway through the NFL season?
full_text:
Paul Jager was browsing the marketplace for Splash Sports' Survivor World Championship on Friday, Nov. 20, when one specific entry caught his eye ahead of Week 11. The seller had other entries listed and hadn't yet listed this one, but Jager found it and was in awe at the teams used to get it to this point. He knew he had to have it.

 Jager purchased the entry on the marketplace for $133,000, the largest transaction that Splash has facilitated since it launched its flagship contest this season. Upon taking ownership of it, he made his Week 11 pick: the Pittsburgh Steelers to defeat the Philadelphia Eagles. 

 "If I can get through with the Steelers, this entry is set up to win the whole thing," Jager told ESPN of his mindset at the time. "I was like, 'I'm going to take one chance, and if Pittsburgh wins, I am literally set.' I knew five minutes into the game, I was regretting taking Pittsburgh."

 The Steelers lost to their in-state rivals, ending that entry's hopes of winning at least a share of the $21 million grand prize. But Jager wasn't out of the running. The investor by trade in Kansas City, Kansas who dabbles a lot in sports betting, currently has six entries alive at Splash and two in Circa Sports' famed Survivor contest, which features a prize pool of over $25 million this season.

 

 Jager's experience is part of what's shaping up to be the new normal for players in high-stakes survivor contests. It fits perfectly into the new look for a sports betting world that is increasingly taking a more stock market-esque approach.

 When Splash announced its completely online contest before this season, it was with the goal of expanding the space on top of the remarkable bedrock Circa (which requires in-person registration and proxies) has built since 2020. That included a built-in marketplace that allows players to buy and sell whole or partial tickets within the app using their connected payment methods. So far this season, Splash has already facilitated more than $4 million in transactions.

 Circa also launched its own official marketplace by partnering with online platform Survivor Sweat. Circa Sports director of operations Jeff Benson says that the partnership "has driven significantly more engagement and activity than in previous years."

 Gabe Patgorski, a former Circa champion, current contestant and founder of the research website Survivor Atlas, describes the contest as more "portfolio-style," given that there is no limit to the number of entries each player can have. Contestants can be more liberal with their selections, knowing that the quantity of entries they keep alive will just increase each's value, if nothing else.

 It's a whole new branch of strategy in a game with over 21 sextillion possible combinations throughout the season. And when the stakes are as high as $1,000 per entry, players are looking for any edge they can get to ultimately come out profitable.

 "The marketplace is a really cool way to turn any static entry you have in a contest to a tradable asset that you can get out of, or take some chips off the table at any time in the year, or buy back in. And so we've actually seen way more activity than I would've expected," Splash co-founder and co-CEO TJ Ross told ESPN. 

 Some of the trade activity comes after a particularly brutal first seven weeks of the season whittled down the fields to a fraction of the original entries. Over that span, favorites of seven points or greater -- the teams toward which many survivor contestants gravitate -- lost eight games straight-up, marking the first time since 1972 in which each of the first seven weeks of the season featured such an upset, according to ESPN Research.

 

 Those results had an extensive impact on survivor contests: Following Week 7, Circa Survivor had lost 97.4% of its field (24,357 of the 25,017 entries). Entering Week 12, Circa Grandissimo, the $100,000 entry contest with a $7.7 million prize pool, is down to just three players from the 77 who started.

 "In short, 2026 has combined the largest field Circa has ever seen with a run of upsets concentrated on the most popular survivor selections," Benson told ESPN via email after Week 7. "The absolute carnage is record-setting in scale; the underlying dynamic (chalk getting eliminated in bunches) is a familiar and defining feature of the format, just playing out more dramatically this year."

 Though the raw volume of eliminations seems shocking, the early portion of the 2026 season was actually not the most carnage the contest has experienced by percentage. That honor belongs to the infamous 2024 season , which saw 99.5% of the field eliminated going into Week 8. The 2022 campaign had 98.0% of its field gone by the same time, which ultimately produced only two winners that year, the fewest in the contest's history. 

 The favorites have been more reliable since Week 7; the top four most-picked teams in Circa Survivor have won each week and favorites of at least seven points have gone 16-1 straight up from Week 8 through Sunday's games. Week 11 featured an average point spread of 8, the third-largest for any week (excluding the final two weeks of the season in which playoff positioning can dramatically affect spreads) in the last 50 years, per ESPN Research. 

 Players in the high-stakes contests must now brace for the holiday season. In the Circa pool, each entry must choose a team playing in one of the five Thanksgiving-adjacent games and one of the four Christmas-adjacent games, in addition to the usual games on Sunday and Monday. In Splash, each entry must choose two teams in Weeks 12 through 16, as well as in Week 9, regardless of when they are played.

 "It's felt like a normal survivor season to me so far, very different from last year but similar to 2024 and 2022 in terms of pace of eliminations," 2025 Circa Survivor champion Jason Somerville told ESPN over text. He has one entry still alive in Circa. "It never feels real to me 'til Thanksgiving anyway, so fingers crossed I have some decisions to make in December."

 

 The way this season has played out supports the notion that this could be a much more generous holiday season for the contestants than usual, especially with how things shook out at the NFL trade deadline. 

 Patgorski noticed that many of the already bad teams got worse at this season's deadline, and teams that began the season with high hopes -- like the  Indianapolis Colts and  Philadelphia Eagles -- became big sellers. There are also teams dealing with injured or underperforming quarterbacks, like the  Baltimore Ravens ,  Los Angeles Chargers and  New England Patriots , for whom the bottom has fallen out.

 "The path to the end seems a lot easier for almost everyone," said Patgorski. "Every week there are so many big favorites where people are going, 'Oh, that's a lock. That's a free square.' And it's a pretty big shift from a few weeks ago where people thought, 'Okay, this contest has a big chance not to go to the end.' And now, everyone's thinking, 'Oh, there's going to be 50 winners. It's so easy to get to Christmas now. It's so easy to get to the end.'"

 Philadelphia presents a juicy opportunity for Circa players given it is one of the few teams playing in both the Thanksgiving and Christmas mini-weeks ... but that in itself creates a paradoxical dilemma unique to high-end survivor contests. 

 As of Tuesday, the Eagles are 8.5-point road underdogs to the  Dallas Cowboys on Thanksgiving according to DraftKings, easily the largest spread between the five games that make up the Wednesday-through-Friday slate. Patgorski estimates that 60-70% of the field will pick Dallas. 

 "The math says you're supposed to avoid that just because randomness happens often enough to pop that bubble. I think a lot of players have a sense of that, but of course you have to weigh that against, 'Well, maybe it's worth joining the crowd because my entry is strong enough where I'm fine just getting…

title: NFL Power Rankings: Stacking all 32 teams for Week 12, plus extension candidates
summary: How does every NFL team stack up heading into Week 12? We made our 1-32 list and picked players who could get a new contract.
full_text:
Week 11 of the 2026 NFL season kicked off Thursday with another strong performance from Texans quarterback C.J. Stroud , who notched his fifth straight game with multiple touchdown passes in a win over the Colts. On Sunday, Jaguars wide receiver  Parker Washington  had his third game with 100 receiving yards this season, though it wasn't enough to defeat the Giants. And Broncos cornerback  Ja'Quan McMillian  put away the Raiders with a late pick-six.

 What do these players have in common? They're all eligible for extensions, whether on their rookie deals or otherwise. They're also all mentioned below, as along with our 1-32 rankings, we asked our NFL Nation reporters to pick a player from each team who could receive a contract extension this offseason.

 To form the 1-32 list, our power panel of more than a dozen NFL analysts evaluates how all 32 teams stack up against one another. Here are a couple of highlights from this week's rankings:

 
 The Jaguars are out of our top six for the first time since Week 4 after their 23-18 loss to the Giants . Before Week 11, Jacksonville was one of two teams that hadn't trailed by more than 10 points this season (Bills), but it trailed by 11 for almost 30 minutes Sunday. Quarterback Trevor Lawrence faced the most pressure he has seen all season, which resulted in two interceptions. 
 The Lions climbed four spots from last week's rankings after their sixth straight game of allowing 21 or fewer points, tied for their second-longest streak over the past 50 seasons, per ESPN Research. On offense, quarterback Jared Goff had his sixth game of 2026 with multiple TD passes and zero INTs. It came  against the Bucs , who entered Sunday with the league's best defensive EPA, per NFL Next Gen Stats. 
 The Eagles showed signs of life in Week 11, snapping a seven-game losing streak with a 19-16 win over the Steelers . Philly rose three spots from last week's rankings, and while it is all but out of the playoff race, it can hurt the Cowboys' chances on  Thanksgiving . Eagles running back Saquon Barkley is on a career-high streak of four straight games with a rushing touchdown. 
 
 Let's get into the full list, starting with the same team as  last week .

 

 
 Jump to a team: 
 ARI | ATL | BAL | BUF | CAR | CHI | CIN 
 CLE | DAL | DEN | DET | GB | HOU | IND 
 JAX | KC | LAC | LAR | LV | MIA | MIN 
 NE | NO | NYG | NYJ | PHI | PIT | SF 
 SEA | TB | TEN | WSH 

 
 

 

 1. San Francisco 49ers (9-1) 
 Week 11 result: Beat the Vikings 35-10 
 Week 11 ranking: 1 

 Extension candidate: G Dominick Puni 

 

 Puni, who will be eligible for an extension for the first time this offseason, is the clear choice based on consistency and production. But it's a bit more complicated than that. Since coach Kyle Shanahan and general manager John Lynch arrived in 2017, they've never given big bucks to a guard. With left tackle Trent Williams closer to retirement, center Jake Brendel slated to be an unrestricted free agent and right tackle Colton McKivitz recovering from a fractured left ankle , finding a fair deal for Puni would at least offer some stability on an O-line that could have plenty of change the next couple of seasons. -- Nick Wagoner 

 
 

 2. Buffalo Bills (9-1) 
 Week 11 result: Beat the Dolphins 26-9 
 Week 11 ranking: 2 

 Extension candidate: G Alec Anderson 

 

 An underrated aspect of the Bills' success since drafting quarterback Josh Allen has been offensive line continuity. The Bills prioritize developing and rewarding homegrown blockers, which in recent years has meant big contracts for OT Dion Dawkins , OT Spencer Brown and G O'Cyrus Torrence . Anderson is a unique case because he arrived in Buffalo as an undrafted rookie and spent four seasons as a reserve before starting in 2026. However, it's certainly within the Bills' M.O. to stick with their developmental player rather than cast him aside. He's a tenacious blocker who is integral to the Bills' run game. -- Nick Suss 

 
 

 

 3. Kansas City Chiefs (8-2) 
 Week 11 result: Beat the Cardinals 34-7 
 Week 11 ranking: 5 

 Extension candidate: WR Josh Downs 

 

 An argument can be made that the Chiefs got ahead of the market by acquiring Downs just ahead of the trade deadline to help convince him to stay with the team beyond this season. He has already made an impact on the Chiefs in only two games, recording eight receptions on nine targets for 112 receiving yards and a touchdown. Because Downs has been able to quickly build a connection with quarterback Patrick Mahomes , the Chiefs should try to offer a quality extension to the receiver to keep him from entering free agency. -- Nate Taylor 

 
 

 4. Chicago Bears (8-2) 
 Week 11 result: Beat the Saints 21-13 
 Week 11 ranking: 4 

 Extension candidate: QB Caleb Williams 

 

 Williams becomes eligible for his first extension after this season. He's the franchise quarterback the Bears searched decades to find, and pairing him with coach Ben Johnson for the foreseeable future is the priority. Chicago's front office has an incentive to get ahead of a rapidly inflating QB market, which will see the likes of C.J. Stroud and Lamar Jackson come to the table, along with others in Williams' draft class. Though Williams said in September that "money's not a motivating factor for me," his top-10 play on a contending team could lead to him earning around $70 million per year. Signing Williams early would allow the Bears to keep his 2027 cap hit low while prorating a massive signing bonus into future years. -- Courtney Cronin 

 
 

 5. Denver Broncos (8-2) 
 Week 11 result: Beat the Raiders 38-24 
 Week 11 ranking: 7 

 Extension candidate: CB Ja'Quan McMillian 

 

 There isn't any guarantee the Broncos can, or will, give McMillian an extension. But his teammates have made their feelings clear while McMillian makes one big-moment play after another -- "they need to make that happen,'' is how CB  Pat Surtain II put it after McMillan's pick-six Sunday. McMillian is also one of the best find-and-develop players of GM George Paton's tenure. He was signed as an undrafted free agent, spent almost all of his rookie season on the practice squad and now approaches unrestricted free agency as one of the league's best nickel corners. That isn't exactly the kind of player the Broncos have re-signed in recent years. -- Jeff Legwold 

 
 

 6. Detroit Lions (8-2) 
 Week 11 result: Beat the Buccaneers 31-21 
 Week 11 ranking: 10 

 Extension candidate: S Brian Branch 

 

 Branch and TE Sam LaPorta are playing out the 2026 season on their four-year rookie deals, but general manager Brad Holmes has reiterated that he would like to reach long-term extensions with both players, though LaPorta has expressed doubts . Branch has made an immediate impact since returning from an Achilles injury that he sustained in Week 7 of last season. In 2026, he has five passes defended and one interception in four games. Depending on how the rest of the season plays out for Branch, the Lions could use the franchise tag or agree to long-term deal with him. -- Eric Woodyard 

 
 

 7. Jacksonville Jaguars (7-3) 
 Week 11 result: Lost to the Giants 23-18 
 Week 11 ranking: 3 

 Extension candidate: WR Parker Washington 

 

 Washington is the Jags' No. 1 receiver, and more importantly, he's the one quarterback Trevor Lawrence goes to in critical situations. Washington leads the team in targets (81), catches (44) and receiving yards (748); his average of 17 yards per catch is tied for third in the NFL. He is also just 100 yards shy of surpassing his career high for receiving yards (847 last season). The 2023 sixth-round pick and the team have been in extension discussions since the offseason, but nothing has materialized yet. The Jaguars might have to use the franchise tag to buy extra time for a deal. -- Michael DiRocco

title: Falcons 'aware' of insinuations Pearce still trying to contact ex Jackson
summary: Kevin Stefanski said he and the team are aware of assertions made by Rickea Jackson that insinuated James Pearce Jr. is still trying to contact her.
full_text:
FLOWERY BRANCH, Ga. -- Atlanta Falcons coach Kevin Stefanski said he and the team are aware of social media assertions made by WNBA player Rickea Jackson that insinuated defensive end James Pearce Jr . is still attempting to contact her, the coach said.
An agreement with a Florida court prohibits Pearce, Jackson's ex-boyfriend, from contacting or coming near Jackson.
"I'm aware," Stefanski said Wednesday. "We've spoken to James. But we don't have much more to add."
A video posted to TikTok by someone seemingly unrelated to the situation showed a scroll of dozens of missed calls from a no-ID number. Jackson reposted the video on her own TikTok and left comments on the original post, saying this is a situation she is "actively going through."
In the comment, Jackson said she has not spoken to or about "this person" in nearly a year and "won't say anything else ever again." She implied that she has not told the court, because she would be told that there isn't enough evidence that the unknown calls are coming from Pearce.
Pearce, 23, was arrested last Feb. 7 after allegedly ramming his car multiple times into a vehicle driven by Jackson in Doral, Florida, and not allowing her to enter a police station. Police responded, and Pearce fled in his car before crashing and then fleeing on foot.
Pearce was charged with felony aggravated battery with a deadly weapon and felony fleeing police and resisting arrest, as well as misdemeanor stalking, before entering into a one-year pretrial diversion program that allowed him to avoid trial . Those charges will be dropped if Pearce stays out of trouble for that one-year period, passes random drug tests and remains compliant with a mental health treatment program.
Jackson filed a petition for a protective order against Pearce in February, and she dropped it in lieu of the intervention program. Pearce must also stay away from Jackson and not contact her as part of that program.
Jackson wrote in the initial petition following Pearce's arrest that she was "in fear of my life" and that if the court did not intervene, she believed "James will kill me," according to Miami-Dade County court documents obtained by ESPN.
Pearce was suspended eight games by the NFL due to a violation of the personal conduct policy at the end of training camp. He returned to the field with the Falcons in Week 9.
Pearce has not spoken to the media at all this season and has declined multiple attempts by media members for comment.

title: NFL Week 12 latest intel, buzz questions, news, fantasy tips: What we're hearing
summary: Where could Daniel Jones and Brandon Aiyuk land? What's the latest on coaching hot seats? What's next for Puka Nacua? And who is getting MVP love in league circles?
full_text:
Week 12 of the  2026 NFL season  comes with a serving of Thanksgiving football, and insiders Jeremy Fowler and Dan Graziano have been calling sources around the league for the latest news and notable buzz.

 We begin this week with updates on the coaching carousel. There were already two changes by this point last season (Titans and Giants), but zero teams have moved on from their head coaches so far in 2026. What's the latest on hot seats around the league? Could we really make it through the regular season with no jobs coming open?

 With Daniel Jones clearing waivers and becoming a free agent this week, our insiders also asked around on potential landing spots for him. And while Puka Nacua 's season might be over, his future is a big talker right now. Fowler and Graziano tried to get a sense of what comes next for the star receiver and whether the Rams will hand him a big extension in the offseason. And finally, they canvassed the league for a quick poll of who should win MVP as of now.

 It's all here, as Fowler and Graziano answer big questions, hand out useful fantasy football nuggets and empty their reporting notebooks heading into Week 12.

 

 
 Jump to: 
 Head coach hot seat updates 
 Fits for Jones  | MVP candidates 
 Nacua's future | Fantasy advice 
 More notes, intel 

 
 

 Still no coaching changes? Where do things stand for head coaches on the hot seat? 
 Graziano: Well, it's not like no team has done anything . The Colts fired their GM weeks ago. The Panthers fired their defensive coordinator . The Cardinals  fired their defensive coordinator . The Cowboys didn't fire their defensive coordinator, instead demoted him and kept him around to suffer with everyone else. But you want to know about head coaches, so fine. Situations I'm watching for potential change at the end of the season include the Jets, Buccaneers, Colts, Eagles and maybe Commanders, though Dan Quinn seems to be turning things around  in D.C.

 

 Would any of those teams move on from their head coach before the end of the season? I personally doubt it, in large part because I'm not sure which coordinators or assistants would be candidates to have audition roles the rest of the season. It is still early, and things could get bad enough in one or more of these spots that a team could decide to change for change's sake, but that's my read right now. Jeremy, how did I do?

 Fowler: Nailed it! To be fair, there's usually a coaching change by this part of the season. The Titans' Brian Callahan and the Giants' Brian Daboll were properly fired before this point last season. Thanksgiving spelled the end for Chicago's Matt Eberflus in 2024. In 2023, Carolina's Frank Reich and Las Vegas' Josh McDaniels were gone before December. So, change is inevitable, and possibly soon. But I'm with you for this season, Dan -- it seems several ownership groups are willing to show some level of patience with their hot seat coaches.

 That seems to be the case in Washington, where Quinn is rallying the Commanders and has a soft schedule coming up. The Bucs could wait until season's end for clarity on Todd Bowles' future, though Monday night vs. Carolina feels important (the Bucs would be three games out in the NFC South with a loss). It seems like Aaron Glenn, fresh off a win , should get the rest of the season with the Jets. Why not give him more time to see what he can do? There's no real rush there. So, if we're taking temperatures, your gauge on the five jobs above is correct, and I'll raise you a few more for the radar: the Saints and Cowboys.

 Saints coach Kellen Moore making run-game staff changes during the bye week wasn't the best sign. And the vibes out of Dallas leadership are not great. The Christian Parker move was not universally well-received in the building. This might be a case where coach Brian Schottenheimer needs a playoff berth to ensure a third season.

 Graziano: A wild note I saw recently is that the Saints have trailed in all 27 games in which Moore has been their head coach. They must figure out if Tyler Shough is their long-term future at QB, and if they don't think Moore is the coach to help get the most out of him, that could spell trouble, even after only two seasons.

 And I agree on Schottenheimer. The Cowboys are more patient with coaches than their reputation would lead you to believe, but they had very high hopes for this season. If it fizzles out because they blew the defensive coordinator hire, and Schottenheimer gets to the end of the year with another losing record, I think there would be some smoke there.

 

 Fowler: The Chargers are firmly on the radar despite coach Jim Harbaugh's massive buyout on a five-year deal (do the math on what was reported as a five-year, $80 million deal in 2024). If Harbaugh finishes, say, 2-15 in Los Angeles, ownership must do some soul-searching at that point, no? (Particularly when the team plays home games in a stadium it doesn't even own.) And if the Chargers still believe in Harbaugh , the bigger question becomes: Do they trust him to hire a third offensive coordinator in as many years? The Mike McDaniel hire has been flashy but has produced a 30th-ranked scoring offense and lack of a clear identity. The McDaniel era pales in comparison to the Greg Roman era (Roman is thriving with the Giants, by the way).

 And Tennessee seems like one to watch because of the Titans' penchant for firings in recent years. I'm curious whether Tennessee breaks precedent and gives Robert Saleh time. The roster is not good, but no rebuild is ever easy for the coach because of the inevitably bad product. The Titans are 1-9, and a 51-30 loss to Dallas  prompted Saleh to call his defense "dogs---" in a news conference. I'm not sure where to go with that, but what I'm saying is Tennessee is usually a wild card based on recent history.

 

 
 Daniel Jones and Brandon Aiyuk are suddenly free agents after their respective releases. What's next, and where they could land? 
 Editor's note: As of Wednesday afternoon, Aiyuk is signing with the Commanders practice squad . 

 Fowler: Let's start with Jones. Now that he has cleared waivers, he must weigh whether to sign somewhere right away or wait this out to see what develops injury-wise around the league as the playoffs approach. Some people I've talked to inside the league wonder whether  he'll choose the latter . The natural fit right now is New England, which is 5-5 and will be without Drake Maye for what looks like the rest of the regular season . But coach Mike Vrabel seems intent on starting Tommy DeVito , at least this week. So, maybe that's the play -- wait this week out, see what happens with New England or if another team develops an opening.

 But I'm not sure which job would actually rebuild Jones' free agency value at this point. It depends what's important to him: a chance to start, take over for an older quarterback, be next season's bridge guy or learn a new system on a winning team.

 Graziano: If I were considering signing Jones, I'd be thinking more about next season than this one based on everything we've seen from him this year. An Achilles injury is awfully serious, and he wouldn't be the first player we've seen look a lot better in his second season after that surgery than his first. The notion that the 2026 version of Jones could step in and help save someone's season is far-fetched.

 

 I believe the Patriots want to go with DeVito in the hopes that he can keep their train on the track, but as we saw with that disastrous Carson Wentz start for the Vikings a couple of Monday nights ago , poor performance can absolutely change a team's plan. Jones seems like a guy who's going to get another chance somewhere at some point, but my expectations for him being a significant help to a team the rest of this season are quite low.

 Fowler: As for Aiyuk, teams I've spoken to this week have real reservations about whether he gets a job right away, though those conversations occurred…

title: Chuba Hubbard makes the difference again in another tight Panthers win
summary: Chuba Hubbard had a second straight week with two touchdowns in Week 11 of the NFL season, and crucially, both performances have been decisive in nail-biting Carolina Panthers wins.
full_text:
Chuba Hubbard had a second straight week with two touchdowns in Week 11 of the NFL season, and crucially, both performances have been decisive in nail-biting Carolina Panthers wins.

 The Panthers edged the Baltimore Ravens 35-33 to go 5-5 for the season. As it stands, they are fourth in the NFC and on course to host a wild card game.

 Hubbard - who is of Nigerian descent through his father - takes our Africa Player of the Week honors, narrowly edging Week 10 winner Emmett Johnson, who plays for the Kansas City Chiefs and has ties to Liberia.

 Africa Player of the Week: Chuba Hubbard (Carolina Panthers) 

 

 Hubbard was the star of another offense-heavy week for Africa's NFL players. The Panthers running back's two touchdowns took his tally for the season to 11 - joint-fifth in the entire NFL.

 The Panthers trailed 12-0 until Mitchell Evans' touchdown late in the first quarter. A third of the way through the second, Hubbard ran round the outside of Malaki Starks and dived over acrobatically in the corner for an 18-yard touchdown to give the Panthers the lead.

 The lead then changed hands back and forth, with the Ravens taking it again before a Tetairoa McMillan touchdown put the Panthers back in front and then Hubbard added the extra two points.

 

 The Ravens clawed their way back in front to take a 26-22 lead into the half-time break, but the third quarter began with a Panthers drive spanning eight plays in just under four minutes before Hubbard finally went over for another touchdown.

 From there, two Ryan Fitzgerald field goals were enough to see the Panthers over the line. Had it not been for Hubbard's efforts, it is doubtful that they could have pulled it off.

 Africa Moment of the Week: Boye Mafe (Cincinnati Bengals) 

 Mafe was hugely unlucky to end up on the losing side 22-20 against the Washington Commanders, but the moment he notched his third sack in the first half of that game for the Bengals was enough to earn Moment of the Week.

 A son of Nigerian immigrants, Mafe sacked Jayden Daniels once in the first quarter and twice in the second.

 The last of those sacks saw him break through the defensive line and then power through Brandon Coleman's last-ditch attempt to stop him before he latched onto Daniels and hauled him down.

 The 27-year-old defensive end became the first player in the league to record three sacks in the first half of a game since Myles Garrett last November for the Cleveland Browns. Garrett has since moved on to the LA Rams.

 Honorable mentions 

 Nigerian linebacker Princely Umanmielen was instrumental on defense for the Panthers in their win over the Ravens, just as Hubbard was on offense. The 24-year-old picked up 1.5 sacks.

 Emmett Johnson, a running back of Liberian descent, had another impressive showing for the Kansas City Chiefs with 143 total yards and one rushing touchdown in a 34-7 win over the Arizona Cardinals.

 Paulson Adebo - a cornerback of Beninese descent - made an impressive interception for the New York Giants in their 23-18 win over an in-form Jacksonville Jaguars side.

 Adetomiwa Adebawore's sack for the Indianapolis Colts came in a 26-3 loss to the Houston Texans, while Alvin Kamara's touchdown for the New Orleans Saints was not enough to prevent a 21-13 defeat to the Chicago Bears.

 Adebawore is of Nigerian descent, while Kamara has family ties to Liberia.

 Africa-born Player Watch 

 The Panthers' Umanmielen - who was born in Lagos - was a clear standout among the African-born contingent in the NFL in Week 11. His performance was the most complete among them. However, Andrew Mukuba also warrants special mention.

 The safety - born in Harare, Zimbabwe, to a family of refugees from the Democratic Republic of Congo - got in the way of a pass at a crucial stage in the Philadelphia Eagles' 19-16 win over the Pittsburgh Steelers. He failed to hang on for the interception and the Steelers did score immediately afterwards, but did not leave themselves enough time to put together a comeback. Mukuba and the Eagles thus emerged with a much-needed win to keep their playoff hopes alive at 3-7 for the season.

title: Ravens cut punt returner LaJohntay Wester after his two muffs in loss
summary: The Ravens waived returner LaJohntay Wester after he muffed two punts in Sunday's loss at Carolina.
full_text:
OWINGS MILLS, Md. -- The Baltimore Ravens waived returner LaJohntay Wester after he muffed two punts in Sunday's loss to the Carolina Panthers .
After struggling all season with his decision-making, Wester put Baltimore in bad spots Sunday when he misplayed two punts in the second quarter at Carolina.
Wester allowed one punt to go through his hands deep in Baltimore territory, which was converted into a touchdown by the Panthers. He then had another punt ricochet off his face mask, which led to the Ravens recovering at their own 1-yard line.
After being benched, an emotional Wester was consoled by team chaplain Johnny Shelton on the sideline.
Ravens coach Jesse Minter said Monday that wide receiver Devontez Walker could be considered for the punt returner job. Walker returned a kickoff 86 yards for a touchdown Sunday.
A sixth-round pick in 2025, Wester ranks 23rd in the NFL this season with an 8.2-yard punt return average.

title: Bills TE Kincaid, CB Benford among 5 starters who are questionable vs. Chiefs
summary: The Bills are listing five starters -- including tight end Dalton Kincaid and cornerback Christian Benford -- as questionable for Thursday night's showdown with the Chiefs.
full_text:
ORCHARD PARK, N.Y. -- The Buffalo Bills are listing five starters as questionable for one of the biggest games of the year.
Tight end Dalton Kincaid , cornerback Christian Benford , guard O'Cyrus Torrence , linebacker Dorian Williams and defensive lineman T.J. Sanders are all questionable for Thursday's night's matchup between the Bills (9-1) and Kansas City Chiefs (8-2) at Highmark Stadium (8:20 p.m. ET, NBC) in a Thanksgiving game with significant AFC playoff implications.
Kincaid (ankle/thumb), Benford (groin), Williams (calf) and Sanders (shoulder) all sat out the Bills' Week 11 win over the Miami Dolphins . Benford was the only player who was listed with a "did not participate" classification on any of the Bills' injury reports this week, a designation that occurred on Monday, a day after the win over Miami.
Instead of holding a full-speed practice Tuesday, Bills coach Joe Brady opted for a walk-through lasting roughly one hour. He credits his team for having the right type of veteran composure and demeanor that allows him to trust that the players will be prepared for Thursday without needing a standard practice day.
Without Benford, the Bills relied on young cornerbacks Davison Igbinosun and Maxwell Hairston as starters versus Miami, but rotated in veteran Tre'Davious White , who was elevated up from the practice squad on Saturday. Kincaid's absence necessitated a full philosophical overhaul; the Bills went from using 11 personnel (1 tight end and 1 running back) on just 44% of plays through the first nine games to a whopping 80% without Kincaid available.
Kincaid still ranks as the Bills' second leading receiver in receptions and yards, even after missing last week's game. Benford is second on the Bills in pass breakups this season. Williams is tied for the team lead with two interceptions while ranking second on the team in tackles.
Torrence's likely replacement would be veteran Austin Corbett , who started one game last month when left guard Alec Anderson was out. Williams' backup is rookie Kaleb Elarms-Orr , and the defensive line rotation minus Sanders consists of Landon Jackson , Greg Gaines and DeWayne Carter .

title: Bears' Johnson has no plan to stop using Swift in run game despite costly fumbles
summary: Chicago Bears running back D'Andre Swift won't have an extended stay in Ben Johnson's doghouse after fumbling in the fourth quarter against the Saints.
full_text:
LAKE FOREST, Ill. -- Chicago Bears running back D'Andre Swift won't have an extended stay in Ben Johnson's doghouse after fumbling in the fourth quarter against the Saints.
Swift has lost three fumbles through 10 games, which are his most since the 2023 season. The 27-year-old back was pulled from the lineup after New Orleans recovered his fumble at its own 46-yard line and did not return to the game.
That's the second time this season Swift has been benched in game after fumbling.
Swift's fumbles have gone from an aberration to an issue that has become more frequent than at any other point of his Bears tenure. But when asked Tuesday whether Swift needs to regain the trust of his head coach, Johnson rebuffed the idea.
"No, he just needs to hold on to the ball and we'll be fine," Johnson said.
The Bears rushed for 146 yards against the Saints, their third-highest output of the season. Still, Johnson was displeased with the run game's efficiency, spotlighted by Swift's 13 carries for 51 yards (3.9 yards per carry). The veteran back also recorded his first touchdown reception of the season.
"We weren't as consistent running the ball as we had wanted to be coming off the bye, that was a point of emphasis for us," Johnson said postgame. "When I looked at our runners, they were under four yards a carry. That efficiency stat that we talked about, we weren't hitting that."
The Bears' offense centers on a rushing attack that ranks third leaguewide at 142.4 yards per game. That figure would not be possible without Swift, who has played in all 10 games and shouldered a heavier load while running back Kyle Monangai missed five straight weeks with turf toe and a thumb injury. Monangai returned in Week 11 but was limited to eight carries for 18 yards.
With a quick turnaround before facing the Lions on Thanksgiving and seeking their first NFC North win, the Bears are quickly searching for a way to get their run game on track.
From Johnson's perspective, the solution is right in front of them.
"We're going to continue to stress that running game," Johnson said Tuesday. "We got too many good players for it to be lacking behind like it is right now. So, we got to continue to sink into that. It's a big part of what we do and who we are. Whether that's Swift, whether that's Monangai, Salvon [Ahmed] came on and played some big snaps for us. We're going to do that, and we're going to continue to possess the ball and those types of things so that opens up our passing game eventually."
Swift ranks 14th in rushing yards (627), and his 10 rushing TDs are tied for the third in the league. He signed a three-year, $33.75 million contract extension with Chicago before Week 1.

title: NFL survivor power rankings: Why this is the week to use the Jaguars or Texans

Last week, there were five double-digit favorites, and all won. The two biggest favorites to lose were the Cincinnati Bengals and Jacksonville Jaguars (both -6), but neither was popular given the alternatives.

 For the first time since Week 4, no teams are on bye. However, with teams like the Los Angeles Chargers , Miami Dolphins , Indianapolis Colts , and Arizona Cardinals all hosting other pedestrian teams, it is a quietly tricky week in Survivor.

 After their upset losses last week, the Jaguars and Bengals are the two biggest favorites of Week 12. However, very few users have those teams available, which will keep their selection down. The Jaguars are the clear preference of the two, as they are much bigger favorites with slightly lower future value, though it's a fine week to burn the Bengals, too.

 Outside of those two, the Dallas Cowboys are the strongest mix of win equity and lack of future value. They have the third-highest win probability blending the betting market and models from ESPN Analytics and Mike Clay, and they are unlikely to be favored again until Week 17.

 However, in a contest like Circa Survivor, the Cowboys could reach 60% selection, and if that is the case, you are likely better off taking the Denver Broncos or Los Angeles Rams , and even the Philadelphia Eagles become a consideration if you like them more than the market does.

 

 Then there are four teams favored around a touchdown. The Washington Commanders and New York Giants are widely available with little future value. The Houston Texans and Minnesota Vikings are the opposite -- very few entries have them, but they also have more value later.

 In double-pick contests like SplashSports, the Commanders' and Giants' percentages could both be over 35%, which could make pivoting to the next group of teams a smart choice. The Giants are trending to be the most popular pick of the week on both ESPN and Splash, which makes the Commanders the preferred pick of the two.

 The last realistic options are the Cleveland Browns and New York Jets , purely because they play the  Las Vegas Raiders  and Dolphins. However, both could have similar spots down the road against other bad teams, with the Browns still hosting the  Atlanta Falcons  and Colts, while the Jets will play the Cardinals and could play the Tommy DeVito -led  New England Patriots . They are an option only in double-pick pools, but in those contests, the selection discount is enough to have me seriously consider pivoting off the Giants and Commanders.

Just look ahead to Weeks 14 and 17 when you map out your path, as those are the main spots for them on the schedule.

It's a tricky spot on the road after a big "Monday Night Football" win, but the Cardinals are priced as the worst team in the NFL in Mike Clay's model, so taking their opponent is a viable strategy every week.
